Commentary of al-Tha'alibi (al-Jawahir al-Hisan) on surah 9, verses 1–5 (part 1 of 2):

Madaniyyah (Medinan). It has 10,480 letters, 4,098 words, and 130 verses.

Hisham ibn Amir reported from al-Sha'bi, from Masruq, from A'ishah, who said: The Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: «The Qur'an was not sent down to me except verse by verse and letter by letter, with the exception of Surat Bara'ah (al-Tawbah), and Qul huwa Allahu ahad (Surat al-Ikhlas). Both were sent down to me accompanied by seventy thousand rows of angels, each saying: "O Muhammad, enjoin upon the one who bears the name of God goodness."» [[Tafsir Majma' al-Bayan: 5/6.]]

Yazid al-Raqqashi reported from Ibn Abbas, who said: I said to Uthman ibn Affan, may God be pleased with him: What led you to place al-Anfal, which is among the mathani (the oft-repeated surahs), and Bara'ah, which is among the mi'un (the surahs of about a hundred verses), side by side, without writing the line "In the name of God, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful" between them, and placed them among the al-sab' al-tiwal (the seven long surahs)?

Uthman, may God be pleased with him, said: The Messenger of God (ﷺ) would be visited by times when surahs of many verses were revealed to him. When something was revealed to him, he would call one of those who wrote for him and say: "Place this verse in the surah in which such-and-such is mentioned." And when a verse was revealed to him, he would say: "Place this verse in the surah in which such-and-such is mentioned." Al-Anfal was among the surahs revealed in Medina, and Bara'ah was among the last things revealed. Its story resembled the story of al-Anfal, so I thought it was part of it. The Messenger of God (ﷺ) passed away without making clear to us that it was part of it. For this reason I placed them together, did not write the line "In the name of God, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful" between them, and put them among the seven long surahs. [[Tafsir al-Tabari: 10/70.]]

I heard Abu al-Qasim al-Habibi say: I heard Abu Abdullah Muhammad ibn Nafi' al-Sijzi say in Herat:
I heard Abu Yazid Hatim ibn Mahbub al-Shami say: I heard Abd al-Jabbar ibn al-Ala' al-Attar say: Sufyan ibn Uyaynah was asked: Why is "In the name of God, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful" not at the beginning of Bara'ah? He said: Because the basmalah is mercy, and mercy is security, and this surah was sent down concerning the hypocrites and with the sword, and there is no security for the hypocrites.

Bara'ah (Immunity/Disavowal) is in the nominative case as the predicate of an omitted subject, meaning: "These are verses of disavowal." It was also said that it is the predicate of a definite description, the meaning being: "The disavowal, from God and His Messenger, is toward those among the polytheists with whom you made covenants." It means disavowal through the annulment of the covenant and the dissolution of the agreement. It is a verbal noun on the pattern fa'alah, like shana'ah (abomination) and dana'ah (baseness).

«from God and His Messenger, toward those among the polytheists with whom you made covenants». Toward those with whom the Messenger of God (ﷺ) made covenants. He was the one who undertook the covenants, and all of his companions were content with this. So it was as if they had made and confirmed the covenant themselves.

﴿So travel freely﴾: the discourse shifts from the third person to the second person. That is, say to them: "Travel," meaning move about ﴿in the land﴾, going and returning, secure and unafraid of any Muslim, with no war, plunder, killing, or capture. [[Tafsir al-Tabari: 10/87.]]

﴿for four months﴾. It is said: he traveled in the land (sahha fi al-ard yasihu siyahah wa suyuhan wa siyahan).

﴿And know that you cannot escape God﴾, that is, you cannot outrun Him or get ahead of Him, ﴿and that God will disgrace the disbelievers﴾, that is, humiliate them and bring them shame in this world and in the Hereafter.

The scholars differed concerning the manner of this deferral, and concerning those from whom God and His Messenger disavowed, regarding the covenants that existed between them and the Messenger of God among the polytheists.

Muhammad ibn Ishaq and other scholars said: They are two groups of polytheists. One group had a covenant with a term of less than four months, so they were given the full four months. The other had a covenant without a specified term, so it was limited to four months so that they could consider their situation. Then [....] [[a word is obliterated in the original.]] they are subject to war after that, for God, His Messenger, and the believers. They may be killed wherever they are found and taken captive until they repent. The beginning of this term was the day of the greater Hajj, and its end was the tenth of Rabi' al-Akhir.

As for those who had no covenant, their term was the expiry of the sacred months, which is fifty days. Al-Zuhri said: They are Shawwal, Dhu al-Qa'dah, Dhu al-Hijjah, and Muharram, because this verse was revealed in Shawwal. Al-Kalbi said: The four months were only for those who had a covenant with the Messenger of God (ﷺ) of less than four months, so the four months were completed for them. Whoever had a covenant of more than four months, this is the one he was commanded to fulfil, and He said: ﴿So fulfil their covenant to them until their term﴾.

Muqatil said: It was revealed concerning three Arab tribes: Khuza'ah, Banu Mudhhij, and Banu Khuzaymah. The Prophet (ﷺ) had made a two-year covenant with them at Hudaybiyyah, so God, mighty and majestic, made their term four months. The Prophet (ﷺ) made no covenant with anyone after this verse.

Al-Hasan said: God sent Muhammad (ﷺ) and commanded him to call to monotheism and obedience, and He prescribed the laws upon him. He commanded him to fight those among the polytheists who fought him, and He said: ﴿Fight in the way of God those who fight you﴾. He would only fight those who fought him. He refrained from the people of the covenant with whom he had agreements of three or four months, until they considered their situation: either they would embrace Islam, or they would be notified of war. Then He commanded him to fight the polytheists and to disavow them, giving them four months, on condition that they either become Muslim or be notified of war. None of them was given a term longer than four months, neither those who had a covenant before the disavowal nor those who had none. The term was four months for all of them. After the term expired, the blood of all the polytheists was made lawful, both those of the covenant and others.

Abd al-Rahman ibn Zayd said: Every covenant that exceeded four months was annulled and reduced to four.

Muhammad ibn Ishaq, Mujahid, and others said: It was revealed concerning the people of Mecca. The Messenger of God (ﷺ) made a covenant with Quraysh in the year of Hudaybiyyah, that they would lay down war for ten years, during which people would be safe and refrain from harming one another. Khuza'ah entered into the covenant of Muhammad (ﷺ), and Banu Bakr entered into the covenant of Quraysh. There were also covenants with the Messenger of God (ﷺ) and with certain Arab tribes. Banu Bakr attacked Khuza'ah [and killed a man] from among them, and Quraysh supplied the attackers with weapons. When Banu Bakr and Quraysh joined forces against Khuza'ah and broke their covenants, Amr ibn Salim al-Khuza'i set out until he stood before the Messenger of God (ﷺ) and said:

O Lord, I appeal to Muhammad
by the covenant of our father and his, which is sworn to be unbroken.
You were a father to us, and we were your sons;
then we submitted and never withdrew our hand.
So help us, may God guide you, with a mighty help,
and call the servants of God, that they may come with reinforcements.
Among them is the Messenger of God, stripped for battle,
white like the sun, rising high.
If his face is set in anger, it turns dark,
in a host upon the sea, flowing in foam.
Indeed, Quraysh have broken their promise to you,
and violated your firm covenant.
They claimed you would not call anyone,
though they are more humiliated and fewer in number.
They attacked us at al-Hatim while we slept,
and they killed us while we bowed and prostrated.

The Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: «Depart, I will help you if I do not help you.» So he set out and prepared for Mecca, and God granted him the conquest of Mecca, which was in the eighth year after the Hijrah. Then, when he went out to the expedition of Tabuk, some of the hypocrites stayed behind and spread rumours. The polytheists began to break their covenants, and God commanded him to cast their covenants back to them so that they might be notified of war. This is His saying, ﴿And if you fear treachery from a people, throw back to them [their covenant] on equal terms﴾, the verse.

When it was the ninth year, the Messenger of God (ﷺ) wished to perform Hajj. He said: "The polytheists will come and circumambulate the House naked." And he did not [........] [[a passage is obliterated in the original.]] perform Hajj so that this would not happen. The Messenger of God (ﷺ) sent Abu Bakr, may God be pleased with him, that year as commander over the pilgrimage season, to lead the people in Hajj, and he sent with him forty verses from the beginning of Bara'ah, to recite to the people of the season. When he had set out, the Prophet (ﷺ) called Ali and said: «Go out with these verses from the beginning of Bara'ah, and proclaim them to the people when they gather.»

Ali, may God be pleased with him, set out on the Messenger of God's (ﷺ) she-camel al-Ja'da', until he overtook Abu Bakr at Dhu al-Hulayfah and took it from him. Abu Bakr, may God be pleased with him, returned to the Prophet (ﷺ) and said: O Messenger of God, may my father and mother be your ransom, has something been revealed concerning me?

He said: «No, but no one may convey on my behalf except me or a man from my own family. Are you not content, O Abu Bakr, that you were with me in the cave, and that you are my companion at the Basin?» [[Zad al-Masir of Ibn al-Jawzi: 3/266.]]

He said: "Yes, O Messenger of God." This is because it was the custom of the Arabs, in making their covenants and breaking them, that a man from the tribe would take charge of that matter. So the Prophet (ﷺ) sent Ali, lest they say: "This contradicts what we know of some covenants."

Jabir said: I was with Ali, may God be pleased with him, until the Messenger of God (ﷺ) sent Abu Bakr after him. When we were [at al-Araj, the people dressed] for the dawn prayer, Abu Bakr stood up to lead the takbir, and he heard the cry of a camel. He stopped and said: "This is the cry of the Messenger of God's (ﷺ) she-camel al-Ja'da'. Something has surely happened to the Messenger of God regarding the Hajj." Then he saw Ali upon her, and Abu Bakr said: "Are you a commander or one commanded?"

He said: "No, the Messenger of God (ﷺ) sent me with Bara'ah to recite it to the people." So Abu Bakr was commander over the Hajj, and Ali was to proclaim Bara'ah. They both arrived at Mecca, and on the day before the Tarwiyah, Abu Bakr stood up, addressed the people, and told them about their rites, and he led the people in Hajj. The Arabs, at that time, in that year, were following their rites which they had practised in the Jahiliyyah during Hajj. Then, when the day of sacrifice came, Ali ibn Abi Talib, may God be pleased with him, stood up and proclaimed to the people the Hajj in accordance with what he had been commanded, and he recited to them the surah of Bara'ah. [[Sunan al-Darimi: 2/67; Sunan al-Tirmidhi: 4/339.]]

Al-Sha'bi said: Muhammad ibn Abi Hurayrah told me, from his father, who said: I was with Ali, may God be pleased with him, when the Prophet (ﷺ) sent him to proclaim. Whenever his voice weakened (dahala — shallow water upon the surface of the ground with no depth; in some sources: idmahalla), I called out for him. I asked: "With what were you proclaiming?" He said: "Four things: no naked person shall circumambulate the Ka'bah; whoever had a covenant with the Messenger of God, his covenant lasts until its term; no one shall enter Paradise except a believing soul; and no polytheist shall perform Hajj after this year of ours." They said: The polytheists said: "We disavow your covenant and the covenant of your cousin, except for stabbing and striking." They began saying: "O God, we have been prevented from being pious toward You." When it was the tenth year, the Prophet (ﷺ) performed the Farewell Hajj, and then returned to Medina. He remained for the rest of Dhu al-Hijjah, Muharram, Safar, and some nights of Rabi' al-Awwal, until he was taken up to God, mighty and majestic.

﴿And a proclamation from God﴾ is coordinated with His saying ﴿disavowal﴾. Its meaning is notification, and from it comes the adhan (call to prayer). It is said: adhantuhu fa-adhana, meaning I informed him so he knew. Its root is from al-udhn (the ear), that is, I made it reach his ear. Ata' al-Awfi said [...] [[unreadable speech.]]

[The adhan] ﴿And a proclamation from God﴾ up to His saying ﴿And if you fear poverty﴾, the verse. That is twenty-eight verses.

﴿and His Messenger to the people on the day of the greater Hajj﴾. Scholars differed about it. Abu Juhayfah, Ata', Tawus, and Mujahid said: it is the day of Arafah. This is also a narration of Amr from Ibn Abbas. The following hadith supports it:

Abu al-Sahba' al-Bakri reported: I asked Ali ibn Abi Talib about the day of the greater Hajj, and he said: The Messenger of God (ﷺ) sent Abu Bakr ibn Abi Quhafah to teach the people the Hajj, and sent me with him with forty verses of Bara'ah, until he came to Arafah. He addressed the people on the day of Arafah. When he finished his sermon, he turned to me and said: "Come, Ali, and deliver the message of the Messenger of God." So I stood and recited to them forty verses of Bara'ah. Then we departed until we reached Mina. I threw the pebbles at the Jamrah, sacrificed the camel, and shaved my head. I knew that the people of the gathering had not all been present at Abu Bakr's sermon on the day of Arafah, so I went around the tents to recite it to them. For this reason I think you reckoned it to be the day of sacrifice, but indeed it is the day of Arafah. [[Al-Bidayah wa al-Nihayah of Ibn Kathir: 5/47.]]

Shihab ibn Abbad al-Qasri reported from his father, who said: I heard Umar ibn al-Khattab, may God be pleased with him, say: "This is the day of Arafah, the day of the greater Hajj, so let no one fast on it." He said: I performed Hajj after my father, and I came to Medina and asked about its best people. They said: Sa'id ibn al-Musayyib. So I went to him and said: "Inform me about fasting on the day of Arafah." He said: "I will inform you about one who is a hundred times better than me: Umar and Ibn Umar. He used to forbid fasting on it and say: it is the day of the greater Hajj."

Ma'qil ibn Dawud said: I heard Ibn al-Zubayr say on the day of Arafah: "This is the day of the greater Hajj, so let no one fast on it." Ghalib ibn Ubaydullah said: I asked Ata' about the day of the greater Hajj, and he said: "It is the day of Arafah. Break your fast before dawn on it."

Qays ibn Makhramah said: The Messenger of God (ﷺ) gave a sermon on the evening of Arafah, and then said: "Amma ba'd" (he never gave a sermon without saying "Amma ba'd"), "Indeed, this is the day of the greater Hajj." [[Tafsir al-Tabari: 10/89.]]

Nafi' ibn Jubayr, Qays ibn Abbad, Abdullah ibn Sharad, al-Sha'bi, al-Nakha'i, al-Suddi, and Ibn Zayd said: It is the day of sacrifice (al-nahr). This is one of the two reports from Ali, may God be pleased with him.

Yahya ibn al-Jawwad said: Ali, may God be pleased with him, went out on the day of sacrifice on a white mule, heading to the cemetery. A man came up, took hold of the bridle of his mount, and asked him about the greater Hajj. He said: "It is this day of yours, so let go of its reins."

Ayyash al-Amiri said: Abdullah ibn Abi Awfa was asked about the day of the greater Hajj, and he said: "Glory be to God! It is the day of sacrifice, the day on which blood is shed, hair is shaved, and the forbidden becomes lawful."

Al-A'mash reported from Abdullah ibn Sinan, who said: Al-Mughirah ibn Shu'bah addressed us on his she-camel on the day of Eid al-Adha, and said: "This is the day of al-Adha, this is the day of sacrifice, and this is the day of the greater Hajj."

Shu'bah ibn Abi Bishr reported: Ali ibn Abdullah ibn Abbas and a man from the family of Shaybah disputed about the day of the greater Hajj. Ali said: "It is the day of sacrifice," and the man from the family of Shaybah said: "It is the day of Arafah." They sent to Sa'id ibn Jubayr and asked him, and he said: "It is the day of sacrifice. Do you not see that whoever misses the day of Arafah has not missed the Hajj, but whoever misses the day of sacrifice has missed the Hajj?" This is supported by what al-Zuhri reported from Abu Bakr ibn Abd al-Rahman, from Abu Hurayrah, who said: Abu Bakr sent me in that pilgrimage, with a group he dispatched on the day of sacrifice, to proclaim in Mina: "No polytheist shall perform Hajj after this year, and no naked person shall circumambulate the House." Then the Messenger of God (ﷺ) sent Ali behind them, commanding him to proclaim Bara'ah. Abu Hurayrah said: Ali, may God ennoble his face, proclaimed Bara'ah to the people of Mina on the day of sacrifice, together with us.

Salih reported from Ibn Shihab that Humayd ibn Abd al-Rahman informed him that Abu Bakr was sent on the pilgrimage that the Messenger of God (ﷺ) had appointed him over, before the Farewell Hajj, with a group to proclaim to the people: "No polytheist shall perform Hajj after this year, and no naked person shall circumambulate the House." Humayd used to say: "The day of sacrifice is the day of the greater Hajj," from the same report as the hadith of Abu Hurayrah.

Ibn Uyaynah reported from Ibn Jurayj from Mujahid, who said: "The day of the greater Hajj" is the time of Hajj, the days of Mina in their entirety, and the gatherings of the polytheists at Ukaz, Dhu al-Majaz, and Makhshah, and the day on which Ali proclaimed what he proclaimed.

Sufyan al-Thawri used to say: "The day of the greater Hajj" refers to all its days, like the day of Siffin, the day of the Camel, and the day of Bu'ath, and the whole period, because each of these battles lasted many days. [Bu'ath: a war between the Aws and the Khazraj.]

They also differed about the reason why this day was called "the day of the greater Hajj." Al-Hasan said: It is called the greater Hajj because the Hajj of the Muslims and the polytheists coincided on it. Abdullah ibn al-Harith ibn Nawfal said: The day of the greater Hajj was the year of the Farewell Hajj, when the Hajj of the Muslims, the festival of the Jews and Christians, and the polytheists came together, and this had not happened before it or after it.

Mansur and Hammad reported from Mujahid, who said: "The greater Hajj" is said to mean the Qur'an, and "the lesser Hajj" means the single Hajj (ifrad). Al-Zuhri, al-Sha'bi, and Ata' said: "The greater Hajj" is the Hajj, and "the lesser Hajj" is the 'Umrah. It was also said of it: [.........] [[unreadable speech in the original.]] its deed [.........] [[unreadable speech in the original.]] of the Hajj.

His mighty and majestic saying: ﴿That God﴾. Ibn Amir and Hamzah read ﴿Inna Allaha﴾... Isa read ﴿inna Allaha﴾ with a kasrah, on the basis of the beginning of a new sentence, because the proclamation is a statement: ﴿disavowed from the polytheists, and so is His Messenger﴾ is the reading of the common people with a damma, on the basis of the new sentence, and its predicate is omitted; the meaning is: "And His Messenger is also disavowed." Ibn Abi Ishaq, Isa, and Ya'qub read ﴿wa rasulahu﴾ with a fatha, coordinating it with the name of God. He did not say "two are disavowed" (bari'an), because the word refers to each one of them, like the saying of the poet:

Commentary of al-Tha'alibi (al-Jawahir al-Hisan) on surah 9, verse 1–5 (part 2 of 2):

Fa-man yak amsa bil-Madinati rahluhu ... fa-inni wa-Qayyar bihā la-gharib [Qayyar: it is said to be the name of a camel, and it is said to be the name of a horse. The verse is in Lisan al-Arab: 5/125.]

It is narrated from al-Hasan that he read wa-rasulihi with a kasra (genitive), as an oath. It has reached me that a Bedouin heard a man reading it in this reading, and said: "If it is a command from His Messenger, then I am also free of it." The man seized him by his garment and dragged him to Umar ibn al-Khattab, and the Bedouin related his story and his statement. At that point Umar ordered the teaching of Arabic (al-'Arabiyyah, the Arabic language).

﴿Then if you repent﴾, that is, return from your disbelief and devote yourselves to Tawhid, ﴿it is better for you; but if you turn away﴾, that is, turn away from faith [to persistence] in disbelief, ﴿then know that you cannot escape Allah﴾, ﴿and give tidings to those who disbelieve of a painful punishment.﴾ Then He said: ﴿except those with whom you made a covenant.﴾

This is an exception from His saying: ﴿[This is] a declaration of immunity from Allah and His Messenger to the people, except those with whom you made a covenant among the polytheists﴾, ﴿then they have not fallen short of you in anything﴾ of your covenant which you made with them, ﴿nor have they supported anyone against you﴾, that is, of your enemies, neither with themselves, nor with weapons, nor with horses, nor with men, nor with wealth.

Ata' ibn Yasar recited thumma lam yanquduukum with a dotted dad (from naqd al-'ahd, breaking the covenant), while the common reading is with a sad.

As for His saying: ﴿then complete for them their covenant until their term﴾, that is, fulfil their covenant to their appointed time, which you agreed with them. ﴿Indeed, Allah loves those who fear Him.﴾ They were the Banu Damrah and Kinanah, and nine months of their term remained, so He commanded that it be completed for them. ﴿Then when the sacred months have passed﴾, that is, have ended and their time has elapsed. It is said from this: "salakhtu ashhur kadha yuslakhuhu salkhan wa-sulukhan," meaning "we came out." The poet said:

"When I have stripped away the month, I begin the next like it;
Enough to kill me is my stripping away of months and my new moon."
[Lisan al-Arab: 3/25.]

From this also comes "shah maslukhah," a sheep stripped of its skin, and "hayyah salikh," when a snake has come out of its skin.

﴿The sacred months﴾ are four: three in succession, and one single. They are: Dhu al-Qa'dah, Dhu al-Hijjah and al-Muharram, which are three in a row, and Rajab, which stands alone.

Mujahid, Ibn Ishaq, Ibn Zayd and Umar ibn Shu'ayb said: they are the months of the covenant. They were called "al-Hurum" because Allah made unlawful for the believers the shedding of the blood of the polytheists and the molestation of them, except in the way of good.

﴿Then kill the polytheists wherever you find them﴾, in the sanctuary and outside it, ﴿wherever you find them, capture them﴾, ﴿and besiege them﴾, that is, prevent them from entering Makkah and from moving about in the lands of Islam, ﴿and sit in wait for them at every place of ambush﴾, that is, on every road and lookout. It is said: "rasadtu fulanan arsaduhu rasadan" when I watched him. 'Amir ibn al-Tufayl said:

"Indeed you knew, and I do not think you forgetful,
That death lies in wait for the youth at the ambush."
[See: Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 8/73.]

﴿But if they repent﴾ from polytheism, ﴿establish prayer and give zakah﴾, ﴿then let them go on their way.﴾ That is, leave them in their cities, and let them enter Makkah. ﴿Indeed, Allah is Forgiving and Merciful.﴾ [........] [Unreadable speech.] regarding the ruling of this verse.

Al-Husayn ibn al-Fadl said: this verse abrogated every verse in the Qur'an that mentions turning away and patience over the harm of enemies. Al-Dahhak, al-Suddi and Ata' said: His saying ﴿kill the polytheists﴾ is abrogated by His saying: ﴿then either grace afterward or ransom﴾ [Surah Muhammad: 4]. Qatadah said: rather, it abrogates His saying: ﴿then either grace afterward or ransom.﴾

The correct view is that the ruling of this verse stands, and that neither of the two is abrogated by the other, because grace, killing, and ransom have never ceased to be part of the ruling of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) toward them from the beginning of fighting them, which was the Day of Badr. His Exalted saying ﴿and seize them﴾ supports this, since seizing means capturing, and capture is only for killing or ransom. Evidence for this also is the report of Ata', who said: The Prophet (ﷺ) was brought a captive called Abu Umamah, who was the chief of Yamamah. The Prophet (ﷺ) said to him:
"O Abu Umamah, which do you prefer: that I free you, or that I ransom you, or that I kill you, or that you submit?" He said: "If you free me, you free a great man; if you ransom me, you ransom a great man; if you kill me, you kill a great man; but as for my submitting, no, by Allah, I will never submit."
He said: "Then I have freed you." He said: "I testify that there is no god but Allah, and I testify that you are His Messenger."

The grain supply of Makkah came from Yamamah. He said to the people of Makkah: "By Him besides whom there is no god, no grain or grain-seed will come to you from Yamamah ever, until you believe in Allah and His Messenger." They were harmed, and they wrote to the Prophet (ﷺ), since they had kinship ties with him, complaining of this to him. He wrote to Abu Umamah: "Do not cut off the grain supply to them that came from you," and Abu Umamah did so.

Commentary of al-Tha'alibi (al-Jawahir al-Hisan) on surah 9, verses 1–5 (part 1 of 2):

Madaniyyah (Medinan). It has 10,480 letters, 4,098 words, and 130 verses.

Hisham ibn Amir reported from al-Sha'bi, from Masruq, from A'ishah, who said: The Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: «The Qur'an was not sent down to me except verse by verse and letter by letter, with the exception of Surat Bara'ah (al-Tawbah), and Qul huwa Allahu ahad (Surat al-Ikhlas). Both were sent down to me accompanied by seventy thousand rows of angels, each saying: "O Muhammad, enjoin upon the one who bears the name of God goodness."» [[Tafsir Majma' al-Bayan: 5/6.]]

Yazid al-Raqqashi reported from Ibn Abbas, who said: I said to Uthman ibn Affan, may God be pleased with him: What led you to place al-Anfal, which is among the mathani (the oft-repeated surahs), and Bara'ah, which is among the mi'un (the surahs of about a hundred verses), side by side, without writing the line "In the name of God, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful" between them, and placed them among the al-sab' al-tiwal (the seven long surahs)?

Uthman, may God be pleased with him, said: The Messenger of God (ﷺ) would be visited by times when surahs of many verses were revealed to him. When something was revealed to him, he would call one of those who wrote for him and say: "Place this verse in the surah in which such-and-such is mentioned." And when a verse was revealed to him, he would say: "Place this verse in the surah in which such-and-such is mentioned." Al-Anfal was among the surahs revealed in Medina, and Bara'ah was among the last things revealed. Its story resembled the story of al-Anfal, so I thought it was part of it. The Messenger of God (ﷺ) passed away without making clear to us that it was part of it. For this reason I placed them together, did not write the line "In the name of God, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful" between them, and put them among the seven long surahs. [[Tafsir al-Tabari: 10/70.]]

I heard Abu al-Qasim al-Habibi say: I heard Abu Abdullah Muhammad ibn Nafi' al-Sijzi say in Herat:
I heard Abu Yazid Hatim ibn Mahbub al-Shami say: I heard Abd al-Jabbar ibn al-Ala' al-Attar say: Sufyan ibn Uyaynah was asked: Why is "In the name of God, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful" not at the beginning of Bara'ah? He said: Because the basmalah is mercy, and mercy is security, and this surah was sent down concerning the hypocrites and with the sword, and there is no security for the hypocrites.

Bara'ah (Immunity/Disavowal) is in the nominative case as the predicate of an omitted subject, meaning: "These are verses of disavowal." It was also said that it is the predicate of a definite description, the meaning being: "The disavowal, from God and His Messenger, is toward those among the polytheists with whom you made covenants." It means disavowal through the annulment of the covenant and the dissolution of the agreement. It is a verbal noun on the pattern fa'alah, like shana'ah (abomination) and dana'ah (baseness).

«from God and His Messenger, toward those among the polytheists with whom you made covenants». Toward those with whom the Messenger of God (ﷺ) made covenants. He was the one who undertook the covenants, and all of his companions were content with this. So it was as if they had made and confirmed the covenant themselves.

﴿So travel freely﴾: the discourse shifts from the third person to the second person. That is, say to them: "Travel," meaning move about ﴿in the land﴾, going and returning, secure and unafraid of any Muslim, with no war, plunder, killing, or capture. [[Tafsir al-Tabari: 10/87.]]

﴿for four months﴾. It is said: he traveled in the land (sahha fi al-ard yasihu siyahah wa suyuhan wa siyahan).

﴿And know that you cannot escape God﴾, that is, you cannot outrun Him or get ahead of Him, ﴿and that God will disgrace the disbelievers﴾, that is, humiliate them and bring them shame in this world and in the Hereafter.

The scholars differed concerning the manner of this deferral, and concerning those from whom God and His Messenger disavowed, regarding the covenants that existed between them and the Messenger of God among the polytheists.

Muhammad ibn Ishaq and other scholars said: They are two groups of polytheists. One group had a covenant with a term of less than four months, so they were given the full four months. The other had a covenant without a specified term, so it was limited to four months so that they could consider their situation. Then [....] [[a word is obliterated in the original.]] they are subject to war after that, for God, His Messenger, and the believers. They may be killed wherever they are found and taken captive until they repent. The beginning of this term was the day of the greater Hajj, and its end was the tenth of Rabi' al-Akhir.

As for those who had no covenant, their term was the expiry of the sacred months, which is fifty days. Al-Zuhri said: They are Shawwal, Dhu al-Qa'dah, Dhu al-Hijjah, and Muharram, because this verse was revealed in Shawwal. Al-Kalbi said: The four months were only for those who had a covenant with the Messenger of God (ﷺ) of less than four months, so the four months were completed for them. Whoever had a covenant of more than four months, this is the one he was commanded to fulfil, and He said: ﴿So fulfil their covenant to them until their term﴾.

Muqatil said: It was revealed concerning three Arab tribes: Khuza'ah, Banu Mudhhij, and Banu Khuzaymah. The Prophet (ﷺ) had made a two-year covenant with them at Hudaybiyyah, so God, mighty and majestic, made their term four months. The Prophet (ﷺ) made no covenant with anyone after this verse.

Al-Hasan said: God sent Muhammad (ﷺ) and commanded him to call to monotheism and obedience, and He prescribed the laws upon him. He commanded him to fight those among the polytheists who fought him, and He said: ﴿Fight in the way of God those who fight you﴾. He would only fight those who fought him. He refrained from the people of the covenant with whom he had agreements of three or four months, until they considered their situation: either they would embrace Islam, or they would be notified of war. Then He commanded him to fight the polytheists and to disavow them, giving them four months, on condition that they either become Muslim or be notified of war. None of them was given a term longer than four months, neither those who had a covenant before the disavowal nor those who had none. The term was four months for all of them. After the term expired, the blood of all the polytheists was made lawful, both those of the covenant and others.

Abd al-Rahman ibn Zayd said: Every covenant that exceeded four months was annulled and reduced to four.

Muhammad ibn Ishaq, Mujahid, and others said: It was revealed concerning the people of Mecca. The Messenger of God (ﷺ) made a covenant with Quraysh in the year of Hudaybiyyah, that they would lay down war for ten years, during which people would be safe and refrain from harming one another. Khuza'ah entered into the covenant of Muhammad (ﷺ), and Banu Bakr entered into the covenant of Quraysh. There were also covenants with the Messenger of God (ﷺ) and with certain Arab tribes. Banu Bakr attacked Khuza'ah [and killed a man] from among them, and Quraysh supplied the attackers with weapons. When Banu Bakr and Quraysh joined forces against Khuza'ah and broke their covenants, Amr ibn Salim al-Khuza'i set out until he stood before the Messenger of God (ﷺ) and said:

O Lord, I appeal to Muhammad
by the covenant of our father and his, which is sworn to be unbroken.
You were a father to us, and we were your sons;
then we submitted and never withdrew our hand.
So help us, may God guide you, with a mighty help,
and call the servants of God, that they may come with reinforcements.
Among them is the Messenger of God, stripped for battle,
white like the sun, rising high.
If his face is set in anger, it turns dark,
in a host upon the sea, flowing in foam.
Indeed, Quraysh have broken their promise to you,
and violated your firm covenant.
They claimed you would not call anyone,
though they are more humiliated and fewer in number.
They attacked us at al-Hatim while we slept,
and they killed us while we bowed and prostrated.

The Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: «Depart, I will help you if I do not help you.» So he set out and prepared for Mecca, and God granted him the conquest of Mecca, which was in the eighth year after the Hijrah. Then, when he went out to the expedition of Tabuk, some of the hypocrites stayed behind and spread rumours. The polytheists began to break their covenants, and God commanded him to cast their covenants back to them so that they might be notified of war. This is His saying, ﴿And if you fear treachery from a people, throw back to them [their covenant] on equal terms﴾, the verse.

When it was the ninth year, the Messenger of God (ﷺ) wished to perform Hajj. He said: "The polytheists will come and circumambulate the House naked." And he did not [........] [[a passage is obliterated in the original.]] perform Hajj so that this would not happen. The Messenger of God (ﷺ) sent Abu Bakr, may God be pleased with him, that year as commander over the pilgrimage season, to lead the people in Hajj, and he sent with him forty verses from the beginning of Bara'ah, to recite to the people of the season. When he had set out, the Prophet (ﷺ) called Ali and said: «Go out with these verses from the beginning of Bara'ah, and proclaim them to the people when they gather.»

Ali, may God be pleased with him, set out on the Messenger of God's (ﷺ) she-camel al-Ja'da', until he overtook Abu Bakr at Dhu al-Hulayfah and took it from him. Abu Bakr, may God be pleased with him, returned to the Prophet (ﷺ) and said: O Messenger of God, may my father and mother be your ransom, has something been revealed concerning me?

He said: «No, but no one may convey on my behalf except me or a man from my own family. Are you not content, O Abu Bakr, that you were with me in the cave, and that you are my companion at the Basin?» [[Zad al-Masir of Ibn al-Jawzi: 3/266.]]

He said: "Yes, O Messenger of God." This is because it was the custom of the Arabs, in making their covenants and breaking them, that a man from the tribe would take charge of that matter. So the Prophet (ﷺ) sent Ali, lest they say: "This contradicts what we know of some covenants."

Jabir said: I was with Ali, may God be pleased with him, until the Messenger of God (ﷺ) sent Abu Bakr after him. When we were [at al-Araj, the people dressed] for the dawn prayer, Abu Bakr stood up to lead the takbir, and he heard the cry of a camel. He stopped and said: "This is the cry of the Messenger of God's (ﷺ) she-camel al-Ja'da'. Something has surely happened to the Messenger of God regarding the Hajj." Then he saw Ali upon her, and Abu Bakr said: "Are you a commander or one commanded?"

He said: "No, the Messenger of God (ﷺ) sent me with Bara'ah to recite it to the people." So Abu Bakr was commander over the Hajj, and Ali was to proclaim Bara'ah. They both arrived at Mecca, and on the day before the Tarwiyah, Abu Bakr stood up, addressed the people, and told them about their rites, and he led the people in Hajj. The Arabs, at that time, in that year, were following their rites which they had practised in the Jahiliyyah during Hajj. Then, when the day of sacrifice came, Ali ibn Abi Talib, may God be pleased with him, stood up and proclaimed to the people the Hajj in accordance with what he had been commanded, and he recited to them the surah of Bara'ah. [[Sunan al-Darimi: 2/67; Sunan al-Tirmidhi: 4/339.]]

Al-Sha'bi said: Muhammad ibn Abi Hurayrah told me, from his father, who said: I was with Ali, may God be pleased with him, when the Prophet (ﷺ) sent him to proclaim. Whenever his voice weakened (dahala — shallow water upon the surface of the ground with no depth; in some sources: idmahalla), I called out for him. I asked: "With what were you proclaiming?" He said: "Four things: no naked person shall circumambulate the Ka'bah; whoever had a covenant with the Messenger of God, his covenant lasts until its term; no one shall enter Paradise except a believing soul; and no polytheist shall perform Hajj after this year of ours." They said: The polytheists said: "We disavow your covenant and the covenant of your cousin, except for stabbing and striking." They began saying: "O God, we have been prevented from being pious toward You." When it was the tenth year, the Prophet (ﷺ) performed the Farewell Hajj, and then returned to Medina. He remained for the rest of Dhu al-Hijjah, Muharram, Safar, and some nights of Rabi' al-Awwal, until he was taken up to God, mighty and majestic.

﴿And a proclamation from God﴾ is coordinated with His saying ﴿disavowal﴾. Its meaning is notification, and from it comes the adhan (call to prayer). It is said: adhantuhu fa-adhana, meaning I informed him so he knew. Its root is from al-udhn (the ear), that is, I made it reach his ear. Ata' al-Awfi said [...] [[unreadable speech.]]

[The adhan] ﴿And a proclamation from God﴾ up to His saying ﴿And if you fear poverty﴾, the verse. That is twenty-eight verses.

﴿and His Messenger to the people on the day of the greater Hajj﴾. Scholars differed about it. Abu Juhayfah, Ata', Tawus, and Mujahid said: it is the day of Arafah. This is also a narration of Amr from Ibn Abbas. The following hadith supports it:

Abu al-Sahba' al-Bakri reported: I asked Ali ibn Abi Talib about the day of the greater Hajj, and he said: The Messenger of God (ﷺ) sent Abu Bakr ibn Abi Quhafah to teach the people the Hajj, and sent me with him with forty verses of Bara'ah, until he came to Arafah. He addressed the people on the day of Arafah. When he finished his sermon, he turned to me and said: "Come, Ali, and deliver the message of the Messenger of God." So I stood and recited to them forty verses of Bara'ah. Then we departed until we reached Mina. I threw the pebbles at the Jamrah, sacrificed the camel, and shaved my head. I knew that the people of the gathering had not all been present at Abu Bakr's sermon on the day of Arafah, so I went around the tents to recite it to them. For this reason I think you reckoned it to be the day of sacrifice, but indeed it is the day of Arafah. [[Al-Bidayah wa al-Nihayah of Ibn Kathir: 5/47.]]

Shihab ibn Abbad al-Qasri reported from his father, who said: I heard Umar ibn al-Khattab, may God be pleased with him, say: "This is the day of Arafah, the day of the greater Hajj, so let no one fast on it." He said: I performed Hajj after my father, and I came to Medina and asked about its best people. They said: Sa'id ibn al-Musayyib. So I went to him and said: "Inform me about fasting on the day of Arafah." He said: "I will inform you about one who is a hundred times better than me: Umar and Ibn Umar. He used to forbid fasting on it and say: it is the day of the greater Hajj."

Ma'qil ibn Dawud said: I heard Ibn al-Zubayr say on the day of Arafah: "This is the day of the greater Hajj, so let no one fast on it." Ghalib ibn Ubaydullah said: I asked Ata' about the day of the greater Hajj, and he said: "It is the day of Arafah. Break your fast before dawn on it."

Qays ibn Makhramah said: The Messenger of God (ﷺ) gave a sermon on the evening of Arafah, and then said: "Amma ba'd" (he never gave a sermon without saying "Amma ba'd"), "Indeed, this is the day of the greater Hajj." [[Tafsir al-Tabari: 10/89.]]

Nafi' ibn Jubayr, Qays ibn Abbad, Abdullah ibn Sharad, al-Sha'bi, al-Nakha'i, al-Suddi, and Ibn Zayd said: It is the day of sacrifice (al-nahr). This is one of the two reports from Ali, may God be pleased with him.

Yahya ibn al-Jawwad said: Ali, may God be pleased with him, went out on the day of sacrifice on a white mule, heading to the cemetery. A man came up, took hold of the bridle of his mount, and asked him about the greater Hajj. He said: "It is this day of yours, so let go of its reins."

Ayyash al-Amiri said: Abdullah ibn Abi Awfa was asked about the day of the greater Hajj, and he said: "Glory be to God! It is the day of sacrifice, the day on which blood is shed, hair is shaved, and the forbidden becomes lawful."

Al-A'mash reported from Abdullah ibn Sinan, who said: Al-Mughirah ibn Shu'bah addressed us on his she-camel on the day of Eid al-Adha, and said: "This is the day of al-Adha, this is the day of sacrifice, and this is the day of the greater Hajj."

Shu'bah ibn Abi Bishr reported: Ali ibn Abdullah ibn Abbas and a man from the family of Shaybah disputed about the day of the greater Hajj. Ali said: "It is the day of sacrifice," and the man from the family of Shaybah said: "It is the day of Arafah." They sent to Sa'id ibn Jubayr and asked him, and he said: "It is the day of sacrifice. Do you not see that whoever misses the day of Arafah has not missed the Hajj, but whoever misses the day of sacrifice has missed the Hajj?" This is supported by what al-Zuhri reported from Abu Bakr ibn Abd al-Rahman, from Abu Hurayrah, who said: Abu Bakr sent me in that pilgrimage, with a group he dispatched on the day of sacrifice, to proclaim in Mina: "No polytheist shall perform Hajj after this year, and no naked person shall circumambulate the House." Then the Messenger of God (ﷺ) sent Ali behind them, commanding him to proclaim Bara'ah. Abu Hurayrah said: Ali, may God ennoble his face, proclaimed Bara'ah to the people of Mina on the day of sacrifice, together with us.

Salih reported from Ibn Shihab that Humayd ibn Abd al-Rahman informed him that Abu Bakr was sent on the pilgrimage that the Messenger of God (ﷺ) had appointed him over, before the Farewell Hajj, with a group to proclaim to the people: "No polytheist shall perform Hajj after this year, and no naked person shall circumambulate the House." Humayd used to say: "The day of sacrifice is the day of the greater Hajj," from the same report as the hadith of Abu Hurayrah.

Ibn Uyaynah reported from Ibn Jurayj from Mujahid, who said: "The day of the greater Hajj" is the time of Hajj, the days of Mina in their entirety, and the gatherings of the polytheists at Ukaz, Dhu al-Majaz, and Makhshah, and the day on which Ali proclaimed what he proclaimed.

Sufyan al-Thawri used to say: "The day of the greater Hajj" refers to all its days, like the day of Siffin, the day of the Camel, and the day of Bu'ath, and the whole period, because each of these battles lasted many days. [Bu'ath: a war between the Aws and the Khazraj.]

They also differed about the reason why this day was called "the day of the greater Hajj." Al-Hasan said: It is called the greater Hajj because the Hajj of the Muslims and the polytheists coincided on it. Abdullah ibn al-Harith ibn Nawfal said: The day of the greater Hajj was the year of the Farewell Hajj, when the Hajj of the Muslims, the festival of the Jews and Christians, and the polytheists came together, and this had not happened before it or after it.

Mansur and Hammad reported from Mujahid, who said: "The greater Hajj" is said to mean the Qur'an, and "the lesser Hajj" means the single Hajj (ifrad). Al-Zuhri, al-Sha'bi, and Ata' said: "The greater Hajj" is the Hajj, and "the lesser Hajj" is the 'Umrah. It was also said of it: [.........] [[unreadable speech in the original.]] its deed [.........] [[unreadable speech in the original.]] of the Hajj.

His mighty and majestic saying: ﴿That God﴾. Ibn Amir and Hamzah read ﴿Inna Allaha﴾... Isa read ﴿inna Allaha﴾ with a kasrah, on the basis of the beginning of a new sentence, because the proclamation is a statement: ﴿disavowed from the polytheists, and so is His Messenger﴾ is the reading of the common people with a damma, on the basis of the new sentence, and its predicate is omitted; the meaning is: "And His Messenger is also disavowed." Ibn Abi Ishaq, Isa, and Ya'qub read ﴿wa rasulahu﴾ with a fatha, coordinating it with the name of God. He did not say "two are disavowed" (bari'an), because the word refers to each one of them, like the saying of the poet:

Commentary of al-Tha'alibi (al-Jawahir al-Hisan) on surah 9, verse 1–5 (part 2 of 2):

Fa-man yak amsa bil-Madinati rahluhu ... fa-inni wa-Qayyar bihā la-gharib [Qayyar: it is said to be the name of a camel, and it is said to be the name of a horse. The verse is in Lisan al-Arab: 5/125.]

It is narrated from al-Hasan that he read wa-rasulihi with a kasra (genitive), as an oath. It has reached me that a Bedouin heard a man reading it in this reading, and said: "If it is a command from His Messenger, then I am also free of it." The man seized him by his garment and dragged him to Umar ibn al-Khattab, and the Bedouin related his story and his statement. At that point Umar ordered the teaching of Arabic (al-'Arabiyyah, the Arabic language).

﴿Then if you repent﴾, that is, return from your disbelief and devote yourselves to Tawhid, ﴿it is better for you; but if you turn away﴾, that is, turn away from faith [to persistence] in disbelief, ﴿then know that you cannot escape Allah﴾, ﴿and give tidings to those who disbelieve of a painful punishment.﴾ Then He said: ﴿except those with whom you made a covenant.﴾

This is an exception from His saying: ﴿[This is] a declaration of immunity from Allah and His Messenger to the people, except those with whom you made a covenant among the polytheists﴾, ﴿then they have not fallen short of you in anything﴾ of your covenant which you made with them, ﴿nor have they supported anyone against you﴾, that is, of your enemies, neither with themselves, nor with weapons, nor with horses, nor with men, nor with wealth.

Ata' ibn Yasar recited thumma lam yanquduukum with a dotted dad (from naqd al-'ahd, breaking the covenant), while the common reading is with a sad.

As for His saying: ﴿then complete for them their covenant until their term﴾, that is, fulfil their covenant to their appointed time, which you agreed with them. ﴿Indeed, Allah loves those who fear Him.﴾ They were the Banu Damrah and Kinanah, and nine months of their term remained, so He commanded that it be completed for them. ﴿Then when the sacred months have passed﴾, that is, have ended and their time has elapsed. It is said from this: "salakhtu ashhur kadha yuslakhuhu salkhan wa-sulukhan," meaning "we came out." The poet said:

"When I have stripped away the month, I begin the next like it;
Enough to kill me is my stripping away of months and my new moon."
[Lisan al-Arab: 3/25.]

From this also comes "shah maslukhah," a sheep stripped of its skin, and "hayyah salikh," when a snake has come out of its skin.

﴿The sacred months﴾ are four: three in succession, and one single. They are: Dhu al-Qa'dah, Dhu al-Hijjah and al-Muharram, which are three in a row, and Rajab, which stands alone.

Mujahid, Ibn Ishaq, Ibn Zayd and Umar ibn Shu'ayb said: they are the months of the covenant. They were called "al-Hurum" because Allah made unlawful for the believers the shedding of the blood of the polytheists and the molestation of them, except in the way of good.

﴿Then kill the polytheists wherever you find them﴾, in the sanctuary and outside it, ﴿wherever you find them, capture them﴾, ﴿and besiege them﴾, that is, prevent them from entering Makkah and from moving about in the lands of Islam, ﴿and sit in wait for them at every place of ambush﴾, that is, on every road and lookout. It is said: "rasadtu fulanan arsaduhu rasadan" when I watched him. 'Amir ibn al-Tufayl said:

"Indeed you knew, and I do not think you forgetful,
That death lies in wait for the youth at the ambush."
[See: Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 8/73.]

﴿But if they repent﴾ from polytheism, ﴿establish prayer and give zakah﴾, ﴿then let them go on their way.﴾ That is, leave them in their cities, and let them enter Makkah. ﴿Indeed, Allah is Forgiving and Merciful.﴾ [........] [Unreadable speech.] regarding the ruling of this verse.

Al-Husayn ibn al-Fadl said: this verse abrogated every verse in the Qur'an that mentions turning away and patience over the harm of enemies. Al-Dahhak, al-Suddi and Ata' said: His saying ﴿kill the polytheists﴾ is abrogated by His saying: ﴿then either grace afterward or ransom﴾ [Surah Muhammad: 4]. Qatadah said: rather, it abrogates His saying: ﴿then either grace afterward or ransom.﴾

The correct view is that the ruling of this verse stands, and that neither of the two is abrogated by the other, because grace, killing, and ransom have never ceased to be part of the ruling of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) toward them from the beginning of fighting them, which was the Day of Badr. His Exalted saying ﴿and seize them﴾ supports this, since seizing means capturing, and capture is only for killing or ransom. Evidence for this also is the report of Ata', who said: The Prophet (ﷺ) was brought a captive called Abu Umamah, who was the chief of Yamamah. The Prophet (ﷺ) said to him:
"O Abu Umamah, which do you prefer: that I free you, or that I ransom you, or that I kill you, or that you submit?" He said: "If you free me, you free a great man; if you ransom me, you ransom a great man; if you kill me, you kill a great man; but as for my submitting, no, by Allah, I will never submit."
He said: "Then I have freed you." He said: "I testify that there is no god but Allah, and I testify that you are His Messenger."

The grain supply of Makkah came from Yamamah. He said to the people of Makkah: "By Him besides whom there is no god, no grain or grain-seed will come to you from Yamamah ever, until you believe in Allah and His Messenger." They were harmed, and they wrote to the Prophet (ﷺ), since they had kinship ties with him, complaining of this to him. He wrote to Abu Umamah: "Do not cut off the grain supply to them that came from you," and Abu Umamah did so.

Commentary of al-Tha'alibi (al-Jawahir al-Hisan) on surah 9, verses 1–5 (part 1 of 2):

Madaniyyah (Medinan). It has 10,480 letters, 4,098 words, and 130 verses.

Hisham ibn Amir reported from al-Sha'bi, from Masruq, from A'ishah, who said: The Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: «The Qur'an was not sent down to me except verse by verse and letter by letter, with the exception of Surat Bara'ah (al-Tawbah), and Qul huwa Allahu ahad (Surat al-Ikhlas). Both were sent down to me accompanied by seventy thousand rows of angels, each saying: "O Muhammad, enjoin upon the one who bears the name of God goodness."» [[Tafsir Majma' al-Bayan: 5/6.]]

Yazid al-Raqqashi reported from Ibn Abbas, who said: I said to Uthman ibn Affan, may God be pleased with him: What led you to place al-Anfal, which is among the mathani (the oft-repeated surahs), and Bara'ah, which is among the mi'un (the surahs of about a hundred verses), side by side, without writing the line "In the name of God, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful" between them, and placed them among the al-sab' al-tiwal (the seven long surahs)?

Uthman, may God be pleased with him, said: The Messenger of God (ﷺ) would be visited by times when surahs of many verses were revealed to him. When something was revealed to him, he would call one of those who wrote for him and say: "Place this verse in the surah in which such-and-such is mentioned." And when a verse was revealed to him, he would say: "Place this verse in the surah in which such-and-such is mentioned." Al-Anfal was among the surahs revealed in Medina, and Bara'ah was among the last things revealed. Its story resembled the story of al-Anfal, so I thought it was part of it. The Messenger of God (ﷺ) passed away without making clear to us that it was part of it. For this reason I placed them together, did not write the line "In the name of God, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful" between them, and put them among the seven long surahs. [[Tafsir al-Tabari: 10/70.]]

I heard Abu al-Qasim al-Habibi say: I heard Abu Abdullah Muhammad ibn Nafi' al-Sijzi say in Herat:
I heard Abu Yazid Hatim ibn Mahbub al-Shami say: I heard Abd al-Jabbar ibn al-Ala' al-Attar say: Sufyan ibn Uyaynah was asked: Why is "In the name of God, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful" not at the beginning of Bara'ah? He said: Because the basmalah is mercy, and mercy is security, and this surah was sent down concerning the hypocrites and with the sword, and there is no security for the hypocrites.

Bara'ah (Immunity/Disavowal) is in the nominative case as the predicate of an omitted subject, meaning: "These are verses of disavowal." It was also said that it is the predicate of a definite description, the meaning being: "The disavowal, from God and His Messenger, is toward those among the polytheists with whom you made covenants." It means disavowal through the annulment of the covenant and the dissolution of the agreement. It is a verbal noun on the pattern fa'alah, like shana'ah (abomination) and dana'ah (baseness).

«from God and His Messenger, toward those among the polytheists with whom you made covenants». Toward those with whom the Messenger of God (ﷺ) made covenants. He was the one who undertook the covenants, and all of his companions were content with this. So it was as if they had made and confirmed the covenant themselves.

﴿So travel freely﴾: the discourse shifts from the third person to the second person. That is, say to them: "Travel," meaning move about ﴿in the land﴾, going and returning, secure and unafraid of any Muslim, with no war, plunder, killing, or capture. [[Tafsir al-Tabari: 10/87.]]

﴿for four months﴾. It is said: he traveled in the land (sahha fi al-ard yasihu siyahah wa suyuhan wa siyahan).

﴿And know that you cannot escape God﴾, that is, you cannot outrun Him or get ahead of Him, ﴿and that God will disgrace the disbelievers﴾, that is, humiliate them and bring them shame in this world and in the Hereafter.

The scholars differed concerning the manner of this deferral, and concerning those from whom God and His Messenger disavowed, regarding the covenants that existed between them and the Messenger of God among the polytheists.

Muhammad ibn Ishaq and other scholars said: They are two groups of polytheists. One group had a covenant with a term of less than four months, so they were given the full four months. The other had a covenant without a specified term, so it was limited to four months so that they could consider their situation. Then [....] [[a word is obliterated in the original.]] they are subject to war after that, for God, His Messenger, and the believers. They may be killed wherever they are found and taken captive until they repent. The beginning of this term was the day of the greater Hajj, and its end was the tenth of Rabi' al-Akhir.

As for those who had no covenant, their term was the expiry of the sacred months, which is fifty days. Al-Zuhri said: They are Shawwal, Dhu al-Qa'dah, Dhu al-Hijjah, and Muharram, because this verse was revealed in Shawwal. Al-Kalbi said: The four months were only for those who had a covenant with the Messenger of God (ﷺ) of less than four months, so the four months were completed for them. Whoever had a covenant of more than four months, this is the one he was commanded to fulfil, and He said: ﴿So fulfil their covenant to them until their term﴾.

Muqatil said: It was revealed concerning three Arab tribes: Khuza'ah, Banu Mudhhij, and Banu Khuzaymah. The Prophet (ﷺ) had made a two-year covenant with them at Hudaybiyyah, so God, mighty and majestic, made their term four months. The Prophet (ﷺ) made no covenant with anyone after this verse.

Al-Hasan said: God sent Muhammad (ﷺ) and commanded him to call to monotheism and obedience, and He prescribed the laws upon him. He commanded him to fight those among the polytheists who fought him, and He said: ﴿Fight in the way of God those who fight you﴾. He would only fight those who fought him. He refrained from the people of the covenant with whom he had agreements of three or four months, until they considered their situation: either they would embrace Islam, or they would be notified of war. Then He commanded him to fight the polytheists and to disavow them, giving them four months, on condition that they either become Muslim or be notified of war. None of them was given a term longer than four months, neither those who had a covenant before the disavowal nor those who had none. The term was four months for all of them. After the term expired, the blood of all the polytheists was made lawful, both those of the covenant and others.

Abd al-Rahman ibn Zayd said: Every covenant that exceeded four months was annulled and reduced to four.

Muhammad ibn Ishaq, Mujahid, and others said: It was revealed concerning the people of Mecca. The Messenger of God (ﷺ) made a covenant with Quraysh in the year of Hudaybiyyah, that they would lay down war for ten years, during which people would be safe and refrain from harming one another. Khuza'ah entered into the covenant of Muhammad (ﷺ), and Banu Bakr entered into the covenant of Quraysh. There were also covenants with the Messenger of God (ﷺ) and with certain Arab tribes. Banu Bakr attacked Khuza'ah [and killed a man] from among them, and Quraysh supplied the attackers with weapons. When Banu Bakr and Quraysh joined forces against Khuza'ah and broke their covenants, Amr ibn Salim al-Khuza'i set out until he stood before the Messenger of God (ﷺ) and said:

O Lord, I appeal to Muhammad
by the covenant of our father and his, which is sworn to be unbroken.
You were a father to us, and we were your sons;
then we submitted and never withdrew our hand.
So help us, may God guide you, with a mighty help,
and call the servants of God, that they may come with reinforcements.
Among them is the Messenger of God, stripped for battle,
white like the sun, rising high.
If his face is set in anger, it turns dark,
in a host upon the sea, flowing in foam.
Indeed, Quraysh have broken their promise to you,
and violated your firm covenant.
They claimed you would not call anyone,
though they are more humiliated and fewer in number.
They attacked us at al-Hatim while we slept,
and they killed us while we bowed and prostrated.

The Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: «Depart, I will help you if I do not help you.» So he set out and prepared for Mecca, and God granted him the conquest of Mecca, which was in the eighth year after the Hijrah. Then, when he went out to the expedition of Tabuk, some of the hypocrites stayed behind and spread rumours. The polytheists began to break their covenants, and God commanded him to cast their covenants back to them so that they might be notified of war. This is His saying, ﴿And if you fear treachery from a people, throw back to them [their covenant] on equal terms﴾, the verse.

When it was the ninth year, the Messenger of God (ﷺ) wished to perform Hajj. He said: "The polytheists will come and circumambulate the House naked." And he did not [........] [[a passage is obliterated in the original.]] perform Hajj so that this would not happen. The Messenger of God (ﷺ) sent Abu Bakr, may God be pleased with him, that year as commander over the pilgrimage season, to lead the people in Hajj, and he sent with him forty verses from the beginning of Bara'ah, to recite to the people of the season. When he had set out, the Prophet (ﷺ) called Ali and said: «Go out with these verses from the beginning of Bara'ah, and proclaim them to the people when they gather.»

Ali, may God be pleased with him, set out on the Messenger of God's (ﷺ) she-camel al-Ja'da', until he overtook Abu Bakr at Dhu al-Hulayfah and took it from him. Abu Bakr, may God be pleased with him, returned to the Prophet (ﷺ) and said: O Messenger of God, may my father and mother be your ransom, has something been revealed concerning me?

He said: «No, but no one may convey on my behalf except me or a man from my own family. Are you not content, O Abu Bakr, that you were with me in the cave, and that you are my companion at the Basin?» [[Zad al-Masir of Ibn al-Jawzi: 3/266.]]

He said: "Yes, O Messenger of God." This is because it was the custom of the Arabs, in making their covenants and breaking them, that a man from the tribe would take charge of that matter. So the Prophet (ﷺ) sent Ali, lest they say: "This contradicts what we know of some covenants."

Jabir said: I was with Ali, may God be pleased with him, until the Messenger of God (ﷺ) sent Abu Bakr after him. When we were [at al-Araj, the people dressed] for the dawn prayer, Abu Bakr stood up to lead the takbir, and he heard the cry of a camel. He stopped and said: "This is the cry of the Messenger of God's (ﷺ) she-camel al-Ja'da'. Something has surely happened to the Messenger of God regarding the Hajj." Then he saw Ali upon her, and Abu Bakr said: "Are you a commander or one commanded?"

He said: "No, the Messenger of God (ﷺ) sent me with Bara'ah to recite it to the people." So Abu Bakr was commander over the Hajj, and Ali was to proclaim Bara'ah. They both arrived at Mecca, and on the day before the Tarwiyah, Abu Bakr stood up, addressed the people, and told them about their rites, and he led the people in Hajj. The Arabs, at that time, in that year, were following their rites which they had practised in the Jahiliyyah during Hajj. Then, when the day of sacrifice came, Ali ibn Abi Talib, may God be pleased with him, stood up and proclaimed to the people the Hajj in accordance with what he had been commanded, and he recited to them the surah of Bara'ah. [[Sunan al-Darimi: 2/67; Sunan al-Tirmidhi: 4/339.]]

Al-Sha'bi said: Muhammad ibn Abi Hurayrah told me, from his father, who said: I was with Ali, may God be pleased with him, when the Prophet (ﷺ) sent him to proclaim. Whenever his voice weakened (dahala — shallow water upon the surface of the ground with no depth; in some sources: idmahalla), I called out for him. I asked: "With what were you proclaiming?" He said: "Four things: no naked person shall circumambulate the Ka'bah; whoever had a covenant with the Messenger of God, his covenant lasts until its term; no one shall enter Paradise except a believing soul; and no polytheist shall perform Hajj after this year of ours." They said: The polytheists said: "We disavow your covenant and the covenant of your cousin, except for stabbing and striking." They began saying: "O God, we have been prevented from being pious toward You." When it was the tenth year, the Prophet (ﷺ) performed the Farewell Hajj, and then returned to Medina. He remained for the rest of Dhu al-Hijjah, Muharram, Safar, and some nights of Rabi' al-Awwal, until he was taken up to God, mighty and majestic.

﴿And a proclamation from God﴾ is coordinated with His saying ﴿disavowal﴾. Its meaning is notification, and from it comes the adhan (call to prayer). It is said: adhantuhu fa-adhana, meaning I informed him so he knew. Its root is from al-udhn (the ear), that is, I made it reach his ear. Ata' al-Awfi said [...] [[unreadable speech.]]

[The adhan] ﴿And a proclamation from God﴾ up to His saying ﴿And if you fear poverty﴾, the verse. That is twenty-eight verses.

﴿and His Messenger to the people on the day of the greater Hajj﴾. Scholars differed about it. Abu Juhayfah, Ata', Tawus, and Mujahid said: it is the day of Arafah. This is also a narration of Amr from Ibn Abbas. The following hadith supports it:

Abu al-Sahba' al-Bakri reported: I asked Ali ibn Abi Talib about the day of the greater Hajj, and he said: The Messenger of God (ﷺ) sent Abu Bakr ibn Abi Quhafah to teach the people the Hajj, and sent me with him with forty verses of Bara'ah, until he came to Arafah. He addressed the people on the day of Arafah. When he finished his sermon, he turned to me and said: "Come, Ali, and deliver the message of the Messenger of God." So I stood and recited to them forty verses of Bara'ah. Then we departed until we reached Mina. I threw the pebbles at the Jamrah, sacrificed the camel, and shaved my head. I knew that the people of the gathering had not all been present at Abu Bakr's sermon on the day of Arafah, so I went around the tents to recite it to them. For this reason I think you reckoned it to be the day of sacrifice, but indeed it is the day of Arafah. [[Al-Bidayah wa al-Nihayah of Ibn Kathir: 5/47.]]

Shihab ibn Abbad al-Qasri reported from his father, who said: I heard Umar ibn al-Khattab, may God be pleased with him, say: "This is the day of Arafah, the day of the greater Hajj, so let no one fast on it." He said: I performed Hajj after my father, and I came to Medina and asked about its best people. They said: Sa'id ibn al-Musayyib. So I went to him and said: "Inform me about fasting on the day of Arafah." He said: "I will inform you about one who is a hundred times better than me: Umar and Ibn Umar. He used to forbid fasting on it and say: it is the day of the greater Hajj."

Ma'qil ibn Dawud said: I heard Ibn al-Zubayr say on the day of Arafah: "This is the day of the greater Hajj, so let no one fast on it." Ghalib ibn Ubaydullah said: I asked Ata' about the day of the greater Hajj, and he said: "It is the day of Arafah. Break your fast before dawn on it."

Qays ibn Makhramah said: The Messenger of God (ﷺ) gave a sermon on the evening of Arafah, and then said: "Amma ba'd" (he never gave a sermon without saying "Amma ba'd"), "Indeed, this is the day of the greater Hajj." [[Tafsir al-Tabari: 10/89.]]

Nafi' ibn Jubayr, Qays ibn Abbad, Abdullah ibn Sharad, al-Sha'bi, al-Nakha'i, al-Suddi, and Ibn Zayd said: It is the day of sacrifice (al-nahr). This is one of the two reports from Ali, may God be pleased with him.

Yahya ibn al-Jawwad said: Ali, may God be pleased with him, went out on the day of sacrifice on a white mule, heading to the cemetery. A man came up, took hold of the bridle of his mount, and asked him about the greater Hajj. He said: "It is this day of yours, so let go of its reins."

Ayyash al-Amiri said: Abdullah ibn Abi Awfa was asked about the day of the greater Hajj, and he said: "Glory be to God! It is the day of sacrifice, the day on which blood is shed, hair is shaved, and the forbidden becomes lawful."

Al-A'mash reported from Abdullah ibn Sinan, who said: Al-Mughirah ibn Shu'bah addressed us on his she-camel on the day of Eid al-Adha, and said: "This is the day of al-Adha, this is the day of sacrifice, and this is the day of the greater Hajj."

Shu'bah ibn Abi Bishr reported: Ali ibn Abdullah ibn Abbas and a man from the family of Shaybah disputed about the day of the greater Hajj. Ali said: "It is the day of sacrifice," and the man from the family of Shaybah said: "It is the day of Arafah." They sent to Sa'id ibn Jubayr and asked him, and he said: "It is the day of sacrifice. Do you not see that whoever misses the day of Arafah has not missed the Hajj, but whoever misses the day of sacrifice has missed the Hajj?" This is supported by what al-Zuhri reported from Abu Bakr ibn Abd al-Rahman, from Abu Hurayrah, who said: Abu Bakr sent me in that pilgrimage, with a group he dispatched on the day of sacrifice, to proclaim in Mina: "No polytheist shall perform Hajj after this year, and no naked person shall circumambulate the House." Then the Messenger of God (ﷺ) sent Ali behind them, commanding him to proclaim Bara'ah. Abu Hurayrah said: Ali, may God ennoble his face, proclaimed Bara'ah to the people of Mina on the day of sacrifice, together with us.

Salih reported from Ibn Shihab that Humayd ibn Abd al-Rahman informed him that Abu Bakr was sent on the pilgrimage that the Messenger of God (ﷺ) had appointed him over, before the Farewell Hajj, with a group to proclaim to the people: "No polytheist shall perform Hajj after this year, and no naked person shall circumambulate the House." Humayd used to say: "The day of sacrifice is the day of the greater Hajj," from the same report as the hadith of Abu Hurayrah.

Ibn Uyaynah reported from Ibn Jurayj from Mujahid, who said: "The day of the greater Hajj" is the time of Hajj, the days of Mina in their entirety, and the gatherings of the polytheists at Ukaz, Dhu al-Majaz, and Makhshah, and the day on which Ali proclaimed what he proclaimed.

Sufyan al-Thawri used to say: "The day of the greater Hajj" refers to all its days, like the day of Siffin, the day of the Camel, and the day of Bu'ath, and the whole period, because each of these battles lasted many days. [Bu'ath: a war between the Aws and the Khazraj.]

They also differed about the reason why this day was called "the day of the greater Hajj." Al-Hasan said: It is called the greater Hajj because the Hajj of the Muslims and the polytheists coincided on it. Abdullah ibn al-Harith ibn Nawfal said: The day of the greater Hajj was the year of the Farewell Hajj, when the Hajj of the Muslims, the festival of the Jews and Christians, and the polytheists came together, and this had not happened before it or after it.

Mansur and Hammad reported from Mujahid, who said: "The greater Hajj" is said to mean the Qur'an, and "the lesser Hajj" means the single Hajj (ifrad). Al-Zuhri, al-Sha'bi, and Ata' said: "The greater Hajj" is the Hajj, and "the lesser Hajj" is the 'Umrah. It was also said of it: [.........] [[unreadable speech in the original.]] its deed [.........] [[unreadable speech in the original.]] of the Hajj.

His mighty and majestic saying: ﴿That God﴾. Ibn Amir and Hamzah read ﴿Inna Allaha﴾... Isa read ﴿inna Allaha﴾ with a kasrah, on the basis of the beginning of a new sentence, because the proclamation is a statement: ﴿disavowed from the polytheists, and so is His Messenger﴾ is the reading of the common people with a damma, on the basis of the new sentence, and its predicate is omitted; the meaning is: "And His Messenger is also disavowed." Ibn Abi Ishaq, Isa, and Ya'qub read ﴿wa rasulahu﴾ with a fatha, coordinating it with the name of God. He did not say "two are disavowed" (bari'an), because the word refers to each one of them, like the saying of the poet:

Commentary of al-Tha'alibi (al-Jawahir al-Hisan) on surah 9, verse 1–5 (part 2 of 2):

Fa-man yak amsa bil-Madinati rahluhu ... fa-inni wa-Qayyar bihā la-gharib [Qayyar: it is said to be the name of a camel, and it is said to be the name of a horse. The verse is in Lisan al-Arab: 5/125.]

It is narrated from al-Hasan that he read wa-rasulihi with a kasra (genitive), as an oath. It has reached me that a Bedouin heard a man reading it in this reading, and said: "If it is a command from His Messenger, then I am also free of it." The man seized him by his garment and dragged him to Umar ibn al-Khattab, and the Bedouin related his story and his statement. At that point Umar ordered the teaching of Arabic (al-'Arabiyyah, the Arabic language).

﴿Then if you repent﴾, that is, return from your disbelief and devote yourselves to Tawhid, ﴿it is better for you; but if you turn away﴾, that is, turn away from faith [to persistence] in disbelief, ﴿then know that you cannot escape Allah﴾, ﴿and give tidings to those who disbelieve of a painful punishment.﴾ Then He said: ﴿except those with whom you made a covenant.﴾

This is an exception from His saying: ﴿[This is] a declaration of immunity from Allah and His Messenger to the people, except those with whom you made a covenant among the polytheists﴾, ﴿then they have not fallen short of you in anything﴾ of your covenant which you made with them, ﴿nor have they supported anyone against you﴾, that is, of your enemies, neither with themselves, nor with weapons, nor with horses, nor with men, nor with wealth.

Ata' ibn Yasar recited thumma lam yanquduukum with a dotted dad (from naqd al-'ahd, breaking the covenant), while the common reading is with a sad.

As for His saying: ﴿then complete for them their covenant until their term﴾, that is, fulfil their covenant to their appointed time, which you agreed with them. ﴿Indeed, Allah loves those who fear Him.﴾ They were the Banu Damrah and Kinanah, and nine months of their term remained, so He commanded that it be completed for them. ﴿Then when the sacred months have passed﴾, that is, have ended and their time has elapsed. It is said from this: "salakhtu ashhur kadha yuslakhuhu salkhan wa-sulukhan," meaning "we came out." The poet said:

"When I have stripped away the month, I begin the next like it;
Enough to kill me is my stripping away of months and my new moon."
[Lisan al-Arab: 3/25.]

From this also comes "shah maslukhah," a sheep stripped of its skin, and "hayyah salikh," when a snake has come out of its skin.

﴿The sacred months﴾ are four: three in succession, and one single. They are: Dhu al-Qa'dah, Dhu al-Hijjah and al-Muharram, which are three in a row, and Rajab, which stands alone.

Mujahid, Ibn Ishaq, Ibn Zayd and Umar ibn Shu'ayb said: they are the months of the covenant. They were called "al-Hurum" because Allah made unlawful for the believers the shedding of the blood of the polytheists and the molestation of them, except in the way of good.

﴿Then kill the polytheists wherever you find them﴾, in the sanctuary and outside it, ﴿wherever you find them, capture them﴾, ﴿and besiege them﴾, that is, prevent them from entering Makkah and from moving about in the lands of Islam, ﴿and sit in wait for them at every place of ambush﴾, that is, on every road and lookout. It is said: "rasadtu fulanan arsaduhu rasadan" when I watched him. 'Amir ibn al-Tufayl said:

"Indeed you knew, and I do not think you forgetful,
That death lies in wait for the youth at the ambush."
[See: Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 8/73.]

﴿But if they repent﴾ from polytheism, ﴿establish prayer and give zakah﴾, ﴿then let them go on their way.﴾ That is, leave them in their cities, and let them enter Makkah. ﴿Indeed, Allah is Forgiving and Merciful.﴾ [........] [Unreadable speech.] regarding the ruling of this verse.

Al-Husayn ibn al-Fadl said: this verse abrogated every verse in the Qur'an that mentions turning away and patience over the harm of enemies. Al-Dahhak, al-Suddi and Ata' said: His saying ﴿kill the polytheists﴾ is abrogated by His saying: ﴿then either grace afterward or ransom﴾ [Surah Muhammad: 4]. Qatadah said: rather, it abrogates His saying: ﴿then either grace afterward or ransom.﴾

The correct view is that the ruling of this verse stands, and that neither of the two is abrogated by the other, because grace, killing, and ransom have never ceased to be part of the ruling of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) toward them from the beginning of fighting them, which was the Day of Badr. His Exalted saying ﴿and seize them﴾ supports this, since seizing means capturing, and capture is only for killing or ransom. Evidence for this also is the report of Ata', who said: The Prophet (ﷺ) was brought a captive called Abu Umamah, who was the chief of Yamamah. The Prophet (ﷺ) said to him:
"O Abu Umamah, which do you prefer: that I free you, or that I ransom you, or that I kill you, or that you submit?" He said: "If you free me, you free a great man; if you ransom me, you ransom a great man; if you kill me, you kill a great man; but as for my submitting, no, by Allah, I will never submit."
He said: "Then I have freed you." He said: "I testify that there is no god but Allah, and I testify that you are His Messenger."

The grain supply of Makkah came from Yamamah. He said to the people of Makkah: "By Him besides whom there is no god, no grain or grain-seed will come to you from Yamamah ever, until you believe in Allah and His Messenger." They were harmed, and they wrote to the Prophet (ﷺ), since they had kinship ties with him, complaining of this to him. He wrote to Abu Umamah: "Do not cut off the grain supply to them that came from you," and Abu Umamah did so.

Commentary of al-Tha'alibi (al-Jawahir al-Hisan) on surah 9, verses 1–5 (part 1 of 2):

Madaniyyah (Medinan). It has 10,480 letters, 4,098 words, and 130 verses.

Hisham ibn Amir reported from al-Sha'bi, from Masruq, from A'ishah, who said: The Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: «The Qur'an was not sent down to me except verse by verse and letter by letter, with the exception of Surat Bara'ah (al-Tawbah), and Qul huwa Allahu ahad (Surat al-Ikhlas). Both were sent down to me accompanied by seventy thousand rows of angels, each saying: "O Muhammad, enjoin upon the one who bears the name of God goodness."» [[Tafsir Majma' al-Bayan: 5/6.]]

Yazid al-Raqqashi reported from Ibn Abbas, who said: I said to Uthman ibn Affan, may God be pleased with him: What led you to place al-Anfal, which is among the mathani (the oft-repeated surahs), and Bara'ah, which is among the mi'un (the surahs of about a hundred verses), side by side, without writing the line "In the name of God, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful" between them, and placed them among the al-sab' al-tiwal (the seven long surahs)?

Uthman, may God be pleased with him, said: The Messenger of God (ﷺ) would be visited by times when surahs of many verses were revealed to him. When something was revealed to him, he would call one of those who wrote for him and say: "Place this verse in the surah in which such-and-such is mentioned." And when a verse was revealed to him, he would say: "Place this verse in the surah in which such-and-such is mentioned." Al-Anfal was among the surahs revealed in Medina, and Bara'ah was among the last things revealed. Its story resembled the story of al-Anfal, so I thought it was part of it. The Messenger of God (ﷺ) passed away without making clear to us that it was part of it. For this reason I placed them together, did not write the line "In the name of God, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful" between them, and put them among the seven long surahs. [[Tafsir al-Tabari: 10/70.]]

I heard Abu al-Qasim al-Habibi say: I heard Abu Abdullah Muhammad ibn Nafi' al-Sijzi say in Herat:
I heard Abu Yazid Hatim ibn Mahbub al-Shami say: I heard Abd al-Jabbar ibn al-Ala' al-Attar say: Sufyan ibn Uyaynah was asked: Why is "In the name of God, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful" not at the beginning of Bara'ah? He said: Because the basmalah is mercy, and mercy is security, and this surah was sent down concerning the hypocrites and with the sword, and there is no security for the hypocrites.

Bara'ah (Immunity/Disavowal) is in the nominative case as the predicate of an omitted subject, meaning: "These are verses of disavowal." It was also said that it is the predicate of a definite description, the meaning being: "The disavowal, from God and His Messenger, is toward those among the polytheists with whom you made covenants."
