They helped their Prophet and strengthened his support
at Hunayn, on the day when the brave men were clashing.

The story of Hunayn, as the commentators have related it in many narrations which were compiled and arranged to be closer to understanding and better [....] [unreadable word in the original], is that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) conquered Makkah while some days of the month of Ramadan remained. Then he set out heading to Hunayn to fight Hawazin and Thaqif with twelve thousand: ten thousand from the Muhajirun and the Ansar, and two thousand from al-Ta'if.

Qatadah said, and Muqatil said: they were eleven thousand five hundred. Al-Kalbi said: they were ten thousand, and they were then more numerous than they had ever been [.......] [unreadable word in the original]. The polytheists were four thousand from Hawazin and Thaqif. Over Hawazin was Malik ibn 'Awf al-Nadri, and over Thaqif was Kinanah ibn 'Abd Yalil ibn 'Amr ibn 'Umayr al-Thaqafi. When the two hosts met, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "We will not be defeated today through lack of numbers." It is also said: rather, a man of the Muslims called Salamah ibn Salamah said that. [And heard] the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) his words, and they relied on the word of the man.

He said: ﴿Then fight them with fierce fighting.﴾ The polytheists fled and left behind their offspring. Then they called out: "O defenders of evil, remember the disgrace!" So they turned back, and the Muslims were routed.

Qatadah said: we were told that the freed captives [ran away] that day, leaving the people behind. A man asked al-Bara' ibn 'Azib: "Did you flee on the day of Hunayn?" He said: "Hawazin were archers. When we charged against them and they broke, we turned to the spoils, and they met us with arrows, so the Muslims were routed away from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ)." Al-Kalbi said: around the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) that day were three hundred of the Muslims, and the rest of the people fled from them.

Others said: none remained with the Prophet (ﷺ) that day except al-Abbas ibn 'Abd al-Muttalib, 'Ali, and Ayman ibn Umm Ayman. Some were killed before the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). The Messenger of Allah began urging his mule toward the disbelievers without holding back. It was a white mule which Farwah al-Judhami had given him as a gift.

Abdullah ibn Hamid informed us, saying: al-'Umari informed us: Ahmad ibn Muhammad related to us: al-Hammami related to us: Shurayk related to us, from Abu Ishaq: It was said to al-Bara': "Was the Prophet (ﷺ) among those who turned their backs on the day of Hunayn?" He said: "By Him besides whom there is no god, the Messenger of Allah never turned his back at all. We saw him, while Abu Sufyan ibn al-Harith was holding the stirrup and al-'Abbas was holding the bridle of the animal, and he was saying:

I am the Prophet, no lie,
I am the son of 'Abd al-Muttalib."

They said: the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said to al-'Abbas: "Call out, O company of the Muhajirun, and O company of the Ansar." Al-'Abbas was a man with a loud voice.

It is related, on account of the great loudness of al-'Abbas's voice, that one day he raided Makkah and called out: "Wa sabahah!" (Alas, morning attack!), and every pregnant woman who heard his voice miscarried her child.

Then he began calling: "O servants of Allah! O companions of the tree! O companions of Surat al-Baqarah!" When the Muslims heard his voice they turned back, like a cow turning to its calves, and they said: "Here we are! Here we are! Here we are!" and they came as one body. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) turned to a band of the Ansar and said: "Is there anyone with you other than yourselves?" They said: "O Prophet of Allah, if you were to go to the camels of Dhu Yaman, we would be with you." Then the polytheists advanced, and they met with the Muslims. The Ansar called out: "O company of the Ansar!" and said: "Has the call been restricted to the Banu al-Harith and the Khazraj?" So they called out together. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) looked, while he was on his mule, as one stretching up toward their fighting, and said: "Now the furnace has grown hot." He took a handful of [dust] [[In the sources: dust; in some: pebbles.]] and threw it at them, saying: "May the faces be ugly!" Then he said: "Retreat, by the Lord of the Ka'bah! Retreat, by the Lord of the Ka'bah!"

He said: By Allah, their affair kept turning back and their boldness weakened until Allah the Exalted routed them.

Ya'la ibn 'Ata' said: my informants among their sons related to me from their fathers that they said: "None of us remained that day without his eyes being filled with that dust." Yazid ibn 'Amir, who was among the polytheists that day, said: "We turned back, and not one of us remained, as if our eyes had been blinded. Then Allah fulfilled His promise, sent down His victory and His hosts, subdued the polytheists, and gave victory to the Muslims."

Sa'id ibn Jubayr said: Allah reinforced the [Muslims] with five thousand angels, ﴿marked﴾ (musawwimin). Al-Hasan said: they were eight thousand angels.

'Ata' said: they were sixteen thousand.

Sa'id ibn al-Musayyab said: a man who was among the polytheists on the day of Hunayn told me: "When we met, we and the companions of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), they did not stand for us for as long as it takes to milk a sheep. When we routed them, we began driving them, until when we reached the owner of the white mule, meaning the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), men with white faces and handsome faces met us and said to us: 'May the faces be ugly! Turn back!' So we turned back, and they rode upon our shoulders, and they were [the angels]," meaning the angels.

It is related that a man from the Banu Nadr called Shajarah said to the believers after the fighting: "Where are the spotted horses, and the men wearing white garments? We did not see you in them [.........] [unreadable statement in the manuscript], and our killing was only by their hands." They informed the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) of that, and he said: "Those were the angels."

Al-Zuhri said: and it reached me that Shaybah ibn 'Uthman said: "On the day of Hunayn I came up behind the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and I intended to kill him in revenge for Talhah ibn 'Uthman and 'Uthman ibn Talhah, who had been killed on the day of Uhud. Allah the Exalted made His Messenger aware of what was in my heart, so he turned to me, struck my chest, and said: 'I seek refuge for you in Allah, O Shaybah!' My joints trembled. I looked at him, and he was dearer to me than my hearing and my sight. I said: 'I testify that you are the Messenger of Allah, and that Allah made you aware of what was in my heart.'"

When Allah routed the polytheists and they turned their backs and fled until they came to [Awtas], where their families and wealth were, the Messenger of Allah sent there a man from the Ash'ariyyin called Abu 'Amir, and appointed him over the people. He went toward them, and they fought there. Then Allah the Exalted routed them, and they stood firm against the polytheists. Their commander Malik ibn 'Awf al-Nadri was routed; he came to al-Ta'if, fortified himself there, and his family and wealth were taken among those taken. The commander of the Muslims, Ibn 'Amir, was killed.

Then the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) went to al-Ta'if straight from that, and besieged them for the rest of that month. When Dhu al-Qa'dah began, which is a sacred month in which fighting is not lawful, he withdrew from them and came to al-Ji'ranah, and he entered into ihram there for 'umrah. Then the Prophet distributed the wealth and the spoils of Hunayn and Awtas, and he won over some people, such as Abu Sufyan ibn Harb, al-Harith ibn Hisham, Suhayl ibn 'Amr, and al-Aqra' ibn Habis, and he gave them. He began giving a man of them fifty or a hundred camels. The Ansar said: "The man has become tender toward his people and has preferred his tribe. How strange! Our swords are dripping with their blood, and yet our spoils are returned to them!" This reached the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), who was in a leather tent, so he gathered them and said to them: "O company of the Ansar, what is this that has reached me from you?"

They said: "It is what has reached you," and they did not lie. He said: "Were you not misguided, and Allah guided you through me? Were you not humbled, and Allah honoured you through me? Were you not such and such?"

Sa'id ibn 'Abdullah said: "May I speak?" He said: "Speak."

He said: "As for your saying, 'You were misguided, and Allah guided you through me,' we were indeed so. And as for your saying, 'You were humbled, and Allah honoured you,' the Arabs know that no tribe among the tribes of the Arabs was more protective of what lay behind its backs than we were." Then 'Umar said: "O Sa'id, do you know to whom you are speaking?" He said: "O 'Umar, I am speaking to the Messenger of Allah."

The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "By Him in whose hand is my soul, if the Ansar were to travel a valley, I would travel the valley of the Ansar. Were it not for the emigration, I would have been a man of the Ansar. The Ansar are my inner garment and my confidants. Accept their good-doers and overlook their wrong-doers." Then he said: "O company of the Ansar, are you not content that the people go back with camels and sheep, and you go back with the Messenger of Allah to your homes?" [5].

The Ansar said: "We are content with Allah and His Messenger. By Allah, we only said that out of concern for Allah and His Messenger." The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Allah and His Messenger confirm you and excuse you." [Its full version is in the Tafsir of al-Tabari: 10/130].

When the Prophet (ﷺ) came to Madinah, he stood and gave a sermon, saying: "Indeed, the orator of the Ansar said: 'You were a fugitive, and we sheltered you; you were fearful, and we gave you security; you were forsaken, and we helped you; you were such and such.' He has indeed spoken the truth." So the Ansar wept and said: "Rather, Allah and His Messenger are greater in our estimation than ourselves."

Qatadah said: we were told that the wet-nurse of the Prophet (ﷺ), who had nursed him from the Banu Sa'd, came to him on the day of Hunayn and asked him for captives of Hunayn. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "I do not own them; I only have my share of them. But come to me tomorrow and ask me while the people are with me, for when I give you my share, the people will give you theirs." She came the next day, and he spread his garment for her, and she sat on it. Then she asked him for that, and he gave her his share. When the people saw that from him, they gave her their shares. [Tafsir al-Tabari: 10/130].

Al-Zuhri said: Sa'id ibn al-Musayyab informed me that on that day they captured six thousand captives. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) had ordered a crier to call on the day of Awtas: "Beware, pregnant women are not to be approached until they give birth, and non-pregnant women are not to be approached until they have a single menstrual cycle to purify them."

Then [....] [unreadable word in the manuscript] of Hawazin came to him as Muslims after that and said: "O Messenger of Allah, you are the best and most generous of people. You have taken our sons, our women, and our wealth." The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "With me are those you see, and the best speech is the most truthful. Choose either your offspring and your women, or your wealth." They said: "We do not put anything on par with our lineage." So the Prophet stood up straight and said: "These people have come to me as Muslims [in al-Musannaf of 'Abd al-Razzaq: 5/381: submitting]. We gave them the choice between the offspring and the wealth, and they did not put anything on par with their lineage. As for what the Banu Hashim obtained, we return it to them. Whoever has something of it in his hand and is willing to return it to them, then that is well. And whoever does not, let him give it to us, and it will be a loan upon us until we obtain something and give him its equivalent. And whoever does not return it, his blood-money is fifty camels."

When the people saw that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) had returned them, they said: "O Prophet of Allah, we are content and submit." The Prophet said: "I do not know; perhaps some of you are not content. Let your leaders order that they raise it to him." So the leaders raised to us that they were content and submitted, and they all returned them except one man, Safwan ibn Umayyah, because he had lain with a woman whom he had captured, and she became pregnant by him. [Tafsir al-Tabari: 10/131].

Then Allah revealed: ﴿Certainly, Allah has given you victory on many battlefields and on the day of Hunayn, when your great number pleased you, but it did not avail you anything, and the earth was constricted for you despite its vastness, then you turned back in retreat.﴾ That is, despite its breadth and spaciousness; both are the infinitive. ﴿Then Allah sent down His tranquillity﴾, meaning security and calm, which is a form from "sakun" (stillness), ﴿upon His Messenger and upon the believers, and sent down hosts you did not see﴾, meaning the angels, ﴿and He punished those who disbelieved﴾ with killing, capture, and the seizure of wealth. ﴿That is the recompense of the disbelievers.﴾ ﴿Then Allah turns in forgiveness after that to whom He wills﴾, guiding him to Islam and not holding him accountable for what has passed. ﴿And Allah is Forgiving to His believing servants and Merciful to them.﴾

Then He said: ﴿Say, O Muhammad, to those who stayed behind from emigration and jihad: "If your fathers, your sons, your brothers, your spouses, and your kinsfolk, and the wealth you have acquired, and the commerce whose slackness you fear, and the dwellings you are pleased with are dearer to you than Allah and His Messenger and jihad in His cause, then wait until Allah brings His command."﴾ Abu Raja' and Ya'qub read ﴿wa-'asheeratukum﴾ (and your clans) with the alif, as a plural. There is a difference of reading on this from 'Asim.

﴿Wa-amwalun iqtaraftumuha﴾ (and wealth you have acquired): you earned it. Qatadah said: you earned it. ﴿Wa-tijaratun takhsharna kasadaha﴾ (and commerce whose slackness you fear): kasad is the opposite of nifaq (hypocrisy), and its root meaning is "to remain". The poet said:

They became slack from poverty among their people,
and my staying has only increased their slackness.

﴿Wa-masakinu tarduwnaha﴾ (and dwellings you are pleased with), meaning: that pleases you. Al-Suddi said: this means palaces and houses. ﴿Ahabba ilaykum min Allahi wa-rasulihi wa-jihadin fi sabilihi﴾ (dearer to you than Allah and His Messenger and jihad in His cause). ﴿Fa-tarabbasu﴾ (then wait): await. ﴿Hatta ya'tiya Allahu bi-amrihi﴾ (until Allah brings His command). 'Ata' said: by His decree. Mujahid and Muqatil said: this means the conquest of Makkah. ﴿Wa-Allahu la yahdi al-qawma al-fasiqin﴾ (and Allah does not guide the defiant people): He does not guide, nor grant success to, those who go out of His obedience into disobedience.

﴿Laqad nasarakumu Allahu﴾ (Allah has certainly given you victory), O believers, ﴿fi mawatina kathirah﴾ (in many battlefields): that is, places of fighting where you have witnessed it, places of war where you settled yourselves ready to meet your enemy. ﴿Wa-yawma Hunayn﴾ (and on the day of Hunayn): meaning, and on the day of Hunayn, which is a valley between Makkah and al-Ta'if.

'Urwah ibn al-Zubayr said: it is a valley beside Dhu al-Majaz and al-Hari. Since it is the name of a masculine noun, its final part may be dropped, and by it is meant the name of the town in which it lies. From this is the poet's saying:

They helped their Prophet and strengthened his support
at Hunayn, on the day when the brave men were clashing.

I am the son of 'Abd al-Muttalib."

Were it not for the emigration, I would have been a man of the Ansar. The Ansar are my inner garment and my confidants. Accept their good-doers and overlook their wrong-doers." Then he said: "O company of the Ansar, are you not content that the people go back with camels and sheep, and you go back with the Messenger of Allah to your homes?" [5].

The Ansar said: "We are content with Allah and His Messenger. By Allah, we only said that out of concern for Allah and His Messenger." The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Allah and His Messenger confirm you and excuse you." [Its full version is in the Tafsir of al-Tabari: 10/130].

When the Prophet (ﷺ) came to Madinah, he stood and gave a sermon, saying: "Indeed, the orator of the Ansar said: 'You were a fugitive, and we sheltered you; you were fearful, and we gave you security; you were forsaken, and we helped you; you were such and such.' He has indeed spoken the truth." So the Ansar wept and said: "Rather, Allah and His Messenger are greater in our estimation than ourselves."

Qatadah said: we were told that the wet-nurse of the Prophet (ﷺ), who had nursed him from the Banu Sa'd, came to him on the day of Hunayn and asked him for captives of Hunayn. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "I do not own them; I only have my share of them. But come to me tomorrow and ask me while the people are with me, for when I give you my share, the people will give you theirs." She came the next day, and he spread his garment for her, and she sat on it. Then she asked him for that, and he gave her his share. When the people saw that from him, they gave her their shares. [Tafsir al-Tabari: 10/130].

Al-Zuhri said: Sa'id ibn al-Musayyab informed me that on that day they captured six thousand captives. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) had ordered a crier to call on the day of Awtas: "Beware, pregnant women are not to be approached until they give birth, and non-pregnant women are not to be approached until they have a single menstrual cycle to purify them."

Then [....] [unreadable word in the manuscript] of Hawazin came to him as Muslims after that and said: "O Messenger of Allah, you are the best and most generous of people. You have taken our sons, our women, and our wealth." The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "With me are those you see, and the best speech is the most truthful. Choose either your offspring and your women, or your wealth." They said: "We do not put anything on par with our lineage." So the Prophet stood up straight and said: "These people have come to me as Muslims [in al-Musannaf of 'Abd al-Razzaq: 5/381: submitting]. We gave them the choice between the offspring and the wealth, and they did not put anything on par with their lineage. As for what the Banu Hashim obtained, we return it to them. Whoever has something of it in his hand and is willing to return it to them, then that is well. And whoever does not, let him give it to us, and it will be a loan upon us until we obtain something and give him its equivalent. And whoever does not return it, his blood-money is fifty camels."

When the people saw that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) had returned them, they said: "O Prophet of Allah, we are content and submit." The Prophet said: "I do not know; perhaps some of you are not content. Let your leaders order that they raise it to him." So the leaders raised to us that they were content and submitted, and they all returned them except one man, Safwan ibn Umayyah, because he had lain with a woman whom he had captured, and she became pregnant by him. [Tafsir al-Tabari: 10/131].

Then Allah revealed: ﴿Certainly, Allah has given you victory on many battlefields and on the day of Hunayn, when your great number pleased you, but it did not avail you anything, and the earth was constricted for you despite its vastness, then you turned back in retreat.﴾ That is, despite its breadth and spaciousness; both are the infinitive. ﴿Then Allah sent down His tranquillity﴾, meaning security and calm, which is a form from "sakun" (stillness), ﴿upon His Messenger and upon the believers, and sent down hosts you did not see﴾, meaning the angels, ﴿and He punished those who disbelieved﴾ with killing, capture, and the seizure of wealth. ﴿That is the recompense of the disbelievers.﴾ ﴿Then Allah turns in forgiveness after that to whom He wills﴾, guiding him to Islam and not holding him accountable for what has passed. ﴿And Allah is Forgiving to His believing servants and Merciful to them.﴾

**Commentary of al-Tha'alibi (al-Jawahir al-Hisan) on Surah 9, verses 28–33 (part 1 of 2)**

﴿O you who believe, the polytheists are only impure (najas)﴾. Al-Dahhak and Abu 'Ubayda said: filth (qadhar). Ibn al-Anbari said: foul (khabith). One says: a man is najas, a woman is najas, two men or two women are najas, men and women are najas, with the nun and the jim vowelled with fatha, or najas with the jim vowelled with damma, and rijs (filth) in these states. It is not made dual or plural, because it is a verbal noun (masdar). As for najas with the nun vowelled with kasra and the jim sukun, it is not said except when rijs is mentioned with it. When it stands alone, one says najas with the nun fatha and the jim kasra, or najas with the jim damma.

Ibn al-Sumayqa' recited: ﴿Indeed the polytheists are impurities (anjas)﴾, like your saying akhbath in the plural. They differed over the meaning of najas and the reason for which Allah named them thus. It is narrated from Ibn 'Abbas: "The polytheists are only the filth of a pig or a dog." This view is not accepted, for two reasons. First, it is narrated from him by a route that is not reliable (ghayr hamid), so it is not authentically attributed to him. Second, this is impurity of ruling (najasat al-hukm), not impurity of substance (najasat al-'ayn), because if their persons were impure like the dog or the pig, Islam would not purify them, and the prohibition of polytheists entering the Sacred Mosque and other mosques would not be the same. Those who hold that their persons are impure cite what is narrated: that 'Umar ibn 'Abd al-'Aziz wrote, "Prevent the Jews and Christians from entering the mosques of the Muslims," and he followed his prohibition with the words of Allah, ﴿The polytheists are only impure﴾.

It is also narrated from al-Hasan that he said: "Do not shake hands with the polytheists. Whoever shakes hands with them should perform ablution." Qatada said: "He called them impure because they become junub (in a state of major impurity) and do not perform ghusl, and they break their minor ablution and do not perform wudu', so they were prevented from entering the mosque, since one in a state of janaba should not enter the mosque."

Al-Husayn ibn al-Fadl said: "This is impurity of ruling, not impurity of substance, so they were called impure as a form of blame." Evidence for this is what is narrated: the Prophet (ﷺ) met Hudhayfa and took his hand. Hudhayfa said, "O Messenger of Allah, I am junub." He said, "Indeed the believer is not impure (la yanjus)."

﴿So let them not approach the Sacred Mosque﴾. The people of meaning (ahl al-ma'ani) said: by this he intended their prevention from entering the Haram, because if they enter the Haram, they have come near the Sacred Mosque. 'Ata' said: "The whole Haram is qibla and mosque," and he recited this verse. [Tafsir al-Tabari 10/136; Tafsir al-Qurtubi 8/105.]

Jabir, from 'Abd Allah, from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ): "No one enters the Haram except the people of the jizya or a slave of a Muslim man, and their women are lawful to you." And he recited: ﴿after this year of theirs﴾, meaning the year in which Abu Bakr (may Allah be pleased with him) led the people in Hajj, and 'Ali (may Allah ennoble his face) proclaimed the Bara'a (immunity declaration), which was in the ninth year after the Hijra.

﴿And if you fear poverty…﴾ The exegetes said: The polytheists used to bring food to the House, and they traded and bought and sold. When they were prevented from entering the Haram, this was difficult for the Muslims, and Satan cast fear into their hearts, saying to them, "From where will you eat and make a living, when the polytheists have gone and the caravans have been cut off from you?"

The believers said: "O Messenger of Allah, we used to profit from their trade and commerce, and now the markets will be cut off from us, and the commerce will cease, and the benefits we used to gain from it will be lost." So Allah, Mighty and Majestic, revealed: ﴿And if you fear poverty﴾.

'Amr ibn Fa'id said: its meaning is "and if you fear," because the people had been afraid. That is the saying of the speaker: "If you are my father, then honour me," meaning "if I fear poverty and want." One says: 'alla ya'ilu 'aylatan and 'uyulan (to be poor, to become needy). The poet said:
"The poor man does not know when his wealth will come,
and the rich man does not know when he will become poor."
[Lisan al-'Arab 11/488, attributed to Uhayha.]

In the codex of 'Abd Allah (ibn Mas'ud): "wa in khiftum 'ayilatan," meaning "a fear that burdens you," i.e., it weighs upon you, and it is difficult for you.

﴿Allah will enrich you from His bounty﴾. This is because He sent down abundant rain upon them, and their goodness increased when the polytheists departed.

Muqatil said: The people of Jeddah, Sana'a and Jurash in Yemen embraced Islam, and they carried food to Makkah on the backs of camels and beasts, and Allah, Mighty and Majestic, sufficed them against what they had feared.

Al-Kalbi said: "[...] (the text is illegible in the manuscript) [...] and Allah sufficed them in what concerned them." Al-Dahhak and Qatada said: Allah apportioned to them what is better for them, which is the jizya, and Allah enriched them. This is His saying: ﴿Fight those who do not believe in Allah﴾.

Mujahid said: This verse was revealed when the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was commanded to fight the Romans, and after its revelation he went out on the expedition of Tabuk.

Al-Kalbi said: It was revealed concerning Qurayza and al-Nadir from the Jews, and the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) wished [to take the jizya, so Allah revealed] — [the manuscript is illegible, and what we have set down is the apparent reading] — Mighty and Majestic: ﴿Fight those who do not believe in Allah, nor in the Last Day, nor forbid what Allah and His Messenger have forbidden, nor adopt the religion of truth﴾. He meant "the religion of truth" but attributed the noun to the adjective.

Qatada said: "The Truth (al-Haqq) is Allah, Mighty and Majestic, and His religion is Islam." Abu 'Ubayda said its meaning is "the obedience of the people of Islam," and everyone who obeys a king or a ruler has given him din (obedience, submission). Zuhayr said:
"If you should alight in the midst of the Banu Asad,
under the religion of 'Amr, and Fadak should come between us…"
[Tafsir al-Tabari 10/141; Lisan al-'Arab 10/473.]
meaning: under the obedience of 'Amr.

﴿From those who were given the Scripture﴾, meaning the Jews and Christians, from whom the jizya is taken, and that they not be fought. The jizya is also taken from the Sabians and the Samaritans, because their standing regarding the People of the Book is the standing of the people of innovations (ahl al-bid'a) regarding them. The jizya is also taken from the Magians (majus). It has been said that they were of the People of the Book, but their scripture was lifted.

Abu Muhammad 'Abd Allah ibn Hamid al-Wazzan informed us: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn al-Husayn informed us: Muhammad ibn Yahya and [...] (illegible in the manuscript) said: 'Uthman ibn Salih informed us: Ibn Wahb informed us: Yunus informed us, from Ibn Shihab, from Sa'id ibn al-Musayyab, that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) took the jizya from the Magians of Hajar, and that 'Umar took it from the Magians of al-Sawad, and that 'Uthman ibn 'Affan took it from the Berbers. [Ahkam al-Qur'an by al-Jassas 2/412; al-Musannaf by 'Abd al-Razzaq 6/69, no. 10027.]

Ibn Hamid informed us: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn al-Husayn informed us: Muhammad ibn Yahya and Ahmad ibn Yusuf said: Abu 'Asim informed us, from Ja'far ibn Muhammad, from his father, who said: 'Umar ibn al-Khattab (may Allah be pleased with him) said, "I do not know how to deal with the Magians." 'Abd al-Rahman ibn 'Awf said, "I heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) say: 'Treat them as you treat the People of the Book.'" [al-Musnad by al-Shafi'i: 209.]

Abu 'Asim said: "I walked a mile and ran a mile until I heard from Ja'far ibn Muhammad, 'Haddathana' (he narrated to us), meaning this hadith."

And we are prevented from marrying their women, eating their slaughtered animals, [and having intercourse with] the private parts (furuj) and the foods, which are under suspicion (al-khatar), and it is not permissible to proceed in them with doubt.

Al-Hasan said: "The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) fought the people of this peninsula for Islam; he would accept nothing else from them. This was the best of jihad. After him there was another jihad concerning this matter of sustenance (al-si'a) regarding the People of the Book." [al-Durr al-Manthur 3/229.]

﴿Fight those who do not believe in Allah nor in the Last Day﴾, [meaning] that they not follow anything other than these two (the Scripture and the Messenger) — innovation and misguidance. The jizya is not taken from idols. ﴿Until they give the jizya﴾, which is what the mu'ahad (covenanted non-Muslim) gives for his covenant. It is a verbal form (fi'la) from jaza, yajzi, when one pays what is due (qada 'alayhi). Jizya is like al-qi'da and al-jalsa (verbal nouns of the form fi'la). The meaning of the words is: "until they give the kharaj (tribute) from their necks, which they expend to the Muslims as a means of defence from them."

As for its amount: Anas said: "The Prophet distributed a dinar upon every adult male (muhtalim)." 'Umar ibn al-Khattab (may Allah be pleased with him) imposed upon the poor among the dhimmis one dirham each, upon the middle-income ones twenty-four, and upon the wealthy forty-eight dirhams, and he did not exceed fifty dirhams. There is no fixed amount, but it is according to what they agreed upon in the settlement (sulh).

﴿'An yad﴾: meaning by transferring it from their hand into the hand of the one to whom it is given, as one says, "I spoke to him, but not with the mouth" (kallamtuhu fama lafam). [Tafsir al-Tabari 10/141.]

Abu 'Ubayda said: "It is said: he gave [...] (unclear in the manuscript) from no good disposition of his, he gave it 'an yad." Al-Qutaybi said: "It is said: he gave it 'an yad and 'an zahr yad when he gave it spontaneously, not under compulsion."

Ibn 'Abbas said: "It means that they give it with their hands, walking with it unwillingly, and they do not bring it riding, nor do they send it." ﴿And they are sagharun (humbled)﴾, meaning abased and subdued. Ibn 'Abbas said: "They are shaken violently when they pay it." 'Ikrima said: "The meaning of al-sagharr is that you take it while you are seated and he is standing." Al-Kalbi said: "When he comes to pay, he is slapped on the back of his neck." It was said: his giving it is the sagharr. It was said: he is not accepted to convey it through a messenger or an agent. It was said: the rulings of Islam are applied to them, and that is the sagharr.

'Abd Allah ibn Hamid informed us: Muhammad ibn Ja'far informed us: 'Ali ibn Harb informed us: al-Sabbat informed us: 'Abd al-'Aziz ibn [...] (illegible word in the manuscript) informed us, from Habib ibn Abi Thabit, who said: A man came to Ibn 'Abbas and said, "The land is of the kharaj land, whose people are unable to cultivate it. Shall I cultivate it, sow it, and pay its kharaj?" He said, "No." Another came and asked him the same, and he said, "No," and he recited His saying: ﴿Fight those who do not believe in Allah…﴾ up to ﴿and they are sagharun﴾. Does one of you deliberately place the sagharr upon the neck of one of them, then remove it and place it upon his own neck? [Tafsir al-Qurtubi 8/116, and he also narrated the following reports.]

Kulayb ibn Wa'il said: I said to Ibn 'Umar, "I bought land." He said, "Buying is good." I said, "But I pay from every jarib of land a dirham and a qafiz of food?" He said, "Then do not put sagharan (humiliation) upon your neck."

Maymun ibn Mihran narrated from Ibn 'Umar, who said: "It does not please me that the whole land be mine for a jizya of five dirhams, in which I accept the sagharr upon myself."

﴿And the Jews said, "'Uzayr is the son of Allah"﴾. Sa'id ibn Jubayr and 'Ikrima narrated from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: Salam ibn Mishkam, al-Nu'man ibn Awfa, Shas ibn Qays and Malik ibn al-Sayf came to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and said: "How shall we follow you, when you have abandoned our qibla, and you do not claim that 'Uzayr is the son of Allah?" So Allah revealed concerning their saying: ﴿And the Jews said, "'Uzayr is the son of Allah"﴾.

Ibn Muhaysin, 'Asim and al-Kisa'i recited ʿUzayrun with tanwin (nunation), and this is the view of Abu 'Ubayd and Abu Hatim. The rest recited it without tanwin. Whoever reads with tanwin says: because it is a light name (ism khafif), its proper form is to be declined, even if it is foreign, like Nuh, Lut and Hud. Abu Hatim and al-Mubarrad said: the preferred reading is tanwin, because it is not a patronymic (mansub), and the statement is incomplete and is in the place of the predicate (khabar), not in the accusative. Tanwin is permitted in the attributive (na't) when the name can dispense with "son of" (ibn), or is attributed to a known name, or to a title that has come to predominate over it, like Muhammad ibn 'Abd Allah and Yazid ibn 'Abd Allah, because the qualifier and the qualified are like one thing. So it is nunated in the predicate and omitted in the attribute. Sometimes they retain tanwin in the attribute. A poet, whom al-Farra' recited, said:
"If there is no wealth there, then indeed
my praise will come to Zayd ibn Mahlahil."
Al-Kisa'i recited [...] (illegible in the manuscript), his school of thought.

Abu 'Ubayda said: This is not attributed to his father; it is rather like your saying "Zayd ibn al-Amir" and "Zayd ibn 'Abd Allah," so 'Uzayr is followed by a predicate.

Whoever omits tanwin says: because it is a foreign name and resembles a diminutive (musaggar) name.

Al-Farra' said: Since the nun of 'Uzayr is quiescent [and it is the nun of tanwin] and the ba' of ibn is quiescent, and two quiescent letters met, the first of them was dropped because vocalising it was burdensome, as the poet said: "You will find me with the commander a dutiful one, and with the spear a stubborn attacker, when Ghutayf al-Sulami flees." [Tafsir al-Tabari 10/144; Lisan al-'Arab 3/438.] So the quiescent nun that came after it was dropped.

Al-Zajjaj said: It is permissible that the predicate be omitted, its estimated form being: "'Uzayr is the son of Allah, our worshipped one."

'Ubayd ibn 'Umayr said: This statement was made by only one man among the Jews, named Finhas ibn 'Azura, who is the one who said: ﴿Indeed Allah is poor and we are rich﴾ [Tafsir al-Tabari 4/259].

'Ata' al-'Awfi narrated from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: "The Jews said, 'Uzayr is the son of Allah,' and they said this only because 'Uzayr was among the People of the Book, and the Torah was with them, as much as Allah willed for them to know. Then they neglected it and acted contrary to the truth. The Ark (al-tabut) was among them. When Allah, Mighty and Majestic, saw that they had neglected the Torah, acted according to their desires, lost the Ark, and that He had made them forget the Torah and removed it from their breasts, He sent upon them a disease, so that their bellies swelled until a man would touch his liver. Thus they forgot the Torah and it was removed from their breasts. 'Uzayr was among them. They remained as long as Allah willed them to remain after the Torah had been removed from their breasts. 'Uzayr had been one of their scholars. He supplicated Allah [...] and implored Him to return to him what had been removed from their breasts. While he was praying, humbly before Allah, Mighty and Majestic, a light descended from the heaven and entered his inside, and what had gone from within him of the Torah returned to him. He called out to his people and said: 'O people, Allah has given me the Torah and returned it to me.' Then he began to teach them. They remained as long as Allah willed them to remain, while he taught them. Then the Ark was left behind, after his death from among them. When they saw the Ark, they compared what was in it with what 'Uzayr had been teaching them, and they found it identical. They said, 'By Allah, 'Uzayr has not come except that he is the son of Allah.'" [In full in Tafsir al-Tabari 10/143.]

Al-Suddi and Ibn 'Abbas, in the narration of 'Ammar ibn 'Ammar, said: The Jews said, "'Uzayr is the son of Allah" because the 'Amalekites overcame them, killed them, took the Torah, and their surviving scholars fled and buried the books of the Torah in the mountains and elsewhere. 'Uzayr went off to the mountains and the wild animals, worshipping in the mountains, not mixing with the people nor coming down except on the day of a festival. He would weep and say, "O Lord, You have left the Children of Israel without a scholar," and he wept until the eyelids of his eyes fell off. Once he came down for the festival, and when he returned he found a woman sitting beside one of those graves, weeping and saying, "O my food-giver! O my clothing-giver!"

'Uzayr said to her, "O woman, fear Allah and be patient, and seek reward. Do you not know that death is the way of people?" He said, "Woe to you! Who used to feed you and clothe you before this man?" — meaning her husband whom she was mourning. She said, "Allah." He said, "Then indeed Allah is living and does not die." She said, "O 'Uzayr, then who used to teach the scholars before the Children of Israel?" He said, "Allah." She said, "Then why do you weep over them, when you know that death is true and that Allah is living and does not die?" When 'Uzayr realised that he had been refuted, he turned away, fleeing.

She said to him: "O 'Uzayr, I am not a woman, but I am the World (al-dunya). Indeed, water will gush forth from your prayer place as a spring, and a tree will grow. Eat from the fruit of that tree, drink from the water of that spring, perform ghusl, and pray two rak'as. Then a shaykh will come to you; take from him whatever he gives you."

When morning came, a spring gushed forth from his prayer place and a tree grew, and he did what she had told him. Then a shaykh came and said to him, "Open your mouth." He opened it, and the shaykh put into it something like a great ember, gathered like glass, three times. Then he said to him, "Enter this spring, and walk in it until you reach your people." He entered it, and every time he lifted his foot his knowledge was increased, until he reached his people. He returned to them, and he was the most knowledgeable of people in the Torah. He said, "O Children of Israel, I have brought you the Torah."

They said, "O 'Uzayr, you were not lying." He tied a quill to each of his fingers and wrote with all his fingers until he had written the Torah from memory. Thus he revived the Torah for them and revived the Sunna for them. When the scholars returned, they brought out the books they had buried, and they found them identical to the Torah of 'Uzayr. They said, "Allah gave him this only because he is His son." [The previous source, with variation.]

Al-Kalbi said: When Bukhtnassar (Nebuchadnezzar) prevailed over the Children of Israel, demolished Bayt al-Maqdis, and killed those who read the Torah, 'Uzayr was then a young boy, and they considered him weak, so they did not accept him, and they did not know that he had read the Torah. When he died after one hundred years and the Children of Israel returned to Bayt al-Maqdis, and there was none among them who could read the Torah, Allah, Mighty and Majestic, sent 'Uzayr to renew the Torah for them and to be a sign for them. 'Uzayr came to them and said, "I am 'Uzayr." They denied him and said, "If you are as you claim, 'Uzayr, then recite the Torah to us." So he wrote it out and said, "This is the Torah."

Then a man said: My father related to me from my grandfather that the Torah was placed [for a prophet] and then buried in a mound. So they set out with him until they dug it up and extracted the Torah, and they compared it with what Ezra had written for them, but they did not find it had lost a single letter or verse. So they were amazed and said: "He is the son of God; the Torah was not placed in the heart of a single man after it had gone from our hearts except that he was his son." At that point the Jews said: "Ezra is the son of God."

As for the Christians, it is said that they were upon one religion for a year after Jesus was raised up: they prayed toward the qibla and fasted Ramadan. Then war broke out between them and the Jews. Among the Jews there was a brave man called Yunus, who killed a group of the companions of Jesus, peace be upon him. Then he said to the Jews: "If the truth is with Jesus, then we have disbelieved and denied, and the Fire is our destination. So we are cheated if they enter Paradise and we enter the Fire. I will devise a plan and lead them astray until they enter the Fire." He had a horse called al-'Uqab that he fought upon, but his horse was drowned. He showed remorse and put dust on his head.

The Christians said to him: "Who are you?" Yunus said: "Your enemy." [I heard] [an addition required by the context.] from the sky: "There is no repentance for you except that you become a Christian, and you have repented." So they brought him into the church, and he entered a room for a year, not coming out by night or day, until he learned the Gospel. Then he came out and said to [them] [a word unclear in the manuscript, and what we have recorded seems right]: "God has accepted your repentance." So they believed him and loved him. Then he went to Jerusalem and appointed Nestor as his successor over them, and taught him that Jesus, Mary and God were three. Then he turned to the Romans and taught them the doctrine of divinity and humanity, and said: "Jesus was not a human who became divine, nor a body that became embodied, but he is the son of God." And he taught this to a man called Ya'qub.

Then he called a man called Malik and said to him: "God has not ceased and will not cease [to be with] Jesus, may Allah be pleased with him." When he had gained power over them, he called these three one by one and said to each of them: "You are my successor, and I have seen Jesus in a dream, and he was pleased with me." And he said to each of them: "Tomorrow I will sacrifice myself, so call the people to the place of sacrifice." Then he entered the place of sacrifice and sacrificed himself, saying: "I am only doing this to seek the pleasure of Jesus." When the third day came, each of them called the people to [his sect], and each followed a group of people, and they fought and disagreed until this day of ours. So all the Christians are of the three sects.

﴿That is their saying with their mouths.﴾ That is, the saying of the Christians that the Messiah is the son of God: they say it with their tongues without knowledge.

The scholars of meanings said: Allah, Mighty and Majestic, does not mention a statement joined with the mention of mouths and tongues except that the statement is falsehood, as in His saying: ﴿They say with their mouths what is not in their hearts﴾, and ﴿They say with their tongues what is not in their hearts﴾, and His saying: ﴿Grave is the word that comes out of their mouths; they say nothing but lies﴾ ... ﴿Imitating﴾. Ibn 'Abbas said: resembling. And from him also: imitating. Mujahid said: conforming. Dhu Nun said: there are two readings, yudahi'una with a hamza, which is the reading of 'Asim, and yudahuna without a hamza, which is the reading of the common readers. It is said: "dahaytuhu" and "dahata'tuhu," with the same meaning. ﴿The saying of those who disbelieved before﴾. Qatadah and al-Suddi said: the Christians imitated the saying of the Jews before them, so the Christians said: the Messiah is the son of God, just as the Jews said: ﴿Ezra is the son of God﴾. Mujahid said: they imitated the saying of the polytheists when they said: al-Lat, al-'Uzza and Manat are the daughters of God. Al-Hasan said: their disbelief was likened to the disbelief of those nations of disbelievers who passed away, and he addressed the polytheists of the Arabs when he related of them: ﴿And those who do not know say: Why does Allah not speak to us, or a sign come to us?﴾, then he said: ﴿Thus said those before them, the like of their saying. Their hearts are alike.﴾ Al-Qutaybi said: he means that those among the Jews and Christians in the time of the Prophet ﷺ said what their predecessors had said.

﴿May Allah destroy them.﴾ Ibn 'Abbas said: may Allah curse them; every "qatala" in the Qur'an means a curse. Similarly Aban ibn Taghlib said:
"May Allah destroy her, she blames me, though she knows
that I am the one who corrupts myself and reforms myself."
[Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 8/119.]
Ibn Juraij said: ﴿May Allah destroy them﴾ is in the sense of wonder. ﴿How are they turned away?﴾ That is, they lie and are turned away from the truth after the proof has been established for it.

﴿They took their rabbis and their monks as lords.﴾ al-Dahhak said: their scholars; and he recited: "monks." The rabbis (aḥbār) are the scholars; the singular is ḥabr and ḥibr, with the ḥā' vowelled with kasra and with fatha, and the kasra is better. Yunus al-Jurmi used to claim that he had only heard it with kasra, and he argued from people's saying: "this is muḥabbar," meaning the ink of a scholar. The monks (ruhban) among the Christians are the people of the hermitages and those who abstain in their religion. It is said: rāhib and ruhbān, like fāris and fursān. Its root is from ruhbah, which is fear, as if they fear God. ﴿As lords besides Allah﴾, obeying them in disobedience to God.

Mus'ab ibn Sa'd related from 'Adi ibn Hatim who said: I came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ with a golden cross around my neck. He said: "O 'Adi, throw this idol from your neck." He said: So I threw it. Then he stood and recited Surat Bara'a, and recited this verse: ﴿They took their rabbis and their monks as lords besides Allah﴾ until he finished it. I said to him: "We do not worship them." He said: "Do they not forbid what Allah has made lawful, so that you forbid it, and make lawful what Allah has forbidden, so that you make it lawful?" He said: I said: "Yes." [Al-Mu'jam al-Kabir of al-Tabarani: 17/92.]

Abu al-Ahwas said, on the authority of 'Ata' ibn Abi al-Bakhtari, concerning the saying of Allah, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿They took their rabbis and their monks as lords﴾: As for [if they had commanded] them to worship them besides Allah, they would not have obeyed them; but they commanded them, and they made what Allah had made lawful unlawful, and what He had made unlawful lawful, and they obeyed them, and that was their lordship. [Al-Ahkam by Ibn Hazm: 6/883.]

Al-Rabi' said: I said to Abu al-'Aliyah: How was that lordship among the Children of Israel? He said: They found in the Book of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, what they were commanded and forbidden, and they said: "We will not go ahead of our rabbis in anything. Whatever they command us, we comply; whatever they forbid us, we refrain," the men... and they cast the Book of Allah behind their backs.

The scholars of meanings said: its meaning is that they took their rabbis and monks as tails, since they obeyed them in everything, like His saying: "Blow" until when He made it fire, i.e., like fire. 'Abd Allah ibn al-Mubarak said:
"Did anything change the religion except kings
and evil rabbis and their monks?" [Al-Jihad of Ibn al-Mubarak: 28.]

﴿And they were commanded only to worship one God; there is no god but Him; glorified is He above what they associate.﴾ The reading is with the yā'; Ibn Abi Ishaq read it with the tā'.

﴿They want to extinguish the light of Allah with their mouths﴾, that is, to nullify the religion of Allah with their tongues, by their denial of it and their turning away from it.

al-Kalbi said: that is, they reject the Qur'an with their tongues, denying it. Ibn 'Abbas said: the Jews and Christians want to impose the unity of the Most Merciful on created beings to whom lordship is not fitting. al-Dahhak said: they want Muhammad and his companions to be destroyed, and that Allah not be worshipped through Islam.

﴿But Allah refuses except to perfect His light﴾, that is, He will exalt His religion, make manifest His word, and complete the truth with which He sent His Messenger. ﴿Though the disbelievers dislike it.﴾ The particle "illa" was introduced because "abā" has a sense of negation within it; do you not see that your saying "yathbutu an af'ala" establishes the act? And because of the ellipsis in it, its estimate is: ﴿And Allah refuses everything except to perfect His light﴾, as he said:
"And have I any mother other than her, if I left her?
Allah refuses except that I be a son to her."

﴿He it is who sent His Messenger﴾, meaning Muhammad ﷺ, ﴿with guidance﴾. Ibn 'Abbas said: with the Qur'an. It was said: the clarification of its obligations to His creatures. ﴿And the religion of truth﴾, which is Islam.

﴿But Allah refuses except to perfect His light﴾, that is, He will exalt His religion, make manifest His word, and complete the truth with which He sent His Messenger. ﴿Though the disbelievers dislike it.﴾ ... ﴿That He may make it prevail﴾, that is, exalt it, support it and grant it victory ﴿over all religion﴾, over all the other communities entirely. ﴿Though the polytheists dislike it.﴾

The scholars differed about the meaning of this verse. Ibn 'Abbas said: the pronoun refers to the Messenger ﷺ, meaning that He teaches him all the laws of the religion and makes him prevail over them, so that nothing of them remains hidden from him. The others said: the pronoun refers to the religion of truth.

Abu Hurairah and al-Dahhak said: this is at the coming of 'Isa, peace be upon him; when he comes down, every religion will follow him, and the communities will all become one, so no people of any religion will remain except that they enter Islam or pay the jizyah to the Muslims.

al-Suddi said: this is at the emergence of the Mahdi; no one will remain except that he enters Islam or pays the kharaj. [Zad al-Masir of Ibn al-Jawzi: 3/290; Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 8/121.]

al-Kalbi said: no religion will remain except that Islam will prevail over it; this will happen, and it has not yet happened, and the Hour will not come until that happens.

al-Miqdad ibn al-Aswad said: I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say: "No dwelling of clay or hair will remain on the face of the earth except that Allah will cause the word of Islam to enter it, either with honour bestowed upon honour or with humiliation imposed upon humiliation: either Allah honours them, making them of its people so they are honoured, or He humiliates them so they submit to it." [8] [Majma' al-Zawa'id: 6/14.]

From al-Aswad or Suwayd ibn al-'Ala', from Abu Salamah, from 'A'ishah who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Night and day will not pass until al-Lat and al-'Uzza are worshipped." [9]

She said: I said: "O Messenger of Allah, I did not think that would happen after Allah had sent down to His Messenger..." ﴿He it is who sent His Messenger with guidance and the religion of truth.﴾ He said: That will happen when Allah, Mighty and Majestic, wills. Then He will send a wind that takes the soul of everyone who has in his heart the weight of an atom's worth of good; then there will remain those with no good in them, and people will return to the religion of their fathers.

al-Husayn ibn al-Fadl said: its meaning is: that He may make it prevail over all religions by clear proofs and shining demonstrations, so that the argument of this religion is the strongest. Some of them said: Allah has already done that, and this promise has been fulfilled, by His saying: ﴿Today I have perfected for you your religion﴾ [Surat al-Ma'idah: 3].

Some of them said: it means that Islam appears in every place where its people were subjected to humiliation, in whatever place they were, such that no jizyah is taken from them as is taken from the dhimmis.

It was said: its meaning is that He makes it prevail over all the religions that are in the Arabian Peninsula, so He makes it prevail over their religion and defeats them in that place.

It was said: it is the operation of His wisdom over them, and Allah knows best.

**Commentary of al-Tha'alibi (al-Jawahir al-Hisan) on Surah 9, verses 28–33 (part 1 of 2)**

﴿O you who believe, the polytheists are only impure (najas)﴾. Al-Dahhak and Abu 'Ubayda said: filth (qadhar). Ibn al-Anbari said: foul (khabith). One says: a man is najas, a woman is najas, two men or two women are najas, men and women are najas, with the nun and the jim vowelled with fatha, or najas with the jim vowelled with damma, and rijs (filth) in these states. It is not made dual or plural, because it is a verbal noun (masdar). As for najas with the nun vowelled with kasra and the jim sukun, it is not said except when rijs is mentioned with it. When it stands alone, one says najas with the nun fatha and the jim kasra, or najas with the jim damma.

Ibn al-Sumayqa' recited: ﴿Indeed the polytheists are impurities (anjas)﴾, like your saying akhbath in the plural. They differed over the meaning of najas and the reason for which Allah named them thus. It is narrated from Ibn 'Abbas: "The polytheists are only the filth of a pig or a dog." This view is not accepted, for two reasons. First, it is narrated from him by a route that is not reliable (ghayr hamid), so it is not authentically attributed to him. Second, this is impurity of ruling (najasat al-hukm), not impurity of substance (najasat al-'ayn), because if their persons were impure like the dog or the pig, Islam would not purify them, and the prohibition of polytheists entering the Sacred Mosque and other mosques would not be the same. Those who hold that their persons are impure cite what is narrated: that 'Umar ibn 'Abd al-'Aziz wrote, "Prevent the Jews and Christians from entering the mosques of the Muslims," and he followed his prohibition with the words of Allah, ﴿The polytheists are only impure﴾.

It is also narrated from al-Hasan that he said: "Do not shake hands with the polytheists. Whoever shakes hands with them should perform ablution." Qatada said: "He called them impure because they become junub (in a state of major impurity) and do not perform ghusl, and they break their minor ablution and do not perform wudu', so they were prevented from entering the mosque, since one in a state of janaba should not enter the mosque."

Al-Husayn ibn al-Fadl said: "This is impurity of ruling, not impurity of substance, so they were called impure as a form of blame." Evidence for this is what is narrated: the Prophet (ﷺ) met Hudhayfa and took his hand. Hudhayfa said, "O Messenger of Allah, I am junub." He said, "Indeed the believer is not impure (la yanjus)."

﴿So let them not approach the Sacred Mosque﴾. The people of meaning (ahl al-ma'ani) said: by this he intended their prevention from entering the Haram, because if they enter the Haram, they have come near the Sacred Mosque. 'Ata' said: "The whole Haram is qibla and mosque," and he recited this verse. [Tafsir al-Tabari 10/136; Tafsir al-Qurtubi 8/105.]

Jabir, from 'Abd Allah, from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ): "No one enters the Haram except the people of the jizya or a slave of a Muslim man, and their women are lawful to you." And he recited: ﴿after this year of theirs﴾, meaning the year in which Abu Bakr (may Allah be pleased with him) led the people in Hajj, and 'Ali (may Allah ennoble his face) proclaimed the Bara'a (immunity declaration), which was in the ninth year after the Hijra.

﴿And if you fear poverty…﴾ The exegetes said: The polytheists used to bring food to the House, and they traded and bought and sold. When they were prevented from entering the Haram, this was difficult for the Muslims, and Satan cast fear into their hearts, saying to them, "From where will you eat and make a living, when the polytheists have gone and the caravans have been cut off from you?"

The believers said: "O Messenger of Allah, we used to profit from their trade and commerce, and now the markets will be cut off from us, and the commerce will cease, and the benefits we used to gain from it will be lost." So Allah, Mighty and Majestic, revealed: ﴿And if you fear poverty﴾.

'Amr ibn Fa'id said: its meaning is "and if you fear," because the people had been afraid. That is the saying of the speaker: "If you are my father, then honour me," meaning "if I fear poverty and want." One says: 'alla ya'ilu 'aylatan and 'uyulan (to be poor, to become needy). The poet said:
"The poor man does not know when his wealth will come,
and the rich man does not know when he will become poor."
[Lisan al-'Arab 11/488, attributed to Uhayha.]

In the codex of 'Abd Allah (ibn Mas'ud): "wa in khiftum 'ayilatan," meaning "a fear that burdens you," i.e., it weighs upon you, and it is difficult for you.

﴿Allah will enrich you from His bounty﴾. This is because He sent down abundant rain upon them, and their goodness increased when the polytheists departed.

Muqatil said: The people of Jeddah, Sana'a and Jurash in Yemen embraced Islam, and they carried food to Makkah on the backs of camels and beasts, and Allah, Mighty and Majestic, sufficed them against what they had feared.

Al-Kalbi said: "[...] (the text is illegible in the manuscript) [...] and Allah sufficed them in what concerned them." Al-Dahhak and Qatada said: Allah apportioned to them what is better for them, which is the jizya, and Allah enriched them. This is His saying: ﴿Fight those who do not believe in Allah﴾.

Mujahid said: This verse was revealed when the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was commanded to fight the Romans, and after its revelation he went out on the expedition of Tabuk.

Al-Kalbi said: It was revealed concerning Qurayza and al-Nadir from the Jews, and the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) wished [to take the jizya, so Allah revealed] — [the manuscript is illegible, and what we have set down is the apparent reading] — Mighty and Majestic: ﴿Fight those who do not believe in Allah, nor in the Last Day, nor forbid what Allah and His Messenger have forbidden, nor adopt the religion of truth﴾. He meant "the religion of truth" but attributed the noun to the adjective.

Qatada said: "The Truth (al-Haqq) is Allah, Mighty and Majestic, and His religion is Islam." Abu 'Ubayda said its meaning is "the obedience of the people of Islam," and everyone who obeys a king or a ruler has given him din (obedience, submission). Zuhayr said:
"If you should alight in the midst of the Banu Asad,
under the religion of 'Amr, and Fadak should come between us…"
[Tafsir al-Tabari 10/141; Lisan al-'Arab 10/473.]
meaning: under the obedience of 'Amr.

﴿From those who were given the Scripture﴾, meaning the Jews and Christians, from whom the jizya is taken, and that they not be fought. The jizya is also taken from the Sabians and the Samaritans, because their standing regarding the People of the Book is the standing of the people of innovations (ahl al-bid'a) regarding them. The jizya is also taken from the Magians (majus). It has been said that they were of the People of the Book, but their scripture was lifted.

Abu Muhammad 'Abd Allah ibn Hamid al-Wazzan informed us: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn al-Husayn informed us: Muhammad ibn Yahya and [...] (illegible in the manuscript) said: 'Uthman ibn Salih informed us: Ibn Wahb informed us: Yunus informed us, from Ibn Shihab, from Sa'id ibn al-Musayyab, that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) took the jizya from the Magians of Hajar, and that 'Umar took it from the Magians of al-Sawad, and that 'Uthman ibn 'Affan took it from the Berbers. [Ahkam al-Qur'an by al-Jassas 2/412; al-Musannaf by 'Abd al-Razzaq 6/69, no. 10027.]

Ibn Hamid informed us: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn al-Husayn informed us: Muhammad ibn Yahya and Ahmad ibn Yusuf said: Abu 'Asim informed us, from Ja'far ibn Muhammad, from his father, who said: 'Umar ibn al-Khattab (may Allah be pleased with him) said, "I do not know how to deal with the Magians." 'Abd al-Rahman ibn 'Awf said, "I heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) say: 'Treat them as you treat the People of the Book.'" [al-Musnad by al-Shafi'i: 209.]

Abu 'Asim said: "I walked a mile and ran a mile until I heard from Ja'far ibn Muhammad, 'Haddathana' (he narrated to us), meaning this hadith."

And we are prevented from marrying their women, eating their slaughtered animals, [and having intercourse with] the private parts (furuj) and the foods, which are under suspicion (al-khatar), and it is not permissible to proceed in them with doubt.

Al-Hasan said: "The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) fought the people of this peninsula for Islam; he would accept nothing else from them. This was the best of jihad. After him there was another jihad concerning this matter of sustenance (al-si'a) regarding the People of the Book." [al-Durr al-Manthur 3/229.]

﴿Fight those who do not believe in Allah nor in the Last Day﴾, [meaning] that they not follow anything other than these two (the Scripture and the Messenger) — innovation and misguidance. The jizya is not taken from idols. ﴿Until they give the jizya﴾, which is what the mu'ahad (covenanted non-Muslim) gives for his covenant. It is a verbal form (fi'la) from jaza, yajzi, when one pays what is due (qada 'alayhi). Jizya is like al-qi'da and al-jalsa (verbal nouns of the form fi'la). The meaning of the words is: "until they give the kharaj (tribute) from their necks, which they expend to the Muslims as a means of defence from them."

As for its amount: Anas said: "The Prophet distributed a dinar upon every adult male (muhtalim)." 'Umar ibn al-Khattab (may Allah be pleased with him) imposed upon the poor among the dhimmis one dirham each, upon the middle-income ones twenty-four, and upon the wealthy forty-eight dirhams, and he did not exceed fifty dirhams. There is no fixed amount, but it is according to what they agreed upon in the settlement (sulh).

﴿'An yad﴾: meaning by transferring it from their hand into the hand of the one to whom it is given, as one says, "I spoke to him, but not with the mouth" (kallamtuhu fama lafam). [Tafsir al-Tabari 10/141.]

Abu 'Ubayda said: "It is said: he gave [...] (unclear in the manuscript) from no good disposition of his, he gave it 'an yad." Al-Qutaybi said: "It is said: he gave it 'an yad and 'an zahr yad when he gave it spontaneously, not under compulsion."

Ibn 'Abbas said: "It means that they give it with their hands, walking with it unwillingly, and they do not bring it riding, nor do they send it." ﴿And they are sagharun (humbled)﴾, meaning abased and subdued. Ibn 'Abbas said: "They are shaken violently when they pay it." 'Ikrima said: "The meaning of al-sagharr is that you take it while you are seated and he is standing." Al-Kalbi said: "When he comes to pay, he is slapped on the back of his neck." It was said: his giving it is the sagharr. It was said: he is not accepted to convey it through a messenger or an agent. It was said: the rulings of Islam are applied to them, and that is the sagharr.

'Abd Allah ibn Hamid informed us: Muhammad ibn Ja'far informed us: 'Ali ibn Harb informed us: al-Sabbat informed us: 'Abd al-'Aziz ibn [...] (illegible word in the manuscript) informed us, from Habib ibn Abi Thabit, who said: A man came to Ibn 'Abbas and said, "The land is of the kharaj land, whose people are unable to cultivate it. Shall I cultivate it, sow it, and pay its kharaj?" He said, "No." Another came and asked him the same, and he said, "No," and he recited His saying: ﴿Fight those who do not believe in Allah…﴾ up to ﴿and they are sagharun﴾. Does one of you deliberately place the sagharr upon the neck of one of them, then remove it and place it upon his own neck? [Tafsir al-Qurtubi 8/116, and he also narrated the following reports.]

Kulayb ibn Wa'il said: I said to Ibn 'Umar, "I bought land." He said, "Buying is good." I said, "But I pay from every jarib of land a dirham and a qafiz of food?" He said, "Then do not put sagharan (humiliation) upon your neck."

Maymun ibn Mihran narrated from Ibn 'Umar, who said: "It does not please me that the whole land be mine for a jizya of five dirhams, in which I accept the sagharr upon myself."

﴿And the Jews said, "'Uzayr is the son of Allah"﴾. Sa'id ibn Jubayr and 'Ikrima narrated from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: Salam ibn Mishkam, al-Nu'man ibn Awfa, Shas ibn Qays and Malik ibn al-Sayf came to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and said: "How shall we follow you, when you have abandoned our qibla, and you do not claim that 'Uzayr is the son of Allah?" So Allah revealed concerning their saying: ﴿And the Jews said, "'Uzayr is the son of Allah"﴾.

Ibn Muhaysin, 'Asim and al-Kisa'i recited ʿUzayrun with tanwin (nunation), and this is the view of Abu 'Ubayd and Abu Hatim. The rest recited it without tanwin. Whoever reads with tanwin says: because it is a light name (ism khafif), its proper form is to be declined, even if it is foreign, like Nuh, Lut and Hud. Abu Hatim and al-Mubarrad said: the preferred reading is tanwin, because it is not a patronymic (mansub), and the statement is incomplete and is in the place of the predicate (khabar), not in the accusative. Tanwin is permitted in the attributive (na't) when the name can dispense with "son of" (ibn), or is attributed to a known name, or to a title that has come to predominate over it, like Muhammad ibn 'Abd Allah and Yazid ibn 'Abd Allah, because the qualifier and the qualified are like one thing. So it is nunated in the predicate and omitted in the attribute. Sometimes they retain tanwin in the attribute. A poet, whom al-Farra' recited, said:
"If there is no wealth there, then indeed
my praise will come to Zayd ibn Mahlahil."
Al-Kisa'i recited [...] (illegible in the manuscript), his school of thought.

Abu 'Ubayda said: This is not attributed to his father; it is rather like your saying "Zayd ibn al-Amir" and "Zayd ibn 'Abd Allah," so 'Uzayr is followed by a predicate.

Whoever omits tanwin says: because it is a foreign name and resembles a diminutive (musaggar) name.

Al-Farra' said: Since the nun of 'Uzayr is quiescent [and it is the nun of tanwin] and the ba' of ibn is quiescent, and two quiescent letters met, the first of them was dropped because vocalising it was burdensome, as the poet said: "You will find me with the commander a dutiful one, and with the spear a stubborn attacker, when Ghutayf al-Sulami flees." [Tafsir al-Tabari 10/144; Lisan al-'Arab 3/438.] So the quiescent nun that came after it was dropped.

Al-Zajjaj said: It is permissible that the predicate be omitted, its estimated form being: "'Uzayr is the son of Allah, our worshipped one."

'Ubayd ibn 'Umayr said: This statement was made by only one man among the Jews, named Finhas ibn 'Azura, who is the one who said: ﴿Indeed Allah is poor and we are rich﴾ [Tafsir al-Tabari 4/259].

'Ata' al-'Awfi narrated from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: "The Jews said, 'Uzayr is the son of Allah,' and they said this only because 'Uzayr was among the People of the Book, and the Torah was with them, as much as Allah willed for them to know. Then they neglected it and acted contrary to the truth. The Ark (al-tabut) was among them. When Allah, Mighty and Majestic, saw that they had neglected the Torah, acted according to their desires, lost the Ark, and that He had made them forget the Torah and removed it from their breasts, He sent upon them a disease, so that their bellies swelled until a man would touch his liver. Thus they forgot the Torah and it was removed from their breasts. 'Uzayr was among them. They remained as long as Allah willed them to remain after the Torah had been removed from their breasts. 'Uzayr had been one of their scholars. He supplicated Allah [...] and implored Him to return to him what had been removed from their breasts. While he was praying, humbly before Allah, Mighty and Majestic, a light descended from the heaven and entered his inside, and what had gone from within him of the Torah returned to him. He called out to his people and said: 'O people, Allah has given me the Torah and returned it to me.' Then he began to teach them. They remained as long as Allah willed them to remain, while he taught them. Then the Ark was left behind, after his death from among them. When they saw the Ark, they compared what was in it with what 'Uzayr had been teaching them, and they found it identical. They said, 'By Allah, 'Uzayr has not come except that he is the son of Allah.'" [In full in Tafsir al-Tabari 10/143.]

Al-Suddi and Ibn 'Abbas, in the narration of 'Ammar ibn 'Ammar, said: The Jews said, "'Uzayr is the son of Allah" because the 'Amalekites overcame them, killed them, took the Torah, and their surviving scholars fled and buried the books of the Torah in the mountains and elsewhere. 'Uzayr went off to the mountains and the wild animals, worshipping in the mountains, not mixing with the people nor coming down except on the day of a festival. He would weep and say, "O Lord, You have left the Children of Israel without a scholar," and he wept until the eyelids of his eyes fell off. Once he came down for the festival, and when he returned he found a woman sitting beside one of those graves, weeping and saying, "O my food-giver! O my clothing-giver!"

'Uzayr said to her, "O woman, fear Allah and be patient, and seek reward. Do you not know that death is the way of people?" He said, "Woe to you! Who used to feed you and clothe you before this man?" — meaning her husband whom she was mourning. She said, "Allah." He said, "Then indeed Allah is living and does not die." She said, "O 'Uzayr, then who used to teach the scholars before the Children of Israel?" He said, "Allah." She said, "Then why do you weep over them, when you know that death is true and that Allah is living and does not die?" When 'Uzayr realised that he had been refuted, he turned away, fleeing.

She said to him: "O 'Uzayr, I am not a woman, but I am the World (al-dunya). Indeed, water will gush forth from your prayer place as a spring, and a tree will grow. Eat from the fruit of that tree, drink from the water of that spring, perform ghusl, and pray two rak'as. Then a shaykh will come to you; take from him whatever he gives you."

When morning came, a spring gushed forth from his prayer place and a tree grew, and he did what she had told him. Then a shaykh came and said to him, "Open your mouth." He opened it, and the shaykh put into it something like a great ember, gathered like glass, three times. Then he said to him, "Enter this spring, and walk in it until you reach your people." He entered it, and every time he lifted his foot his knowledge was increased, until he reached his people. He returned to them, and he was the most knowledgeable of people in the Torah. He said, "O Children of Israel, I have brought you the Torah."

They said, "O 'Uzayr, you were not lying." He tied a quill to each of his fingers and wrote with all his fingers until he had written the Torah from memory. Thus he revived the Torah for them and revived the Sunna for them. When the scholars returned, they brought out the books they had buried, and they found them identical to the Torah of 'Uzayr. They said, "Allah gave him this only because he is His son." [The previous source, with variation.]

Al-Kalbi said: When Bukhtnassar (Nebuchadnezzar) prevailed over the Children of Israel, demolished Bayt al-Maqdis, and killed those who read the Torah, 'Uzayr was then a young boy, and they considered him weak, so they did not accept him, and they did not know that he had read the Torah. When he died after one hundred years and the Children of Israel returned to Bayt al-Maqdis, and there was none among them who could read the Torah, Allah, Mighty and Majestic, sent 'Uzayr to renew the Torah for them and to be a sign for them. 'Uzayr came to them and said, "I am 'Uzayr." They denied him and said, "If you are as you claim, 'Uzayr, then recite the Torah to us." So he wrote it out and said, "This is the Torah."

Then a man said: My father related to me from my grandfather that the Torah was placed [for a prophet] and then buried in a mound. So they set out with him until they dug it up and extracted the Torah, and they compared it with what Ezra had written for them, but they did not find it had lost a single letter or verse. So they were amazed and said: "He is the son of God; the Torah was not placed in the heart of a single man after it had gone from our hearts except that he was his son." At that point the Jews said: "Ezra is the son of God."

As for the Christians, it is said that they were upon one religion for a year after Jesus was raised up: they prayed toward the qibla and fasted Ramadan. Then war broke out between them and the Jews. Among the Jews there was a brave man called Yunus, who killed a group of the companions of Jesus, peace be upon him. Then he said to the Jews: "If the truth is with Jesus, then we have disbelieved and denied, and the Fire is our destination. So we are cheated if they enter Paradise and we enter the Fire. I will devise a plan and lead them astray until they enter the Fire." He had a horse called al-'Uqab that he fought upon, but his horse was drowned. He showed remorse and put dust on his head.

The Christians said to him: "Who are you?" Yunus said: "Your enemy." [I heard] [an addition required by the context.] from the sky: "There is no repentance for you except that you become a Christian, and you have repented." So they brought him into the church, and he entered a room for a year, not coming out by night or day, until he learned the Gospel. Then he came out and said to [them] [a word unclear in the manuscript, and what we have recorded seems right]: "God has accepted your repentance." So they believed him and loved him. Then he went to Jerusalem and appointed Nestor as his successor over them, and taught him that Jesus, Mary and God were three. Then he turned to the Romans and taught them the doctrine of divinity and humanity, and said: "Jesus was not a human who became divine, nor a body that became embodied, but he is the son of God." And he taught this to a man called Ya'qub.

Then he called a man called Malik and said to him: "God has not ceased and will not cease [to be with] Jesus, may Allah be pleased with him." When he had gained power over them, he called these three one by one and said to each of them: "You are my successor, and I have seen Jesus in a dream, and he was pleased with me." And he said to each of them: "Tomorrow I will sacrifice myself, so call the people to the place of sacrifice." Then he entered the place of sacrifice and sacrificed himself, saying: "I am only doing this to seek the pleasure of Jesus." When the third day came, each of them called the people to [his sect], and each followed a group of people, and they fought and disagreed until this day of ours. So all the Christians are of the three sects.

﴿That is their saying with their mouths.﴾ That is, the saying of the Christians that the Messiah is the son of God: they say it with their tongues without knowledge.

The scholars of meanings said: Allah, Mighty and Majestic, does not mention a statement joined with the mention of mouths and tongues except that the statement is falsehood, as in His saying: ﴿They say with their mouths what is not in their hearts﴾, and ﴿They say with their tongues what is not in their hearts﴾, and His saying: ﴿Grave is the word that comes out of their mouths; they say nothing but lies﴾ ... ﴿Imitating﴾. Ibn 'Abbas said: resembling. And from him also: imitating. Mujahid said: conforming. Dhu Nun said: there are two readings, yudahi'una with a hamza, which is the reading of 'Asim, and yudahuna without a hamza, which is the reading of the common readers. It is said: "dahaytuhu" and "dahata'tuhu," with the same meaning. ﴿The saying of those who disbelieved before﴾. Qatadah and al-Suddi said: the Christians imitated the saying of the Jews before them, so the Christians said: the Messiah is the son of God, just as the Jews said: ﴿Ezra is the son of God﴾. Mujahid said: they imitated the saying of the polytheists when they said: al-Lat, al-'Uzza and Manat are the daughters of God. Al-Hasan said: their disbelief was likened to the disbelief of those nations of disbelievers who passed away, and he addressed the polytheists of the Arabs when he related of them: ﴿And those who do not know say: Why does Allah not speak to us, or a sign come to us?﴾, then he said: ﴿Thus said those before them, the like of their saying. Their hearts are alike.﴾ Al-Qutaybi said: he means that those among the Jews and Christians in the time of the Prophet ﷺ said what their predecessors had said.

﴿May Allah destroy them.﴾ Ibn 'Abbas said: may Allah curse them; every "qatala" in the Qur'an means a curse. Similarly Aban ibn Taghlib said:
"May Allah destroy her, she blames me, though she knows
that I am the one who corrupts myself and reforms myself."
[Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 8/119.]
Ibn Juraij said: ﴿May Allah destroy them﴾ is in the sense of wonder. ﴿How are they turned away?﴾ That is, they lie and are turned away from the truth after the proof has been established for it.

﴿They took their rabbis and their monks as lords.﴾ al-Dahhak said: their scholars; and he recited: "monks." The rabbis (aḥbār) are the scholars; the singular is ḥabr and ḥibr, with the ḥā' vowelled with kasra and with fatha, and the kasra is better. Yunus al-Jurmi used to claim that he had only heard it with kasra, and he argued from people's saying: "this is muḥabbar," meaning the ink of a scholar. The monks (ruhban) among the Christians are the people of the hermitages and those who abstain in their religion. It is said: rāhib and ruhbān, like fāris and fursān. Its root is from ruhbah, which is fear, as if they fear God. ﴿As lords besides Allah﴾, obeying them in disobedience to God.

Mus'ab ibn Sa'd related from 'Adi ibn Hatim who said: I came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ with a golden cross around my neck. He said: "O 'Adi, throw this idol from your neck." He said: So I threw it. Then he stood and recited Surat Bara'a, and recited this verse: ﴿They took their rabbis and their monks as lords besides Allah﴾ until he finished it. I said to him: "We do not worship them." He said: "Do they not forbid what Allah has made lawful, so that you forbid it, and make lawful what Allah has forbidden, so that you make it lawful?" He said: I said: "Yes." [Al-Mu'jam al-Kabir of al-Tabarani: 17/92.]

Abu al-Ahwas said, on the authority of 'Ata' ibn Abi al-Bakhtari, concerning the saying of Allah, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿They took their rabbis and their monks as lords﴾: As for [if they had commanded] them to worship them besides Allah, they would not have obeyed them; but they commanded them, and they made what Allah had made lawful unlawful, and what He had made unlawful lawful, and they obeyed them, and that was their lordship. [Al-Ahkam by Ibn Hazm: 6/883.]

Al-Rabi' said: I said to Abu al-'Aliyah: How was that lordship among the Children of Israel? He said: They found in the Book of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, what they were commanded and forbidden, and they said: "We will not go ahead of our rabbis in anything. Whatever they command us, we comply; whatever they forbid us, we refrain," the men... and they cast the Book of Allah behind their backs.

The scholars of meanings said: its meaning is that they took their rabbis and monks as tails, since they obeyed them in everything, like His saying: "Blow" until when He made it fire, i.e., like fire. 'Abd Allah ibn al-Mubarak said:
"Did anything change the religion except kings
and evil rabbis and their monks?" [Al-Jihad of Ibn al-Mubarak: 28.]
