They differed about who first practised the nasi'. Ibn Abbas, Qatadah and al-Dahhak said: The first to practise the nasi' were the Banu Malik ibn Kinanah, and there was Abu Thumamah Ubadah ibn Awf ibn Umayyah al-Kinani, who would attend the season every year on a donkey and say: O people, I speak and I am not afraid, and what I say cannot be turned back. We have made Muharram forbidden and postponed Safar; then the following year he would say: We have made Safar forbidden and postponed Muharram.

al-Kalbi said: The first to do that was a man from Kinanah called Nu'aym ibn Tha'labah, who would be ahead of people at the season, and when people resolved to depart, he would stand and address the people, saying: There is no turning back of what I have decreed; I am the one who is not ghā'ib and not disappointed. The polytheists would say to him: Labbayk! Then he would ask them to postpone for him a month in which they would make a change, and he would say: Indeed, general fighting is forbidden. When he said that, they unstrung their bows, broke their spearheads and sheaths, and if he said: It is lawful, they tied their bows, strengthened their sheaths, and raided the people.

[And it is said, after] Nu'aym ibn Tha'labah, a man called Junadah ibn Awf, who is the one whom the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) encountered.

Juwaybir related from al-Dahhak from Ibn Abbas that the first to practise the nasi' was Amr ibn Luhayy ibn Ba'lathah ibn Khindif. Abd al-Rahman ibn Zayd ibn Aslam said: he was a man of Banu Kinanah called al-Qalmas in the Jahiliyyah. The people of the Jahiliyyah did not raid one another in the sacred months; a man would meet the killer of his father or brother and not be touched; then one of them would say: Let us go out. He would be told: This is Muharram. Al-Qalmas would say: I have postponed it this year, so two Safars; and when the following year comes, we will decide and make them both forbidden. [............] [A torn passage in the original.] al-Kumayt said:

Are we not the postponers over Mudar, making the months of lawfulness forbidden?

[Lisan al-Arab: 1/167.]

That is the nasi' of which Allah the Exalted said: ﴿Indeed, the postponement is an increase in disbelief, by which those who disbelieve are led astray﴾. The people of Medina, Asim and Abu Amr read yudallu with a fatha on the ya' and a kasra on the dad, and Abu Hatim chose it because the misguided are joined to it, for His saying: ﴿by which those who disbelieve are led astray, they make it lawful one year and forbid it another year﴾. Abu Raja', al-Hasan, Abu Abd al-Rahman, Qatadah, Mujahid and Ibn Muhaysin read yadillu with a kasra on the dad, and it has two aspects: one is that alladhina kafaru is in the accusative position, meaning Allah leads astray by it those who disbelieve. The second aspect is that alladhina is in the nominative position, meaning those who disbelieve are led astray by it, that is, the misguided among them. The people of Kufa read yuddallu with a damma on the ya' and a fatha on the dad, which is the reading of Ibn Mas'ud and the choice of Abu Ubaydah, for His saying: ﴿Made attractive to them is the evil of their deeds﴾. They make it lawful, meaning the nasi', one year, and forbid it another year, ﴿to make conform﴾, i.e., to agree with, ﴿Ibn Abbas said: to resemble.﴾ The historian said: it means that they would not make lawful a month of the sacred months without forbidding in its place a month of the lawful months, and would not forbid a month of the lawful months without making lawful in its place a month of the sacred months, so that the sacred months would not exceed four months of what Allah had forbidden, thereby matching the number. That is what is meant.

﴿So that they make lawful what Allah has forbidden. The evil of their deeds has been made attractive to them. And Allah does not guide the disbelieving people.﴾

Commentary of al-Tha'labi (*al-Jawahir al-Hisan*) on surah 9, verses 34–37 (part 1 of 2):

﴿O you who believe, indeed many of the rabbis and the monks﴾, meaning the scholars and reciters among the People of the Book, ﴿devour the wealth of people unjustly﴾, that is, they take bribes in their rulings and distort the Book of God, and they write with their own hands books and say, "This is from God," and they take for them a small price from their inferiors. These are the gains they used to receive from them in return for denying Muhammad (ﷺ). Had they believed in him, those gains would have been lost to them. ﴿And they hinder﴾, that is, they turn people away and prevent them ﴿from the way of God﴾, the religion of God. ﴿And those who hoard gold and silver﴾, meaning they too consume wealth unjustly, those who hoard gold and silver.

I heard Abu al-Qasim al-Habibi say: I heard Abu al-Hasan al-Muzaffar ibn Muhammad ibn Ghalib al-Hamadhani say: I heard Ibrahim ibn Muhammad ibn 'Arafa al-Iji, known as Ibn Naftawayh, say: Gold (*dhahab*) was so named because it goes away (*yadhhabu*) and does not remain, and silver (*fidda*) was so named because it scatters (*tanfudu*), that is, it disperses and does not remain. The two names are sufficient evidence of their perishing, and God knows best about them.

The scholars differed about the meaning of hoarding (*kanz*). Nafi' narrated from Ibn 'Umar, who said: "Any wealth whose zakat is paid is not hoarding, even if it is beneath seven earths, and any wealth whose zakat is not paid is hoarding, even if it is above the ground."

Ibn 'Abbas, al-Dahhak and al-Suddi said the same. This is supported by what is narrated from Ibn al-Zubayr, that he heard Jabir ibn 'Abd Allah say: "When you remove the charity from your wealth, you have removed its evil, and it is not hoarding."

Sa'id ibn al-Musayyab said: 'Umar asked a man about land he had sold: "What is the best place to put this money?" He said: "Where shall I put it?" 'Umar said: "Bury it under your wife's bed." The man said: "O Commander of the Faithful, is that not hoarding?" 'Umar said: "What has had its zakat paid is not hoarding." [Musannaf 'Abd al-Razzaq: 4/108, no. 7146, and the wording is corrected from it.]

'Ali ibn Abi Talib (may God be pleased with him) said: "Whatever exceeds four thousand dirhams is hoarding, whether or not its zakat is paid, and what is below that is provision (*nafaqa*)."

He also said, narrated from al-Walid ibn Zayd: "Whatever wealth exceeds its owner's need for it is hoarding."

Mansur, from 'Umar ibn Murra, from Salim ibn Abi al-Ja'd, from Thawban, said: When this verse was revealed, ﴿And those who hoard gold and silver﴾, the Prophet (ﷺ) said, "Woe to gold, woe to silver," saying it three times. This was difficult for the Companions of the Messenger of God (ﷺ). The Muhajirun said: "Then what wealth should we acquire?" 'Umar said: "I will ask the Prophet (ﷺ) about that." He said: "I caught up with him and said: 'O Messenger of God, the Muhajirun said: What wealth should we acquire?'"

The Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: "A remembering tongue, a grateful heart, and a believing wife who helps one of you in his religion." [Musnad Ahmad: 5/366.] [10]

Abdullah ibn Hamid al-Wazzan informed us, Talha ibn 'Abdan informed us, Muhammad ibn Yahya narrated to us, Muhammad ibn 'Abdal narrated to us, al-A'mash narrated to us, from [al-Ma'rur] ibn Suwayd, from Abu Dharr, who said: I came to the Messenger of God (ﷺ) while he was in front of the Ka'ba. When he saw me approaching, he said: "They are the greatest losers, by the Lord of the Ka'ba. They are the greatest losers, by the Lord of the Ka'ba. They are the greatest losers, by the Lord of the Ka'ba."

He said: Grief entered me, and I could hardly breathe. I said: "Has something happened concerning me?" I said: "Who are they, may my father and mother be your ransom?" He said: "The ones with much wealth, except those who spend wealth in the ways of God's servants like this and like this, to his right, his left, above him, and in front of him, and from [.........] [Illegible text in the original.] Every gold and silver that its owner has kept back is hoarding [.........] [Illegible text in the original.] Whoever leaves the good of something, it will be his on the Day of Resurrection." [Musnad Ahmad: 2/309, with variation and without the end of the hadith.]

Talha ibn 'Abd Allah ibn Kurayz al-Khuza'i narrated from Abu al-Dayf, from Abu Hurayra, who said: "Whoever leaves ten thousand dirhams, they will be made into plates with which its owner will be punished on the Day of Resurrection before the judgment."

And from Salman ibn Thawaran, who said: I heard 'Ammar ibn Yasir say: "The People of the Table asked for a table, then it was sent down, and they disbelieved in it. The people of Salih asked for the she-camel, and when they were given it, they disbelieved in it. You have been forbidden to hoard gold and silver, yet you will hoard them." A man said: "Shall we hoard them while we have heard His saying?" He said: "Yes, and some of you will kill others over it."

Shu'ba said: The ring of Abu Hurayra's sword was of silver, and Abu Dharr forbade him from it, saying: The Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: "Whoever leaves gold and silver, he will be branded with them." [11] [Tafsir al-Tabari: 10/153.]

Qatada narrated from Shahr ibn Hawshab, from Abu Umama Suday ibn 'Ajlan, who said: A man from the People of the Bench (*ahl al-suffa*) died, and a dinar was found in his loincloth. The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "A brand." Then another man died, and two dinars were found in his loincloth. He (peace be upon him) said: "Two brands." [12] [Tafsir al-Tabari: 10/154.]

The most correct of the opinions is the first, because the threat is directed at withholding zakat, not at gathering lawful wealth.

This is supported by the saying of the Prophet (ﷺ): "Whoever pays the zakat of his wealth has paid the right that is upon him, and whoever gives more, it is better for him." [Al-Jami' al-Saghir of al-Suyuti: 2/560, no. 836.]

He (ﷺ) also said: "How excellent is righteous wealth for a righteous man." [13] [Kashf al-Khafa' of al-'Ajluni: 2/320, no. 2823.]

Ibn 'Umar was asked about this verse and said: "Whoever hoards it and does not pay its zakat, woe to him." Then he said: "I would not mind if I had wealth equal to Mount Uhud in gold, whose number I know, which I would pay zakat on and use in obedience to God, Mighty and Majestic."

As for the basic meaning of *kanz* (hoarding) in the speech of the Arabs: it is anything gathered, some of it upon other parts of it, whether on the surface of the earth or within it. This is shown by the saying of the poet:

"No good to me if I feed my guests [...] while I have gold hoarded."
[Lisan al-'Arab: 4/55, and al-Sihah: 6/2308.]

He meant: gathered, some of it upon the rest. *Al-Hatiy* is the fruit of the doum palm. Likewise the Arabs say of a gathered thing: *maknaz*, because its parts are pressed together.

Yahya ibn 'Umar read *yaknuzuna* with a *damma* on the *nun*, while the common reading is with a *kasra*. Both are dialects, like *ya'kufuna* and *ya'kufuna*, and *ya'rishuna* and *ya'rushuna*.

*Wa la yunfiquna fi sabil Allah*: he did not say *fa-yunfiquunahuma* (their both). The grammarians differed about this. Qutrub said: it means the zakat, or the hoards, or [.....] [An unclear word in the original.] gold and silver. Al-Farra' said: it dispensed with the one in the pronoun referring to the other, because the context shows that the statement about one applies to the other, as the statement about the one is the same as about the other. This exists in Arabic speech and reports. The poet said:

"We are content with what we have, and you with what you have, though our opinions differ."
[Mughni al-Labib: 2/622. Lisan al-'Arab: 3/360. This verse is attributed to Qays ibn al-'Azim, one of the great poets of the pre-Islamic period. See Sharh Ibn 'Aqil: 1/244, footnote.]

Ibn al-Anbari said: the intended reference is to the more prevalent and general, because silver is more general and gold is more specific. Like His saying, ﴿And seek help through patience and prayer, and indeed it is a great thing﴾ [2:45], where the pronoun refers to prayer because it is more general. And His saying, ﴿When they saw a trade or a diversion, they dispersed toward it﴾ [62:11], where the pronoun refers to trade because it is more general and more excellent.

﴿So give them good tidings﴾, that is, inform them and warn them, ﴿of a painful punishment, on a day when it will be heated in the fire of Hell﴾, that is, it will enter the Fire, the treasures being made red-hot. From this one says: "I heated the iron in the fire." ﴿And their foreheads will be branded therewith﴾, the foreheads of those who hoard, ﴿and their sides and their backs﴾.

'Abd Allah ibn Mas'ud said: "By Him other than whom there is no god, no man who hoards will be branded on the place of a dinar on a dinar or a dirham on a dirham. Rather, his skin will be widened and each dinar and dirham placed upon his two cheeks."

Abu Bakr al-Warraq was asked: Why were the foreheads, sides, and backs singled out for branding? He said: Because the rich man who owns hoarded wealth shrinks when he sees the poor man. When he gathers with him in one assembly, he turns away from him and turns his back to him. Muhammad ibn 'Ali al-Tirmidhi said: That is because he exults and is arrogant with his wealth, and he leans upon his hoard with his sides and reclines against it.

Al-Ahnaf ibn Qays said: I came to Medina, and while I was in a circle containing a group of the Quraysh, a man came, rough of clothing, rough of body, rough of face. He stood over them and said: "Give glad tidings to the hoarders of a heated stone (*radf*) to be heated in the fire of Hell, which will be placed on the nipple of one of them until it comes out from the top of his shoulder blade, and it will be placed on the top of his shoulder blade until it comes out from the nipples of his two breasts, and it will shake, and it will brand the foreheads, sides, and backs until the heat meets in their bellies."

[Note: *radf* means stones on the surface of the earth that have been heated (Lisan al-'Arab: 9/121).]

He said: The people lowered their heads, and I did not see any one of them respond to him with anything. He said: He turned away, and I followed him until he sat by a pillar. I said: "I did not see these people except that they disliked what you said to them." He said: "These people do not understand anything." [Jami' al-Bayan of al-Tabari: 10/160. Sahih Ibn Hibban: 8/51.]

﴿This is what you hoarded for yourselves﴾, that is, it will be said to them: "This is what you hoarded for yourselves," like His saying, ﴿As for those whose faces turn black: "Did you disbelieve after your belief? Taste the punishment for what you used to deny"﴾ [3:106]. That is, you denied God's rights in your wealth and withheld them.

The scholars differed about the ruling of this verse and about who it was revealed concerning. Ibn Shihab narrated from Khalid ibn Zayd ibn Aslam, from Ibn 'Umar, who was asked about the verse ﴿Those who hoard gold and silver﴾, and Ibn 'Umar said: "This was before zakat was revealed. When it was revealed, God made it a purification of wealth."

Mujahid narrated from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: When this verse was revealed, it was difficult for the Muslims, and they said: "None of us can leave for his child wealth that he will not leave behind." 'Umar (may God be pleased with him) said: "I will relieve you of this, so go." 'Umar set out, and Thawban followed him. He came to the Prophet (ﷺ) and said: "O Prophet of God, this has been difficult for your Companions." He said: "God, Mighty and Majestic, did not enjoin zakat except to purify what remains of your wealth, and He enjoined inheritance on wealth that will remain after you." Then he said: "Shall I not tell you the best thing a man can hoard? A righteous wife: when he looks at her, she pleases him; when he commands her, she obeys him; and when he is absent from her, she guards him." [Sunan Abi Dawud: 1/375.] [14]

Some Companions said: It refers specifically to the People of the Book. Al-Suddi said: It refers to the People of the Qibla (the Muslims). Al-Dahhak said: It is general, covering the People of the Book and the Muslims. Whoever earns lawful wealth but does not give God's right from it, it is a hoard, even if it is little and above the surface of the earth. And what has had God's right given from it is not a hoard, even if it is much and buried in the earth.

Zayd ibn Wahb narrated: I passed by al-Rabadha and found Abu Dharr, so I said to him: "What brought you to this place?" He said: "I was in Syria, and I disagreed with Mu'awiya about this verse, ﴿And those who hoard﴾, the verse. Mu'awiya said: It was revealed concerning the People of the Book. I said: It was revealed concerning us and them. There was an argument between me and them about it, so he wrote to 'Uthman (may God be pleased with him) complaining about me. 'Uthman wrote to me to come to Medina. I came to Medina, and the people crowded around me as if they had not seen me before. I mentioned that to 'Uthman, and he said: 'If you wish, you may withdraw and stay nearby.' That is what brought me to this place. If they had appointed me over an army, I would have listened and obeyed."

Some said: It was revealed specifically concerning those who withhold zakat, and this is the most sound of the opinions. It is supported by what Suhayl narrated from his father, from Abu Hurayra, who said: The Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: "No owner of hoarded wealth who does not pay its zakat will have it heated for him in the fire of Hell, and plates will be made of it, and his forehead and his sides will be branded with them, until God judges between His servants on a day whose length is fifty thousand years. Then he will be sent either to Paradise or to the Fire. No owner of sheep who does not pay their zakat will have them spread for him on a level plain, as large as they ever were, and they will trample him with their hooves and gore him with their horns, having neither a bent horn nor a broken horn. Whenever the last of them passes over him, the first of them returns to him, until God judges between His servants on a day whose length is fifty thousand years. Then he will be sent either to Paradise or to the Fire. No owner of camels who does not pay their zakat will have them spread for him on a level plain, as large as they ever were [.........] [Unreadable text in the manuscript.] Whenever the last of them passes over him, the first of them returns to him, until God judges between His servants on a day whose length is fifty thousand years. Then he will be sent either to Paradise or to the Fire." [15] [Musnad Ahmad: 2/262, with slight variation.] Suhayl said: "I do not know whether he mentioned cattle or not."

Thawban narrated that the Prophet (ﷺ) used to say: "Whoever leaves behind him a hoard, it will be presented to him on the Day of Resurrection as a bald poisonous serpent with two black spots on its head. It will follow him, saying: 'Woe to you, what are you?' He will say: 'I am your hoard that you left behind you.' It will not cease following him until it reaches his hand and bites it, then it will swallow the rest of his body." [16] [Tafsir al-Tabari: 10/160, Musnad Ahmad: 2/156, 279, with variation, and Kitab al-Musnad of al-Shafi'i: 87.]

﴿Indeed, the number of months﴾, meaning the number of months of the year, ﴿with God is twelve﴾. The common reading is with a *fatha* on the *ayn* and the *shin*. Abu Ja'far read with a *sukun* on the *shin*, and Talha ibn Sulayman read with a *sukun* on the *shin*. *Shahran* (months) is in the accusative as a specification (*tamyiz*).

They are: Muharram, Safar, Rabi' al-Awwal, Rabi' al-Akhir, Jumada al-Ula, Jumada al-Akhira, Rajab, Sha'ban, Ramadan, Shawwal, Dhu al-Qa'da, and Dhu al-Hijja.

As for Muharram, it was so named because fighting is forbidden in it. Safar was so named because Mecca becomes empty (*tasfaru*) of people in it, that is, it becomes deserted. It was also said: A plague occurred in it, and their faces turned yellow. Abu 'Ubayda said: Safar was so named because they emptied (*safarat*) their waterskins of milk in it. The two Rabi'es were so named because water freezes in them. Rajab was so named because they used to honor it (*yurajjibunahu*), that is, they glorify it: *rajabtuhu* and *rajjabtuhu*, with light and heavy forms, when you glorify him. Al-Kumayt said:

"I do not seek for myself any protection other than them, nor other than those I revere and glorify."

It was also said: It was so named because fighting is abandoned in it, from the saying of the Arabs: "A man is *arjab* when he is cut off and unable to work."

It is narrated from the Prophet (ﷺ) that he said: "In Paradise there is a river called Rajab, whose water is whiter than snow and sweeter than honey. Whoever fasts one day of Rajab will drink from it." [Fada'il al-Awqat of al-Bayhaqi: 90.]

'Umar said: Sha'ban was so named because the tribes disperse (*yatasha'ab*) in it.

Zayad ibn Maymun narrated that the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Sha'ban was so named because much good branches out (*yatashabba*) in it for Ramadan." [17] [Kanz al-'Ummal: 8/591, no. 24293.]

The discussion of Ramadan has already passed. Shawwal was so named because of the *shawlan* of she-camels, the milk-giving ones, lifting their tails in it. [Lisan al-'Arab: 11/377.]

Abu Zayd al-Balkhi said: It was so named because the tribes move (*tashul*) in it, that is, they depart from their places. Dhu al-Qa'da was so named because they sit (*qu'ud*) in it, abstaining from fighting. Dhu al-Hijja was so named because they perform their Hajj in it. God knows best.

Some eloquent speakers said: When the Arabs saw the nobles abandoning their customs and forbidding raids, they called it *Muharram*. When their pillars weakened, their bodies fell ill, and their complexions turned yellow, they called it *Safar*. When the flowers appeared and the gardens bloomed, they called them *Rabi'ani*. When fruits became scarce and water froze, they called them *Jumadiyan*. When the seas stirred, the rivers were hot, and the trees were stripped of leaves, they called it *Rajab*. When virtues became manifest and the tribes branched out, they called it *Sha'ban*. When the *fada* (tamarisk) grew hot and the embers of the *ghada* (saxaul) were extinguished, they called it *Ramadan*. When the clouds cleared, the flies multiplied, and the she-camels lifted their tails, all but those slaughtered, they called it *Shawwal*. When the merchants stopped travelling, they called it *Dhu al-Qa'da*. When they set out for Hajj from every deep valley, showing their chanting and their cries, they called it *Dhu al-Hijja*.

﴿In the Book of God﴾, meaning the Preserved Tablet. It was also said: in His decree, which He decreed ﴿on the day He created the heavens and the earth﴾, ﴿of them four are sacred﴾, the months the Arabs used to glorify, forbidding fighting in them, so that if a man met the slayer of his father or brother, he would not attack him. They are: Rajab, Dhu al-Qa'da, Dhu al-Hijja, and Muharram. One is single and three are consecutive. [Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 6/39.]

﴿That is the upright religion﴾, the straight reckoning. ﴿So do not wrong yourselves therein﴾, that is, in the sacred months, by doing sin against God, Mighty and Majestic, and abandoning His obedience. Ibn 'Abbas said: It means making fighting and raiding in them lawful. Muhammad ibn Ishaq narrated from Yasar: Do not make what is lawful in them unlawful, nor what is unlawful in them lawful, as the people of polytheism did. Qatada said: Righteous deeds and reward are greater in the sacred months, and sin and wrongdoing in them are greater than wrongdoing in other months, although wrongdoing is always grave. But God magnifies what He wills of His command, just as He chooses from His creation whom He wills.

And fight against the polytheists all together, just as they fight against you all together. Know that Allah is with the God-fearing.

Scholars differed regarding the prohibition of fighting in the sacred months (al-ashhur al-hurum). A group said that it has been abrogated (mansukh). Qatadah and Ata al-Khurasani said: fighting used to be prohibited much in the sacred months, then it was abrogated and fighting in them was made lawful by His saying: ﴿And fight against the polytheists all together﴾, meaning: in them and in other than them.

al-Zuhri said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) used to forbid fighting in the sacred months, by what Allah the Glorified had revealed of its prohibition, until Surah Bara'ah was revealed, and so fighting the polytheists was made lawful.

Abu Ishaq said: I asked Sufyan al-Thawri about fighting in the sacred month, and he said: This is abrogated, and it has passed; there is no harm in fighting in it or in other than it. They said: Because the Prophet (ﷺ) fought the Hawazin at Hunayn and the Thaqif at al-Ta'if in Shawwal and part of Dhu al-Qa'dah, which indicates that it is abrogated.

Others said: it is not abrogated. Ibn Jurayj said: Ata ibn Abi Rabah swore by Allah that it is not lawful for people to raid in Muharram or in the sacred months, except that they fight in them; and it was not abrogated. Ibn Hayyan said: this verse abrogated every verse that contains a concession.

﴿Indeed, the postponement (al-nasi')﴾: al-Hasan, Alqamah, Qatadah, Mujahid, Nafi' (other than Warsh), Abu Amir, Isa, al-A'mash, Asim, Hamzah, al-Kisa'i and Ibn Amir read al-nasi' with a long vowel and a hamzah, and this was chosen by Abu Ubaydah and Abu Hatim. It is a verbal noun (masdar) like al-kharir, al-si'ir and al-hariq and the like; it could also be a passive form shifted to the pattern fa'il like al-jarih, al-qatil and al-ghariq, its implied meaning being: the postponed month. Abu Abd al-Rahman, Talhah, al-Ashhab and Shibl read (al-nasu') with a sukun on the sin and a hamzah, as a masdar only. Abu Amr and Warsh [Warsh: he is Abu Sa'id, and Abu Amr Uthman ibn Sa'id ibn Abd Allah ibn Amr] read al-nasiyy with shaddah and without hamzah.

This was narrated from Ibn Kathir, meaning al-nasiyy, i.e. the abandoned, as Allah the Exalted said: ﴿They forgot Allah, so He forgot them﴾, from forgetting. It may be that its origin is the hamzah, lightened. They differed about the root of the word. al-Akhfash said: it is from postponement, and from it comes al-nasi'ah in sale; it is said: Allah postponed (anså) his term, and he postponed (nasa'a) in his term, i.e., delayed it. Qutrub said: it is from increase; every increase that occurs in something is nasi', and likewise it is said of milk when it is increased with water: nasi' and nasu', and of a pregnant woman: nasu'at, due to the addition of the waw in it. And "I postponed the she-camel (nasa'at al-naqah) and made her go (anse'tuha)" when you drive her so that her pace increases. Qatadah said: some people of the people of error made an agreement, and they added Safar to the sacred months. A man would stand at the season (al-mawsim) and say: Behold, your gods have made Muharram forbidden, so they would forbid it that year; then he would stand the following year and say: Behold, your gods have made Safar forbidden, so they would forbid it that year. And these two were called: the two Safars.

As for the meaning of the nasi' and the beginning of its matter, as the scholars have related it in different wordings but with one agreed meaning: the Arabs used to forbid the four months, and this was among the things they held to from the religion of Abraham the Friend and his son Ishmael. The Arabs were people of wars and raids, and it was hard for them to remain three consecutive months without raiding in them. They said: If three sacred months follow one another for us, in which we gain nothing, we will surely go hungry, for we gain only on the backs of our animals. So they would sometimes need, along with that, to make lawful the forbidden month, or another of the sacred months, due to a war that occurs between them; they would dislike making it lawful and would make lawful the forbidden month.

They would continue this for a time: they forbid Safar, meaning Muharram, and they say: it is one of the two Safars. Some people have interpreted the saying of the Prophet (ﷺ): "There is no Safar" in this light. Then they would also need to postpone Safar to the month after it, as they needed to postpone Muharram; so they postpone its prohibition to Rabi'. Then they would continue in this as long as Allah willed, then they would need the same again, and so on, so the prohibition keeps shifting from month to month until the prohibition circled through the entire year. Then Islam came when Muharram had returned to its original place which Allah the Mighty and Majestic had set, and that was after a long time.

Mujahid said: The polytheists would perform Hajj in each month for two years. So they performed Hajj in Dhu al-Hijjah for two years, then they performed Hajj in Muharram for two years, then they performed Hajj in Safar for two years. Likewise, in the months that coincided with the Hajj of Abu Bakr, which he performed before the Farewell Hajj, in the second year, in Dhu al-Qa'dah; then the Prophet (ﷺ) performed the Farewell Hajj in the following year, and it coincided with Dhu al-Hijjah. That is when the Prophet (ﷺ) said in his sermon: "Behold, time has returned to the form in which it was on the day Allah created the heavens and the earth. The number of months is twelve, of which four are sacred: three consecutive, Dhu al-Qa'dah, Dhu al-Hijjah and Muharram, and Rajab, which lies between Jumada and Sha'ban." [18] [Musnad Ahmad: 5/37.]

He (ﷺ) meant that the sacred months had returned to their places, the Hajj had returned to Dhu al-Hijjah, and the nasi' was abolished.

They differed about who first practised the nasi'. Ibn Abbas, Qatadah and al-Dahhak said: The first to practise the nasi' were the Banu Malik ibn Kinanah, and there was Abu Thumamah Ubadah ibn Awf ibn Umayyah al-Kinani, who would attend the season every year on a donkey and say: O people, I speak and I am not afraid, and what I say cannot be turned back. We have made Muharram forbidden and postponed Safar; then the following year he would say: We have made Safar forbidden and postponed Muharram.

al-Kalbi said: The first to do that was a man from Kinanah called Nu'aym ibn Tha'labah, who would be ahead of people at the season, and when people resolved to depart, he would stand and address the people, saying: There is no turning back of what I have decreed; I am the one who is not ghā'ib and not disappointed. The polytheists would say to him: Labbayk! Then he would ask them to postpone for him a month in which they would make a change, and he would say: Indeed, general fighting is forbidden. When he said that, they unstrung their bows, broke their spearheads and sheaths, and if he said: It is lawful, they tied their bows, strengthened their sheaths, and raided the people.

[And it is said, after] Nu'aym ibn Tha'labah, a man called Junadah ibn Awf, who is the one whom the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) encountered.

Juwaybir related from al-Dahhak from Ibn Abbas that the first to practise the nasi' was Amr ibn Luhayy ibn Ba'lathah ibn Khindif. Abd al-Rahman ibn Zayd ibn Aslam said: he was a man of Banu Kinanah called al-Qalmas in the Jahiliyyah. The people of the Jahiliyyah did not raid one another in the sacred months; a man would meet the killer of his father or brother and not be touched; then one of them would say: Let us go out. He would be told: This is Muharram. Al-Qalmas would say: I have postponed it this year, so two Safars; and when the following year comes, we will decide and make them both forbidden. [............] [A torn passage in the original.] al-Kumayt said:

Are we not the postponers over Mudar, making the months of lawfulness forbidden?

[Lisan al-Arab: 1/167.]

That is the nasi' of which Allah the Exalted said: ﴿Indeed, the postponement is an increase in disbelief, by which those who disbelieve are led astray﴾. The people of Medina, Asim and Abu Amr read yudallu with a fatha on the ya' and a kasra on the dad, and Abu Hatim chose it because the misguided are joined to it, for His saying: ﴿by which those who disbelieve are led astray, they make it lawful one year and forbid it another year﴾. Abu Raja', al-Hasan, Abu Abd al-Rahman, Qatadah, Mujahid and Ibn Muhaysin read yadillu with a kasra on the dad, and it has two aspects: one is that alladhina kafaru is in the accusative position, meaning Allah leads astray by it those who disbelieve. The second aspect is that alladhina is in the nominative position, meaning those who disbelieve are led astray by it, that is, the misguided among them. The people of Kufa read yuddallu with a damma on the ya' and a fatha on the dad, which is the reading of Ibn Mas'ud and the choice of Abu Ubaydah, for His saying: ﴿Made attractive to them is the evil of their deeds﴾. They make it lawful, meaning the nasi', one year, and forbid it another year, ﴿to make conform﴾, i.e., to agree with, ﴿Ibn Abbas said: to resemble.﴾ The historian said: it means that they would not make lawful a month of the sacred months without forbidding in its place a month of the lawful months, and would not forbid a month of the lawful months without making lawful in its place a month of the sacred months, so that the sacred months would not exceed four months of what Allah had forbidden, thereby matching the number. That is what is meant.

﴿So that they make lawful what Allah has forbidden. The evil of their deeds has been made attractive to them. And Allah does not guide the disbelieving people.﴾

Commentary of al-Tha'labi (*al-Jawahir al-Hisan*) on surah 9, verses 34–37 (part 1 of 2):

﴿O you who believe, indeed many of the rabbis and the monks﴾, meaning the scholars and reciters among the People of the Book, ﴿devour the wealth of people unjustly﴾, that is, they take bribes in their rulings and distort the Book of God, and they write with their own hands books and say, "This is from God," and they take for them a small price from their inferiors. These are the gains they used to receive from them in return for denying Muhammad (ﷺ). Had they believed in him, those gains would have been lost to them. ﴿And they hinder﴾, that is, they turn people away and prevent them ﴿from the way of God﴾, the religion of God. ﴿And those who hoard gold and silver﴾, meaning they too consume wealth unjustly, those who hoard gold and silver.

I heard Abu al-Qasim al-Habibi say: I heard Abu al-Hasan al-Muzaffar ibn Muhammad ibn Ghalib al-Hamadhani say: I heard Ibrahim ibn Muhammad ibn 'Arafa al-Iji, known as Ibn Naftawayh, say: Gold (*dhahab*) was so named because it goes away (*yadhhabu*) and does not remain, and silver (*fidda*) was so named because it scatters (*tanfudu*), that is, it disperses and does not remain. The two names are sufficient evidence of their perishing, and God knows best about them.

The scholars differed about the meaning of hoarding (*kanz*). Nafi' narrated from Ibn 'Umar, who said: "Any wealth whose zakat is paid is not hoarding, even if it is beneath seven earths, and any wealth whose zakat is not paid is hoarding, even if it is above the ground."

Ibn 'Abbas, al-Dahhak and al-Suddi said the same. This is supported by what is narrated from Ibn al-Zubayr, that he heard Jabir ibn 'Abd Allah say: "When you remove the charity from your wealth, you have removed its evil, and it is not hoarding."

Sa'id ibn al-Musayyab said: 'Umar asked a man about land he had sold: "What is the best place to put this money?" He said: "Where shall I put it?" 'Umar said: "Bury it under your wife's bed." The man said: "O Commander of the Faithful, is that not hoarding?" 'Umar said: "What has had its zakat paid is not hoarding." [Musannaf 'Abd al-Razzaq: 4/108, no. 7146, and the wording is corrected from it.]

'Ali ibn Abi Talib (may God be pleased with him) said: "Whatever exceeds four thousand dirhams is hoarding, whether or not its zakat is paid, and what is below that is provision (*nafaqa*)."

He also said, narrated from al-Walid ibn Zayd: "Whatever wealth exceeds its owner's need for it is hoarding."

Mansur, from 'Umar ibn Murra, from Salim ibn Abi al-Ja'd, from Thawban, said: When this verse was revealed, ﴿And those who hoard gold and silver﴾, the Prophet (ﷺ) said, "Woe to gold, woe to silver," saying it three times. This was difficult for the Companions of the Messenger of God (ﷺ). The Muhajirun said: "Then what wealth should we acquire?" 'Umar said: "I will ask the Prophet (ﷺ) about that." He said: "I caught up with him and said: 'O Messenger of God, the Muhajirun said: What wealth should we acquire?'"

The Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: "A remembering tongue, a grateful heart, and a believing wife who helps one of you in his religion." [Musnad Ahmad: 5/366.] [10]

Abdullah ibn Hamid al-Wazzan informed us, Talha ibn 'Abdan informed us, Muhammad ibn Yahya narrated to us, Muhammad ibn 'Abdal narrated to us, al-A'mash narrated to us, from [al-Ma'rur] ibn Suwayd, from Abu Dharr, who said: I came to the Messenger of God (ﷺ) while he was in front of the Ka'ba. When he saw me approaching, he said: "They are the greatest losers, by the Lord of the Ka'ba. They are the greatest losers, by the Lord of the Ka'ba. They are the greatest losers, by the Lord of the Ka'ba."

He said: Grief entered me, and I could hardly breathe. I said: "Has something happened concerning me?" I said: "Who are they, may my father and mother be your ransom?" He said: "The ones with much wealth, except those who spend wealth in the ways of God's servants like this and like this, to his right, his left, above him, and in front of him, and from [.........] [Illegible text in the original.] Every gold and silver that its owner has kept back is hoarding [.........] [Illegible text in the original.] Whoever leaves the good of something, it will be his on the Day of Resurrection." [Musnad Ahmad: 2/309, with variation and without the end of the hadith.]

Talha ibn 'Abd Allah ibn Kurayz al-Khuza'i narrated from Abu al-Dayf, from Abu Hurayra, who said: "Whoever leaves ten thousand dirhams, they will be made into plates with which its owner will be punished on the Day of Resurrection before the judgment."

And from Salman ibn Thawaran, who said: I heard 'Ammar ibn Yasir say: "The People of the Table asked for a table, then it was sent down, and they disbelieved in it. The people of Salih asked for the she-camel, and when they were given it, they disbelieved in it. You have been forbidden to hoard gold and silver, yet you will hoard them." A man said: "Shall we hoard them while we have heard His saying?" He said: "Yes, and some of you will kill others over it."

Shu'ba said: The ring of Abu Hurayra's sword was of silver, and Abu Dharr forbade him from it, saying: The Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: "Whoever leaves gold and silver, he will be branded with them." [11] [Tafsir al-Tabari: 10/153.]

Qatada narrated from Shahr ibn Hawshab, from Abu Umama Suday ibn 'Ajlan, who said: A man from the People of the Bench (*ahl al-suffa*) died, and a dinar was found in his loincloth. The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "A brand." Then another man died, and two dinars were found in his loincloth. He (peace be upon him) said: "Two brands." [12] [Tafsir al-Tabari: 10/154.]

The most correct of the opinions is the first, because the threat is directed at withholding zakat, not at gathering lawful wealth.

This is supported by the saying of the Prophet (ﷺ): "Whoever pays the zakat of his wealth has paid the right that is upon him, and whoever gives more, it is better for him." [Al-Jami' al-Saghir of al-Suyuti: 2/560, no. 836.]

He (ﷺ) also said: "How excellent is righteous wealth for a righteous man." [13] [Kashf al-Khafa' of al-'Ajluni: 2/320, no. 2823.]

Ibn 'Umar was asked about this verse and said: "Whoever hoards it and does not pay its zakat, woe to him." Then he said: "I would not mind if I had wealth equal to Mount Uhud in gold, whose number I know, which I would pay zakat on and use in obedience to God, Mighty and Majestic."

As for the basic meaning of *kanz* (hoarding) in the speech of the Arabs: it is anything gathered, some of it upon other parts of it, whether on the surface of the earth or within it. This is shown by the saying of the poet:

"No good to me if I feed my guests [...] while I have gold hoarded."
[Lisan al-'Arab: 4/55, and al-Sihah: 6/2308.]

He meant: gathered, some of it upon the rest. *Al-Hatiy* is the fruit of the doum palm. Likewise the Arabs say of a gathered thing: *maknaz*, because its parts are pressed together.

Yahya ibn 'Umar read *yaknuzuna* with a *damma* on the *nun*, while the common reading is with a *kasra*. Both are dialects, like *ya'kufuna* and *ya'kufuna*, and *ya'rishuna* and *ya'rushuna*.

*Wa la yunfiquna fi sabil Allah*: he did not say *fa-yunfiquunahuma* (their both). The grammarians differed about this. Qutrub said: it means the zakat, or the hoards, or [.....] [An unclear word in the original.] gold and silver. Al-Farra' said: it dispensed with the one in the pronoun referring to the other, because the context shows that the statement about one applies to the other, as the statement about the one is the same as about the other. This exists in Arabic speech and reports. The poet said:

"We are content with what we have, and you with what you have, though our opinions differ."
[Mughni al-Labib: 2/622. Lisan al-'Arab: 3/360. This verse is attributed to Qays ibn al-'Azim, one of the great poets of the pre-Islamic period. See Sharh Ibn 'Aqil: 1/244, footnote.]

Ibn al-Anbari said: the intended reference is to the more prevalent and general, because silver is more general and gold is more specific. Like His saying, ﴿And seek help through patience and prayer, and indeed it is a great thing﴾ [2:45], where the pronoun refers to prayer because it is more general. And His saying, ﴿When they saw a trade or a diversion, they dispersed toward it﴾ [62:11], where the pronoun refers to trade because it is more general and more excellent.

﴿So give them good tidings﴾, that is, inform them and warn them, ﴿of a painful punishment, on a day when it will be heated in the fire of Hell﴾, that is, it will enter the Fire, the treasures being made red-hot. From this one says: "I heated the iron in the fire." ﴿And their foreheads will be branded therewith﴾, the foreheads of those who hoard, ﴿and their sides and their backs﴾.

'Abd Allah ibn Mas'ud said: "By Him other than whom there is no god, no man who hoards will be branded on the place of a dinar on a dinar or a dirham on a dirham. Rather, his skin will be widened and each dinar and dirham placed upon his two cheeks."

Abu Bakr al-Warraq was asked: Why were the foreheads, sides, and backs singled out for branding? He said: Because the rich man who owns hoarded wealth shrinks when he sees the poor man. When he gathers with him in one assembly, he turns away from him and turns his back to him. Muhammad ibn 'Ali al-Tirmidhi said: That is because he exults and is arrogant with his wealth, and he leans upon his hoard with his sides and reclines against it.

Al-Ahnaf ibn Qays said: I came to Medina, and while I was in a circle containing a group of the Quraysh, a man came, rough of clothing, rough of body, rough of face. He stood over them and said: "Give glad tidings to the hoarders of a heated stone (*radf*) to be heated in the fire of Hell, which will be placed on the nipple of one of them until it comes out from the top of his shoulder blade, and it will be placed on the top of his shoulder blade until it comes out from the nipples of his two breasts, and it will shake, and it will brand the foreheads, sides, and backs until the heat meets in their bellies."

[Note: *radf* means stones on the surface of the earth that have been heated (Lisan al-'Arab: 9/121).]

He said: The people lowered their heads, and I did not see any one of them respond to him with anything. He said: He turned away, and I followed him until he sat by a pillar. I said: "I did not see these people except that they disliked what you said to them." He said: "These people do not understand anything." [Jami' al-Bayan of al-Tabari: 10/160. Sahih Ibn Hibban: 8/51.]

﴿This is what you hoarded for yourselves﴾, that is, it will be said to them: "This is what you hoarded for yourselves," like His saying, ﴿As for those whose faces turn black: "Did you disbelieve after your belief? Taste the punishment for what you used to deny"﴾ [3:106]. That is, you denied God's rights in your wealth and withheld them.

The scholars differed about the ruling of this verse and about who it was revealed concerning. Ibn Shihab narrated from Khalid ibn Zayd ibn Aslam, from Ibn 'Umar, who was asked about the verse ﴿Those who hoard gold and silver﴾, and Ibn 'Umar said: "This was before zakat was revealed. When it was revealed, God made it a purification of wealth."

Mujahid narrated from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: When this verse was revealed, it was difficult for the Muslims, and they said: "None of us can leave for his child wealth that he will not leave behind." 'Umar (may God be pleased with him) said: "I will relieve you of this, so go." 'Umar set out, and Thawban followed him. He came to the Prophet (ﷺ) and said: "O Prophet of God, this has been difficult for your Companions." He said: "God, Mighty and Majestic, did not enjoin zakat except to purify what remains of your wealth, and He enjoined inheritance on wealth that will remain after you." Then he said: "Shall I not tell you the best thing a man can hoard? A righteous wife: when he looks at her, she pleases him; when he commands her, she obeys him; and when he is absent from her, she guards him." [Sunan Abi Dawud: 1/375.] [14]

Some Companions said: It refers specifically to the People of the Book. Al-Suddi said: It refers to the People of the Qibla (the Muslims). Al-Dahhak said: It is general, covering the People of the Book and the Muslims. Whoever earns lawful wealth but does not give God's right from it, it is a hoard, even if it is little and above the surface of the earth. And what has had God's right given from it is not a hoard, even if it is much and buried in the earth.

Zayd ibn Wahb narrated: I passed by al-Rabadha and found Abu Dharr, so I said to him: "What brought you to this place?" He said: "I was in Syria, and I disagreed with Mu'awiya about this verse, ﴿And those who hoard﴾, the verse. Mu'awiya said: It was revealed concerning the People of the Book. I said: It was revealed concerning us and them. There was an argument between me and them about it, so he wrote to 'Uthman (may God be pleased with him) complaining about me. 'Uthman wrote to me to come to Medina. I came to Medina, and the people crowded around me as if they had not seen me before. I mentioned that to 'Uthman, and he said: 'If you wish, you may withdraw and stay nearby.' That is what brought me to this place. If they had appointed me over an army, I would have listened and obeyed."

Some said: It was revealed specifically concerning those who withhold zakat, and this is the most sound of the opinions. It is supported by what Suhayl narrated from his father, from Abu Hurayra, who said: The Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: "No owner of hoarded wealth who does not pay its zakat will have it heated for him in the fire of Hell, and plates will be made of it, and his forehead and his sides will be branded with them, until God judges between His servants on a day whose length is fifty thousand years. Then he will be sent either to Paradise or to the Fire. No owner of sheep who does not pay their zakat will have them spread for him on a level plain, as large as they ever were, and they will trample him with their hooves and gore him with their horns, having neither a bent horn nor a broken horn. Whenever the last of them passes over him, the first of them returns to him, until God judges between His servants on a day whose length is fifty thousand years. Then he will be sent either to Paradise or to the Fire. No owner of camels who does not pay their zakat will have them spread for him on a level plain, as large as they ever were [.........] [Unreadable text in the manuscript.] Whenever the last of them passes over him, the first of them returns to him, until God judges between His servants on a day whose length is fifty thousand years. Then he will be sent either to Paradise or to the Fire." [15] [Musnad Ahmad: 2/262, with slight variation.] Suhayl said: "I do not know whether he mentioned cattle or not."

Thawban narrated that the Prophet (ﷺ) used to say: "Whoever leaves behind him a hoard, it will be presented to him on the Day of Resurrection as a bald poisonous serpent with two black spots on its head. It will follow him, saying: 'Woe to you, what are you?' He will say: 'I am your hoard that you left behind you.' It will not cease following him until it reaches his hand and bites it, then it will swallow the rest of his body." [16] [Tafsir al-Tabari: 10/160, Musnad Ahmad: 2/156, 279, with variation, and Kitab al-Musnad of al-Shafi'i: 87.]

﴿Indeed, the number of months﴾, meaning the number of months of the year, ﴿with God is twelve﴾. The common reading is with a *fatha* on the *ayn* and the *shin*. Abu Ja'far read with a *sukun* on the *shin*, and Talha ibn Sulayman read with a *sukun* on the *shin*. *Shahran* (months) is in the accusative as a specification (*tamyiz*).

They are: Muharram, Safar, Rabi' al-Awwal, Rabi' al-Akhir, Jumada al-Ula, Jumada al-Akhira, Rajab, Sha'ban, Ramadan, Shawwal, Dhu al-Qa'da, and Dhu al-Hijja.

As for Muharram, it was so named because fighting is forbidden in it. Safar was so named because Mecca becomes empty (*tasfaru*) of people in it, that is, it becomes deserted. It was also said: A plague occurred in it, and their faces turned yellow. Abu 'Ubayda said: Safar was so named because they emptied (*safarat*) their waterskins of milk in it. The two Rabi'es were so named because water freezes in them. Rajab was so named because they used to honor it (*yurajjibunahu*), that is, they glorify it: *rajabtuhu* and *rajjabtuhu*, with light and heavy forms, when you glorify him. Al-Kumayt said:

"I do not seek for myself any protection other than them, nor other than those I revere and glorify."

It was also said: It was so named because fighting is abandoned in it, from the saying of the Arabs: "A man is *arjab* when he is cut off and unable to work."

It is narrated from the Prophet (ﷺ) that he said: "In Paradise there is a river called Rajab, whose water is whiter than snow and sweeter than honey. Whoever fasts one day of Rajab will drink from it." [Fada'il al-Awqat of al-Bayhaqi: 90.]

'Umar said: Sha'ban was so named because the tribes disperse (*yatasha'ab*) in it.

Zayad ibn Maymun narrated that the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Sha'ban was so named because much good branches out (*yatashabba*) in it for Ramadan." [17] [Kanz al-'Ummal: 8/591, no. 24293.]

The discussion of Ramadan has already passed. Shawwal was so named because of the *shawlan* of she-camels, the milk-giving ones, lifting their tails in it. [Lisan al-'Arab: 11/377.]

Abu Zayd al-Balkhi said: It was so named because the tribes move (*tashul*) in it, that is, they depart from their places. Dhu al-Qa'da was so named because they sit (*qu'ud*) in it, abstaining from fighting. Dhu al-Hijja was so named because they perform their Hajj in it. God knows best.

Some eloquent speakers said: When the Arabs saw the nobles abandoning their customs and forbidding raids, they called it *Muharram*. When their pillars weakened, their bodies fell ill, and their complexions turned yellow, they called it *Safar*. When the flowers appeared and the gardens bloomed, they called them *Rabi'ani*. When fruits became scarce and water froze, they called them *Jumadiyan*. When the seas stirred, the rivers were hot, and the trees were stripped of leaves, they called it *Rajab*. When virtues became manifest and the tribes branched out, they called it *Sha'ban*. When the *fada* (tamarisk) grew hot and the embers of the *ghada* (saxaul) were extinguished, they called it *Ramadan*. When the clouds cleared, the flies multiplied, and the she-camels lifted their tails, all but those slaughtered, they called it *Shawwal*. When the merchants stopped travelling, they called it *Dhu al-Qa'da*. When they set out for Hajj from every deep valley, showing their chanting and their cries, they called it *Dhu al-Hijja*.

﴿In the Book of God﴾, meaning the Preserved Tablet. It was also said: in His decree, which He decreed ﴿on the day He created the heavens and the earth﴾, ﴿of them four are sacred﴾, the months the Arabs used to glorify, forbidding fighting in them, so that if a man met the slayer of his father or brother, he would not attack him. They are: Rajab, Dhu al-Qa'da, Dhu al-Hijja, and Muharram. One is single and three are consecutive. [Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 6/39.]

﴿That is the upright religion﴾, the straight reckoning. ﴿So do not wrong yourselves therein﴾, that is, in the sacred months, by doing sin against God, Mighty and Majestic, and abandoning His obedience. Ibn 'Abbas said: It means making fighting and raiding in them lawful. Muhammad ibn Ishaq narrated from Yasar: Do not make what is lawful in them unlawful, nor what is unlawful in them lawful, as the people of polytheism did. Qatada said: Righteous deeds and reward are greater in the sacred months, and sin and wrongdoing in them are greater than wrongdoing in other months, although wrongdoing is always grave. But God magnifies what He wills of His command, just as He chooses from His creation whom He wills.

And fight against the polytheists all together, just as they fight against you all together. Know that Allah is with the God-fearing.

Scholars differed regarding the prohibition of fighting in the sacred months (al-ashhur al-hurum). A group said that it has been abrogated (mansukh). Qatadah and Ata al-Khurasani said: fighting used to be prohibited much in the sacred months, then it was abrogated and fighting in them was made lawful by His saying: ﴿And fight against the polytheists all together﴾, meaning: in them and in other than them.

al-Zuhri said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) used to forbid fighting in the sacred months, by what Allah the Glorified had revealed of its prohibition, until Surah Bara'ah was revealed, and so fighting the polytheists was made lawful.

Abu Ishaq said: I asked Sufyan al-Thawri about fighting in the sacred month, and he said: This is abrogated, and it has passed; there is no harm in fighting in it or in other than it. They said: Because the Prophet (ﷺ) fought the Hawazin at Hunayn and the Thaqif at al-Ta'if in Shawwal and part of Dhu al-Qa'dah, which indicates that it is abrogated.

Others said: it is not abrogated. Ibn Jurayj said: Ata ibn Abi Rabah swore by Allah that it is not lawful for people to raid in Muharram or in the sacred months, except that they fight in them; and it was not abrogated. Ibn Hayyan said: this verse abrogated every verse that contains a concession.

﴿Indeed, the postponement (al-nasi')﴾: al-Hasan, Alqamah, Qatadah, Mujahid, Nafi' (other than Warsh), Abu Amir, Isa, al-A'mash, Asim, Hamzah, al-Kisa'i and Ibn Amir read al-nasi' with a long vowel and a hamzah, and this was chosen by Abu Ubaydah and Abu Hatim. It is a verbal noun (masdar) like al-kharir, al-si'ir and al-hariq and the like; it could also be a passive form shifted to the pattern fa'il like al-jarih, al-qatil and al-ghariq, its implied meaning being: the postponed month. Abu Abd al-Rahman, Talhah, al-Ashhab and Shibl read (al-nasu') with a sukun on the sin and a hamzah, as a masdar only. Abu Amr and Warsh [Warsh: he is Abu Sa'id, and Abu Amr Uthman ibn Sa'id ibn Abd Allah ibn Amr] read al-nasiyy with shaddah and without hamzah.

This was narrated from Ibn Kathir, meaning al-nasiyy, i.e. the abandoned, as Allah the Exalted said: ﴿They forgot Allah, so He forgot them﴾, from forgetting. It may be that its origin is the hamzah, lightened. They differed about the root of the word. al-Akhfash said: it is from postponement, and from it comes al-nasi'ah in sale; it is said: Allah postponed (anså) his term, and he postponed (nasa'a) in his term, i.e., delayed it. Qutrub said: it is from increase; every increase that occurs in something is nasi', and likewise it is said of milk when it is increased with water: nasi' and nasu', and of a pregnant woman: nasu'at, due to the addition of the waw in it. And "I postponed the she-camel (nasa'at al-naqah) and made her go (anse'tuha)" when you drive her so that her pace increases. Qatadah said: some people of the people of error made an agreement, and they added Safar to the sacred months. A man would stand at the season (al-mawsim) and say: Behold, your gods have made Muharram forbidden, so they would forbid it that year; then he would stand the following year and say: Behold, your gods have made Safar forbidden, so they would forbid it that year. And these two were called: the two Safars.

As for the meaning of the nasi' and the beginning of its matter, as the scholars have related it in different wordings but with one agreed meaning: the Arabs used to forbid the four months, and this was among the things they held to from the religion of Abraham the Friend and his son Ishmael. The Arabs were people of wars and raids, and it was hard for them to remain three consecutive months without raiding in them. They said: If three sacred months follow one another for us, in which we gain nothing, we will surely go hungry, for we gain only on the backs of our animals. So they would sometimes need, along with that, to make lawful the forbidden month, or another of the sacred months, due to a war that occurs between them; they would dislike making it lawful and would make lawful the forbidden month.

They would continue this for a time: they forbid Safar, meaning Muharram, and they say: it is one of the two Safars. Some people have interpreted the saying of the Prophet (ﷺ): "There is no Safar" in this light. Then they would also need to postpone Safar to the month after it, as they needed to postpone Muharram; so they postpone its prohibition to Rabi'. Then they would continue in this as long as Allah willed, then they would need the same again, and so on, so the prohibition keeps shifting from month to month until the prohibition circled through the entire year. Then Islam came when Muharram had returned to its original place which Allah the Mighty and Majestic had set, and that was after a long time.

Mujahid said: The polytheists would perform Hajj in each month for two years. So they performed Hajj in Dhu al-Hijjah for two years, then they performed Hajj in Muharram for two years, then they performed Hajj in Safar for two years. Likewise, in the months that coincided with the Hajj of Abu Bakr, which he performed before the Farewell Hajj, in the second year, in Dhu al-Qa'dah; then the Prophet (ﷺ) performed the Farewell Hajj in the following year, and it coincided with Dhu al-Hijjah. That is when the Prophet (ﷺ) said in his sermon: "Behold, time has returned to the form in which it was on the day Allah created the heavens and the earth. The number of months is twelve, of which four are sacred: three consecutive, Dhu al-Qa'dah, Dhu al-Hijjah and Muharram, and Rajab, which lies between Jumada and Sha'ban." [18] [Musnad Ahmad: 5/37.]

He (ﷺ) meant that the sacred months had returned to their places, the Hajj had returned to Dhu al-Hijjah, and the nasi' was abolished.

They differed about who first practised the nasi'. Ibn Abbas, Qatadah and al-Dahhak said: The first to practise the nasi' were the Banu Malik ibn Kinanah, and there was Abu Thumamah Ubadah ibn Awf ibn Umayyah al-Kinani, who would attend the season every year on a donkey and say: O people, I speak and I am not afraid, and what I say cannot be turned back. We have made Muharram forbidden and postponed Safar; then the following year he would say: We have made Safar forbidden and postponed Muharram.

al-Kalbi said: The first to do that was a man from Kinanah called Nu'aym ibn Tha'labah, who would be ahead of people at the season, and when people resolved to depart, he would stand and address the people, saying: There is no turning back of what I have decreed; I am the one who is not ghā'ib and not disappointed. The polytheists would say to him: Labbayk! Then he would ask them to postpone for him a month in which they would make a change, and he would say: Indeed, general fighting is forbidden. When he said that, they unstrung their bows, broke their spearheads and sheaths, and if he said: It is lawful, they tied their bows, strengthened their sheaths, and raided the people.

[And it is said, after] Nu'aym ibn Tha'labah, a man called Junadah ibn Awf, who is the one whom the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) encountered.

Juwaybir related from al-Dahhak from Ibn Abbas that the first to practise the nasi' was Amr ibn Luhayy ibn Ba'lathah ibn Khindif. Abd al-Rahman ibn Zayd ibn Aslam said: he was a man of Banu Kinanah called al-Qalmas in the Jahiliyyah. The people of the Jahiliyyah did not raid one another in the sacred months; a man would meet the killer of his father or brother and not be touched; then one of them would say: Let us go out. He would be told: This is Muharram. Al-Qalmas would say: I have postponed it this year, so two Safars; and when the following year comes, we will decide and make them both forbidden. [............] [A torn passage in the original.] al-Kumayt said:

Are we not the postponers over Mudar, making the months of lawfulness forbidden?

[Lisan al-Arab: 1/167.]

That is the nasi' of which Allah the Exalted said: ﴿Indeed, the postponement is an increase in disbelief, by which those who disbelieve are led astray﴾. The people of Medina, Asim and Abu Amr read yudallu with a fatha on the ya' and a kasra on the dad, and Abu Hatim chose it because the misguided are joined to it, for His saying: ﴿by which those who disbelieve are led astray, they make it lawful one year and forbid it another year﴾. Abu Raja', al-Hasan, Abu Abd al-Rahman, Qatadah, Mujahid and Ibn Muhaysin read yadillu with a kasra on the dad, and it has two aspects: one is that alladhina kafaru is in the accusative position, meaning Allah leads astray by it those who disbelieve. The second aspect is that alladhina is in the nominative position, meaning those who disbelieve are led astray by it, that is, the misguided among them. The people of Kufa read yuddallu with a damma on the ya' and a fatha on the dad, which is the reading of Ibn Mas'ud and the choice of Abu Ubaydah, for His saying: ﴿Made attractive to them is the evil of their deeds﴾. They make it lawful, meaning the nasi', one year, and forbid it another year, ﴿to make conform﴾, i.e., to agree with, ﴿Ibn Abbas said: to resemble.﴾ The historian said: it means that they would not make lawful a month of the sacred months without forbidding in its place a month of the lawful months, and would not forbid a month of the lawful months without making lawful in its place a month of the sacred months, so that the sacred months would not exceed four months of what Allah had forbidden, thereby matching the number. That is what is meant.

﴿So that they make lawful what Allah has forbidden. The evil of their deeds has been made attractive to them. And Allah does not guide the disbelieving people.﴾

Commentary of al-Tha'labi (*al-Jawahir al-Hisan*) on surah 9, verses 34–37 (part 1 of 2):

﴿O you who believe, indeed many of the rabbis and the monks﴾, meaning the scholars and reciters among the People of the Book, ﴿devour the wealth of people unjustly﴾, that is, they take bribes in their rulings and distort the Book of God, and they write with their own hands books and say, "This is from God," and they take for them a small price from their inferiors. These are the gains they used to receive from them in return for denying Muhammad (ﷺ). Had they believed in him, those gains would have been lost to them. ﴿And they hinder﴾, that is, they turn people away and prevent them ﴿from the way of God﴾, the religion of God. ﴿And those who hoard gold and silver﴾, meaning they too consume wealth unjustly, those who hoard gold and silver.

I heard Abu al-Qasim al-Habibi say: I heard Abu al-Hasan al-Muzaffar ibn Muhammad ibn Ghalib al-Hamadhani say: I heard Ibrahim ibn Muhammad ibn 'Arafa al-Iji, known as Ibn Naftawayh, say: Gold (*dhahab*) was so named because it goes away (*yadhhabu*) and does not remain, and silver (*fidda*) was so named because it scatters (*tanfudu*), that is, it disperses and does not remain. The two names are sufficient evidence of their perishing, and God knows best about them.

The scholars differed about the meaning of hoarding (*kanz*). Nafi' narrated from Ibn 'Umar, who said: "Any wealth whose zakat is paid is not hoarding, even if it is beneath seven earths, and any wealth whose zakat is not paid is hoarding, even if it is above the ground."

Ibn 'Abbas, al-Dahhak and al-Suddi said the same. This is supported by what is narrated from Ibn al-Zubayr, that he heard Jabir ibn 'Abd Allah say: "When you remove the charity from your wealth, you have removed its evil, and it is not hoarding."

Sa'id ibn al-Musayyab said: 'Umar asked a man about land he had sold: "What is the best place to put this money?" He said: "Where shall I put it?" 'Umar said: "Bury it under your wife's bed." The man said: "O Commander of the Faithful, is that not hoarding?" 'Umar said: "What has had its zakat paid is not hoarding." [Musannaf 'Abd al-Razzaq: 4/108, no. 7146, and the wording is corrected from it.]

'Ali ibn Abi Talib (may God be pleased with him) said: "Whatever exceeds four thousand dirhams is hoarding, whether or not its zakat is paid, and what is below that is provision (*nafaqa*)."

He also said, narrated from al-Walid ibn Zayd: "Whatever wealth exceeds its owner's need for it is hoarding."

Mansur, from 'Umar ibn Murra, from Salim ibn Abi al-Ja'd, from Thawban, said: When this verse was revealed, ﴿And those who hoard gold and silver﴾, the Prophet (ﷺ) said, "Woe to gold, woe to silver," saying it three times. This was difficult for the Companions of the Messenger of God (ﷺ). The Muhajirun said: "Then what wealth should we acquire?" 'Umar said: "I will ask the Prophet (ﷺ) about that." He said: "I caught up with him and said: 'O Messenger of God, the Muhajirun said: What wealth should we acquire?'"

The Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: "A remembering tongue, a grateful heart, and a believing wife who helps one of you in his religion." [Musnad Ahmad: 5/366.] [10]

Abdullah ibn Hamid al-Wazzan informed us, Talha ibn 'Abdan informed us, Muhammad ibn Yahya narrated to us, Muhammad ibn 'Abdal narrated to us, al-A'mash narrated to us, from [al-Ma'rur] ibn Suwayd, from Abu Dharr, who said: I came to the Messenger of God (ﷺ) while he was in front of the Ka'ba. When he saw me approaching, he said: "They are the greatest losers, by the Lord of the Ka'ba. They are the greatest losers, by the Lord of the Ka'ba. They are the greatest losers, by the Lord of the Ka'ba."

He said: Grief entered me, and I could hardly breathe. I said: "Has something happened concerning me?" I said: "Who are they, may my father and mother be your ransom?" He said: "The ones with much wealth, except those who spend wealth in the ways of God's servants like this and like this, to his right, his left, above him, and in front of him, and from [.........] [Illegible text in the original.] Every gold and silver that its owner has kept back is hoarding [.........] [Illegible text in the original.] Whoever leaves the good of something, it will be his on the Day of Resurrection." [Musnad Ahmad: 2/309, with variation and without the end of the hadith.]

Talha ibn 'Abd Allah ibn Kurayz al-Khuza'i narrated from Abu al-Dayf, from Abu Hurayra, who said: "Whoever leaves ten thousand dirhams, they will be made into plates with which its owner will be punished on the Day of Resurrection before the judgment."

And from Salman ibn Thawaran, who said: I heard 'Ammar ibn Yasir say: "The People of the Table asked for a table, then it was sent down, and they disbelieved in it. The people of Salih asked for the she-camel, and when they were given it, they disbelieved in it. You have been forbidden to hoard gold and silver, yet you will hoard them." A man said: "Shall we hoard them while we have heard His saying?" He said: "Yes, and some of you will kill others over it."

Shu'ba said: The ring of Abu Hurayra's sword was of silver, and Abu Dharr forbade him from it, saying: The Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: "Whoever leaves gold and silver, he will be branded with them." [11] [Tafsir al-Tabari: 10/153.]

Qatada narrated from Shahr ibn Hawshab, from Abu Umama Suday ibn 'Ajlan, who said: A man from the People of the Bench (*ahl al-suffa*) died, and a dinar was found in his loincloth. The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "A brand." Then another man died, and two dinars were found in his loincloth. He (peace be upon him) said: "Two brands." [12] [Tafsir al-Tabari: 10/154.]

The most correct of the opinions is the first, because the threat is directed at withholding zakat, not at gathering lawful wealth.

This is supported by the saying of the Prophet (ﷺ): "Whoever pays the zakat of his wealth has paid the right that is upon him, and whoever gives more, it is better for him." [Al-Jami' al-Saghir of al-Suyuti: 2/560, no. 836.]

He (ﷺ) also said: "How excellent is righteous wealth for a righteous man." [13] [Kashf al-Khafa' of al-'Ajluni: 2/320, no. 2823.]

Ibn 'Umar was asked about this verse and said: "Whoever hoards it and does not pay its zakat, woe to him." Then he said: "I would not mind if I had wealth equal to Mount Uhud in gold, whose number I know, which I would pay zakat on and use in obedience to God, Mighty and Majestic."

As for the basic meaning of *kanz* (hoarding) in the speech of the Arabs: it is anything gathered, some of it upon other parts of it, whether on the surface of the earth or within it. This is shown by the saying of the poet:

"No good to me if I feed my guests [...] while I have gold hoarded."
[Lisan al-'Arab: 4/55, and al-Sihah: 6/2308.]

He meant: gathered, some of it upon the rest. *Al-Hatiy* is the fruit of the doum palm. Likewise the Arabs say of a gathered thing: *maknaz*, because its parts are pressed together.

Yahya ibn 'Umar read *yaknuzuna* with a *damma* on the *nun*, while the common reading is with a *kasra*. Both are dialects, like *ya'kufuna* and *ya'kufuna*, and *ya'rishuna* and *ya'rushuna*.

*Wa la yunfiquna fi sabil Allah*: he did not say *fa-yunfiquunahuma* (their both). The grammarians differed about this. Qutrub said: it means the zakat, or the hoards, or [.....] [An unclear word in the original.] gold and silver. Al-Farra' said: it dispensed with the one in the pronoun referring to the other, because the context shows that the statement about one applies to the other, as the statement about the one is the same as about the other. This exists in Arabic speech and reports. The poet said:

"We are content with what we have, and you with what you have, though our opinions differ."
[Mughni al-Labib: 2/622. Lisan al-'Arab: 3/360. This verse is attributed to Qays ibn al-'Azim, one of the great poets of the pre-Islamic period. See Sharh Ibn 'Aqil: 1/244, footnote.]

Ibn al-Anbari said: the intended reference is to the more prevalent and general, because silver is more general and gold is more specific. Like His saying, ﴿And seek help through patience and prayer, and indeed it is a great thing﴾ [2:45], where the pronoun refers to prayer because it is more general. And His saying, ﴿When they saw a trade or a diversion, they dispersed toward it﴾ [62:11], where the pronoun refers to trade because it is more general and more excellent.

﴿So give them good tidings﴾, that is, inform them and warn them, ﴿of a painful punishment, on a day when it will be heated in the fire of Hell﴾, that is, it will enter the Fire, the treasures being made red-hot. From this one says: "I heated the iron in the fire." ﴿And their foreheads will be branded therewith﴾, the foreheads of those who hoard, ﴿and their sides and their backs﴾.

'Abd Allah ibn Mas'ud said: "By Him other than whom there is no god, no man who hoards will be branded on the place of a dinar on a dinar or a dirham on a dirham. Rather, his skin will be widened and each dinar and dirham placed upon his two cheeks."

Abu Bakr al-Warraq was asked: Why were the foreheads, sides, and backs singled out for branding? He said: Because the rich man who owns hoarded wealth shrinks when he sees the poor man. When he gathers with him in one assembly, he turns away from him and turns his back to him. Muhammad ibn 'Ali al-Tirmidhi said: That is because he exults and is arrogant with his wealth, and he leans upon his hoard with his sides and reclines against it.

Al-Ahnaf ibn Qays said: I came to Medina, and while I was in a circle containing a group of the Quraysh, a man came, rough of clothing, rough of body, rough of face. He stood over them and said: "Give glad tidings to the hoarders of a heated stone (*radf*) to be heated in the fire of Hell, which will be placed on the nipple of one of them until it comes out from the top of his shoulder blade, and it will be placed on the top of his shoulder blade until it comes out from the nipples of his two breasts, and it will shake, and it will brand the foreheads, sides, and backs until the heat meets in their bellies."

[Note: *radf* means stones on the surface of the earth that have been heated (Lisan al-'Arab: 9/121).]

He said: The people lowered their heads, and I did not see any one of them respond to him with anything. He said: He turned away, and I followed him until he sat by a pillar. I said: "I did not see these people except that they disliked what you said to them." He said: "These people do not understand anything." [Jami' al-Bayan of al-Tabari: 10/160. Sahih Ibn Hibban: 8/51.]

﴿This is what you hoarded for yourselves﴾, that is, it will be said to them: "This is what you hoarded for yourselves," like His saying, ﴿As for those whose faces turn black: "Did you disbelieve after your belief? Taste the punishment for what you used to deny"﴾ [3:106]. That is, you denied God's rights in your wealth and withheld them.

The scholars differed about the ruling of this verse and about who it was revealed concerning. Ibn Shihab narrated from Khalid ibn Zayd ibn Aslam, from Ibn 'Umar, who was asked about the verse ﴿Those who hoard gold and silver﴾, and Ibn 'Umar said: "This was before zakat was revealed. When it was revealed, God made it a purification of wealth."

Mujahid narrated from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: When this verse was revealed, it was difficult for the Muslims, and they said: "None of us can leave for his child wealth that he will not leave behind." 'Umar (may God be pleased with him) said: "I will relieve you of this, so go." 'Umar set out, and Thawban followed him. He came to the Prophet (ﷺ) and said: "O Prophet of God, this has been difficult for your Companions." He said: "God, Mighty and Majestic, did not enjoin zakat except to purify what remains of your wealth, and He enjoined inheritance on wealth that will remain after you." Then he said: "Shall I not tell you the best thing a man can hoard? A righteous wife: when he looks at her, she pleases him; when he commands her, she obeys him; and when he is absent from her, she guards him." [Sunan Abi Dawud: 1/375.] [14]

Some Companions said: It refers specifically to the People of the Book. Al-Suddi said: It refers to the People of the Qibla (the Muslims). Al-Dahhak said: It is general, covering the People of the Book and the Muslims. Whoever earns lawful wealth but does not give God's right from it, it is a hoard, even if it is little and above the surface of the earth. And what has had God's right given from it is not a hoard, even if it is much and buried in the earth.

Zayd ibn Wahb narrated: I passed by al-Rabadha and found Abu Dharr, so I said to him: "What brought you to this place?" He said: "I was in Syria, and I disagreed with Mu'awiya about this verse, ﴿And those who hoard﴾, the verse. Mu'awiya said: It was revealed concerning the People of the Book. I said: It was revealed concerning us and them. There was an argument between me and them about it, so he wrote to 'Uthman (may God be pleased with him) complaining about me. 'Uthman wrote to me to come to Medina. I came to Medina, and the people crowded around me as if they had not seen me before. I mentioned that to 'Uthman, and he said: 'If you wish, you may withdraw and stay nearby.' That is what brought me to this place. If they had appointed me over an army, I would have listened and obeyed."

Some said: It was revealed specifically concerning those who withhold zakat, and this is the most sound of the opinions. It is supported by what Suhayl narrated from his father, from Abu Hurayra, who said: The Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: "No owner of hoarded wealth who does not pay its zakat will have it heated for him in the fire of Hell, and plates will be made of it, and his forehead and his sides will be branded with them, until God judges between His servants on a day whose length is fifty thousand years. Then he will be sent either to Paradise or to the Fire. No owner of sheep who does not pay their zakat will have them spread for him on a level plain, as large as they ever were, and they will trample him with their hooves and gore him with their horns, having neither a bent horn nor a broken horn. Whenever the last of them passes over him, the first of them returns to him, until God judges between His servants on a day whose length is fifty thousand years. Then he will be sent either to Paradise or to the Fire. No owner of camels who does not pay their zakat will have them spread for him on a level plain, as large as they ever were [.........] [Unreadable text in the manuscript.] Whenever the last of them passes over him, the first of them returns to him, until God judges between His servants on a day whose length is fifty thousand years. Then he will be sent either to Paradise or to the Fire." [15] [Musnad Ahmad: 2/262, with slight variation.] Suhayl said: "I do not know whether he mentioned cattle or not."

Thawban narrated that the Prophet (ﷺ) used to say: "Whoever leaves behind him a hoard, it will be presented to him on the Day of Resurrection as a bald poisonous serpent with two black spots on its head. It will follow him, saying: 'Woe to you, what are you?' He will say: 'I am your hoard that you left behind you.' It will not cease following him until it reaches his hand and bites it, then it will swallow the rest of his body." [16] [Tafsir al-Tabari: 10/160, Musnad Ahmad: 2/156, 279, with variation, and Kitab al-Musnad of al-Shafi'i: 87.]

﴿Indeed, the number of months﴾, meaning the number of months of the year, ﴿with God is twelve﴾. The common reading is with a *fatha* on the *ayn* and the *shin*. Abu Ja'far read with a *sukun* on the *shin*, and Talha ibn Sulayman read with a *sukun* on the *shin*. *Shahran* (months) is in the accusative as a specification (*tamyiz*).

They are: Muharram, Safar, Rabi' al-Awwal, Rabi' al-Akhir, Jumada al-Ula, Jumada al-Akhira, Rajab, Sha'ban, Ramadan, Shawwal, Dhu al-Qa'da, and Dhu al-Hijja.

As for Muharram, it was so named because fighting is forbidden in it. Safar was so named because Mecca becomes empty (*tasfaru*) of people in it, that is, it becomes deserted. It was also said: A plague occurred in it, and their faces turned yellow. Abu 'Ubayda said: Safar was so named because they emptied (*safarat*) their waterskins of milk in it. The two Rabi'es were so named because water freezes in them.
