Its origin is that the giver extends his hand and spreads it with goodness, so it is said of one who is stingy and withholds: "He has withheld his hand." From this is His saying: ﴿And the Jews say: "The hand of God is chained"﴾, meaning withheld from spending.

﴿They forgot God, so He forgot them﴾: they abandoned obedience to God, so God abandoned them, withdrawing His success and guidance in this world and His saving mercy from His punishment and His fire in the next. ﴿Indeed the hypocrites are the defiantly disobedient.﴾ ﴿God has promised the hypocrite men and women and the disbelievers the fire of Hell, abiding eternally therein. It is sufficient for them.﴾ That is, sufficient for them as punishment and recompense for their disbelief. ﴿God has cursed them﴾, meaning expelled them and removed them far from His mercy. ﴿And for them is a lasting punishment.﴾

﴿Like those before you﴾: meaning you have done as those before you did, and you have been cursed and punished just as the ones before you were cursed, namely the disbelievers of the earlier nations. ﴿They were stronger than you in might﴾, in force and in defence, ﴿and more abundant in wealth and children. They enjoyed their portion﴾, meaning they enjoyed and benefited from their share of this world, and were content with it in exchange for the Hereafter.

Abu Hurayrah said: *al-khalaq* means religion. ﴿So you have enjoyed your portion as those before you enjoyed theirs, and you have plunged into falsehood and lying about God, denying His messengers and mocking the believers, like those who plunged﴾. He meant "like those who plunged." This is because *alladhi* is a defective noun, like *ma* and *man*, used to refer to the singular and the plural, similar to His saying: ﴿Their likeness is that of one who kindled a fire...﴾ and then He said: ﴿God took away their light and left them in darknesses﴾ [[Surah al-Baqarah: 17.]]. The poet said:

*Indeed those whose blood was spilled at Falj*
*Are the people, all of the people, O Umm Khalid.* [[Kitab al-ʿAyn of al-Farahidi: 8/209. The verse is by al-Ashhab ibn Zumayla, as in the margin of al-Sahah of al-Jawhari: 1/335.]]

If you wish, you may make *alladhi* refer to a pronoun, and His saying ﴿you have plunged﴾ is like the plunging in which they plunged, up to His saying ﴿the losers﴾.

Abu Hurayrah narrated from the Prophet ﷺ: "You will certainly follow the path of the nations before you, a cubit for a cubit, a span for a span, and a fathom for a fathom, until if one of those had entered a lizard's burrow, you would enter it too." Abu Hurayrah said: "Recite, if you wish: ﴿Like those before you, who were stronger than you in might...﴾ the verse." They said: "O Messenger of God, like what Persia and Rome and the People of the Book did?" He said: "And who are the people other than them?" [[Tafsir al-Tabari: 10/225, and Musnad Abi Ya'la: 11/182.]] [26] [[Musnad Abi Ya'la: 11/182.]].

Ibn ʿAbbas said concerning this verse: "How similar tonight is to yesterday! These are the Children of Israel; we are likened to them." Ibn Mas'ud said: "You are the nation most similar to the Children of Israel in manner and guidance; you follow their deeds exactly, step by step, feather by feather, except that I do not know whether you will worship the calf or not" [[Majma' al-Zawa'id: 7/261. Ibn Mas'ud narrated it from the Prophet (ﷺ).]].

Hudhayfah said: "The hypocrites among you today are worse than the hypocrites who were in the time of the Prophet ﷺ." We said: "And how?" He said: "Those used to conceal their hypocrisy, but these have made it public."

Commentary of al-Tha'alibi (al-Jawahir al-Hisan) on surah 9, verses 70–72:

﴿Has there not come to them⦆ meaning the hypocrites and the disbelievers, ﴿the news⦆ (naba') ﴿of those before them⦆ when they disobeyed Our messengers and opposed Our command, how We destroyed them and punished them. Then he mentioned them, saying: ﴿the people of Noah⦆ as an apposition, in meaning, to those who were destroyed by the flood; ﴿and ʿAd⦆, who were destroyed by the wind; ﴿and Thamud⦆, who were destroyed by the earthquake; ﴿and the people of Abraham⦆, by the removal of blessing and the destruction of Nimrod; ﴿and the companions of Madyan⦆, meaning the people of Shuʿayb, by the punishment of the Day of the Canopy; ﴿and the overturned cities⦆, the overturned settlements whose upper part He made their lower part, and they are the people of Lot. ﴿Their messengers came to them with clear proofs⦆, but they denied them and disobeyed them, just as you have done, O company of disbelievers, so beware lest the vengeance hasten upon you. ﴿So Allah would not have wronged them⦆ up to His saying ﴿some of them are allies of others⦆ in religion, community, help, support, love and mercy.

Jarir ibn ʿAbdullah said: I heard the Prophet (ﷺ) say: "The Emigrants and the Helpers are allies of one another in this world and the Hereafter, and the freed captives of Quraysh and the freed captives of Thaqif are allies of one another in this world and the Hereafter." [27] [[al-Mustadrak: 4/81.]]

﴿They enjoin what is right⦆ with faith and goodness, ﴿and forbid what is wrong⦆, that which is not recognised in the Law or the Sunnah.

Abu al-ʿAliyah said: Whenever Allah mentions "enjoining what is right" in His Book, it means returning from polytheism to Islam, and "forbidding what is wrong" means forbidding the worship of idols and Satan. ﴿And they establish prayer⦆, the prescribed prayer, ﴿and obey Allah and His Messenger⦆. Those up to His saying ﴿and pleasant dwellings⦆, and goodly abodes.

al-Hasan said: I asked Abu Hurayrah and ʿImran ibn Husayn about the words of Allah ﴿and pleasant dwellings in Gardens of Eden⦆. They said: "You have asked one who knows. We asked the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) about that, and he said: 'A palace in Paradise of pearls, in which are seventy houses of red ruby, in each house seventy chambers of green emerald, in each chamber seventy beds, on each bed seventy mattresses, on each mattress a wife of the wide-eyed houris, and in each chamber a table, and on each table seventy kinds of food, and in each chamber a maidservant, and the believer will be given strength in a single morning sufficient for all of that.'" [28] [[Majmaʿ al-Zawaʾid: 3/141.]]

﴿In Gardens of Eden⦆: in orchards of shade and abode. It is said: "ʿadana bi-al-makan" when one stays in a place, and from it comes the word *maʿdin* (mine).

The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "ʿAdan is the abode of Allah which no eye has seen and which has not occurred to the heart of any human; none dwells in it except three: of the Prophets, the Truthful ones, and the Martyrs. Allah says: 'Blessed is whoever enters you.'" [29]

ʿAbdullah ibn Masʿud said: It is the middle of Paradise (*bitnan al-jannah*), that is, its centre. Ibn ʿAbbas said: I asked Kaʿb about the Gardens of Eden, and he said: They are the vineyards and grapes, in Syriac. [[Tafsir al-Tabari: 10/230.]] ʿAbdullah ibn ʿUmar said: Indeed in Paradise there is a palace called ʿAdan, around it are the towers and meadows, it has five thousand doors, and at every door is a *ḥabrah* (a delight); none enters it except a prophet, a truthful one, or a martyr.

al-Hasan said: "Gardens of Eden; and what will make you know what the Gardens of Eden are?" A palace of gold which none enters except a prophet, a truthful one, a martyr, or a just ruler, and he raised his voice with it. [In another narration: a palace] in Paradise called ʿAdan, around it are towers and meadows, it has fifty thousand doors. al-Dahhak said: It is the city of Paradise, in which are the Messengers, the Prophets, the martyrs and the leaders of guidance, and the people are around them, and the gardens are around it.

ʿAta' ibn al-Sa'ib said: ʿAdan is a river in Paradise, its gardens on its two banks. Muqatil and al-Kalbi said: It is the highest rank in Paradise, and in it is the spring of Tasnim, and the gardens surround it, encircling it, and it has been covered since the day Allah created it until its people, the Prophets, the truthful ones, the martyrs, the righteous, and whomever Allah wills, descend into it. In it are palaces of pearl, ruby and gold; a pleasant wind blows from beneath the Throne and enters upon them with the sweetest heaps of musk. ʿAta' al-Khurasani said regarding His words ﴿and pleasant dwellings in Gardens of Eden⦆: a palace of chrysolite, pearl and ruby whose fragrance wafts from a distance of five hundred years, in the Gardens of Eden; it is the capital of Paradise, and its ceiling is the Throne of the Most Merciful.

﴿And the pleasure of Allah is greater⦆: it is in the nominative as a beginning (*mubtada'*), meaning the pleasure of Allah with them is greater than all of that.

Malik ibn Anas narrated from Zayd ibn Aslam, from ʿAta' ibn Yasar, from Abu Sa'id al-Khudri, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Allah says to the people of Paradise: 'O people of Paradise!' They say: 'Here we are, our Lord, at Your service.' He says: 'Are you pleased?' They say: 'And why would we not be pleased, when You have given us what You have not given anyone of Your creation?' He says: 'Shall I not tell you of something better than that?' They say: 'And what is better than that?' He says: 'I shall let My pleasure descend upon you, and I shall never be displeased with you after it, ever.'" [30] [[Musnad Ahmad: 3/88.]]

﴿That is the great triumph.⦆

**Commentary of al-Tha'labi (al-Jawahir al-Hisan) on Surah 9, verses 73–74:**

﴿O Prophet, strive against the disbelievers with the sword and fighting, and against the hypocrites.﴾

They differed about the manner of striving against the hypocrites. Ibn Mas'ud said: "With the hand. If one cannot, then with the tongue. If one cannot, then with the heart. If one cannot, then frown (iktafhara) in their face." Ibn 'Abbas said: "With the tongue, and by severe rebuke through harsh speech." al-Hasan and Qatada said: "By establishing the legal punishments (hudud) upon them."

Then He said: ﴿Their refuge is Hell, and wretched is the destination.﴾ [Ibn Mas'ud and Ibn 'Abbas] said: "This verse abrogated (naskh) everything of pardon, reconciliation and forgiveness."

﴿They swear by Allah that they did not say [it].﴾

Ibn 'Abbas said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was sitting in the shade of a tree, and he said: "A man will come to you who looks at you with the eye of a devil. When he comes, do not speak to him." Not long after, a man with blue eyes appeared, and the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) called him and said: "Why do you and your companions revile me?" The man went off and brought his companions, and they swore by Allah that they had not said it. So Allah, the Exalted, revealed this verse. [Tafsir al-Tabari: 10/237.]

al-Dahhak said: The hypocrites went out with the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) to Tabuk, and whenever some of them were alone with one another, they reviled the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and his companions and attacked the religion. Hudhayfah conveyed what they had said to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and the Prophet said: "O people of hypocrisy, what is this that has reached me about you?" [31] They swore to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) that they had said nothing of that kind, so Allah, the Exalted, revealed this verse as a refutation of them. [Asbab al-Nuzul of al-Wahidi: 169.]

al-Kalbi said: It was revealed concerning al-Jullas ibn Suwayd ibn al-Samit. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) delivered a sermon one day at Tabuk, mentioned the hypocrites, called them filth and denounced them. al-Jullas said: "By Allah, if Muhammad is truthful in what he says, then we are worse than donkeys." 'Amir ibn Qays heard him and said: "Indeed, by Allah, Muhammad is truthful and believed, and you are worse than donkeys."

When the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) returned to Medina, 'Amir ibn Qays came to him and informed him of what al-Jullas had said. al-Jullas said: "He lied against me, O Messenger of Allah; I said nothing of that." The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) ordered that the two of them swear at the pulpit after the afternoon prayer. Al-Jullas swore by Allah, besides whom there is no god, that he had not said it, and that 'Amir had lied against him. Then 'Amir stood and swore by Allah, besides whom there is no god, that he had indeed said it and had not lied against him. Then 'Amir raised his hands to the sky and said: "O Allah, send down upon Your Prophet, who is truthful and believed by us." The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and the believers said: "Amen." Then Jibril came down to the Prophet (ﷺ) before they had separated, with this verse, up to ﴿But if they repent, it will be better for them﴾. Al-Jullas stood up and said: "O Messenger of Allah, I hear that Allah has offered me repentance. 'Amir ibn Qays was right about that. I said it, and I seek Allah's forgiveness and turn to Him in repentance." The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) accepted that from him, and then he repented and his repentance was good.

Qatada said: We were told that two men fought, one a man of Juhayna and the other a man of Ghifar. Juhayna were allies of the Ansar. The Ghifari overcame the Juhayni, and 'Abd Allah ibn Ubayy called out: "O (tribe of) al-Aws, support your brother! By Allah, our case and Muhammad's is only like the saying: 'Fatten your dog and it will devour you.'"

He then said: ﴿If we return to Medina, the mightier will surely expel the meaner from it.﴾ A man among the Muslims reported this to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), who sent for him, and he began to swear by Allah that he had not said it. So Allah, Mighty and Majestic, revealed: ﴿They swear by Allah that they did not say [it], but they certainly uttered the word of disbelief and disbelieved after their submission.﴾

Mujahid said: They were the hypocrites who transmitted the statement of the believer who said "we are worse than donkeys," so that he would not disclose it against them.

al-Suddi said: They said, "When we reach Medina, we will place a crown on the head of 'Abd Allah ibn Ubayy, to boast of him to [...........] [an unreadable word] him."

al-Kalbi said: They were fifteen men, among them 'Abd Allah ibn Ubayy, 'Abd Allah ibn Sa'd ibn Abi Sarh, Ta'mah ibn Ubayriq, al-Jullas ibn Suwayd, 'Amir ibn al-Nu'man and Abu al-Ahwas. They resolved to kill the Prophet (ﷺ) during the expedition to Tabuk, and Jibril informed the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) of this. It was also said that they were from Quraysh, who resolved to kill the Prophet (ﷺ), but Allah, Mighty and Majestic, prevented him.

Jabir reported from Mujahid, from Ibn 'Abbas (may Allah be pleased with him), concerning this verse, that he said: A man of Quraysh called al-Aswad resolved to kill the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). ﴿And they found fault with him only because Allah and His Messenger had enriched them from His bounty.﴾ [They did not] resent him, [i.e.] they did not disapprove of him, and they did not [resent] except that. [It is said that] the slain man was a freedman of al-Jullas, and he was killed. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) ordered that his blood-money be twelve thousand [dirhams], and so they became wealthy.

al-Kalbi said: Before the Prophet (ﷺ) arrived, they were in hardship in their livelihood, not riding horses and not acquiring booty. When the Prophet (ﷺ) arrived, they became wealthy through the spoils.

This is a well-known saying: "Beware of the one to whom you have shown kindness."

Then Allah, Mighty and Majestic, said: ﴿So if they repent﴾ from their hypocrisy and disbelief, ﴿it will be better for them. But if they turn away﴾ from faith, ﴿Allah will punish them with a painful punishment in this world﴾ by killing and disgrace, ﴿and in the Hereafter﴾ with the Fire. ﴿And they will have no protector or helper on earth.﴾

**Commentary of al-Tha'labi (al-Jawahir al-Hisan) on Surah 9, verses 73–74:**

﴿O Prophet, strive against the disbelievers with the sword and fighting, and against the hypocrites.﴾

They differed about the manner of striving against the hypocrites. Ibn Mas'ud said: "With the hand. If one cannot, then with the tongue. If one cannot, then with the heart. If one cannot, then frown (iktafhara) in their face." Ibn 'Abbas said: "With the tongue, and by severe rebuke through harsh speech." al-Hasan and Qatada said: "By establishing the legal punishments (hudud) upon them."

Then He said: ﴿Their refuge is Hell, and wretched is the destination.﴾ [Ibn Mas'ud and Ibn 'Abbas] said: "This verse abrogated (naskh) everything of pardon, reconciliation and forgiveness."

﴿They swear by Allah that they did not say [it].﴾

Ibn 'Abbas said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was sitting in the shade of a tree, and he said: "A man will come to you who looks at you with the eye of a devil. When he comes, do not speak to him." Commentary of al-Tha'alibi (al-Jawahir al-Hisan) on surah 9, verses 75–78:

Wa minhum man ʿahada Allah (the verse)

Al-Qasim ibn ʿAbd al-Rahman narrated from Abu Umama al-Bahili, who said: Thaʿlaba ibn Hatib al-Ansari came to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and said: "O Messenger of Allah, pray to Allah that He grant me wealth." The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Woe to you, O Thaʿlaba! A little that you can give thanks for is better than a lot that you cannot bear." Then he came to him again after that and said: "O Messenger of Allah, pray to Allah that He grant me wealth." The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Lakum fi Rasul Allah uswa hasana" [﴿You have in the Messenger of Allah an excellent example﴾], "and by Him in whose hand my soul is, if you wished that the mountains would move with me as gold and silver, they would." Then he came to him after that and said: "O Messenger of Allah, pray to Allah that He grant me wealth. By Him who sent you with the truth, if Allah grants me wealth I will surely give every person with a right his right." The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "O Allah, grant Thaʿlaba wealth." [32]

He said: So he acquired sheep, and they multiplied as worms multiply, so the city became too narrow for him, and he moved away from it and settled in one of its valleys, and they kept multiplying as worms multiply. He used to pray the Zuhr prayer with the Prophet (ﷺ), and he prayed the other prayers with his sheep. Then they increased and multiplied until he was far from Madina, so that he attended only the Friday prayer. Then they increased and multiplied further, and he moved further away, until he would attend neither the Friday prayer nor the congregation. Whenever it was Friday, he would pass by the people and ask them for news. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) mentioned him, and one day he asked: "What has Thaʿlaba done?" They said: "O Messenger of Allah, Thaʿlaba has acquired sheep that no valley can contain."

The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Woe to Thaʿlaba! Woe to Thaʿlaba! Woe to Thaʿlaba!" Then Allah revealed the verse of charity (zakat). The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) sent a man from Banu Sulaym and a man from Juhayna, and he wrote for them the instructions on collecting charity and how they should take it. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said to them: "Pass by Thaʿlaba ibn Hatib and a man from Banu Sulaym, and take their charities."

So the two set out until they came to Thaʿlaba, asked him for the charity, and read to him the letter of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). He said: "This is nothing but a jizya (poll tax); this is nothing but a sister of the jizya. Go on until you finish, then return to me." So they went on. The Sulami heard of them, so he looked at the best of the camels' ages, set them aside for the charity, and then met them with them. When he offered them, they said: "This is not required of you." He said: "Take it, for my soul is content with that." So they passed by the people and took the charities, then returned to Thaʿlaba, who said:

"Show me your letter." He read it and then said: "This is nothing but a jizya, this is nothing but a sister of the jizya. Go away until I see my opinion." So they set out. When the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) saw them coming, before they spoke he said: "Woe to Thaʿlaba! Woe to Thaʿlaba! Woe to Thaʿlaba!" Then he prayed good for the Sulami. They informed him of what Thaʿlaba had done, and Allah revealed concerning him: ﴿And among them are those who made a covenant with Allah: "If He gives us of His bounty, we will surely give charity..."﴾ up to His words ﴿...and because they used to lie﴾. A relative of Thaʿlaba was with the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and he heard this, so he went out and came to him and said: "Woe to you, O Thaʿlaba! Allah the Mighty and Majestic has revealed such-and-such about you." Thaʿlaba went out and came to the Prophet (ﷺ) and asked him to accept his charity.

He said: "Allah has forbidden me to accept your charity." So Thaʿlaba began throwing dust on his head. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said to him: "This is your deed; I commanded you, but you did not obey me." [33] When the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) passed away, he returned to his home, and the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) died without having accepted anything from him. Then he came to Abu Bakr (may Allah be pleased with him) when he became caliph and said: "You know my standing with the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and my position among the Ansar, so accept my charity." Abu Bakr said: "The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) did not accept it from you, and shall I accept it?" So he did not accept it. Abu Bakr died without accepting it. When ʿUmar (may Allah be pleased with him) became caliph, he came to him and said: "O Commander of the Faithful, accept my charity." He said: "The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) did not accept it from you, nor did Abu Bakr. I will not accept it." ʿUmar died without accepting it. Then ʿUthman became caliph, and he came to him and asked him to accept his charity. He said: "The Messenger of Allah did not accept it from you, nor did Abu Bakr or ʿUmar. I will not accept it from you." So he did not accept it from him, and he died during the caliphate of ʿUthman. [[Full version in Tafsir al-Tabari: 10/242, and Usd al-Ghaba: 1/238.]]

Ibn ʿAbbas, Saʿid ibn Jubayr and Qatada said: Thaʿlaba came to a gathering of the Ansar and called them to witness, saying: "If Allah grants me of His bounty, I will give every person with a right his right, I will give charity from it, and I will maintain the ties of kinship." Then a paternal cousin of his died and left him wealth, but he did not fulfill what he had said. So Allah revealed this verse.

Muqatil said: Thaʿlaba passed by the Ansar while he was in need, and said: "If Allah grants me of His bounty, I will surely give charity and surely be among the righteous." Then Allah granted him of His bounty. The reason was that a client of ʿUmar ibn al-Khattab had killed a man from the hypocrites by mistake, and the Prophet (ﷺ) gave his blood-money to Thaʿlaba, who was a relative of the one killed. He was stingy and withheld the right of Allah, so Allah revealed this verse.

Al-Hasan and Mujahid said: This verse was revealed concerning Thaʿlaba ibn Hatib and Muʿattib ibn Qushayr, two men from Banu ʿAmr ibn ʿAwf, who went out among a group sitting together and said: "By Allah, if Allah provides for us, we will surely give charity." When Allah provided for them, they became stingy.

Al-Dahhak said: It was revealed concerning men among the hypocrites: [Nabtal] ibn al-Harith, Jadd ibn Qays, Thaʿlaba ibn Hatib, and Muʿattib ibn Qushayr. They said: ﴿If Allah gives us of His bounty, we will surely give charity﴾... ﴿So when He gave them of His bounty, they became stingy with it and withheld zakat.﴾

Al-Kalbi said: It was revealed concerning Hatib ibn Abi Balta'a. He had wealth in Syria and struggled greatly for it, so he swore by Allah: "If Allah gives us of His bounty, of His provision, meaning the wealth that is in Syria, I will surely give charity from it, I will maintain ties, and I will surely give Allah's right from it." Then Allah gave him that wealth, but he did not do what he had said. So Allah the Mighty and Majestic revealed: ﴿And among them, meaning among the hypocrites, are those who made a covenant with Allah: "If He gives us of His bounty, we will surely give charity and surely pay Allah's right from it, and we will surely be among the righteous"﴾, i.e., that we act as the righteous act with their wealth, by maintaining kinship and spending in good causes. ﴿So when He gave them of His bounty, they became stingy with it, and turned away while they were averse﴾; ﴿so He caused to follow﴾, i.e., He followed them with it; and it was said: ﴿He repaid them for their stinginess.﴾ Al-Nabigha said:

"Whoever obeys you, benefit him by his obedience, as he obeyed you, and guide him to right guidance." [[Tarikh Dimashq: 35/426.]]

﴿Hypocrisy in their hearts until the Day they meet Him﴾: Allah deprived them of repentance. ﴿Because they broke to Allah what they had promised Him, and because they used to lie.﴾ Ma'bad ibn Thabit said: It is only something [apparent] in their souls which they did not speak. Have you not heard the words of Allah the Mighty and Majestic: ﴿Do they not know that Allah knows their secret and their private talk, and that Allah is the Knower of the unseen?﴾

From Masruq, from Abdullah ibn Umar, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Whoever has four traits is a pure hypocrite, and whoever has one of them has a trait of hypocrisy until he abandons it: when he speaks he lies, when he promises he breaks it, when he makes a covenant he betrays it, and when he disputes he acts wickedly." [34] [[Sahih al-Bukhari: 1/14.]]

Al-Ashʿath from al-Hasan, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Whoever has three traits is a hypocrite, even if he prays, fasts, and claims to be a believer: when he speaks he lies, when he promises he breaks it, and when he is entrusted he betrays." [35]

ʿAbdullah ibn Masʿud said: Consider the hypocrite by three signs: when he speaks he lies, when he promises he breaks it, and when he makes a covenant he betrays it. Allah revealed the confirmation of this in His Book: ﴿And among them are those who made a covenant with Allah﴾ up to His words ﴿because they used to lie.﴾ This report is difficult in its apparent meaning; whoever does not know its interpretation, his error and his explanation will be great.

My teacher al-Hasan ibn Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Jaʿfar informed me, saying: My father informed me from my grandfather al-Husayn ibn Jaʿfar, who said: Muhammad ibn Yazid al-Sulami narrated to us, saying: ʿAmmar ibn Qirat narrated to us from Bukayr ibn Maʿruf from Muqatil ibn Hayyan, who said: I was in charge of judgeship in Samarqand. One day I read the hadith of al-Maqburi from Abu Hurayra from the Prophet (ﷺ): "Whoever has three traits is a hypocrite: when he speaks he lies, when he is entrusted he betrays, and when he promises he breaks it." [36]

My thoughts became confused, my heart was divided, I feared for myself and for all people, and I said: Who will be saved from these traits? So I neglected the judgeship and came to Bukhara and asked its scholars, but found no relief. I came to Marw and found no relief. I came to Nishapur and found no relief with its scholars. Then I heard that Shahr ibn Hawshab was in Jurjan, so I went to him, presented my matter to him, and asked about the report. He said to me: "When I heard this report, I was like a grain on a frying pan out of fear [[A simile; a maqla is a copper or other vessel in which food is fried.]]. Go and seek Saʿid ibn Jubayr, for he has settled in al-Rayy. Perhaps you will find for me and for you; I have heard that he has relief." So I went to al-Rayy, sought Saʿid, came to him, presented the matter to him, and asked him about the meaning of the report.

He said: "I have been fearful for myself since this report reached me, and I fear for you and for myself from these traits. I have endured and suffered a long journey and trials. So go to al-Hasan al-Basri, for I hope you will find with him relief for me, for you, and for the Muslims." I came to Basra, sought al-Hasan, and related the whole story to him. He said: "May Allah have mercy on Shahr, he has reached half of the report and not the other half. When the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said this report, it preoccupied the hearts of his companions, and they were too shy to ask him. So they came to Fatima and mentioned to her the preoccupation of their hearts with the report. Fatima (may Allah be pleased with her) went to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and informed him of the preoccupation of his companions. He commanded Salman, who called out: 'Prayer, gathered!' When they had gathered, he ascended the pulpit and said: 'O people, I did say: Whoever has three traits is a hypocrite: when he speaks he lies, when he is entrusted he betrays, and when he promises he breaks it. I did not mean you by it; I meant only the hypocrites. As for my saying: when he speaks he lies, the hypocrites came to me and said: By Allah, our faith is like your faith and the confirmation of our hearts is like the confirmation of your heart. So Allah the Mighty and Majestic revealed: ﴿When the hypocrites come to you, they say: We bear witness that you are the Messenger of Allah﴾ to the end of the verse. As for my saying: when he is entrusted he betrays, trust is the prayer, and the whole religion is a trust. Allah the Exalted said: ﴿Indeed, the hypocrites deceive Allah, and He is deceiving them. And when they stand up to prayer, they stand lazily, showing off to the people and not remembering Allah except a little.﴾ And concerning them He said: ﴿So woe to those who pray, who are heedless of their prayer.﴾ As for my saying: when he promises he breaks it, Thaʿlaba ibn Hatib came to me and said: 'I am poor, and I have a few sheep; pray to Allah that He bless them.' So I prayed, and they multiplied and increased until the roads became too narrow for them. Then I asked him for the charity, but he refused and withheld it. So Allah the Mighty and Majestic revealed: ﴿And among them are those who made a covenant with Allah﴾ to His words ﴿because they broke to Allah what they had promised Him.﴾'" [37]

The Companions of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) rejoiced, glorified Allah, and gave charity of great wealth. [[Full version in Tafsir al-Tabari: 10/244–245.]]

Al-Qasim ibn Bishr narrated from Usama, from Muhammad [al-Makhrami], who said: I heard al-Hasan say: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Whoever has three traits is a hypocrite, even if he fasts, prays, and claims to be a Muslim: when he speaks he lies, when he promises he breaks it, and when he is entrusted he betrays." [38] [[Sahih Muslim: 1/56.]] Then al-Hasan said: O Abu Saʿid, by Allah, if a man has a debt owed by me, and he meets me and demands it from me while I have nothing, and I fear that he will imprison me and destroy me, so I promise him that I will repay it at the new moon, and I do not do so, am I a hypocrite?! This is how the hadith has come.

Then he narrated from Abdullah ibn Amr that when his father was near death, he said: "Marry so-and-so, for I promised him that I would marry him. I do not want to meet Allah with a third of hypocrisy." I said: O Abu Saʿid, would a man have a third of him hypocritical and two-thirds believing? He said: This is how the hadith has come.

Muhammad said: So I performed the pilgrimage and met ʿAta' ibn Abi Rabah, and I informed him of the hadith I had heard from al-Hasan, and what I had said to him about the hypocrite, and what he had said to me. He said to me: "Were you unable to say to him: Tell me about the brothers of Joseph. Did they not promise their father and break it, and speak to him and lie to him, and was he trusted by them and they betrayed him? Were they hypocrites? Were they not prophets, when their father was a prophet and their grandfather was a prophet?"

I said to ʿAta': "O Abu Muhammad, tell me the origin of this hadith." He said: Jabir ibn Abdullah narrated to me that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said this hadith only concerning the hypocrites specifically, who spoke to the Prophet (ﷺ) and lied to him, were trusted with his secret and betrayed him, and promised him that they would go out with him to the expedition and broke it. He said: Abu Sufyan left Mecca, and Jibril came and said: "Abu Sufyan is in such-and-such a place." The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Abu Sufyan is in such-and-such a place; go out to him and keep it secret." A man from the hypocrites wrote to him: "Muhammad intends to send you forth." So Allah the Mighty and Majestic revealed: ﴿O you who believe, do not betray Allah and the Messenger, nor betray your trusts﴾ [[Surah al-Anfal: 27.]], and He revealed concerning the hypocrites: ﴿And among them are those who made a covenant with Allah: "If He gives us of His bounty..."﴾ to His words ﴿because they used to lie.﴾ He said: When you come to al-Hasan, convey my greetings to him and inform him of the origin of this hadith and what I said to you.

So I came to al-Hasan and said: "O Abu Saʿid, your brother Muhammad sends you his greetings," and I informed him of the hadith he had narrated. Al-Hasan took my hand and shook it, and said: "O people of Iraq, were you unable to be like this? He heard a hadith from us but did not accept it until he derived its origin. ʿAta' spoke the truth. This is how the hadith is: it concerns the hypocrites specifically." [[Full version in Tafsir al-Tabari: 10/245–246, no. 13215.]]

Commentary of al-Tha'alibi (al-Jawahir al-Hisan) on surah 9, verses 75–78:

Wa minhum man ʿahada Allah (the verse)

Then a paternal cousin of his died and left him wealth, but he did not fulfill what he had said. So Allah revealed this verse.

Muqatil said: Thaʿlaba passed by the Ansar while he was in need, and said: "If Allah grants me of His bounty, I will surely give charity and surely be among the righteous." Then Allah granted him of His bounty. The reason was that a client of ʿUmar ibn al-Khattab had killed a man from the hypocrites by mistake, and the Prophet (ﷺ) gave his blood-money to Thaʿlaba, who was a relative of the one killed. Al-Hasan and Mujahid said: This verse was revealed concerning Thaʿlaba ibn Hatib and Muʿattib ibn Qushayr, two men from Banu ʿAmr ibn ʿAwf, who went out among a group sitting together and said: "By Allah, if Allah provides for us, we will surely give charity." When Allah provided for them, they became stingy.

Al-Dahhak said: It was revealed concerning men among the hypocrites: [Nabtal] ibn al-Harith, Jadd ibn Qays, Thaʿlaba ibn Hatib, and Muʿattib ibn Qushayr. They said: ﴿If Allah gives us of His bounty, we will surely give charity﴾... ﴿So when He gave them of His bounty, they became stingy with it and withheld zakat.﴾

Al-Kalbi said: It was revealed concerning Hatib ibn Abi Balta'a. He had wealth in Syria and struggled greatly for it, so he swore by Allah: "If Allah gives us of His bounty, of His provision, meaning the wealth that is in Syria, I will surely give charity from it, I will maintain ties, and I will surely give Allah's right from it." Then Allah gave him that wealth, but he did not do what he had said. Have you not heard the words of Allah the Mighty and Majestic: ﴿Do they not know that Allah knows their secret and their private talk, and that Allah is the Knower of the unseen?﴾

[34] [[Sahih al-Bukhari: 1/14.]]

Al-Ashʿath from al-Hasan, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Whoever has three traits is a hypocrite, even if he prays, fasts, and claims to be a believer: when he speaks he lies, when he promises he breaks it, and when he is entrusted he betrays." [35]

ʿAbdullah ibn Masʿud said: Consider the hypocrite by three signs: when he speaks he lies, when he promises he breaks it, and when he makes a covenant he betrays it. Allah revealed the confirmation of this in His Book: ﴿And among them are those who made a covenant with Allah﴾ up to His words ﴿because they used to lie.﴾ This report is difficult in its apparent meaning; whoever does not know its interpretation, his error and his explanation will be great.

My teacher al-Hasan ibn Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Jaʿfar informed me, saying: My father informed me from my grandfather al-Husayn ibn Jaʿfar, who said: Muhammad ibn Yazid al-Sulami narrated to us, saying: ʿAmmar ibn Qirat narrated to us from Bukayr ibn Maʿruf from Muqatil ibn Hayyan, who said: I was in charge of judgeship in Samarqand. One day I read the hadith of al-Maqburi from Abu Hurayra from the Prophet (ﷺ): "Whoever has three traits is a hypocrite: when he speaks he lies, when he is entrusted he betrays, and when he promises he breaks it." [36]

My thoughts became confused, my heart was divided, I feared for myself and for all people, and I said: Who will be saved from these traits? So I neglected the judgeship and came to Bukhara and asked its scholars, but found no relief. I came to Marw and found no relief. I came to Nishapur and found no relief with its scholars. Then I heard that Shahr ibn Hawshab was in Jurjan, so I went to him, presented my matter to him, and asked about the report. He said to me: "When I heard this report, I was like a grain on a frying pan out of fear [[A simile; a maqla is a copper or other vessel in which food is fried.]]. He said: "I have been fearful for myself since this report reached me, and I fear for you and for myself from these traits. I have endured and suffered a long journey and trials. So I prayed, and they multiplied and increased until the roads became too narrow for them. Then I asked him for the charity, but he refused and withheld it. The Companions of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) rejoiced, glorified Allah, and gave charity of great wealth. [[Full version in Tafsir al-Tabari: 10/244–245.]]

[38] [[Sahih Muslim: 1/56.]] Then al-Hasan said: O Abu Saʿid, by Allah, if a man has a debt owed by me, and he meets me and demands it from me while I have nothing, and I fear that he will imprison me and destroy me, so I promise him that I will repay it at the new moon, and I do not do so, am I a hypocrite?! This is how the hadith has come.

Then he narrated from Abdullah ibn Amr that when his father was near death, he said: "Marry so-and-so, for I promised him that I would marry him. I do not want to meet Allah with a third of hypocrisy." I said: O Abu Saʿid, would a man have a third of him hypocritical and two-thirds believing? He said: This is how the hadith has come.

Muhammad said: So I performed the pilgrimage and met ʿAta' ibn Abi Rabah, and I informed him of the hadith I had heard from al-Hasan, and what I had said to him about the hypocrite, and what he had said to me. He said to me: "Were you unable to say to him: Tell me about the brothers of Joseph. Did they not promise their father and break it, and speak to him and lie to him, and was he trusted by them and they betrayed him? Were they hypocrites? Were they not prophets, when their father was a prophet and their grandfather was a prophet?"

I said to ʿAta': "O Abu Muhammad, tell me the origin of this hadith." He said: Jabir ibn Abdullah narrated to me that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said this hadith only concerning the hypocrites specifically, who spoke to the Prophet (ﷺ) and lied to him, were trusted with his secret and betrayed him, and promised him that they would go out with him to the expedition and broke it. He said: Abu Sufyan left Mecca, and Jibril came and said: "Abu Sufyan is in such-and-such a place." The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Abu Sufyan is in such-and-such a place; go out to him and keep it secret." A man from the hypocrites wrote to him: "Muhammad intends to send you forth." So Allah the Mighty and Majestic revealed: ﴿O you who believe, do not betray Allah and the Messenger, nor betray your trusts﴾ [[Surah al-Anfal: 27.]], and He revealed concerning the hypocrites: ﴿And among them are those who made a covenant with Allah: "If He gives us of His bounty..."﴾ to His words ﴿because they used to lie.﴾ He said: When you come to al-Hasan, convey my greetings to him and inform him of the origin of this hadith and what I said to you.

So I came to al-Hasan and said: "O Abu Saʿid, your brother Muhammad sends you his greetings," and I informed him of the hadith he had narrated. Al-Hasan took my hand and shook it, and said: "O people of Iraq, were you unable to be like this? He heard a hadith from us but did not accept it until he derived its origin. ʿAta' spoke the truth. This is how the hadith is: it concerns the hypocrites specifically." [[Full version in Tafsir al-Tabari: 10/245–246, no. 13215.]]

And when they stand up to prayer, they stand lazily, showing off to the people and not remembering Allah except a little.﴾ And concerning them He said: ﴿So woe to those who pray, who are heedless of their prayer.﴾ As for my saying: when he promises he breaks it, Thaʿlaba ibn Hatib came to me and said: 'I am poor, and I have a few sheep; pray to Allah that He bless them.' So I prayed, and they multiplied and increased until the roads became too narrow for them. Then I asked him for the charity, but he refused and withheld it. So Allah the Mighty and Majestic revealed: ﴿And among them are those who made a covenant with Allah﴾ to His words ﴿because they broke to Allah what they had promised Him.﴾'" [37]

The Companions of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) rejoiced, glorified Allah, and gave charity of great wealth. [[Full version in Tafsir al-Tabari: 10/244–245.]]

Al-Qasim ibn Bishr narrated from Usama, from Muhammad [al-Makhrami], who said: I heard al-Hasan say: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Whoever has three traits is a hypocrite, even if he fasts, prays, and claims to be a Muslim: when he speaks he lies, when he promises he breaks it, and when he is entrusted he betrays." [38] [[Sahih Muslim: 1/56.]] Then al-Hasan said: O Abu Saʿid, by Allah, if a man has a debt owed by me, and he meets me and demands it from me while I have nothing, and I fear that he will imprison me and destroy me, so I promise him that I will repay it at the new moon, and I do not do so, am I a hypocrite?! This is how the hadith has come.

Then he narrated from Abdullah ibn Amr that when his father was near death, he said: "Marry so-and-so, for I promised him that I would marry him. I do not want to meet Allah with a third of hypocrisy." I said: O Abu Saʿid, would a man have a third of him hypocritical and two-thirds believing? He said: This is how the hadith has come.

Muhammad said: So I performed the pilgrimage and met ʿAta' ibn Abi Rabah, and I informed him of the hadith I had heard from al-Hasan, and what I had said to him about the hypocrite, and what he had said to me. He said to me: "Were you unable to say to him: Tell me about the brothers of Joseph. Did they not promise their father and break it, and speak to him and lie to him, and was he trusted by them and they betrayed him? Were they hypocrites? Were they not prophets, when their father was a prophet and their grandfather was a prophet?"

I said to ʿAta': "O Abu Muhammad, tell me the origin of this hadith." He said: Jabir ibn Abdullah narrated to me that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said this hadith only concerning the hypocrites specifically, who spoke to the Prophet (ﷺ) and lied to him, were trusted with his secret and betrayed him, and promised him that they would go out with him to the expedition and broke it. He said: Abu Sufyan left Mecca, and Jibril came and said: "Abu Sufyan is in such-and-such a place." The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Abu Sufyan is in such-and-such a place; go out to him and keep it secret." A man from the hypocrites wrote to him: "Muhammad intends to send you forth." So Allah the Mighty and Majestic revealed: ﴿O you who believe, do not betray Allah and the Messenger, nor betray your trusts﴾ [[Surah al-Anfal: 27.]], and He revealed concerning the hypocrites: ﴿And among them are those who made a covenant with Allah: "If He gives us of His bounty..."﴾ to His words ﴿because they used to lie.﴾ He said: When you come to al-Hasan, convey my greetings to him and inform him of the origin of this hadith and what I said to you.

So I came to al-Hasan and said: "O Abu Saʿid, your brother Muhammad sends you his greetings," and I informed him of the hadith he had narrated. Al-Hasan took my hand and shook it, and said: "O people of Iraq, were you unable to be like this? He heard a hadith from us but did not accept it until he derived its origin. ʿAta' spoke the truth. This is how the hadith is: it concerns the hypocrites specifically." [[Full version in Tafsir al-Tabari: 10/245–246, no. 13215.]]

Commentary of al-Tha'alibi (al-Jawahir al-Hisan) on surah 9, verses 75–78:

Wa minhum man ʿahada Allah (the verse)

Al-Qasim ibn ʿAbd al-Rahman narrated from Abu Umama al-Bahili, who said: Thaʿlaba ibn Hatib al-Ansari came to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and said: "O Messenger of Allah, pray to Allah that He grant me wealth." The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Woe to you, O Thaʿlaba! A little that you can give thanks for is better than a lot that you cannot bear." Then he came to him again after that and said: "O Messenger of Allah, pray to Allah that He grant me wealth." The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Lakum fi Rasul Allah uswa hasana" [﴿You have in the Messenger of Allah an excellent example﴾], "and by Him in whose hand my soul is, if you wished that the mountains would move with me as gold and silver, they would." Then he came to him after that and said: "O Messenger of Allah, pray to Allah that He grant me wealth. By Him who sent you with the truth, if Allah grants me wealth I will surely give every person with a right his right." The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "O Allah, grant Thaʿlaba wealth." [32]

He said: So he acquired sheep, and they multiplied as worms multiply, so the city became too narrow for him, and he moved away from it and settled in one of its valleys, and they kept multiplying as worms multiply. He used to pray the Zuhr prayer with the Prophet (ﷺ), and he prayed the other prayers with his sheep. Then they increased and multiplied until he was far from Madina, so that he attended only the Friday prayer. Then they increased and multiplied further, and he moved further away, until he would attend neither the Friday prayer nor the congregation. Whenever it was Friday, he would pass by the people and ask them for news. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) mentioned him, and one day he asked: "What has Thaʿlaba done?" They said: "O Messenger of Allah, Thaʿlaba has acquired sheep that no valley can contain."

The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Woe to Thaʿlaba! Woe to Thaʿlaba! Woe to Thaʿlaba!" Then Allah revealed the verse of charity (zakat). The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) sent a man from Banu Sulaym and a man from Juhayna, and he wrote for them the instructions on collecting charity and how they should take it. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said to them: "Pass by Thaʿlaba ibn Hatib and a man from Banu Sulaym, and take their charities."

So the two set out until they came to Thaʿlaba, asked him for the charity, and read to him the letter of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). He said: "This is nothing but a jizya (poll tax); this is nothing but a sister of the jizya. Go on until you finish, then return to me." So they went on. The Sulami heard of them, so he looked at the best of the camels' ages, set them aside for the charity, and then met them with them. When he offered them, they said: "This is not required of you." He said: "Take it, for my soul is content with that." So they passed by the people and took the charities, then returned to Thaʿlaba, who said:

"Show me your letter." He read it and then said: "This is nothing but a jizya, this is nothing but a sister of the jizya. Go away until I see my opinion." So they set out. When the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) saw them coming, before they spoke he said: "Woe to Thaʿlaba! Woe to Thaʿlaba! Woe to Thaʿlaba!" Then he prayed good for the Sulami. They informed him of what Thaʿlaba had done, and Allah revealed concerning him: ﴿And among them are those who made a covenant with Allah: "If He gives us of His bounty, we will surely give charity..."﴾ up to His words ﴿...and because they used to lie﴾. A relative of Thaʿlaba was with the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and he heard this, so he went out and came to him and said: "Woe to you, O Thaʿlaba! Allah the Mighty and Majestic has revealed such-and-such about you." Thaʿlaba went out and came to the Prophet (ﷺ) and asked him to accept his charity.

He said: "Allah has forbidden me to accept your charity." So Thaʿlaba began throwing dust on his head. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said to him: "This is your deed; I commanded you, but you did not obey me." [33] When the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) passed away, he returned to his home, and the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) died without having accepted anything from him. Then he came to Abu Bakr (may Allah be pleased with him) when he became caliph and said: "You know my standing with the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and my position among the Ansar, so accept my charity." Abu Bakr said: "The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) did not accept it from you, and shall I accept it?" So he did not accept it. Abu Bakr died without accepting it. When ʿUmar (may Allah be pleased with him) became caliph, he came to him and said: "O Commander of the Faithful, accept my charity." He said: "The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) did not accept it from you, nor did Abu Bakr. I will not accept it." ʿUmar died without accepting it. Then ʿUthman became caliph, and he came to him and asked him to accept his charity. He said: "The Messenger of Allah did not accept it from you, nor did Abu Bakr or ʿUmar. I will not accept it from you." So he did not accept it from him, and he died during the caliphate of ʿUthman. [[Full version in Tafsir al-Tabari: 10/242, and Usd al-Ghaba: 1/238.]]

Ibn ʿAbbas, Saʿid ibn Jubayr and Qatada said: Thaʿlaba came to a gathering of the Ansar and called them to witness, saying: "If Allah grants me of His bounty, I will give every person with a right his right, I will give charity from it, and I will maintain the ties of kinship." Then a paternal cousin of his died and left him wealth, but he did not fulfill what he had said. So Allah revealed this verse.

Muqatil said: Thaʿlaba passed by the Ansar while he was in need, and said: "If Allah grants me of His bounty, I will surely give charity and surely be among the righteous." Then Allah granted him of His bounty. The reason was that a client of ʿUmar ibn al-Khattab had killed a man from the hypocrites by mistake, and the Prophet (ﷺ) gave his blood-money to Thaʿlaba, who was a relative of the one killed. He was stingy and withheld the right of Allah, so Allah revealed this verse.

Al-Hasan and Mujahid said: This verse was revealed concerning Thaʿlaba ibn Hatib and Muʿattib ibn Qushayr, two men from Banu ʿAmr ibn ʿAwf, who went out among a group sitting together and said: "By Allah, if Allah provides for us, we will surely give charity." When Allah provided for them, they became stingy.

Al-Dahhak said: It was revealed concerning men among the hypocrites: [Nabtal] ibn al-Harith, Jadd ibn Qays, Thaʿlaba ibn Hatib, and Muʿattib ibn Qushayr. They said: ﴿If Allah gives us of His bounty, we will surely give charity﴾... ﴿So when He gave them of His bounty, they became stingy with it and withheld zakat.﴾

Al-Kalbi said: It was revealed concerning Hatib ibn Abi Balta'a. He had wealth in Syria and struggled greatly for it, so he swore by Allah: "If Allah gives us of His bounty, of His provision, meaning the wealth that is in Syria, I will surely give charity from it, I will maintain ties, and I will surely give Allah's right from it." Then Allah gave him that wealth, but he did not do what he had said. So Allah the Mighty and Majestic revealed: ﴿And among them, meaning among the hypocrites, are those who made a covenant with Allah: "If He gives us of His bounty, we will surely give charity and surely pay Allah's right from it, and we will surely be among the righteous"﴾, i.e., that we act as the righteous act with their wealth, by maintaining kinship and spending in good causes. ﴿So when He gave them of His bounty, they became stingy with it, and turned away while they were averse﴾; ﴿so He caused to follow﴾, i.e., He followed them with it; and it was said: ﴿He repaid them for their stinginess.﴾ Al-Nabigha said:

"Whoever obeys you, benefit him by his obedience, as he obeyed you, and guide him to right guidance." [[Tarikh Dimashq: 35/426.]]

﴿Hypocrisy in their hearts until the Day they meet Him﴾: Allah deprived them of repentance. ﴿Because they broke to Allah what they had promised Him, and because they used to lie.﴾ Ma'bad ibn Thabit said: It is only something [apparent] in their souls which they did not speak. Have you not heard the words of Allah the Mighty and Majestic: ﴿Do they not know that Allah knows their secret and their private talk, and that Allah is the Knower of the unseen?﴾

From Masruq, from Abdullah ibn Umar, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Whoever has four traits is a pure hypocrite, and whoever has one of them has a trait of hypocrisy until he abandons it: when he speaks he lies, when he promises he breaks it, when he makes a covenant he betrays it, and when he disputes he acts wickedly." [34] [[Sahih al-Bukhari: 1/14.]]

Al-Ashʿath from al-Hasan, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Whoever has three traits is a hypocrite, even if he prays, fasts, and claims to be a believer: when he speaks he lies, when he promises he breaks it, and when he is entrusted he betrays." [35]

ʿAbdullah ibn Masʿud said: Consider the hypocrite by three signs: when he speaks he lies, when he promises he breaks it, and when he makes a covenant he betrays it. Allah revealed the confirmation of this in His Book: ﴿And among them are those who made a covenant with Allah﴾ up to His words ﴿because they used to lie.﴾ This report is difficult in its apparent meaning; whoever does not know its interpretation, his error and his explanation will be great.

My teacher al-Hasan ibn Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Jaʿfar informed me, saying: My father informed me from my grandfather al-Husayn ibn Jaʿfar, who said: Muhammad ibn Yazid al-Sulami narrated to us, saying: ʿAmmar ibn Qirat narrated to us from Bukayr ibn Maʿruf from Muqatil ibn Hayyan, who said: I was in charge of judgeship in Samarqand. One day I read the hadith of al-Maqburi from Abu Hurayra from the Prophet (ﷺ): "Whoever has three traits is a hypocrite: when he speaks he lies, when he is entrusted he betrays, and when he promises he breaks it." [36]

My thoughts became confused, my heart was divided, I feared for myself and for all people, and I said: Who will be saved from these traits? So I neglected the judgeship and came to Bukhara and asked its scholars, but found no relief. I came to Marw and found no relief. I came to Nishapur and found no relief with its scholars. Then I heard that Shahr ibn Hawshab was in Jurjan, so I went to him, presented my matter to him, and asked about the report. He said to me: "When I heard this report, I was like a grain on a frying pan out of fear [[A simile; a maqla is a copper or other vessel in which food is fried.]]. Go and seek Saʿid ibn Jubayr, for he has settled in al-Rayy. Perhaps you will find for me and for you; I have heard that he has relief." So I went to al-Rayy, sought Saʿid, came to him, presented the matter to him, and asked him about the meaning of the report.

He said: "I have been fearful for myself since this report reached me, and I fear for you and for myself from these traits. I have endured and suffered a long journey and trials. So go to al-Hasan al-Basri, for I hope you will find with him relief for me, for you, and for the Muslims." I came to Basra, sought al-Hasan, and related the whole story to him. He said: "May Allah have mercy on Shahr, he has reached half of the report and not the other half. When the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said this report, it preoccupied the hearts of his companions, and they were too shy to ask him. So they came to Fatima and mentioned to her the preoccupation of their hearts with the report. Fatima (may Allah be pleased with her) went to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and informed him of the preoccupation of his companions. He commanded Salman, who called out: 'Prayer, gathered!' When they had gathered, he ascended the pulpit and said: 'O people, I did say: Whoever has three traits is a hypocrite: when he speaks he lies, when he is entrusted he betrays, and when he promises he breaks it. I did not mean you by it; I meant only the hypocrites. As for my saying: when he speaks he lies, the hypocrites came to me and said: By Allah, our faith is like your faith and the confirmation of our hearts is like the confirmation of your heart. So Allah the Mighty and Majestic revealed: ﴿When the hypocrites come to you, they say: We bear witness that you are the Messenger of Allah﴾ to the end of the verse. As for my saying: when he is entrusted he betrays, trust is the prayer, and the whole religion is a trust. Allah the Exalted said: ﴿Indeed, the hypocrites deceive Allah, and He is deceiving them. And when they stand up to prayer, they stand lazily, showing off to the people and not remembering Allah except a little.﴾ And concerning them He said: ﴿So woe to those who pray, who are heedless of their prayer.﴾ As for my saying: when he promises he breaks it, Thaʿlaba ibn Hatib came to me and said: 'I am poor, and I have a few sheep; pray to Allah that He bless them.' So I prayed, and they multiplied and increased until the roads became too narrow for them. Then I asked him for the charity, but he refused and withheld it. So Allah the Mighty and Majestic revealed: ﴿And among them are those who made a covenant with Allah﴾ to His words ﴿because they broke to Allah what they had promised Him.﴾'" [37]

The Companions of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) rejoiced, glorified Allah, and gave charity of great wealth. [[Full version in Tafsir al-Tabari: 10/244–245.]]

[38] [[Sahih Muslim: 1/56.]] Then al-Hasan said: O Abu Saʿid, by Allah, if a man has a debt owed by me, and he meets me and demands it from me while I have nothing, and I fear that he will imprison me and destroy me, so I promise him that I will repay it at the new moon, and I do not do so, am I a hypocrite?! This is how the hadith has come.

Then he narrated from Abdullah ibn Amr that when his father was near death, he said: "Marry so-and-so, for I promised him that I would marry him. I do not want to meet Allah with a third of hypocrisy." I said: O Abu Saʿid, would a man have a third of him hypocritical and two-thirds believing? He said: This is how the hadith has come.

Muhammad said: So I performed the pilgrimage and met ʿAta' ibn Abi Rabah, and I informed him of the hadith I had heard from al-Hasan, and what I had said to him about the hypocrite, and what he had said to me. He said to me: "Were you unable to say to him: Tell me about the brothers of Joseph. Did they not promise their father and break it, and speak to him and lie to him, and was he trusted by them and they betrayed him? Were they hypocrites? Were they not prophets, when their father was a prophet and their grandfather was a prophet?"

I said to ʿAta': "O Abu Muhammad, tell me the origin of this hadith." He said: Jabir ibn Abdullah narrated to me that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said this hadith only concerning the hypocrites specifically, who spoke to the Prophet (ﷺ) and lied to him, were trusted with his secret and betrayed him, and promised him that they would go out with him to the expedition and broke it. He said: Abu Sufyan left Mecca, and Jibril came and said: "Abu Sufyan is in such-and-such a place." The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Abu Sufyan is in such-and-such a place; go out to him and keep it secret." A man from the hypocrites wrote to him: "Muhammad intends to send you forth." So Allah the Mighty and Majestic revealed: ﴿O you who believe, do not betray Allah and the Messenger, nor betray your trusts﴾ [[Surah al-Anfal: 27.]], and He revealed concerning the hypocrites: ﴿And among them are those who made a covenant with Allah: "If He gives us of His bounty..."﴾ to His words ﴿because they used to lie.﴾ He said: When you come to al-Hasan, convey my greetings to him and inform him of the origin of this hadith and what I said to you.

So I came to al-Hasan and said: "O Abu Saʿid, your brother Muhammad sends you his greetings," and I informed him of the hadith he had narrated. Al-Hasan took my hand and shook it, and said: "O people of Iraq, were you unable to be like this? He heard a hadith from us but did not accept it until he derived its origin. ʿAta' spoke the truth. This is how the hadith is: it concerns the hypocrites specifically." [[Full version in Tafsir al-Tabari: 10/245–246, no. 13215.]]

Commentary of al-Tha'alibi (al-Jawahir al-Hisan) on surah 9, verse 79–91:

﴿The ones who find fault with those among the believers who give charity voluntarily...﴾

The people of tafsir said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) urged people to give charity. ʿAbd al-Rahman ibn ʿAwf came with four thousand dirhams and said: "O Messenger of Allah, I had eight thousand dirhams, so I have brought you four thousand, so put it to use in the way of Allah, and I have kept four thousand for my dependents." The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "May Allah bless you in what you gave and in what you kept back."

So Allah blessed ʿAbd al-Rahman's wealth until he died, and on the day he died he had two wives, and the value of their share came to one hundred and sixty thousand dirhams, eighty thousand for each of them. On that day ʿAsim ibn ʿAdi al-ʿAjlani gave in charity one hundred and sixty wasqs of dates. Abu ʿAqil al-Ansari, whose name was al-Habbab, came with a sa' of dates and said: "O Messenger of Allah, I spent my night hauling a bucket with a rope, drawing water, until I earned two sa's of dates. I kept one for my family and brought you the other." The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) commanded him to scatter it among the charities. The hypocrites found fault with them and said: "ʿAbd al-Rahman and ʿAsim only gave out of show, and Allah and His Messenger had no need of Abu ʿAqil's sa', but he wanted to purify himself so that he could give charity." [Tafsir al-Tabari: 10/251; Fath al-Bari: 2508; Asbab al-Nuzul of al-Wahidi: 172–173.] Then Allah, mighty and majestic, revealed: ﴿The ones who find fault with those among the believers who give charity voluntarily﴾, meaning they criticise and backbite. ﴿those who give voluntarily﴾ means those who give charity willingly; ﴿among the believers﴾.

Al-Nadr ibn Shumayl said: he is "good of soul in charity", meaning ʿAbd al-Rahman and ʿAsim.

﴿And those who find nothing but their effort﴾ — their capacity — meaning Abu ʿAqil.

ʿAta' and al-Aʿraj read ﴿juhdahum﴾ with a fatha on the jim. Both are dialectal variants, like al-juhd and al-juhayd. The damma is the dialect of the people of the Hijaz, and the fatha the dialect of the people of Najd.

al-Sha'bi used to distinguish between them, saying: al-juhd is in work, and al-jahd is in strength. Al-Qutabi said: al-juhd means capacity, and al-jahd means hardship. ﴿they mock them; Allah has mocked them, or repaid them for their mockery﴾, and ﴿for them is a painful punishment﴾.

Ibn ʿUlayyah narrated from al-Hariri, from Abu al-ʿAlil, who said: A man stood on the stone and said: My father or my uncle told me: "I witnessed the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) saying: 'Whoever gives charity today, I will testify for him before Allah on the Day of Resurrection.'" He said: I had a turban on, and I took off one or two cloths from it to give in charity, then something that befalls the son of Adam overtook me, so I bound my head with it. He said: Then a man came, and I have not seen in al-Baqi' a man shorter in stature, darker in complexion, or more brown-skinned than him, leading a she-camel. I have not seen in al-Baqi' a camel more beautiful or finer than her. He said: "She and what is in her belly are a charity, O Messenger of Allah," and he handed him her halter. He said: A man sitting nearby found fault with him and said: "By Allah, he did not give her in charity, and she is better than him." The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) looked at him and said: "Rather, he is better than you and her [Jami' al-Bayan of al-Tabari: 10/250] [41]." He said this at length, and then Allah, mighty and majestic, revealed this verse. Then He said: ﴿Ask forgiveness for them, or do not ask forgiveness for them﴾, meaning for these hypocrites.

The wording [is an imperative but its meaning is] a conditional: its implied sense is that whether you ask forgiveness for them or do not ask forgiveness for them, Allah will not forgive them. ﴿If you ask forgiveness for them seventy times, Allah will not forgive them﴾. For the Arabs, seventy is a limit reached by counting, like seven, and the limbs; seven completes the number of creation, like the heavens, the earth, the seas, and the climes.

In some tafsir texts I have seen: ﴿If you ask forgiveness for them seventy times﴾ alongside your prayers over the [grave of] Hamzah [as in the manuscript; the word "grave" is an addition by us] — Allah will not forgive them.

al-Dahhak said: When this verse was revealed, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Allah has granted me a concession, so I will increase beyond the seventy, perhaps Allah will forgive them." [42]

Then Allah, mighty and majestic, revealed: ﴿It is the same for them whether you ask forgiveness for them or do not ask forgiveness for them; Allah will never forgive them﴾ [Surah al-Munafiqun: 6].

ʿUrwah ibn al-Zubayr mentioned that these verses were revealed about ʿAbd Allah ibn Ubayy when he said to his companions: "If you did not spend on Muhammad and his companions, they would disperse from around him." Then he said: "If we return to Medina, the mightier will expel the weaker from it." So Allah, exalted, revealed: ﴿Ask forgiveness for them.﴾ The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "I will increase beyond the seventy." Then Allah revealed: ﴿It is the same for them whether you ask forgiveness for them or do not ask forgiveness for them; Allah will never forgive them.﴾

Allah refused to forgive them. ﴿That is because they disbelieved in Allah and His Messenger, and Allah does not guide the defiant people.﴾

﴿Those who stayed behind from the expedition of Tabuk rejoiced in their sitting [at home] against the Messenger of Allah.﴾ Qutrub and the historian said: meaning, in opposition to the Messenger of Allah when he set out and they stayed behind. Abu ʿUbaydah said: meaning after the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ).

al-Harith ibn Khalid recited:

"The spring came after them, so it was as if / the palm-leaf weavers spread a mat between them."

That is, after them. This interpretation is supported by the reading of ʿAmr ibn Maymun: ﴿khalfa Rasul Allah﴾, and ﴿they said: Do not march in the heat﴾. The expedition of Tabuk was in intense heat. ﴿Say: The fire of Hell is more intense in heat, if only they understood﴾, meaning, if they knew this. It is in the codex of ʿAbd Allah. ﴿So let them laugh a little, and let them weep much, as a recompense for what they used to earn.﴾ Abu Musa al-Ash'ari said: The people of the Fire will weep tears in the Fire until, if ships were sailed on their tears, they would sail. Then they will weep blood after the tears, and for something like what they are in, let him weep.

Ibn ʿAbbas said: The people of hypocrisy will weep in the Fire for the lifespan of the world, and tears will not dry up for them, nor will they be able to close their eyes in sleep.

Shuʿbah, from Qatadah, from Anas, who said: Anas said: "If you knew what I know, you would laugh a little and weep much, much."

The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "May Allah bless you in what you gave and in what you kept back."

So Allah blessed ʿAbd al-Rahman's wealth until he died, and on the day he died he had two wives, and the value of their share came to one hundred and sixty thousand dirhams, eighty thousand for each of them. On that day ʿAsim ibn ʿAdi al-ʿAjlani gave in charity one hundred and sixty wasqs of dates. Abu ʿAqil al-Ansari, whose name was al-Habbab, came with a sa' of dates and said: "O Messenger of Allah, I spent my night hauling a bucket with a rope, drawing water, until I earned two sa's of dates. I kept one for my family and brought you the other." The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) commanded him to scatter it among the charities. The hypocrites found fault with them and said: "ʿAbd al-Rahman and ʿAsim only gave out of show, and Allah and His Messenger had no need of Abu ʿAqil's sa', but he wanted to purify himself so that he could give charity." [Tafsir al-Tabari: 10/251; Fath al-Bari: 2508; Asbab al-Nuzul of al-Wahidi: 172–173.] Then Allah, mighty and majestic, revealed: ﴿The ones who find fault with those among the believers who give charity voluntarily﴾, meaning they criticise and backbite. ﴿those who give voluntarily﴾ means those who give charity willingly; ﴿among the believers﴾.

Al-Nadr ibn Shumayl said: he is "good of soul in charity", meaning ʿAbd al-Rahman and ʿAsim.

﴿And those who find nothing but their effort﴾ — their capacity — meaning Abu ʿAqil.

ʿAta' and al-Aʿraj read ﴿juhdahum﴾ with a fatha on the jim. Both are dialectal variants, like al-juhd and al-juhayd. The damma is the dialect of the people of the Hijaz, and the fatha the dialect of the people of Najd.

al-Sha'bi used to distinguish between them, saying: al-juhd is in work, and al-jahd is in strength. Al-Qutabi said: al-juhd means capacity, and al-jahd means hardship. ﴿they mock them; Allah has mocked them, or repaid them for their mockery﴾, and ﴿for them is a painful punishment﴾.

Ibn ʿUlayyah narrated from al-Hariri, from Abu al-ʿAlil, who said: A man stood on the stone and said: My father or my uncle told me: "I witnessed the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) saying: 'Whoever gives charity today, I will testify for him before Allah on the Day of Resurrection.'" He said: I had a turban on, and I took off one or two cloths from it to give in charity, then something that befalls the son of Adam overtook me, so I bound my head with it. He said: Then a man came, and I have not seen in al-Baqi' a man shorter in stature, darker in complexion, or more brown-skinned than him, leading a she-camel. I have not seen in al-Baqi' a camel more beautiful or finer than her. He said: "She and what is in her belly are a charity, O Messenger of Allah," and he handed him her halter. He said: A man sitting nearby found fault with him and said: "By Allah, he did not give her in charity, and she is better than him." The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) looked at him and said: "Rather, he is better than you and her [Jami' al-Bayan of al-Tabari: 10/250] [41]." He said this at length, and then Allah, mighty and majestic, revealed this verse. Then He said: ﴿Ask forgiveness for them, or do not ask forgiveness for them﴾, meaning for these hypocrites.

The wording [is an imperative but its meaning is] a conditional: its implied sense is that whether you ask forgiveness for them or do not ask forgiveness for them, Allah will not forgive them. ﴿If you ask forgiveness for them seventy times, Allah will not forgive them﴾. For the Arabs, seventy is a limit reached by counting, like seven, and the limbs; seven completes the number of creation, like the heavens, the earth, the seas, and the climes.

In some tafsir texts I have seen: ﴿If you ask forgiveness for them seventy times﴾ alongside your prayers over the [grave of] Hamzah [as in the manuscript; the word "grave" is an addition by us] — Allah will not forgive them.

al-Dahhak said: When this verse was revealed, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Allah has granted me a concession, so I will increase beyond the seventy, perhaps Allah will forgive them." [42]

Then Allah, mighty and majestic, revealed: ﴿It is the same for them whether you ask forgiveness for them or do not ask forgiveness for them; Allah will never forgive them﴾ [Surah al-Munafiqun: 6].

ʿUrwah ibn al-Zubayr mentioned that these verses were revealed about ʿAbd Allah ibn Ubayy when he said to his companions: "If you did not spend on Muhammad and his companions, they would disperse from around him." Then he said: "If we return to Medina, the mightier will expel the weaker from it." So Allah, exalted, revealed: ﴿Ask forgiveness for them.﴾ The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "I will increase beyond the seventy." Then Allah revealed: ﴿It is the same for them whether you ask forgiveness for them or do not ask forgiveness for them; Allah will never forgive them.﴾

Allah refused to forgive them. ﴿That is because they disbelieved in Allah and His Messenger, and Allah does not guide the defiant people.﴾

﴿Those who stayed behind from the expedition of Tabuk rejoiced in their sitting [at home] against the Messenger of Allah.﴾ Qutrub and the historian said: meaning, in opposition to the Messenger of Allah when he set out and they stayed behind. Abu ʿUbaydah said: meaning after the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ).

al-Harith ibn Khalid recited:

"The spring came after them, so it was as if / the palm-leaf weavers spread a mat between them."

That is, after them. This interpretation is supported by the reading of ʿAmr ibn Maymun: ﴿khalfa Rasul Allah﴾, and ﴿they said: Do not march in the heat﴾. The expedition of Tabuk was in intense heat. ﴿Say: The fire of Hell is more intense in heat, if only they understood﴾, meaning, if they knew this. It is in the codex of ʿAbd Allah. ﴿So let them laugh a little, and let them weep much, as a recompense for what they used to earn.﴾ Abu Musa al-Ash'ari said: The people of the Fire will weep tears in the Fire until, if ships were sailed on their tears, they would sail. Then they will weep blood after the tears, and for something like what they are in, let him weep.

Ibn ʿAbbas said: The people of hypocrisy will weep in the Fire for the lifespan of the world, and tears will not dry up for them, nor will they be able to close their eyes in sleep.

Shuʿbah, from Qatadah, from Anas, who said: Anas said: "If you knew what I know, you would laugh a little and weep much, much."

﴿So if Allah returns you﴾ — Allah returns you from the expedition of Tabuk — ﴿to a group of them﴾, meaning of those who stayed behind; He said "a group of them" because not everyone who stayed behind at Tabuk was a hypocrite. ﴿and they ask your permission to go out on another expedition, say to them: "You will never go out with me, and you will never fight an enemy with me." As a punishment for their staying behind.﴾ ﴿You were pleased with sitting the first time﴾, meaning you stayed behind from the expedition of Tabuk. ﴿So sit with those who stay behind.﴾ Ibn ʿAbbas said: the men who stayed behind without excuse.

al-Dahhak: the women, the children, the sick, and the chronically disabled. It was also said: ﴿with the ones who stay behind.﴾ Al-Farra' said: It is said: "a slack servant" (ʿabd khalif) and "one who lags behind" (takhalluf) when he is lagging behind. It was also said: [the weak] people. It is said: "khalaf of his family" when they are his folk. It was also said: with the people of corruption, from the saying "khalaf al-rajul ʿala ahlihi yakhlufu khuluf," when he became corrupt; and "nabidh khalif," meaning spoiled; "khalaf al-laban khulufan" when milk turned sour from long standing in the waterskin; and "khalaf fam al-sa'im" when the breath of the fasting person changed; and from it "khalaf su'" (an evil successor). Malik ibn Dinar read: ﴿maʿa al-mukhalifin﴾.

﴿And do not pray over any of them who dies, ever.﴾

The exegetes said, with varying reports: ʿAbd Allah ibn Ubayy ibn Salul sent to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) while he was ill. When the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) entered upon him, he said to him: "Has Judaism destroyed you?" He said: "O Messenger of Allah, I did not send for you to rebuke me, but I sent for you so that you would ask forgiveness for me," and he asked him to shroud him in his shirt and pray over him. He said: "al-Habbab ibn ʿAbd Allah." He said (ﷺ): "You are ʿAbd Allah ibn ʿAbd Allah, for al-Habbab is the devil." "I have certainly pierced the joints of the thighs / the thighs of Hind, the best of queens."

﴿And those are the successful. The rest read with a shadda on the dhal, and they are the ones who fell short.

It is said: "aʿdhara fi al-amr" by making an excuse, and "ʿadhara" when he fell short.

al-Farra' said: The original is al-muʿtadhirun, so the taʾ was assimilated into the dhal and the vowel of the taʾ was moved to the ʿayn.

﴿And those who lied to Allah sat [at home].﴾ The common reading is with a light dhal, meaning the hypocrites. Ubayy and al-Hasan read kaddhabu Allah with a shadda. ﴿Those among them who disbelieved will be struck by a painful punishment.﴾ Then he mentioned the people of excuse, saying: ﴿There is no blame upon the weak,﴾ Ibn ʿAbbas said: meaning the chronically disabled, the elderly, and the infirm; ﴿nor upon the sick,﴾ ﴿nor upon those who find nothing to spend,﴾ meaning the poor. ﴿There is no sin upon them when they are sincere to Allah and His Messenger in their absence.﴾ ﴿There is no path against the good-doers.﴾ ﴿And Allah is Forgiving and Merciful.﴾

Commentary of al-Tha'alibi (al-Jawahir al-Hisan) on surah 9, verses 92–105 (part 1 of 2):

Qatadah said: It was revealed concerning Ayidh ibn Amr and his companions. Al-Dahhak said: It was revealed concerning Abdullah ibn Za'id, who is Ibn Umm Maktum, and he was blind. He said: "O Prophet of Allah, I am an old man, blind in sight, of little means, and frail of body, and I have no means. Do I have a concession to stay behind from jihad?" The Prophet (ﷺ) remained silent, so Allah the Exalted revealed this verse: ﴿Nor [is there blame] upon those who come to you to be provided with mounts, [and] you say, "I find not that upon which to mount you"...﴾

It was revealed concerning the "Weepers," who were seven: Ma'qil ibn Yasar, Sakhr ibn Khansa' [see Usd al-Ghabah 3/13, where he is mentioned as Sakhr ibn Sulayman; in al-Isabah, he is Sakhr ibn Umayyah ibn Khansa'], who is the one who had intercourse with his wife in Ramadan, and the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) instructed him to make expiation [Ibn Hajar said in al-Isabah (3/332, biography no. 4064): "The well-known view is that the person in the story of intercourse was Salamah ibn Sakhr, so perhaps this is an error by al-Tha'labi"]; Abdullah ibn Ka'b al-Ansari, Ulbah ibn Zayd al-Ansari, Salim ibn Umayr, Tha'labah ibn Ghanamah, and Abdullah ibn Ma'qil. They came to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and said: "O Prophet of Allah, Allah the Mighty and Majestic has called us to go out with you. So carry us on the thin-soled shoes and the patched sandals, and we will campaign with you." The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "I do not find anything upon which to carry you." So they turned away weeping [Asbab al-Nuzul, p. 174]. That is the meaning of His saying: ﴿They turned back while their eyes overflowed with tears, out of grief that they could not find what they could spend﴾.

Mujahid said: This verse was revealed [concerning Abdullah, Abd al-Rahman, Aqil, al-Nu'man, and Suwayd] [and Sinan] [Note from the margin of Tafsir al-Qurtubi; in Asbab al-Nuzul it reads: concerning the Banu Muqarrin: Ma'qil, Suwayd, and al-Nu'man; the manuscript is damaged]: ﴿The blame is only upon those who ask your permission while they are rich...﴾ [to the end of the verse]. ﴿They will make excuses to you when you return to them. Say, "Make no excuse; we will never believe you. Allah has already informed us of your news.
