They all said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) took a third of their wealth and left two-thirds, because Allah, mighty and majestic, said: ﴿Take from their wealth﴾ and did not say "their wealth" (in full), so he did not take all of it.

Al-Hasan and Qatadah said: these were other than the three who stayed behind, [and the charity] purifies them from their sins by it. The reading with the raised vowel (dammah) is a circumstantial clause (hal), not a response (jawab), meaning: ﴿Take from their wealth a charity﴾ being purifying and cleansing, like the saying of al-Hutay'ah:

"Whenever you come to him, seeking the light of his fire,
You will find the best fire and the best station with him."

Maslamah ibn Muharib read "tutahhiruhum wa tuzakkihim" with the jussive, as a response (jawab). Al-Hasan read "tutahhiruhum" (with a light form from "atahhara"), and "wa tuzakkihim," meaning he purifies them. It was also said: he sets them right. It was also said: he elevates them from the stations of the hypocrites to the stations of the sincere. It was also said: "it" refers to their wealth.

﴿And pray for them﴾: meaning seek forgiveness for them and supplicate for them. It was said: it is the saying of the official who takes the charity: "May Allah reward you for what you have given, and bless you in what you have kept." Prayer (salah) in the language means supplication, and from it is the saying of the Prophet (ﷺ): "When one of you is invited to a meal, let him accept; if he is fasting, let him pray (fa-l-yusalli)," meaning let him supplicate. Al-A'sha said:

"The wind meets its wine jar,
And he prays over its jar and is marked (with its sign)."

Meaning he supplicated for it safety and blessing.

He also said:

"My daughter says, when I have come near to departing:
'O Lord, keep away from my father illnesses and pain.'
Upon you is like what you prayed, so sleep,
For the side of a man has a resting place."

﴿Indeed, your prayer﴾: the people of Kufa read "ṣalātuka" in the singular here and in Surah Hud (﴿a-ṣalātuka﴾), and "wa-l-mu'minīn" with a suppressed (idmar). Abu Ubayd said: because "salah" is one of the prayers. This was related from Ibn Abbas. Do you not hear Allah saying: ﴿Establish the prayer﴾? This is the prayer of eternity, and "ṣalawāt" is for the plural, as in the saying: "I prayed the prayers (ṣalawāt) four and five." The others read all of them in the plural, and Abu Hatim chose this. He said: Whoever claims that "ṣalawāt" is from "ṣalāh" because the plural with the feminine suffix (-āt) is rare, has erred, for Allah, exalted is He, said: ﴿The words of Allah would not be exhausted﴾ and ﴿and she affirmed the words of her Lord﴾; He did not mean what is few.

﴿Is a comfort for them﴾: Ibn Abbas said: a mercy for them. Qatadah said: a dignity for them. Al-Kalbi said: a reassurance for them, that Allah has accepted their repentance. Mu'adh said: a purification for them from you. Abu 'Ubaydah said: a steadying.

﴿And Allah is Hearing, Knowing.﴾

Shu'bah, from 'Amr ibn Murrah, from 'Abd Allah ibn Abi Awfa, who was one of the companions of the tree (of the Pledge of Ridwan): that the Prophet (ﷺ), when people came to him with their charities, would say: "O Allah, send your blessings upon them." When I came to him with my charity, he said: "O Allah, send your blessings upon Abu Awfa." Ibn Abbas said: This is not an obligatory charity (zakat al-fard); it is like the charity of expiation for an oath. 'Ikrimah said: it is the obligatory charity. When the repentance of these people was revealed, those who had not sinned and had stayed behind said: "These were with us yesterday; they did not speak nor sit with us. What is the matter with them?" Then Allah, mighty and majestic, revealed: ﴿Do they not know that it is Allah who accepts repentance from His servants﴾, the verse.

The meaning of "taking the charities" is accepting them.

Al-Shafi'i, from Sufyan ibn 'Uyaynah, from Ibn 'Ajlan, from Sa'id ibn Yasar, from Abu Hurayrah, who said: I heard Abu al-Qasim (ﷺ) say: "By Him in whose hand is my soul, no servant gives a charity from the earnings of his livelihood, and Allah accepts nothing but what is good, and it does not ascend to heaven except that it is placed in the hand of the Most Merciful, who nurtures it as one of you nurtures his foal, until a morsel will come on the Day of Resurrection as great as a mountain." Then he recited: ﴿That Allah is the One who accepts repentance from His servants﴾, and the confirmation of this is in the revealed Book of Allah: ﴿Allah deprives usury of blessing and gives increase for charities﴾ to His saying ﴿for what you used to do﴾.

Mujahid said: this is a warning (wa'id) to them.

It is related in a report: If a servant were to come with his deed to a rock that has no door and no window, his deed would come out to the people, whatever it may be.

Commentary of al-Tha'alibi (al-Jawahir al-Hisan) on surah 9, verses 92–105 (part 1 of 2):

Qatadah said: It was revealed concerning Ayidh ibn Amr and his companions. Al-Dahhak said: It was revealed concerning Abdullah ibn Za'id, who is Ibn Umm Maktum, and he was blind. He said: "O Prophet of Allah, I am an old man, blind in sight, of little means, and frail of body, and I have no means. Do I have a concession to stay behind from jihad?" The Prophet (ﷺ) remained silent, so Allah the Exalted revealed this verse: ﴿Nor [is there blame] upon those who come to you to be provided with mounts, [and] you say, "I find not that upon which to mount you"...﴾

It was revealed concerning the "Weepers," who were seven: Ma'qil ibn Yasar, Sakhr ibn Khansa' [see Usd al-Ghabah 3/13, where he is mentioned as Sakhr ibn Sulayman; in al-Isabah, he is Sakhr ibn Umayyah ibn Khansa'], who is the one who had intercourse with his wife in Ramadan, and the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) instructed him to make expiation [Ibn Hajar said in al-Isabah (3/332, biography no. 4064): "The well-known view is that the person in the story of intercourse was Salamah ibn Sakhr, so perhaps this is an error by al-Tha'labi"]; Abdullah ibn Ka'b al-Ansari, Ulbah ibn Zayd al-Ansari, Salim ibn Umayr, Tha'labah ibn Ghanamah, and Abdullah ibn Ma'qil. They came to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and said: "O Prophet of Allah, Allah the Mighty and Majestic has called us to go out with you. So carry us on the thin-soled shoes and the patched sandals, and we will campaign with you." The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "I do not find anything upon which to carry you." So they turned away weeping [Asbab al-Nuzul, p. 174]. That is the meaning of His saying: ﴿They turned back while their eyes overflowed with tears, out of grief that they could not find what they could spend﴾.

Mujahid said: This verse was revealed [concerning Abdullah, Abd al-Rahman, Aqil, al-Nu'man, and Suwayd] [and Sinan] [Note from the margin of Tafsir al-Qurtubi; in Asbab al-Nuzul it reads: concerning the Banu Muqarrin: Ma'qil, Suwayd, and al-Nu'man; the manuscript is damaged]: ﴿The blame is only upon those who ask your permission while they are rich...﴾ [to the end of the verse]. ﴿They will make excuses to you when you return to them. Say, "Make no excuse; we will never believe you. Allah has already informed us of your news. And Allah will see your deeds, and [so will] His Messenger..."﴾ Afterward: will you repent of your hypocrisy or will you persist in it? ﴿Then you will be returned to the Knower of the unseen and the witnessed, and He will inform you of what you used to do﴾, of good and evil. ﴿They will swear by Allah to you when you return [i.e., have come back] to them, that you may turn away from them﴾ [that you may overlook their sin], and not rebuke or reprimand them. ﴿So turn away from them﴾, leave them and what they have chosen for themselves of affair and disobedience. ﴿Indeed, they are impure﴾, i.e., unclean. Ata said: Their deeds are unclean. ﴿And their refuge is Hell, as recompense for what they used to earn.﴾

Ibn Abbas said: It was revealed concerning Jadd ibn Qays, Mu'attib ibn Qushayr, and their companions, who were eighty men among the hypocrites. The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "When they come to Madinah, do not sit with them or speak to them" [47] [see Zad al-Masir 3/331].

Muqatil said: It was revealed concerning Abdullah ibn Ubayy, who swore to the Prophet (ﷺ) by the One besides whom there is no god that he would not be pleased with them after this, and that he would be with him against his enemy; and he asked the Prophet (ﷺ) to be pleased with him. So Allah the Mighty and Majestic revealed this verse: ﴿They swear to you to please you. But if you should be pleased with them, indeed Allah is not pleased with the defiantly disobedient people.﴾

﴿The bedouins are stronger in disbelief and hypocrisy﴾, meaning the people of the desert, ﴿and more likely not to know the limits of what Allah has revealed to His Messenger. And Allah is Knowing and Wise.﴾ Qatadah said: They have less knowledge of the sunnah.

Al-A'mash narrated from Ibrahim, who said: A bedouin sat with Zayd ibn Suhan while he was with his companions, and his hand had been injured on the day of Nahawand. The bedouin said: "By Allah, I do not know: your speech pleases me, but your hand frightens me." He said: "Which of my hands? It is the left." The bedouin said: "By Allah, I do not know whether they cut off the right or the left [hand]?" Zayd ibn Suhan said: "Allah has spoken the truth: ﴿The bedouins are stronger in disbelief and hypocrisy﴾ [the verse]" [Jami al-Bayan 11/6].

﴿And among the bedouins is he who takes what he spends as a loss﴾. Ata said: He does not expect reward for his giving, nor does he fear loss by withholding; he spends only out of fear and show-off. ﴿And he awaits misfortunes to befall you﴾, meaning the vicissitudes of time, which sometimes bring good and sometimes evil. He said: [He waits] for when time turns against you, so that the Messenger dies and the polytheists prevail. ﴿Upon them is the cycle of evil.﴾ Ibn Kathir, Ibn Muhsin, Mujahid, and Abu Amr read *al-saw'* with a damma on the sin here and in Surah al-Fath; it means evil, harm, affliction, and what is disliked. The rest read it with a fatha as a verbal noun, and this is what Abu Ubayd and Abu Hatim chose in this verse. ﴿And among the bedouins﴾, the Asad, Ghatafan, and Tamim, and the bedouins who live near Madinah. Then He made an exception, saying: ﴿And among the bedouins is he who believes in Allah and the Last Day﴾. Mujahid said: They are the Banu Muqarrin of Muzaynah. Al-Dahhak said: It means Abdullah dhu al-Najadayn and his people.

Al-Kalbi said: Aslam and Ghifar and the Banu Juhaynah. ﴿And takes what he spends as means of nearness [qurubat] to Allah﴾, plural of qarabah, ﴿and [means of] the prayers of the Messenger﴾, meaning his supplication and his seeking forgiveness. ﴿Unquestionably, they are a means of nearness for them. Allah will admit them into His mercy. Indeed, Allah is Forgiving and Merciful.﴾

﴿And the foremost [in precedence] among the Muhajirun [those who emigrated] and the Ansar [the Helpers]﴾: ﴿the Muhajirun﴾ are those who emigrated from their people and kin and left their homes and homelands; ﴿the Ansar﴾ are those who supported the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) against his enemies from the people of Madinah and strengthened his companions, and they had believed two years before the Muhajirun came to them. ﴿And those who followed them in good conduct﴾, meaning those who followed their path in faith, emigration, and support until the Day of Resurrection.

Ata said: They are those who mention the Muhajirun with loyalty, compassion, and supplication, mention their having been neighbors, and ask Allah to unite them with them.

It is narrated that Umar ibn al-Khattab (may Allah be pleased with him) recited: "as-sabiqun al-awwalun min al-muhajirina wa-l-ansari alladhina ittaba'uhum bi-ihsanin," with *al-ansari* in the nominative and the *wa* dropped from *alladhina*. Ubayy ibn Ka'b said to him: "It is actually *wa-l-ansari wa-lladhina ittaba'uhum bi-ihsan*," and he repeated it three times. Umar said to him: "By Allah, I recited it to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) as *wa-lladhina ittaba'uhum bi-ihsan*, and on that day you were an old man living in Baqi' al-Gharqad." Ubayy said: "You memorized and we forgot; you were free and we were busy; you witnessed and we were absent." Then Umar asked Ubayy: "Are the Ansar among them?" He said: "Yes, and the Khattab family was not included." Hence Umar said: "I used to think that we had attained a rank that no one after us would reach." Ubayy said: "Yes. The confirmation of that is the beginning of Surah al-Jumu'ah, the middle of Surah al-Hashr, and the end of Surah al-Anfal."

[Regarding] His saying: ﴿And others among them who have not yet joined them﴾ to the end of it; and His saying: ﴿And those who came after them﴾ to the end of the verse; and His saying: ﴿And those who believed after [that] and emigrated and fought with you — those are of you﴾.

Al-Hasan, Salam, and Ya'qub read *wal-ansaru* in the nominative, coordinated with *al-sabiqun*, and did not include them among the foremost; they assigned precedence to the Muhajirun only, and they took *al-muqasah* [sic] as a coordinated subject following the Muhajirun.

The scholars differed about who the "foremost, the first" are. Abu Musa al-Ash'ari, Sa'id ibn al-Musayyab, Qatadah, and Ibn Sirin said: They are those who prayed toward both qiblahs.

Ata ibn Abi Rabah said: They are those who witnessed Badr.

Al-Sha'bi said: They are those who witnessed the Pledge of Ridwan [Bay'at al-Ridwan].

They also differed about who first believed in the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) after his wife Khadijah bint Khuwaylid, although they agreed that she was the first to believe in the Prophet (ﷺ) and affirm him.

Some of them said: The first male to believe in the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and pray with him was Ali ibn Abi Talib (may Allah be pleased with him). This is the view of Ibn Abbas, Jabir, Zayd ibn Arqam, Muhammad ibn al-Munkadir, Rabi'ah al-Ra'y, and Abu Hazim al-Madani.

Al-Kalbi said: Ali embraced Islam when he was nine years old. Mujahid and Ibn Ishaq said: He embraced Islam when he was ten years old.

Ibn Ishaq said: Abdullah ibn Abi Najih narrated to me from Mujahid, who said: Among the favors of Allah upon Ali ibn Abi Talib (may Allah be pleased with him), and what Allah did for him and intended for him of good, was that the Quraysh were struck by a severe famine, and Abu Talib had a large family. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said to al-Abbas, who was one of the wealthiest of the Banu Hashim: "O Abbas, your brother Abu Talib has a large family, and people have been struck by this famine that you see. Come, let us lighten his burden of his dependents: I will take one of his sons, and you take one of his sons, and we will take care of them for him."

Al-Abbas said: "Yes." So they went until they came to Abu Talib [and said: "We want to lighten your burden of your dependents until people are relieved of what they are in." Abu Talib said to them]: "If you leave Aqil to me, do as you wish." So the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) took Ali (may Allah honor his face) and embraced him, and al-Abbas took Ja'far and embraced him. Ali (may Allah be pleased with him) remained with the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) until Allah sent him as a prophet, and Ali followed him. He believed in him and affirmed him, and Ja'far remained with al-Abbas (may Allah be pleased with him) until he embraced Islam and became independent of him [48] [Tarikh al-Tabari 2/58; al-Mustadrak 3/576; what is between the brackets we have inserted from the sources].

Isma'il ibn Ayyash ibn Ufayf narrated from his father, from his grandfather Ufayf, who said: I was a merchant. I came to Makkah during the days of Hajj and stayed with al-Abbas ibn Abd al-Muttalib, who was my friend. He used to travel to Yemen to buy cotton and sell it during the season. While I and al-Abbas were at Mina, a young man came when the sun had risen high in the sky. He looked up at the sky, then faced the Ka'bah and stood facing it. Then a boy came and stood on his right. Soon a woman came and stood behind them. The young man bowed, the boy bowed, and the woman bowed. Then the young man prostrated, and they prostrated with him. Then the boy and the woman rose. I said: "O Abbas, this is a great matter!" He said: "A great matter." I said: "Woe to you! What is this?" He said: "This is the son of my brother, Muhammad ibn Abdullah ibn Abd al-Muttalib. He claims that Allah the Exalted has sent him as a messenger, and that the treasures of Khosrow and Caesar will be opened to him. This boy is the son of my brother Ali ibn Abi Talib, and this woman is Khadijah bint Khuwaylid, the wife of Muhammad. They have followed him in his religion. There is no one on the face of the earth, all of it, who follows this religion except these."

Abdullah al-Kindi said, after Islam had taken firm root in his heart: "Would that I had been the fourth." It is related that Abu Talib said to Ali (may Allah be pleased with him): "My son, what is this that you are upon?" He said: "I have believed in Allah and His Messenger, and I affirm him in what he has brought, and I have prayed with him for Allah's sake." He said to him: "As for Muhammad, he calls only to good, so hold fast to him" [Tarikh al-Tabari 2/58; Uyun al-Athar by Ibn Sayyid al-Nas 1/126; Dhakha'ir al-Uqba, p. 60].

Abdullah ibn Musa narrated from al-Ala' ibn Salih, from al-Minhal ibn Amr, from Abbad ibn Abdullah, who said: I heard Ali say: "I am the servant of Allah and the brother of His Messenger, and I am the greatest Siddiq. No one will say this after me except a liar and a fabricator. I prayed seven years before the people" [Sunan Ibn Majah 1/44; al-Mustadrak 3/112; al-Musannaf of Ibn Abi Shaybah 7/498].

Some of them said: The first to embrace Islam after Khadijah was Abu Bakr (may Allah be pleased with him). This is the view of Ibrahim al-Nakha'i and a group, and what indicates it is what Abu Umamah al-Bahili narrated from Amr ibn Anbasah, who said: "I came to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) while he was staying at Ukaz. I said: 'O Messenger of Allah, who has followed you in this matter?' He (ﷺ) said: 'Two men followed me: a free man and a slave, Abu Bakr and Bilal.'" So I embraced Islam at that time, and I saw myself then as a quarter of Islam.

He said: I heard Abu al-Qasim al-Habibi say: I heard Abu al-Hasan Ali ibn Abdullah al-Badakhshi say: I heard Abu Hurayrah Muzahim ibn Muhammad ibn Shadhah al-Kushi say: I heard Ghiyath ibn Mu'adh say: I heard Waki' ibn al-Jarrah say, from Isma'il ibn Khalid, from al-Shafahi, who said: A man said to Ibn Abbas: "Who was the first of people to embrace Islam?" He said: "Abu Bakr (may Allah be pleased with him). Have you not heard the words of Hassan ibn Thabit:

When you remember a sorrow of a trustworthy brother,
then remember your brother Abu Bakr for what he did.
The best of creation, the purest and most just of them after the Prophet,
and the most faithful in what he carried.
The second, the follower, whose station is praised,
and the first of people who affirmed the Messengers."
[al-Musannaf of Ibn Abi Shaybah 8/44; Tafsir al-Qurtubi 8/236; Tarikh Baghdad 15/51.]

Some of them said: The first man to embrace Islam was Zayd ibn Harithah. This is the view of al-Zuhri, Sulayman ibn Yasar, Urwah ibn al-Zubayr, and Imran ibn Abi Anas. Ishaq ibn Ibrahim al-Hanzali combined the reports and said: The first man to embrace Islam was Abu Bakr; the first woman was Khadijah; the first youth was Ali; and the first freedman was Zayd ibn Harithah.

Ibn Ishaq said: When Abu Bakr al-Siddiq (may Allah be pleased with him) embraced Islam, he made his Islam known and called to Allah and to His Messenger. He said: Abu Bakr was a man who was agreeable to his people, loving and easygoing, and he was the most knowledgeable of the Quraysh about their genealogies, and the most knowledgeable of the Quraysh about them and about what had occurred among them of good or evil. He was a man [of noble character] with good manners and generosity. The men of his people revered him and came to him for many matters because of his knowledge, his experience, and his good company. So he began to call to Islam those among his people whom he trusted, who frequented him and sat with him. Through him, it is reported to me, there embraced Islam Uthman ibn Affan, al-Zubayr ibn al-Awwam, Abd al-Rahman ibn Awf, Sa'd ibn Abi Waqqas, and Talhah ibn Ubayd Allah. He brought them to the Messenger of Allah (may Allah be pleased with him) when they responded to him, and they embraced Islam and prayed. These eight men were the first of the Muhajirun to precede others into Islam.

As for the foremost of the Ansar, they were the people of the First Pledge of al-Aqabah, who were seven, and those of the Second, who were seventy, and those who believed when Abu Zurarah Mus'ab ibn Umayr ibn Hashim ibn Abd al-Dar came to them and taught them the Qur'an. He was the first to gather the prayer in Madinah. The Ansar loved him, and Sa'd ibn Mu'adh, Amr ibn al-Jamuh, and all of the Banu Abd al-Ashhal, along with a group of women and children, embraced Islam through him. Mus'ab ibn Umayr was the standard-bearer of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) at Badr and at Uhud. At Uhud, when the people fled, he protected the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) with his own self, and the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) remained until the arrowheads penetrated his body. Mus'ab was martyred that day. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "I reckon him with Allah. I have never seen anyone more noble than him. I saw him in Makkah wearing two cloaks, and he did not know their value, and the straps of his sandals were of gold. On his right were two boys, and on his left were two boys, and each of them held a bowl of food, eating and feeding the people. Then Allah preferred him with martyrdom" [50] [see Tafsir al-Qurtubi 19/208].

When the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was given a gift of a rare fruit, he would hold it for Mus'ab ibn Umayr. Then Allah revealed concerning him: ﴿But as for one who feared the standing before his Lord﴾ [Surah al-Nazi'at 40], the verse.

On the day of Badr, his brother Abu Ghadir ibn Umayr was taken captive and said: "I am Abu Ghadir ibn Umayr, the brother of Mus'ab." They did not tighten his bonds among the captives, and they said: "This is the road; go wherever you wish." He said: "I fear that Quraysh will kill me." They took him to [...] [unreadable text] and he would extend his hand for the bread and the dates. He would reach for the dates and leave the bread, though bread was more precious to the people of Madinah, and dates were more precious to the people of Makkah. When morning came, they told Mus'ab ibn Umayr and said to him: "Your brother is with us," and they informed him of what they had done to him. He said: "He is no brother of mine, and there is no honor in him. Tighten his bonds, for his mother is the richest of the people of al-Batha in ornaments." His mother sent someone to ransom him. Then he came out on the day of Uhud. When he saw his brother Mus'ab ibn Umayr, he said to himself: "By Allah, no one but me will kill you," and he did not stop until he killed him. Concerning him Allah the Exalted revealed: ﴿And as for one who transgressed and preferred the worldly life, indeed Hellfire will be the refuge﴾ [Surah al-Nazi'at 37]. Then He gathered them together in reward, saying: ﴿Allah is pleased with them, and they are pleased with Him, and He has prepared for them gardens beneath which rivers flow, abiding therein forever. That is the great achievement.﴾ The people of Makkah read: "min tahtiha al-anhar" [with the preposition *min*] [Ibn Kathir, cited in Zad al-Masir 3/334], and so it is in their codices [Mus'af], *khalidina fiha abadan*. That is the great triumph.

Al-Hasan ibn al-Fadl said: The difference between them is that His saying, "Rivers flow beneath them," means that rivers flow beneath the trees. His saying, "flow from beneath them" (﴿تجري من تحتها﴾), means that water springs up from beneath them and then flows beneath the trees.

It is related regarding this verse that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said to Mu'adh ibn Jabal: "Where are the foremost (al-sabiqun)?" Mu'adh said: "Some people have passed on." He said: "The foremost are those who are absorbed in the remembrance of Allah. Whoever wishes to graze in the gardens of Paradise, let him increase his remembrance of Allah, exalted is He."

﴿And among those around you of the Bedouins are hypocrites﴾. It was revealed concerning the tribes of Muzaynah, Juhaynah, Aslam, Ashja', and Ghifar, whose dwellings were around Madinah.

﴿And among the people of Madinah﴾: there is ellipsis (ikhtisar) and an implied element (idmar) in this, its meaning being: "And among the people of Madinah are people who have become hardened (marridu) in hypocrisy," meaning they became accustomed to it and were trained in it. It is said: "So-and-so rebelled (tamarrada) against his Lord," and "he became hardened (marada) in his disobedience," meaning he persisted in it, remained steadfast upon it, and habituated himself to it. From this come "tamrid" and "marid" (a rebellious, obstinate one). In the proverb: "The rebel has rebelled, and the runaway has grown mighty."

Ibn Ishaq said: they persisted in it and refused anything else. Qatadah and Ibn Zayd and Aban ibn Taghlib said: they remained upon it and did not repent as the others repented. The poet recited:

"The people became hardened in their clan,
People of transgression, misguidance, and wickedness."

﴿You do not know them, O Muhammad; We know them.﴾ Qatadah said regarding this verse: What is the matter with people who burden themselves regarding others, saying, "So-and-so is in Paradise and so-and-so is in the Fire"? Yet when you ask one of them about himself, he says: "I do not know." Tell me, do you know yourself better than you know the deeds of people? You have taken upon yourself something that the prophets before you did not undertake. The Prophet of Allah Nuh (peace be upon him) said: ﴿And I have no knowledge of what they used to do﴾. And the Prophet of Allah Shu'ayb (peace be upon him) said: ﴿And I am not a guardian over you﴾. And Allah said to His Prophet (peace be upon him): ﴿You do not know them; We know them. We will punish them twice.﴾ They differed regarding these two punishments.

It is related from Abu Malik, from Ibn Abbas, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) stood delivering a sermon on Friday and said: "Go out, O so-and-so, for you are a hypocrite. Go out, O so-and-so, for you are a hypocrite." So he removed from the mosque some people and exposed them. This is the first punishment, and the second is the punishment of the grave.

Mujahid said: [the two punishments are] with hunger and the punishment of the grave. Also from him: with hunger and killing. Also from him: with hunger twice. Also from him: with fear and killing.

Qatadah said: the punishment of this world and the punishment of the grave, and in this regard is the story of the twelve in the hadith of Hudhayfah.

Ibn Zayd said: the first time is the calamities in wealth and children, and the other time is in Hell.

Ibn Abbas said: the first time is the establishment of the prescribed punishments (hudud) upon them, and the second is the punishment of the grave.

Al-Hasan said: one of the two times is the taking of zakat from their wealth, and the other is the punishment of the grave. Its explanation is in Surah al-Nahl: ﴿Then they will be returned to a great punishment﴾.

Ibn Ishaq said: it is what enters upon them in Islam, and their entry without sincere intention; then their punishment in the graves when they come to them; then the great punishment in the Hereafter, and abiding eternally therein.

In some tafsirs: the first is the angels striking their faces and their backs at the taking of their souls, and the second is the punishment of the grave.

It was said: its explanation is in Surah al-Nahl: ﴿We will increase them in punishment upon punishment﴾.

Muqatil ibn Hayyan said: the first is by the sword on the day of Badr, and the second is at death.

Ma'mar, from al-Zuhri, from al-Hasan, said: "The punishment of the Prophet and the punishment of Allah." By "the punishment of the Prophet (ﷺ)" is meant His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Cursed, wherever they are found, they will be seized and killed with a [terrible] killing﴾.

'Ata said: [the two punishments are] illnesses in this world and in the Hereafter. For whoever among the believers falls ill, Allah expiates his sins and purifies his wrongdoings, replacing for him flesh from his flesh and much blood from his blood, and granting him a great reward. And whoever among the hypocrites falls ill, Allah increases him in hypocrisy, sin, and weakness, as He said in this surah: ﴿Do they not see that they are tested every year?﴾, meaning they become ill every year once or twice, then they are returned to a great, severe, and dreadful punishment.

Al-Rabi' said: the afflictions of this world and the punishment of the Hereafter. Then "they will be returned to a great punishment," which is the punishment of Hell.

Isma'il ibn Ziyad said: one of the two punishments is the striking of the angels upon the faces and the backs, and the second is at the Resurrection, when a guardian of the Fire will be assigned to them.

Al-Dahhak said: once in the grave and once in the Fire. It was also said: the first time was by burning their mosque, the Mosque of Harm, and the second by burning them in the Fire of Hell. It was also said: once by the spending of their wealth being taken, and once by their being killed by the sword if they manifested what was in their hearts.

﴿And others﴾: meaning, and among the people of Madinah, or among the Bedouins, others; and it does not refer back to the hypocrites. ﴿Have acknowledged (i'tarafu)﴾: they admitted to you and to their Lord. ﴿They mixed a righteous deed﴾, which is their admission and repentance, ﴿and another wicked﴾: meaning with a wicked deed. The waw (و) is placed in the position of the ba' (ب), just as one says: "The water mixed with the filth," meaning with the filth; and "I mixed the water and the milk," meaning with the milk. The wicked deed is their staying behind from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and their abandonment of jihad.

﴿It may be that Allah will turn to them in forgiveness﴾. "Asa" (it may be) and "la'alla" (perhaps) from Allah are obligatory, and both are particles of expectation.

﴿Indeed, Allah is Forgiving and Merciful.﴾

This verse was revealed concerning a people who had stayed behind from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) in the Battle of Tabuk, then regretted it and felt ashamed. They said: "We remain in shade and shelter with the women, while the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) is in jihad! By Allah, we will bind ourselves with chains in our hands until the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) himself releases us or punishes us." They tied themselves to the pillars of the mosque. When the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) returned, he passed by them and saw them, and said: "Who are these?" They said: "They stayed behind from you." So they made a covenant with Allah that they would not release themselves until you are the one who releases them and excuses them. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "I swear by Allah, I will not release them nor excuse them until I am commanded to release them. They turned away from me and stayed behind from the expedition with the Muslims." Then Allah revealed this verse. When it was revealed, the Prophet (ﷺ) sent for them, released them, and excused them. When they were released, they said: "O Messenger of Allah, this is our wealth which kept us away from you; so give charity from it on our behalf, purify us, and seek forgiveness for us."

The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "I have not been commanded to take anything from your wealth." Then Allah, mighty and majestic, revealed: ﴿Take from their wealth a charity﴾, the verse.

They differed regarding the number of these people and their names. Ali ibn Abi Talhah related from Ibn Abbas, who said: They were ten men, among them Abu Lubabah. Sa'id ibn Jubayr and Zayd ibn Aslam said: Abu [Muniyah]: among them were Hilal, Abu Lubabah, Kirdam, Mirdas, and Abu Qays. Qatadah and al-Dahhak said: They were seven, among them Jadd ibn Qays, Abu Lubabah, Judham, and Aws, all of them from the Ansar.

'Atiyyah said from Ibn Abbas: They were five, one of whom was Abu Lubabah. Others said: it was revealed concerning Abu Lubabah, and they differed regarding his sin. Mujahid said: this verse was revealed concerning Abu Lubabah when he said to the Banu Qurayzah: "If you come down to his judgment, it is slaughter," and he pointed to his throat. The story has passed in Surah al-Anfal. He regretted it and repented, and he admitted his sin, so Allah, mighty and majestic, revealed this verse.

Al-Zuhri said: It was revealed concerning his staying behind from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) in the Battle of Tabuk. He tied himself to a pillar and said: "By Allah, I will not free myself from it, nor taste food or drink, until I die or Allah accepts my repentance." He remained seven days without tasting food or drink, until he fell unconscious. Then Allah, exalted is He, revealed: ﴿And others have acknowledged their sins﴾, the verse. It was said to him: "Allah has accepted your repentance, O Abu Lubabah." He said: "By Allah, I will not free myself until the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) is the one who frees me." So the Prophet (ﷺ) came and untied him with his own hand. Then Abu Lubabah said: "O Messenger of Allah, part of my repentance is that I should abandon the house of my people in which I committed the sin, and that I should strip myself of all my wealth as charity to Allah and His Messenger." He said: "It suffices you, O Abu Lubabah, to give a third." [Al-Tabari, Jami' al-Bayan.]

They all said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) took a third of their wealth and left two-thirds, because Allah, mighty and majestic, said: ﴿Take from their wealth﴾ and did not say "their wealth" (in full), so he did not take all of it.

Al-Hasan and Qatadah said: these were other than the three who stayed behind, [and the charity] purifies them from their sins by it. The reading with the raised vowel (dammah) is a circumstantial clause (hal), not a response (jawab), meaning: ﴿Take from their wealth a charity﴾ being purifying and cleansing, like the saying of al-Hutay'ah:

"Whenever you come to him, seeking the light of his fire,
You will find the best fire and the best station with him."

Maslamah ibn Muharib read "tutahhiruhum wa tuzakkihim" with the jussive, as a response (jawab). Al-Hasan read "tutahhiruhum" (with a light form from "atahhara"), and "wa tuzakkihim," meaning he purifies them. It was also said: he sets them right. It was also said: he elevates them from the stations of the hypocrites to the stations of the sincere. It was also said: "it" refers to their wealth.

﴿And pray for them﴾: meaning seek forgiveness for them and supplicate for them. It was said: it is the saying of the official who takes the charity: "May Allah reward you for what you have given, and bless you in what you have kept." Prayer (salah) in the language means supplication, and from it is the saying of the Prophet (ﷺ): "When one of you is invited to a meal, let him accept; if he is fasting, let him pray (fa-l-yusalli)," meaning let him supplicate. Al-A'sha said:

"The wind meets its wine jar,
And he prays over its jar and is marked (with its sign)."

Meaning he supplicated for it safety and blessing.

He also said:

"My daughter says, when I have come near to departing:
'O Lord, keep away from my father illnesses and pain.'
Upon you is like what you prayed, so sleep,
For the side of a man has a resting place."

﴿Indeed, your prayer﴾: the people of Kufa read "ṣalātuka" in the singular here and in Surah Hud (﴿a-ṣalātuka﴾), and "wa-l-mu'minīn" with a suppressed (idmar). Abu Ubayd said: because "salah" is one of the prayers. This was related from Ibn Abbas. Do you not hear Allah saying: ﴿Establish the prayer﴾? This is the prayer of eternity, and "ṣalawāt" is for the plural, as in the saying: "I prayed the prayers (ṣalawāt) four and five." The others read all of them in the plural, and Abu Hatim chose this. He said: Whoever claims that "ṣalawāt" is from "ṣalāh" because the plural with the feminine suffix (-āt) is rare, has erred, for Allah, exalted is He, said: ﴿The words of Allah would not be exhausted﴾ and ﴿and she affirmed the words of her Lord﴾; He did not mean what is few.

﴿Is a comfort for them﴾: Ibn Abbas said: a mercy for them. Qatadah said: a dignity for them. Al-Kalbi said: a reassurance for them, that Allah has accepted their repentance. Mu'adh said: a purification for them from you. Abu 'Ubaydah said: a steadying.

﴿And Allah is Hearing, Knowing.﴾

Shu'bah, from 'Amr ibn Murrah, from 'Abd Allah ibn Abi Awfa, who was one of the companions of the tree (of the Pledge of Ridwan): that the Prophet (ﷺ), when people came to him with their charities, would say: "O Allah, send your blessings upon them." When I came to him with my charity, he said: "O Allah, send your blessings upon Abu Awfa." Ibn Abbas said: This is not an obligatory charity (zakat al-fard); it is like the charity of expiation for an oath. 'Ikrimah said: it is the obligatory charity. When the repentance of these people was revealed, those who had not sinned and had stayed behind said: "These were with us yesterday; they did not speak nor sit with us. What is the matter with them?" Then Allah, mighty and majestic, revealed: ﴿Do they not know that it is Allah who accepts repentance from His servants﴾, the verse.

The meaning of "taking the charities" is accepting them.

Al-Shafi'i, from Sufyan ibn 'Uyaynah, from Ibn 'Ajlan, from Sa'id ibn Yasar, from Abu Hurayrah, who said: I heard Abu al-Qasim (ﷺ) say: "By Him in whose hand is my soul, no servant gives a charity from the earnings of his livelihood, and Allah accepts nothing but what is good, and it does not ascend to heaven except that it is placed in the hand of the Most Merciful, who nurtures it as one of you nurtures his foal, until a morsel will come on the Day of Resurrection as great as a mountain." Then he recited: ﴿That Allah is the One who accepts repentance from His servants﴾, and the confirmation of this is in the revealed Book of Allah: ﴿Allah deprives usury of blessing and gives increase for charities﴾ to His saying ﴿for what you used to do﴾.

Mujahid said: this is a warning (wa'id) to them.

It is related in a report: If a servant were to come with his deed to a rock that has no door and no window, his deed would come out to the people, whatever it may be.

Commentary of al-Tha'alibi (al-Jawahir al-Hisan) on surah 9, verses 92–105 (part 1 of 2):

Qatadah said: It was revealed concerning Ayidh ibn Amr and his companions. Al-Dahhak said: It was revealed concerning Abdullah ibn Za'id, who is Ibn Umm Maktum, and he was blind. He said: "O Prophet of Allah, I am an old man, blind in sight, of little means, and frail of body, and I have no means. Do I have a concession to stay behind from jihad?" The Prophet (ﷺ) remained silent, so Allah the Exalted revealed this verse: ﴿Nor [is there blame] upon those who come to you to be provided with mounts, [and] you say, "I find not that upon which to mount you"...﴾

It was revealed concerning the "Weepers," who were seven: Ma'qil ibn Yasar, Sakhr ibn Khansa' [see Usd al-Ghabah 3/13, where he is mentioned as Sakhr ibn Sulayman; in al-Isabah, he is Sakhr ibn Umayyah ibn Khansa'], who is the one who had intercourse with his wife in Ramadan, and the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) instructed him to make expiation [Ibn Hajar said in al-Isabah (3/332, biography no. 4064): "The well-known view is that the person in the story of intercourse was Salamah ibn Sakhr, so perhaps this is an error by al-Tha'labi"]; Abdullah ibn Ka'b al-Ansari, Ulbah ibn Zayd al-Ansari, Salim ibn Umayr, Tha'labah ibn Ghanamah, and Abdullah ibn Ma'qil. They came to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and said: "O Prophet of Allah, Allah the Mighty and Majestic has called us to go out with you. So carry us on the thin-soled shoes and the patched sandals, and we will campaign with you." The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "I do not find anything upon which to carry you." So they turned away weeping [Asbab al-Nuzul, p. 174]. That is the meaning of His saying: ﴿They turned back while their eyes overflowed with tears, out of grief that they could not find what they could spend﴾.

Mujahid said: This verse was revealed [concerning Abdullah, Abd al-Rahman, Aqil, al-Nu'man, and Suwayd] [and Sinan] [Note from the margin of Tafsir al-Qurtubi; in Asbab al-Nuzul it reads: concerning the Banu Muqarrin: Ma'qil, Suwayd, and al-Nu'man; the manuscript is damaged]: ﴿The blame is only upon those who ask your permission while they are rich...﴾ [to the end of the verse]. ﴿They will make excuses to you when you return to them. Say, "Make no excuse; we will never believe you. Allah has already informed us of your news. And Allah will see your deeds, and [so will] His Messenger..."﴾ Afterward: will you repent of your hypocrisy or will you persist in it? ﴿Then you will be returned to the Knower of the unseen and the witnessed, and He will inform you of what you used to do﴾, of good and evil. ﴿They will swear by Allah to you when you return [i.e., have come back] to them, that you may turn away from them﴾ [that you may overlook their sin], and not rebuke or reprimand them. ﴿So turn away from them﴾, leave them and what they have chosen for themselves of affair and disobedience. ﴿Indeed, they are impure﴾, i.e., unclean. Ata said: Their deeds are unclean. ﴿And their refuge is Hell, as recompense for what they used to earn.﴾

Ibn Abbas said: It was revealed concerning Jadd ibn Qays, Mu'attib ibn Qushayr, and their companions, who were eighty men among the hypocrites. The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "When they come to Madinah, do not sit with them or speak to them" [47] [see Zad al-Masir 3/331].

Muqatil said: It was revealed concerning Abdullah ibn Ubayy, who swore to the Prophet (ﷺ) by the One besides whom there is no god that he would not be pleased with them after this, and that he would be with him against his enemy; and he asked the Prophet (ﷺ) to be pleased with him. So Allah the Mighty and Majestic revealed this verse: ﴿They swear to you to please you. But if you should be pleased with them, indeed Allah is not pleased with the defiantly disobedient people.﴾

﴿The bedouins are stronger in disbelief and hypocrisy﴾, meaning the people of the desert, ﴿and more likely not to know the limits of what Allah has revealed to His Messenger. And Allah is Knowing and Wise.﴾ Qatadah said: They have less knowledge of the sunnah.

Al-A'mash narrated from Ibrahim, who said: A bedouin sat with Zayd ibn Suhan while he was with his companions, and his hand had been injured on the day of Nahawand. The bedouin said: "By Allah, I do not know: your speech pleases me, but your hand frightens me." He said: "Which of my hands? It is the left." The bedouin said: "By Allah, I do not know whether they cut off the right or the left [hand]?" Zayd ibn Suhan said: "Allah has spoken the truth: ﴿The bedouins are stronger in disbelief and hypocrisy﴾ [the verse]" [Jami al-Bayan 11/6].

﴿And among the bedouins is he who takes what he spends as a loss﴾. Ata said: He does not expect reward for his giving, nor does he fear loss by withholding; he spends only out of fear and show-off. ﴿And he awaits misfortunes to befall you﴾, meaning the vicissitudes of time, which sometimes bring good and sometimes evil. He said: [He waits] for when time turns against you, so that the Messenger dies and the polytheists prevail. ﴿Upon them is the cycle of evil.﴾ Ibn Kathir, Ibn Muhsin, Mujahid, and Abu Amr read *al-saw'* with a damma on the sin here and in Surah al-Fath; it means evil, harm, affliction, and what is disliked. The rest read it with a fatha as a verbal noun, and this is what Abu Ubayd and Abu Hatim chose in this verse. ﴿And among the bedouins﴾, the Asad, Ghatafan, and Tamim, and the bedouins who live near Madinah. Then He made an exception, saying: ﴿And among the bedouins is he who believes in Allah and the Last Day﴾. Mujahid said: They are the Banu Muqarrin of Muzaynah. Al-Dahhak said: It means Abdullah dhu al-Najadayn and his people.

Al-Kalbi said: Aslam and Ghifar and the Banu Juhaynah. ﴿And takes what he spends as means of nearness [qurubat] to Allah﴾, plural of qarabah, ﴿and [means of] the prayers of the Messenger﴾, meaning his supplication and his seeking forgiveness. ﴿Unquestionably, they are a means of nearness for them. Allah will admit them into His mercy. Indeed, Allah is Forgiving and Merciful.﴾

﴿And the foremost [in precedence] among the Muhajirun [those who emigrated] and the Ansar [the Helpers]﴾: ﴿the Muhajirun﴾ are those who emigrated from their people and kin and left their homes and homelands; ﴿the Ansar﴾ are those who supported the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) against his enemies from the people of Madinah and strengthened his companions, and they had believed two years before the Muhajirun came to them. ﴿And those who followed them in good conduct﴾, meaning those who followed their path in faith, emigration, and support until the Day of Resurrection.

Ata said: They are those who mention the Muhajirun with loyalty, compassion, and supplication, mention their having been neighbors, and ask Allah to unite them with them.

It is narrated that Umar ibn al-Khattab (may Allah be pleased with him) recited: "as-sabiqun al-awwalun min al-muhajirina wa-l-ansari alladhina ittaba'uhum bi-ihsanin," with *al-ansari* in the nominative and the *wa* dropped from *alladhina*. Ubayy ibn Ka'b said to him: "It is actually *wa-l-ansari wa-lladhina ittaba'uhum bi-ihsan*," and he repeated it three times. Umar said to him: "By Allah, I recited it to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) as *wa-lladhina ittaba'uhum bi-ihsan*, and on that day you were an old man living in Baqi' al-Gharqad." Ubayy said: "You memorized and we forgot; you were free and we were busy; you witnessed and we were absent." Then Umar asked Ubayy: "Are the Ansar among them?" He said: "Yes, and the Khattab family was not included." Hence Umar said: "I used to think that we had attained a rank that no one after us would reach." Ubayy said: "Yes. The confirmation of that is the beginning of Surah al-Jumu'ah, the middle of Surah al-Hashr, and the end of Surah al-Anfal."

[Regarding] His saying: ﴿And others among them who have not yet joined them﴾ to the end of it; and His saying: ﴿And those who came after them﴾ to the end of the verse; and His saying: ﴿And those who believed after [that] and emigrated and fought with you — those are of you﴾.

Al-Hasan, Salam, and Ya'qub read *wal-ansaru* in the nominative, coordinated with *al-sabiqun*, and did not include them among the foremost; they assigned precedence to the Muhajirun only, and they took *al-muqasah* [sic] as a coordinated subject following the Muhajirun.

The scholars differed about who the "foremost, the first" are. Abu Musa al-Ash'ari, Sa'id ibn al-Musayyab, Qatadah, and Ibn Sirin said: They are those who prayed toward both qiblahs.

Ata ibn Abi Rabah said: They are those who witnessed Badr.

Al-Sha'bi said: They are those who witnessed the Pledge of Ridwan [Bay'at al-Ridwan].

They also differed about who first believed in the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) after his wife Khadijah bint Khuwaylid, although they agreed that she was the first to believe in the Prophet (ﷺ) and affirm him.

Some of them said: The first male to believe in the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and pray with him was Ali ibn Abi Talib (may Allah be pleased with him). This is the view of Ibn Abbas, Jabir, Zayd ibn Arqam, Muhammad ibn al-Munkadir, Rabi'ah al-Ra'y, and Abu Hazim al-Madani.

Al-Kalbi said: Ali embraced Islam when he was nine years old. Mujahid and Ibn Ishaq said: He embraced Islam when he was ten years old.

Ibn Ishaq said: Abdullah ibn Abi Najih narrated to me from Mujahid, who said: Among the favors of Allah upon Ali ibn Abi Talib (may Allah be pleased with him), and what Allah did for him and intended for him of good, was that the Quraysh were struck by a severe famine, and Abu Talib had a large family. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said to al-Abbas, who was one of the wealthiest of the Banu Hashim: "O Abbas, your brother Abu Talib has a large family, and people have been struck by this famine that you see. Come, let us lighten his burden of his dependents: I will take one of his sons, and you take one of his sons, and we will take care of them for him."

Al-Abbas said: "Yes." So they went until they came to Abu Talib [and said: "We want to lighten your burden of your dependents until people are relieved of what they are in." Abu Talib said to them]: "If you leave Aqil to me, do as you wish." So the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) took Ali (may Allah honor his face) and embraced him, and al-Abbas took Ja'far and embraced him. Ali (may Allah be pleased with him) remained with the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) until Allah sent him as a prophet, and Ali followed him. He believed in him and affirmed him, and Ja'far remained with al-Abbas (may Allah be pleased with him) until he embraced Islam and became independent of him [48] [Tarikh al-Tabari 2/58; al-Mustadrak 3/576; what is between the brackets we have inserted from the sources].

Isma'il ibn Ayyash ibn Ufayf narrated from his father, from his grandfather Ufayf, who said: I was a merchant. I came to Makkah during the days of Hajj and stayed with al-Abbas ibn Abd al-Muttalib, who was my friend. He used to travel to Yemen to buy cotton and sell it during the season. While I and al-Abbas were at Mina, a young man came when the sun had risen high in the sky. He looked up at the sky, then faced the Ka'bah and stood facing it. Then a boy came and stood on his right. Soon a woman came and stood behind them. The young man bowed, the boy bowed, and the woman bowed. Then the young man prostrated, and they prostrated with him. Then the boy and the woman rose. I said: "O Abbas, this is a great matter!" He said: "A great matter." I said: "Woe to you! What is this?" He said: "This is the son of my brother, Muhammad ibn Abdullah ibn Abd al-Muttalib. He claims that Allah the Exalted has sent him as a messenger, and that the treasures of Khosrow and Caesar will be opened to him. This boy is the son of my brother Ali ibn Abi Talib, and this woman is Khadijah bint Khuwaylid, the wife of Muhammad. They have followed him in his religion. There is no one on the face of the earth, all of it, who follows this religion except these."

Abdullah al-Kindi said, after Islam had taken firm root in his heart: "Would that I had been the fourth." It is related that Abu Talib said to Ali (may Allah be pleased with him): "My son, what is this that you are upon?" He said: "I have believed in Allah and His Messenger, and I affirm him in what he has brought, and I have prayed with him for Allah's sake." He said to him: "As for Muhammad, he calls only to good, so hold fast to him" [Tarikh al-Tabari 2/58; Uyun al-Athar by Ibn Sayyid al-Nas 1/126; Dhakha'ir al-Uqba, p. 60].

Abdullah ibn Musa narrated from al-Ala' ibn Salih, from al-Minhal ibn Amr, from Abbad ibn Abdullah, who said: I heard Ali say: "I am the servant of Allah and the brother of His Messenger, and I am the greatest Siddiq. No one will say this after me except a liar and a fabricator. I prayed seven years before the people" [Sunan Ibn Majah 1/44; al-Mustadrak 3/112; al-Musannaf of Ibn Abi Shaybah 7/498].

Some of them said: The first to embrace Islam after Khadijah was Abu Bakr (may Allah be pleased with him). This is the view of Ibrahim al-Nakha'i and a group, and what indicates it is what Abu Umamah al-Bahili narrated from Amr ibn Anbasah, who said: "I came to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) while he was staying at Ukaz. I said: 'O Messenger of Allah, who has followed you in this matter?' He (ﷺ) said: 'Two men followed me: a free man and a slave, Abu Bakr and Bilal.'" So I embraced Islam at that time, and I saw myself then as a quarter of Islam.

He said: I heard Abu al-Qasim al-Habibi say: I heard Abu al-Hasan Ali ibn Abdullah al-Badakhshi say: I heard Abu Hurayrah Muzahim ibn Muhammad ibn Shadhah al-Kushi say: I heard Ghiyath ibn Mu'adh say: I heard Waki' ibn al-Jarrah say, from Isma'il ibn Khalid, from al-Shafahi, who said: A man said to Ibn Abbas: "Who was the first of people to embrace Islam?" He said: "Abu Bakr (may Allah be pleased with him). Have you not heard the words of Hassan ibn Thabit:

When you remember a sorrow of a trustworthy brother,
then remember your brother Abu Bakr for what he did.
The best of creation, the purest and most just of them after the Prophet,
and the most faithful in what he carried.
The second, the follower, whose station is praised,
and the first of people who affirmed the Messengers."
[al-Musannaf of Ibn Abi Shaybah 8/44; Tafsir al-Qurtubi 8/236; Tarikh Baghdad 15/51.]

Some of them said: The first man to embrace Islam was Zayd ibn Harithah. This is the view of al-Zuhri, Sulayman ibn Yasar, Urwah ibn al-Zubayr, and Imran ibn Abi Anas. Ishaq ibn Ibrahim al-Hanzali combined the reports and said: The first man to embrace Islam was Abu Bakr; the first woman was Khadijah; the first youth was Ali; and the first freedman was Zayd ibn Harithah.

Ibn Ishaq said: When Abu Bakr al-Siddiq (may Allah be pleased with him) embraced Islam, he made his Islam known and called to Allah and to His Messenger. He said: Abu Bakr was a man who was agreeable to his people, loving and easygoing, and he was the most knowledgeable of the Quraysh about their genealogies, and the most knowledgeable of the Quraysh about them and about what had occurred among them of good or evil. He was a man [of noble character] with good manners and generosity. The men of his people revered him and came to him for many matters because of his knowledge, his experience, and his good company. So he began to call to Islam those among his people whom he trusted, who frequented him and sat with him. Through him, it is reported to me, there embraced Islam Uthman ibn Affan, al-Zubayr ibn al-Awwam, Abd al-Rahman ibn Awf, Sa'd ibn Abi Waqqas, and Talhah ibn Ubayd Allah. He brought them to the Messenger of Allah (may Allah be pleased with him) when they responded to him, and they embraced Islam and prayed. These eight men were the first of the Muhajirun to precede others into Islam.

As for the foremost of the Ansar, they were the people of the First Pledge of al-Aqabah, who were seven, and those of the Second, who were seventy, and those who believed when Abu Zurarah Mus'ab ibn Umayr ibn Hashim ibn Abd al-Dar came to them and taught them the Qur'an. He was the first to gather the prayer in Madinah. The Ansar loved him, and Sa'd ibn Mu'adh, Amr ibn al-Jamuh, and all of the Banu Abd al-Ashhal, along with a group of women and children, embraced Islam through him. Mus'ab ibn Umayr was the standard-bearer of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) at Badr and at Uhud. At Uhud, when the people fled, he protected the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) with his own self, and the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) remained until the arrowheads penetrated his body. Mus'ab was martyred that day. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "I reckon him with Allah. I have never seen anyone more noble than him. I saw him in Makkah wearing two cloaks, and he did not know their value, and the straps of his sandals were of gold. On his right were two boys, and on his left were two boys, and each of them held a bowl of food, eating and feeding the people. Then Allah preferred him with martyrdom" [50] [see Tafsir al-Qurtubi 19/208].

When the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was given a gift of a rare fruit, he would hold it for Mus'ab ibn Umayr. Then Allah revealed concerning him: ﴿But as for one who feared the standing before his Lord﴾ [Surah al-Nazi'at 40], the verse.

On the day of Badr, his brother Abu Ghadir ibn Umayr was taken captive and said: "I am Abu Ghadir ibn Umayr, the brother of Mus'ab." They did not tighten his bonds among the captives, and they said: "This is the road; go wherever you wish." He said: "I fear that Quraysh will kill me." They took him to [...] [unreadable text] and he would extend his hand for the bread and the dates. He would reach for the dates and leave the bread, though bread was more precious to the people of Madinah, and dates were more precious to the people of Makkah. When morning came, they told Mus'ab ibn Umayr and said to him: "Your brother is with us," and they informed him of what they had done to him. He said: "He is no brother of mine, and there is no honor in him. Tighten his bonds, for his mother is the richest of the people of al-Batha in ornaments." His mother sent someone to ransom him. Then he came out on the day of Uhud. When he saw his brother Mus'ab ibn Umayr, he said to himself: "By Allah, no one but me will kill you," and he did not stop until he killed him. Concerning him Allah the Exalted revealed: ﴿And as for one who transgressed and preferred the worldly life, indeed Hellfire will be the refuge﴾ [Surah al-Nazi'at 37]. Then He gathered them together in reward, saying: ﴿Allah is pleased with them, and they are pleased with Him, and He has prepared for them gardens beneath which rivers flow, abiding therein forever. That is the great achievement.﴾ The people of Makkah read: "min tahtiha al-anhar" [with the preposition *min*] [Ibn Kathir, cited in Zad al-Masir 3/334], and so it is in their codices [Mus'af], *khalidina fiha abadan*. That is the great triumph.

Al-Hasan ibn al-Fadl said: The difference between them is that His saying, "Rivers flow beneath them," means that rivers flow beneath the trees. His saying, "flow from beneath them" (﴿تجري من تحتها﴾), means that water springs up from beneath them and then flows beneath the trees.

It is related regarding this verse that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said to Mu'adh ibn Jabal: "Where are the foremost (al-sabiqun)?" Mu'adh said: "Some people have passed on." He said: "The foremost are those who are absorbed in the remembrance of Allah. Whoever wishes to graze in the gardens of Paradise, let him increase his remembrance of Allah, exalted is He."

﴿And among those around you of the Bedouins are hypocrites﴾. It was revealed concerning the tribes of Muzaynah, Juhaynah, Aslam, Ashja', and Ghifar, whose dwellings were around Madinah.

﴿And among the people of Madinah﴾: there is ellipsis (ikhtisar) and an implied element (idmar) in this, its meaning being: "And among the people of Madinah are people who have become hardened (marridu) in hypocrisy," meaning they became accustomed to it and were trained in it. It is said: "So-and-so rebelled (tamarrada) against his Lord," and "he became hardened (marada) in his disobedience," meaning he persisted in it, remained steadfast upon it, and habituated himself to it. From this come "tamrid" and "marid" (a rebellious, obstinate one). In the proverb: "The rebel has rebelled, and the runaway has grown mighty."

Ibn Ishaq said: they persisted in it and refused anything else. Qatadah and Ibn Zayd and Aban ibn Taghlib said: they remained upon it and did not repent as the others repented. The poet recited:

"The people became hardened in their clan,
People of transgression, misguidance, and wickedness."

﴿You do not know them, O Muhammad; We know them.﴾ Qatadah said regarding this verse: What is the matter with people who burden themselves regarding others, saying, "So-and-so is in Paradise and so-and-so is in the Fire"? Yet when you ask one of them about himself, he says: "I do not know." Tell me, do you know yourself better than you know the deeds of people? You have taken upon yourself something that the prophets before you did not undertake. The Prophet of Allah Nuh (peace be upon him) said: ﴿And I have no knowledge of what they used to do﴾. And the Prophet of Allah Shu'ayb (peace be upon him) said: ﴿And I am not a guardian over you﴾. And Allah said to His Prophet (peace be upon him): ﴿You do not know them; We know them. We will punish them twice.﴾ They differed regarding these two punishments.

It is related from Abu Malik, from Ibn Abbas, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) stood delivering a sermon on Friday and said: "Go out, O so-and-so, for you are a hypocrite. Go out, O so-and-so, for you are a hypocrite." So he removed from the mosque some people and exposed them. This is the first punishment, and the second is the punishment of the grave.

Mujahid said: [the two punishments are] with hunger and the punishment of the grave. Also from him: with hunger and killing. Also from him: with hunger twice. Also from him: with fear and killing.

Qatadah said: the punishment of this world and the punishment of the grave, and in this regard is the story of the twelve in the hadith of Hudhayfah.

Ibn Zayd said: the first time is the calamities in wealth and children, and the other time is in Hell.

Ibn Abbas said: the first time is the establishment of the prescribed punishments (hudud) upon them, and the second is the punishment of the grave.

Al-Hasan said: one of the two times is the taking of zakat from their wealth, and the other is the punishment of the grave. Its explanation is in Surah al-Nahl: ﴿Then they will be returned to a great punishment﴾.

Ibn Ishaq said: it is what enters upon them in Islam, and their entry without sincere intention; then their punishment in the graves when they come to them; then the great punishment in the Hereafter, and abiding eternally therein.

In some tafsirs: the first is the angels striking their faces and their backs at the taking of their souls, and the second is the punishment of the grave.

It was said: its explanation is in Surah al-Nahl: ﴿We will increase them in punishment upon punishment﴾.

Muqatil ibn Hayyan said: the first is by the sword on the day of Badr, and the second is at death.

Ma'mar, from al-Zuhri, from al-Hasan, said: "The punishment of the Prophet and the punishment of Allah." By "the punishment of the Prophet (ﷺ)" is meant His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Cursed, wherever they are found, they will be seized and killed with a [terrible] killing﴾.

'Ata said: [the two punishments are] illnesses in this world and in the Hereafter. For whoever among the believers falls ill, Allah expiates his sins and purifies his wrongdoings, replacing for him flesh from his flesh and much blood from his blood, and granting him a great reward. And whoever among the hypocrites falls ill, Allah increases him in hypocrisy, sin, and weakness, as He said in this surah: ﴿Do they not see that they are tested every year?﴾, meaning they become ill every year once or twice, then they are returned to a great, severe, and dreadful punishment.

Al-Rabi' said: the afflictions of this world and the punishment of the Hereafter. Then "they will be returned to a great punishment," which is the punishment of Hell.

Isma'il ibn Ziyad said: one of the two punishments is the striking of the angels upon the faces and the backs, and the second is at the Resurrection, when a guardian of the Fire will be assigned to them.

Al-Dahhak said: once in the grave and once in the Fire. It was also said: the first time was by burning their mosque, the Mosque of Harm, and the second by burning them in the Fire of Hell. It was also said: once by the spending of their wealth being taken, and once by their being killed by the sword if they manifested what was in their hearts.

﴿And others﴾: meaning, and among the people of Madinah, or among the Bedouins, others; and it does not refer back to the hypocrites. ﴿Have acknowledged (i'tarafu)﴾: they admitted to you and to their Lord. ﴿They mixed a righteous deed﴾, which is their admission and repentance, ﴿and another wicked﴾: meaning with a wicked deed. The waw (و) is placed in the position of the ba' (ب), just as one says: "The water mixed with the filth," meaning with the filth; and "I mixed the water and the milk," meaning with the milk. The wicked deed is their staying behind from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and their abandonment of jihad.

﴿It may be that Allah will turn to them in forgiveness﴾. "Asa" (it may be) and "la'alla" (perhaps) from Allah are obligatory, and both are particles of expectation.

﴿Indeed, Allah is Forgiving and Merciful.﴾

This verse was revealed concerning a people who had stayed behind from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) in the Battle of Tabuk, then regretted it and felt ashamed. They said: "We remain in shade and shelter with the women, while the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) is in jihad! By Allah, we will bind ourselves with chains in our hands until the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) himself releases us or punishes us." They tied themselves to the pillars of the mosque. When the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) returned, he passed by them and saw them, and said: "Who are these?" They said: "They stayed behind from you." So they made a covenant with Allah that they would not release themselves until you are the one who releases them and excuses them. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "I swear by Allah, I will not release them nor excuse them until I am commanded to release them. They turned away from me and stayed behind from the expedition with the Muslims." Then Allah revealed this verse. When it was revealed, the Prophet (ﷺ) sent for them, released them, and excused them. When they were released, they said: "O Messenger of Allah, this is our wealth which kept us away from you; so give charity from it on our behalf, purify us, and seek forgiveness for us."

The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "I have not been commanded to take anything from your wealth." Then Allah, mighty and majestic, revealed: ﴿Take from their wealth a charity﴾, the verse.

They differed regarding the number of these people and their names. Ali ibn Abi Talhah related from Ibn Abbas, who said: They were ten men, among them Abu Lubabah. Sa'id ibn Jubayr and Zayd ibn Aslam said: Abu [Muniyah]: among them were Hilal, Abu Lubabah, Kirdam, Mirdas, and Abu Qays. Qatadah and al-Dahhak said: They were seven, among them Jadd ibn Qays, Abu Lubabah, Judham, and Aws, all of them from the Ansar.

'Atiyyah said from Ibn Abbas: They were five, one of whom was Abu Lubabah. Others said: it was revealed concerning Abu Lubabah, and they differed regarding his sin. Mujahid said: this verse was revealed concerning Abu Lubabah when he said to the Banu Qurayzah: "If you come down to his judgment, it is slaughter," and he pointed to his throat. The story has passed in Surah al-Anfal. He regretted it and repented, and he admitted his sin, so Allah, mighty and majestic, revealed this verse.

Al-Zuhri said: It was revealed concerning his staying behind from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) in the Battle of Tabuk. He tied himself to a pillar and said: "By Allah, I will not free myself from it, nor taste food or drink, until I die or Allah accepts my repentance." He remained seven days without tasting food or drink, until he fell unconscious. Then Allah, exalted is He, revealed: ﴿And others have acknowledged their sins﴾, the verse. It was said to him: "Allah has accepted your repentance, O Abu Lubabah." He said: "By Allah, I will not free myself until the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) is the one who frees me." So the Prophet (ﷺ) came and untied him with his own hand. Then Abu Lubabah said: "O Messenger of Allah, part of my repentance is that I should abandon the house of my people in which I committed the sin, and that I should strip myself of all my wealth as charity to Allah and His Messenger." He said: "It suffices you, O Abu Lubabah, to give a third." [Al-Tabari, Jami' al-Bayan.]

They all said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) took a third of their wealth and left two-thirds, because Allah, mighty and majestic, said: ﴿Take from their wealth﴾ and did not say "their wealth" (in full), so he did not take all of it.

Al-Hasan and Qatadah said: these were other than the three who stayed behind, [and the charity] purifies them from their sins by it. The reading with the raised vowel (dammah) is a circumstantial clause (hal), not a response (jawab), meaning: ﴿Take from their wealth a charity﴾ being purifying and cleansing, like the saying of al-Hutay'ah:

"Whenever you come to him, seeking the light of his fire,
You will find the best fire and the best station with him."

Maslamah ibn Muharib read "tutahhiruhum wa tuzakkihim" with the jussive, as a response (jawab). Al-Hasan read "tutahhiruhum" (with a light form from "atahhara"), and "wa tuzakkihim," meaning he purifies them. It was also said: he sets them right. It was also said: he elevates them from the stations of the hypocrites to the stations of the sincere. It was also said: "it" refers to their wealth.

﴿And pray for them﴾: meaning seek forgiveness for them and supplicate for them. It was said: it is the saying of the official who takes the charity: "May Allah reward you for what you have given, and bless you in what you have kept." Prayer (salah) in the language means supplication, and from it is the saying of the Prophet (ﷺ): "When one of you is invited to a meal, let him accept; if he is fasting, let him pray (fa-l-yusalli)," meaning let him supplicate. Al-A'sha said:

"The wind meets its wine jar,
And he prays over its jar and is marked (with its sign)."

Meaning he supplicated for it safety and blessing.

He also said:

"My daughter says, when I have come near to departing:
'O Lord, keep away from my father illnesses and pain.'
Upon you is like what you prayed, so sleep,
For the side of a man has a resting place."

﴿Indeed, your prayer﴾: the people of Kufa read "ṣalātuka" in the singular here and in Surah Hud (﴿a-ṣalātuka﴾), and "wa-l-mu'minīn" with a suppressed (idmar). Abu Ubayd said: because "salah" is one of the prayers. This was related from Ibn Abbas. Do you not hear Allah saying: ﴿Establish the prayer﴾? This is the prayer of eternity, and "ṣalawāt" is for the plural, as in the saying: "I prayed the prayers (ṣalawāt) four and five." The others read all of them in the plural, and Abu Hatim chose this. He said: Whoever claims that "ṣalawāt" is from "ṣalāh" because the plural with the feminine suffix (-āt) is rare, has erred, for Allah, exalted is He, said: ﴿The words of Allah would not be exhausted﴾ and ﴿and she affirmed the words of her Lord﴾; He did not mean what is few.

﴿Is a comfort for them﴾: Ibn Abbas said: a mercy for them. Qatadah said: a dignity for them. Al-Kalbi said: a reassurance for them, that Allah has accepted their repentance. Mu'adh said: a purification for them from you. Abu 'Ubaydah said: a steadying.

﴿And Allah is Hearing, Knowing.﴾

Shu'bah, from 'Amr ibn Murrah, from 'Abd Allah ibn Abi Awfa, who was one of the companions of the tree (of the Pledge of Ridwan): that the Prophet (ﷺ), when people came to him with their charities, would say: "O Allah, send your blessings upon them." When I came to him with my charity, he said: "O Allah, send your blessings upon Abu Awfa." Ibn Abbas said: This is not an obligatory charity (zakat al-fard); it is like the charity of expiation for an oath. 'Ikrimah said: it is the obligatory charity. When the repentance of these people was revealed, those who had not sinned and had stayed behind said: "These were with us yesterday; they did not speak nor sit with us. What is the matter with them?" Then Allah, mighty and majestic, revealed: ﴿Do they not know that it is Allah who accepts repentance from His servants﴾, the verse.

The meaning of "taking the charities" is accepting them.

Al-Shafi'i, from Sufyan ibn 'Uyaynah, from Ibn 'Ajlan, from Sa'id ibn Yasar, from Abu Hurayrah, who said: I heard Abu al-Qasim (ﷺ) say: "By Him in whose hand is my soul, no servant gives a charity from the earnings of his livelihood, and Allah accepts nothing but what is good, and it does not ascend to heaven except that it is placed in the hand of the Most Merciful, who nurtures it as one of you nurtures his foal, until a morsel will come on the Day of Resurrection as great as a mountain." Then he recited: ﴿That Allah is the One who accepts repentance from His servants﴾, and the confirmation of this is in the revealed Book of Allah: ﴿Allah deprives usury of blessing and gives increase for charities﴾ to His saying ﴿for what you used to do﴾.

Mujahid said: this is a warning (wa'id) to them.

It is related in a report: If a servant were to come with his deed to a rock that has no door and no window, his deed would come out to the people, whatever it may be.

And others are deferred until Allah's command: that is, delayed, so that He may decide concerning them what He decides.

They are the three who stayed behind and tied themselves to the pillars, and who did not go to great lengths in repentance and apology as Abu Lubabah and his companions did. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was gentle with them, forbade people from speaking to them, and ordered their wives to separate from them, until anxiety overwhelmed them and grief tore them apart. The earth became constricted for them despite its vastness. They had been among the people of Badr, so people began saying, "They are ruined, unless an excuse is revealed for them." Others began saying, "Perhaps Allah will forgive them." They were left waiting for Allah's command, not knowing whether they would be punished or shown mercy, until Allah accepted their repentance after fifty nights and revealed ﴿And [He also turned in forgiveness] to the three who were left behind﴾.

Allah's words: ﴿And those who took a mosque for harm﴾, the verse.

The exegetes said: The Banu Amr ibn Awf built the Mosque of Quba and sent to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), asking him to come and pray in it. He came and prayed in it. Their brothers, the Banu Ghanm ibn Awf, envied them and said, "We will build a mosque and send to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) to pray in it, as he prayed in our brothers' mosque, and Abu Amir al-Nu'man the monk will pray in it when he returns from Syria." Abu Amir was a man from among them; he was the father of Hanzalah, "the one washed by the angels." He had become a monk in the Jahiliyyah, had embraced Christianity, and had worn coarse wool. When the Prophet (ﷺ) came to Madinah, Abu Amir said to him, "What is this that you have brought?" He said, "I have brought the Hanifiyyah, the religion of Ibrahim." Abu Amir said, "I am upon it." The Prophet (ﷺ) said, "You are not upon it." He said, "Yes, but you have introduced into the Hanifiyyah what is not part of it." The Prophet (ﷺ) said, "I have not done that; rather, I have brought it pure and white." Then he said to the Prophet (ﷺ):

"May Allah cause the liar among us to die, a lone exile."

The Prophet (ﷺ) said, "Amin." He was named "the Fasiq" (the transgressor). When the day of Uhud came, Abu Amir said to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), "If I find a people who fight you, I will fight you alongside them." He continued fighting him until the day of Hunayn. When Hawazin was defeated, he went out to the Romans seeking support, and he sent to the hypocrites: "Prepare whatever strength and weapons you can, and build me a mosque, for I am going to Caesar, the king of the Romans, to bring an army of Romans to expel Muhammad and his companions." This is Allah's words: ﴿and in preparation for those who had warred against Allah and His Messenger﴾.

So they built a mosque beside the Mosque of Quba. Those who built it were twelve men: Khidham ibn Khalid, from whose house the mosque was taken; Tha'labah ibn Hatib; Mu'tib ibn Qushayr; Abu al-Ara'd; Abbad ibn Hunayf; Harithah ibn Amir; [Jariyah and his two sons] [[The correction is from Asbab al-Nuzul by al-Wahidi: 175.]] Mujammi' and Zayd; Nabtal ibn al-Harith; Lahhad ibn Uthman; and Wadi'ah ibn Thabit. Mujammi' ibn Yazid led them in prayer. When they finished, they came to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) while he was preparing for Tabuk, and said, "O Messenger of Allah, we have built a mosque for the sick, for those in need, for rainy nights and cold nights. We would love for you to come to us, pray in it for us, and invoke blessing." The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said, "I am about to set out on a journey. If we return, Allah willing, we will come to you and pray for you there" [57].

When the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) returned from Tabuk and stopped at Dhu Awan, a place an hour's distance from Madinah, they asked him to come to their mosque. He called for his garment to wear, intending to go to them, but the Qur'an was revealed to him, and Allah, Mighty and Majestic, informed him about the Mosque of Harm and what they had planned. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) summoned Malik ibn al-Dukhshum, Ma'n ibn Adi, Amir ibn al-Sakan, and al-Wahshi, the slayer of Hamzah, and said to them, "Go to this wrongdoing mosque and its people; demolish it and burn it." They went out quickly until they reached Salim ibn Awf. They also came to the family of Malik ibn al-Dukhshum. Malik said to them, "Wait until I bring you fire from my family." He entered his household, took palm fronds, and lit them into fire. Then they went out chanting until they entered the mosque while its people were inside. They burned and demolished it, and its people scattered from it. The Prophet (ﷺ) commanded that it be made into a dunghill where carrion, filth, and refuse would be thrown. Abu Amir the monk died in Syria, alone and a stranger. About it Ka'b ibn Malik said:

"Allah forbid, from the deed of the wicked,
like your effort among the clan, O Abd Amr.
As for your claim that you have nobility and palms,
you have sold faith for disbelief."

[[The full story is mentioned in Asbab al-Nuzul by al-Wahidi, 175; Zad al-Masir: 3/339; and the poem in al-Sirah al-Nabawiyyah by Ibn Hisham: 2/424.]]

Ikrimah said: Umar ibn al-Khattab asked one of them, "What did you contribute to this mosque?" He said, "I contributed a pillar." Umar said, "Rejoice in it, around your neck in the Fire of Hell."

It is also narrated that the Banu Amr ibn Awf, who built the Mosque of Quba, asked Umar ibn al-Khattab during his caliphate to permit Mujammi' ibn Harithah to lead them in prayer in their mosque. He said, "No, and no blessing to the eye. Is it not the Mosque of Harm?" Mujammi' said to him, "O Commander of the Faithful, do not hasten against me. By Allah, I prayed in it, and I do not know what they concealed in it. I was a young man who recited the Qur'an, and they were a steadfast people who were eager, and they knew nothing of the Qur'an. So I prayed, and I do not think they were prevented from anything, except that they were humbling themselves before Allah. I did not know what was in their hearts."

Umar accepted his excuse, believed him, and ordered him to pray in the Mosque of Quba.

This is the story of the Mosque of Harm in which Allah, Mighty and Majestic, revealed ﴿And those who took a mosque﴾. The common readers recited it with the wa (and), while the people of Madinah and Syria recited it without the wa. It is also so in the codices of the people of Madinah and Syria.

Ata' said: When Allah granted Umar ibn al-Khattab the conquest of the cities, he ordered the Muslims to build mosques and ordered them not to make two mosques in one city, one adjacent to the other.

Layth narrated that Shaqiq did not attend prayer in the mosque of Banu Amir. It was said to him, "The mosque of Banu so-and-so, they have not prayed in it yet." He said, "I do not like to pray in it, for it was built on harm. Every mosque built for harm, display, or reputation will ultimately trace back to the Mosque of Harm" [[Tafsir al-Tabari: 11/36.]].

﴿And disbelief﴾: hypocrisy. ﴿And division among the believers﴾: they divide their community with it, because they used to pray together in the Mosque of Quba.
