al-Zuhri reported from Sa'id ibn al-Musayyab from his father who said: When death approached Abu Talib, the Prophet (ﷺ) entered upon him, and with him were Abu Jahl and Abdullah ibn Abi Umayyah. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said to him: "O uncle, you are the greatest of people in right over me and the best in word to me, and you are greater in right over me than my father. So say a word by which I may plead for you on the Day of Resurrection. Say: 'There is no god but Allah'; I will argue on your behalf with it before Allah."

Abu Jahl and Abdullah ibn Abi Umayyah said: "O Abu Talib, will you turn away from the religion of Abd al-Muttalib?" They kept speaking to him until the last thing he said was: "I am upon the religion of Abd al-Muttalib." The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "I will certainly ask forgiveness for you, O uncle, from Allah." [62] Then there was revealed: ﴿It is not for the Prophet and those who believe to ask forgiveness for the polytheists...﴾ the verse, and there was revealed: ﴿Indeed, you do not guide whom you love...﴾ [[Surah al-Qasas: 56.]] the verse. [[al-Mustadrak 2/336.]]

al-Hasan ibn al-Fadl said: "This is far-fetched, because the surah is among the last of the Qur'an to be revealed, and Abu Talib died at the beginning of Islam while the Prophet (ﷺ) was in Makkah."

Amr ibn Dinar said: The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Ibrahim asked forgiveness for his father while he was a polytheist, so I will not cease to ask forgiveness for Abu Talib until my Lord forbids me from it." His companions said: "We will surely ask forgiveness for our fathers just as the Prophet (ﷺ) asked forgiveness for his uncle."

Then Allah the Exalted revealed this verse. [[Ibn Hajar said in Fath al-Bari: "This has a difficulty, because Abu Talib's death was in Makkah before the Hijrah by agreement, and it is established that the Prophet (ﷺ) went to the grave of his mother when he performed 'umrah and asked his Lord to ask forgiveness for her, and this verse was revealed; and the principle is that revelation does not recur." Then he mentioned several narrations on this from various chains, until he said: "These chains support one another, and in them is an indication that the revelation of the verse was after the death of Abu Talib... and the delay of the revelation is supported by what preceded in the tafsir of Bara'ah concerning his (ﷺ) asking forgiveness for the hypocrites until the prohibition was revealed..." End of his words. (Fath al-Bari: 8/391, tafsir of Surah al-Qasas, hadith 4494.)]]

Ja'far ibn Awn reported from Musa ibn Ubaydah from Muhammad ibn Ka'b [he said: Muhammad ibn Abd al-Wahhab informed us, Ja'far ibn Awn informed us] [[Addition from Asbab al-Nuzul of al-Wahidi: 177.]] who said: It reached me that when Abu Talib became ill with the illness in which he died, the Quraysh said to him: "O Abu Talib, send to your nephew, so that he may send you something from this Paradise, and it will be a cure for you." The messenger went out until he found the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) sitting with Abu Bakr beside him. Zayd said: "Indeed your uncle says to you: 'O my nephew, I am old and a weak elder; call for me something from this garden of yours that you mention, of its food and drink, that may be a cure for me.'"

Abu Bakr said: "Indeed Allah has forbidden them to the disbelievers." He said: The messenger returned to them and said: "I conveyed to Muhammad what you sent me with, but he did not answer me with anything." Abu Bakr said: "Indeed Allah has forbidden them to the disbelievers." He said:

They pressed themselves upon him until he sent a messenger of his own, who found the messenger in his assembly and said to him the same thing. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Indeed Allah has forbidden both of them to the disbelievers, its food and its drink." Then he rose in his wake until he entered the house with him and found it filled with men. He said: "Leave me and my uncle." They said: "We will not do so, and you have no greater right to him than we do. If you have kinship, then we have kinship like yours." So he sat with him and said: "O uncle, may you be rewarded on my behalf with good. You took care of me when I was small, and you protected me when I was grown; so may you be rewarded on my behalf with good. O uncle, help me against yourself with a word by which I may plead for you before Allah on the Day of Resurrection." He said: "And what is it, O nephew?" He said: "Say: 'There is no god but Allah alone, with no partner.'" He said: "Indeed you are a sincere advisor to me. By Allah, were it not that I would be reproached for it after me, that it would be said: 'Your uncle panicked at death,' I would have gladdened your eye with it." Then the people shouted: "O Abu Talib, you are the head of the Hanifiyyah, the religion of the elders! Do not let the women of Quraysh say that I panicked at death." Then the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "I will not cease to ask forgiveness for you, until my Lord forbids me." So he asked forgiveness for him after he died. [63]

The Muslims said: "What prevented us from asking forgiveness for our fathers and our close relatives, when Ibrahim asked forgiveness for his father and this Muhammad asks forgiveness for his uncle?" So this verse was revealed.

The evidence, according to what has been said, is that Abu Talib died a disbeliever. Ibn Ishaq, Ibn Asakir and others narrated the hearing by al-Abbas, the uncle of the Prophet, of the testimony "There is no god but Allah" from Abu Talib. [[See Tarikh Dimashq: 70/245, ed. Dar Ihya' al-Turath; Sirah of Ibn Ishaq: 238; al-Mawahib al-Laduniyyah: 1/133; Tarikh al-Khamis: 1/300.]]

Abdullah ibn Hamid informed us, saying: al-Muzani informed us, saying: Ahmad ibn Najdah recounted to us, Sa'd ibn Mansur recounted to us, Abu al-Ahwas recounted to us, Abu Ishaq informed us, who said: Ali (peace be upon him) said when Abu Talib died: "I came to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and said: 'O Messenger of Allah, indeed your uncle...'" [[He mentioned an ugly word, as it is said, and Ali (peace be upon him) is too exalted to utter such words about an ordinary person, let alone about his own father.]] ... He said: "Go and bury him, and do not say anything until you come to me." So I went and buried him, then returned to the Prophet (ﷺ) with the dust still on me, and he invoked for me supplications that would not please me if I had all that is on the earth in exchange for them.

Abu Hurayrah and Buraydah said: When the Prophet (ﷺ) came to Makkah, he went to the grave of his mother Aminah and stood at it until the sun grew hot upon him, hoping to be permitted to ask forgiveness for her. Then there was revealed: ﴿It is not for the Prophet and those who believe...﴾ the verse. He stood, wept, and those around him wept. He said: "I asked my Lord for permission to visit her, and He permitted me; and I asked Him for permission to ask forgiveness for her, and He did not permit me. So visit the graves, for they remind you of death." We never saw anyone weep more than on that day.

Ali ibn Abi Talhah reported from Ibn Abbas: They used to ask forgiveness for their dead polytheists, so this verse was revealed, and they refrained from asking forgiveness; then He forbade them, but they did not cease asking forgiveness for the living until they died.

Qatadah said: Some men from among the Companions of the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "O Prophet of Allah, among our fathers were those who were good to neighbours, kept the ties of kinship, freed captives and kept their covenants. Should we not ask forgiveness for them?" The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Yes indeed, and by Allah, I will surely ask forgiveness for my father as Ibrahim asked forgiveness for his father." [65] Then Allah the Exalted revealed: ﴿It is not for the Prophet﴾, i.e., it is not fitting for the Prophet, ﴿and those who believe to ask forgiveness for the polytheists.﴾

The scholars of meanings said: What occurs in the Qur'an has two forms. One is in the sense of negation, as in His saying: ﴿It was not for you to cause its trees to grow﴾ [[Surah al-Naml: 60.]] and ﴿No soul could die except by the permission of Allah﴾ [[Surah Al 'Imran: 145.]]. The other is in the sense of prohibition, as in His saying: ﴿It is not for you to harm the Messenger of Allah﴾ [[Surah al-Ahzab: 53.]], and His saying: ﴿It is not for the Prophet and those who believe...﴾ is a prohibition.

﴿After it has become clear to them that they are companions of the Hellfire﴾, by their dying in disbelief. Some interpreters took the asking forgiveness in this verse to mean prayer. 'Ata' ibn Abi Rabah said: "I would never abandon praying over anyone from the people of this qiblah, even if she were an Abyssinian pregnant from fornication, for I have not heard that Allah has withheld prayer except from the polytheists." [[Tafsir al-Tabari: 11/61.]] Like His saying: ﴿It is not for the Prophet and those who believe to ask forgiveness...﴾ the verse. Then He excused His friend Ibrahim, peace be upon him, saying: ﴿And the asking of forgiveness by Ibrahim for his father was only because of a promise he had made to him...﴾ the verse.

Ali ibn Abi Talib (may Allah be pleased with him) said: Allah revealed His words, relating about Ibrahim (ﷺ), that he said: ﴿Peace be upon you. I will ask forgiveness for you of my Lord; indeed He is ever gracious to me.﴾ [[Surah Maryam: 47.]] [He said:] I heard a certain man asking forgiveness for his parents while they were both polytheists, so I said to him: "Do you ask forgiveness for two polytheists?" He said: "Did Ibrahim not ask forgiveness for his father?" I came to the Prophet (ﷺ) and related that to him, so Allah revealed this verse. [[Tafsir al-Tabari: 11/60.]]

And He revealed His words: ﴿There has already been for you an excellent example in Ibrahim... except for the saying of Ibrahim to his father, "I will surely ask forgiveness for you."﴾ [[Surah al-Mumtahanah: 4.]] And His words: ﴿except for a promise he had made to him﴾, meaning after his promise.

Some of them said: The pronoun in "iyyahu" refers to Ibrahim, because his father had promised him that he would become Muslim, and at that point Ibrahim said: ﴿I will ask forgiveness for you of my Lord.﴾ Others said: It refers to Ibrahim, because Ibrahim had promised his father that he would ask forgiveness for him, hoping for his conversion; this is His saying: ﴿I will ask forgiveness for you of my Lord,﴾ and His saying: ﴿I will surely ask forgiveness for you﴾ (the verse) indicates it; the reading of al-Hasan "wa'adaha abahu" with the letter ba' supports it.

﴿So when it became clear to him that he was an enemy of Allah [by his father's death], he disassociated himself from him.﴾ It was also said: its meaning is: ﴿when it became clear to him﴾ in the Hereafter ﴿that he was an enemy of Allah﴾, and that is in accordance with what has been reported in the traditions: that Ibrahim (ﷺ) will say on the Day of Resurrection: "O Lord, my father! O Lord, my father!" When it is the third time, Allah will show him [his father] and Ibrahim will say to him: "I used to command you in the world and you disobeyed me, and I will not abandon you today for anything; so take [my hem]," and he will cling to him until he wants to cross the Sirat with him. When he wants to pass him over it, Ibrahim (peace be upon him) looks back and there is his father in the form of a hyena; then he releases him and disassociates himself from him on that day.

On this interpretation the meaning of the statement is future: it will become clear and he will disassociate himself.

﴿Indeed Ibrahim was ever compassionate and forbearing﴾. They differed regarding its meaning. Shahr ibn Hawshab reported from Abdullah ibn Shaddad ibn al-Hadi, as a mursal report, that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was asked about "al-awwah" and said: "The humble one who is submissive and supplicating." Anas said: A woman spoke in the presence of the Prophet (ﷺ) something he disliked, and Umar (may Allah be pleased with him) rebuked her, so the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Turn away from her, for she is awwahah." It was asked: "O Messenger of Allah, what is the awwahah?" He said: "The humble one." [66]

Abdullah ibn Rabah reported from Ka'b concerning the words of Allah: ﴿Indeed Ibrahim was awwah﴾, that he would say "awwah" whenever he remembered the Fire.

Abdullah ibn Mas'ud and Ubayd ibn Umayr said: "al-awwah" is one who supplicates much. al-Dahhak said: it is one who gathers supplication.

al-A'mash reported from al-Hakam from Yahya ibn al-Jarrar who said: Abu al-Ubaydi, a man from the countryside who was blind, came to Ibn Mas'ud and said: "O Abd al-Rahman, who will ask when you do not ask? What is the awwah?" Ibn Mas'ud was moved with compassion for him and said: "The awwah is the merciful."

al-Hasan and Qatadah said: "The awwah is the merciful toward the servants of Allah." Abu Maysarah said: "The awwah is the merciful on the Day of Gathering." Atiyyah reported from Ibn Abbas: "The awwah is the believer, in Abyssinian." Ali ibn Abi Talhah reported from Ibn Abbas: "The awwah is the believer, the penitent." Mujahid: "The awwah is the believer, the certain [one]; it is reported [...] from Ibn Abbas and Ali; Ibn al-Hakam from al-Dahhak." ['Ikrimah said: "He is the one who is certain, in the language of Abyssinia. Do you not see that when you say something to an Abyssinian and he understands it, he says: 'awwah'?"] Ibn Abi Najih: "the trustworthy." al-Kalbi: "The awwah is the one who glorifies, who remembers Allah in the desolate, lonely land." 'Uqbah ibn 'Amir said: "The awwah is the one who remembers Allah much."

al-Hakam reported from al-Hasan ibn Muslim ibn [...] that a man used to remember Allah much and glorify Him, and this was mentioned to the Prophet (ﷺ), who said: "Indeed he is awwah." It is also said: he is the one who recites the Qur'an much.

Ibn Abbas said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) buried a dead person and said: "May Allah have mercy on you; indeed you were truly awwah," meaning the recitation of the Qur'an. [67] [[Tafsir al-Tabari: 11/69.]]

It is also said: he is the one who raises his voice with remembrance, supplication and the Qur'an and recites it much. Ibrahim (peace be upon him) used to say: "Ah from the Fire, before 'ah' no longer benefits." [[Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 8/275.]]

Al-Tha'alibi's commentary (al-Jawahir al-Hisan) on surah 9, verses 111–114 (part 2 of 2):

Shu'bah narrated from Abu Yunus al-Bahili, from a judge who used to collect hadith, from Abu Dhar, who said: A man used to circumambulate the House (the Ka'bah) and say in his supplication: "Awwah, awwah." Abu Dhar complained about him to the Prophet (ﷺ). He said: "Leave him, for he is an awwah." He (Abu Dhar) said: "So I went out one night, and there was the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) burying that man at night, with the lamp with him." [68] [[Tafsir al-Tabari: 11/69.]]

al-Nakha'i said: "The awwah is the jurist (faqih)." al-Farra' said: "He is the one who laments (yatauwahu) over sins." Sa'id ibn Jubayr said: "The awwah is the one who teaches goodness." 'Abd al-'Aziz ibn Yahya said: "He is the compassionate (mushfiq)," and Abu Bakr (may Allah be pleased with him) used to be called the awwah because of his compassion and mercy. 'Ata' said: "He is the one who turns back from a word that displeases Allah," and he also said: "He is the one who fears the Fire." Abu 'Ubaydah said: "He is the one who laments out of compassion and fear, the one who humbles himself out of certainty and adherence to obedience." al-Zajjaj said: "The statement of Abu 'Ubaydah combines everything that has been said about the awwah. Its root is from ta'awwuh, which is to hear from the chest a sound of sighing deeply (tanaffus al-sa'ada), and the verb from it is awwah and ta'awwah." al-Muthaqqib al-'Abdi said:

"When I rise to saddle her at night, / she laments a lament like a sorrowful man."

The rajaz poet said:

"So the shepherd cried 'awwah' and his dog barked, / and no verb of the form yaf'ilu is derived from it."

[He is] forbearing (halim) toward one who abuses him and harms him with what is disliked. It has been said that he (peace be upon him) asked forgiveness for his father when he promised him and reviled him, and his saying: ﴿Indeed, if you do not desist, I will surely stone you, so leave me for a long time﴾ [[Surah Maryam: 46.]], and he said to him: ﴿Peace be upon you. I will ask forgiveness for you from my Lord; indeed He is ever gracious to me﴾ [[Surah Maryam: 47.]]. Ibn 'Abbas said: "The halim is the lord (sayyid)."

Commentary of al-Tha'alibi (al-Jawahir al-Hisan) on surah 9, verse 111–114 (part 1 of 2):

﴿Indeed, Allah has purchased from the believers their lives and their properties.﴾

Muhammad ibn Ka'b al-Qurazi said: When the Ansar pledged allegiance to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) on the night of al-'Aqaba in Makkah, they were seventy souls. Abdullah ibn Rawaha said: "O Messenger of Allah, stipulate for your Lord and for yourself whatever you wish." He said: "I stipulate for my Lord that you worship Him and associate nothing with Him, and I stipulate for myself that you protect me from what you protect yourselves and your properties from." They said: "If we do that, what will we have?" He said: "Paradise." [60] [[Jami' al-Bayan of al-Tabari: 11/49.]]

Al-A'mash said: "Paradise." It is also the reading of Umar ibn al-Khattab (may Allah be pleased with him): ﴿they fight in the cause of Allah, so they kill and are killed﴾. Ibrahim al-Nakha'i, al-A'mash, Hamzah, al-Kisa'i and Khalaf read it with the object preceding the subject, in the sense that some of them are killed and the rest kill; the others read it with the subject preceding the object. ﴿A promise﴾ is in the accusative as a verbal noun, ﴿binding upon Him in the Torah, the Gospel and the Qur'an﴾. Then He congratulated them, the Mighty One, the Majestic, saying:
﴿So rejoice in your transaction which you have made, and that is the great triumph.﴾ Qatadah said: "He was the most expensive of their price." al-Hasan said: "Hear of a profitable transaction which Allah made with every believer. By Allah, there is not a believer on the face of the earth except that he has entered into this transaction."

He said: A Bedouin passed by the Prophet (ﷺ) while he was reciting this verse, and said: "Whose speech is this?" He said: "It is the speech of Allah." He said: "By Allah, it is a profitable transaction; we will neither cancel it nor ask for its cancellation." So he went out to the military expedition and was martyred. [[See: Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 8/268.]]

Abu al-Qasim al-Hasan ibn Muhammad al-Habibi recited to us. He said: Abu al-Hasan al-Aqili recited to us. Bishr ibn Musa al-Asadi recited to us. al-Asma'i recited to me, from Ja'far al-Sadiq (may Allah be pleased with him):

"Shall I sell the precious soul to its Lord? For among all creatures there is no price for it.
By it Paradises are purchased, if I sell it for something other than it; that would indeed be a loss.
If I lose my soul for a worldly thing I have obtained, then the world is lost and the price is lost too." [[Cf. Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 8/268, where the last hemistich is instead: "Indeed my soul is lost and the price is lost too."]]

Al-Sadiq used to say: "O you whose soul has no value, indeed your bodies have no price except Paradise, so do not sell them except for it."

Abu al-Qasim al-Habibi recited to us. al-Qadi Abu al-Rabi' Muhammad ibn Ali recited to us. Abu Ali al-Hasan ibn Asim al-Kufi recited to us:

"Whoever desires a lofty dome in Eden, high in the shade of Tuba, its structures elevated;
its price is the Chosen One, and by Allah He has sold it, so whoever wishes, and Jibril is calling to it."

Then He described them, saying: ﴿the repentant﴾, i.e., they are the repentant. Ibn Mas'ud read "al-ta'ibin al-'abidin" with the final word in the accusative. The commentators said: they repented from polytheism and were cleared of hypocrisy. ﴿The worshippers﴾: those who obey, who devoted sincere worship and testimony.

al-Hasan and Qatadah said: They are a people who made their bodies a means of worship in their night and day, worshipping Allah at all times, in ease and in hardship. ﴿The praisers﴾: those who praise Allah in every state and for every blessing. ﴿The wanderers﴾: the fasting ones.

al-A'mash reported from Abu Salih from Abu Hurayrah who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "The wanderers are the fasting ones." [61] [[Jami' al-Bayan of al-Tabari: 11/52.]]

Shayban ibn Abd al-Rahman reported from al-Ash'ath who said: I asked Sa'id ibn Jubayr about "the wanderers," and he said:
"They are the fasting ones. Do you not see that when Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, mentions the fasting ones, He does not mention the wanderers, and when He mentions the wanderers, He does not mention the fasting ones?"

Sufyan ibn 'Uyaynah said: "Indeed the fasting person is a wanderer, for he abandons all pleasures: food, drink and intercourse."

A poet said regarding fasting:
"You see him praying through his night and day, ever abundant in the remembrance of Allah, a wanderer."  [[Fath al-Qadir: 2/408.]]

al-Hasan said: "The wanderers are those who fast from what is lawful and refrain from what is unlawful. By Allah, here there are people whom we have seen fasting from what is lawful but not refraining from what is unlawful; Allah is displeased with them." 'Ata' said: "The wanderers are the warriors and the strivers." It is reported from Amr ibn Nafi' who said: I heard Ikrimah, when asked about the words of Allah the Exalted, "the wanderers," say: "They are the seekers of knowledge." ﴿The bowers, the prostrators﴾: meaning those who pray. ﴿Those who enjoin what is right and forbid what is wrong﴾. Bassam ibn Abdullah said: "The right is the Sunnah and the wrong is innovation."

﴿And those who guard the limits of Allah﴾. Ibn Abbas said: "Those who keep to the obedience of Allah." al-Hasan said: "The people who fulfil the pledge of Allah." ﴿And give good tidings to the believers.﴾

﴿It is not for the Prophet and those who believe to ask forgiveness for the polytheists...﴾ the verse. The scholars differed concerning the occasion of revelation of this verse.

al-Zuhri reported from Sa'id ibn al-Musayyab from his father who said: When death approached Abu Talib, the Prophet (ﷺ) entered upon him, and with him were Abu Jahl and Abdullah ibn Abi Umayyah. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said to him: "O uncle, you are the greatest of people in right over me and the best in word to me, and you are greater in right over me than my father. So say a word by which I may plead for you on the Day of Resurrection. Say: 'There is no god but Allah'; I will argue on your behalf with it before Allah."

Abu Jahl and Abdullah ibn Abi Umayyah said: "O Abu Talib, will you turn away from the religion of Abd al-Muttalib?" They kept speaking to him until the last thing he said was: "I am upon the religion of Abd al-Muttalib." The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "I will certainly ask forgiveness for you, O uncle, from Allah." [62] Then there was revealed: ﴿It is not for the Prophet and those who believe to ask forgiveness for the polytheists...﴾ the verse, and there was revealed: ﴿Indeed, you do not guide whom you love...﴾ [[Surah al-Qasas: 56.]] the verse. [[al-Mustadrak 2/336.]]

al-Hasan ibn al-Fadl said: "This is far-fetched, because the surah is among the last of the Qur'an to be revealed, and Abu Talib died at the beginning of Islam while the Prophet (ﷺ) was in Makkah."

Amr ibn Dinar said: The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Ibrahim asked forgiveness for his father while he was a polytheist, so I will not cease to ask forgiveness for Abu Talib until my Lord forbids me from it." His companions said: "We will surely ask forgiveness for our fathers just as the Prophet (ﷺ) asked forgiveness for his uncle."

Then Allah the Exalted revealed this verse. [[Ibn Hajar said in Fath al-Bari: "This has a difficulty, because Abu Talib's death was in Makkah before the Hijrah by agreement, and it is established that the Prophet (ﷺ) went to the grave of his mother when he performed 'umrah and asked his Lord to ask forgiveness for her, and this verse was revealed; and the principle is that revelation does not recur." Then he mentioned several narrations on this from various chains, until he said: "These chains support one another, and in them is an indication that the revelation of the verse was after the death of Abu Talib... and the delay of the revelation is supported by what preceded in the tafsir of Bara'ah concerning his (ﷺ) asking forgiveness for the hypocrites until the prohibition was revealed..." End of his words. (Fath al-Bari: 8/391, tafsir of Surah al-Qasas, hadith 4494.)]]

Ja'far ibn Awn reported from Musa ibn Ubaydah from Muhammad ibn Ka'b [he said: Muhammad ibn Abd al-Wahhab informed us, Ja'far ibn Awn informed us] [[Addition from Asbab al-Nuzul of al-Wahidi: 177.]] who said: It reached me that when Abu Talib became ill with the illness in which he died, the Quraysh said to him: "O Abu Talib, send to your nephew, so that he may send you something from this Paradise, and it will be a cure for you." The messenger went out until he found the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) sitting with Abu Bakr beside him. Zayd said: "Indeed your uncle says to you: 'O my nephew, I am old and a weak elder; call for me something from this garden of yours that you mention, of its food and drink, that may be a cure for me.'"

Abu Bakr said: "Indeed Allah has forbidden them to the disbelievers." He said: The messenger returned to them and said: "I conveyed to Muhammad what you sent me with, but he did not answer me with anything." Abu Bakr said: "Indeed Allah has forbidden them to the disbelievers." He said:

They pressed themselves upon him until he sent a messenger of his own, who found the messenger in his assembly and said to him the same thing. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Indeed Allah has forbidden both of them to the disbelievers, its food and its drink." Then he rose in his wake until he entered the house with him and found it filled with men. He said: "Leave me and my uncle." They said: "We will not do so, and you have no greater right to him than we do. If you have kinship, then we have kinship like yours." So he sat with him and said: "O uncle, may you be rewarded on my behalf with good. You took care of me when I was small, and you protected me when I was grown; so may you be rewarded on my behalf with good. O uncle, help me against yourself with a word by which I may plead for you before Allah on the Day of Resurrection." He said: "And what is it, O nephew?" He said: "Say: 'There is no god but Allah alone, with no partner.'" He said: "Indeed you are a sincere advisor to me. By Allah, were it not that I would be reproached for it after me, that it would be said: 'Your uncle panicked at death,' I would have gladdened your eye with it." Then the people shouted: "O Abu Talib, you are the head of the Hanifiyyah, the religion of the elders! Do not let the women of Quraysh say that I panicked at death." Then the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "I will not cease to ask forgiveness for you, until my Lord forbids me." So he asked forgiveness for him after he died. [63]

The Muslims said: "What prevented us from asking forgiveness for our fathers and our close relatives, when Ibrahim asked forgiveness for his father and this Muhammad asks forgiveness for his uncle?" So this verse was revealed.

The evidence, according to what has been said, is that Abu Talib died a disbeliever. Ibn Ishaq, Ibn Asakir and others narrated the hearing by al-Abbas, the uncle of the Prophet, of the testimony "There is no god but Allah" from Abu Talib. [[See Tarikh Dimashq: 70/245, ed. Dar Ihya' al-Turath; Sirah of Ibn Ishaq: 238; al-Mawahib al-Laduniyyah: 1/133; Tarikh al-Khamis: 1/300.]]

Abdullah ibn Hamid informed us, saying: al-Muzani informed us, saying: Ahmad ibn Najdah recounted to us, Sa'd ibn Mansur recounted to us, Abu al-Ahwas recounted to us, Abu Ishaq informed us, who said: Ali (peace be upon him) said when Abu Talib died: "I came to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and said: 'O Messenger of Allah, indeed your uncle...'" [[He mentioned an ugly word, as it is said, and Ali (peace be upon him) is too exalted to utter such words about an ordinary person, let alone about his own father.]] ... He said: "Go and bury him, and do not say anything until you come to me." So I went and buried him, then returned to the Prophet (ﷺ) with the dust still on me, and he invoked for me supplications that would not please me if I had all that is on the earth in exchange for them.

Abu Hurayrah and Buraydah said: When the Prophet (ﷺ) came to Makkah, he went to the grave of his mother Aminah and stood at it until the sun grew hot upon him, hoping to be permitted to ask forgiveness for her. Then there was revealed: ﴿It is not for the Prophet and those who believe...﴾ the verse. He stood, wept, and those around him wept. He said: "I asked my Lord for permission to visit her, and He permitted me; and I asked Him for permission to ask forgiveness for her, and He did not permit me. So visit the graves, for they remind you of death." We never saw anyone weep more than on that day.

Ali ibn Abi Talhah reported from Ibn Abbas: They used to ask forgiveness for their dead polytheists, so this verse was revealed, and they refrained from asking forgiveness; then He forbade them, but they did not cease asking forgiveness for the living until they died.

Qatadah said: Some men from among the Companions of the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "O Prophet of Allah, among our fathers were those who were good to neighbours, kept the ties of kinship, freed captives and kept their covenants. Should we not ask forgiveness for them?" The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Yes indeed, and by Allah, I will surely ask forgiveness for my father as Ibrahim asked forgiveness for his father." [65] Then Allah the Exalted revealed: ﴿It is not for the Prophet﴾, i.e., it is not fitting for the Prophet, ﴿and those who believe to ask forgiveness for the polytheists.﴾

The scholars of meanings said: What occurs in the Qur'an has two forms. One is in the sense of negation, as in His saying: ﴿It was not for you to cause its trees to grow﴾ [[Surah al-Naml: 60.]] and ﴿No soul could die except by the permission of Allah﴾ [[Surah Al 'Imran: 145.]]. The other is in the sense of prohibition, as in His saying: ﴿It is not for you to harm the Messenger of Allah﴾ [[Surah al-Ahzab: 53.]], and His saying: ﴿It is not for the Prophet and those who believe...﴾ is a prohibition.

﴿After it has become clear to them that they are companions of the Hellfire﴾, by their dying in disbelief. Some interpreters took the asking forgiveness in this verse to mean prayer. 'Ata' ibn Abi Rabah said: "I would never abandon praying over anyone from the people of this qiblah, even if she were an Abyssinian pregnant from fornication, for I have not heard that Allah has withheld prayer except from the polytheists." [[Tafsir al-Tabari: 11/61.]] Like His saying: ﴿It is not for the Prophet and those who believe to ask forgiveness...﴾ the verse. Then He excused His friend Ibrahim, peace be upon him, saying: ﴿And the asking of forgiveness by Ibrahim for his father was only because of a promise he had made to him...﴾ the verse.

Ali ibn Abi Talib (may Allah be pleased with him) said: Allah revealed His words, relating about Ibrahim (ﷺ), that he said: ﴿Peace be upon you. I will ask forgiveness for you of my Lord; indeed He is ever gracious to me.﴾ [[Surah Maryam: 47.]] [He said:] I heard a certain man asking forgiveness for his parents while they were both polytheists, so I said to him: "Do you ask forgiveness for two polytheists?" He said: "Did Ibrahim not ask forgiveness for his father?" I came to the Prophet (ﷺ) and related that to him, so Allah revealed this verse. [[Tafsir al-Tabari: 11/60.]]

And He revealed His words: ﴿There has already been for you an excellent example in Ibrahim... except for the saying of Ibrahim to his father, "I will surely ask forgiveness for you."﴾ [[Surah al-Mumtahanah: 4.]] And His words: ﴿except for a promise he had made to him﴾, meaning after his promise.

Some of them said: The pronoun in "iyyahu" refers to Ibrahim, because his father had promised him that he would become Muslim, and at that point Ibrahim said: ﴿I will ask forgiveness for you of my Lord.﴾ Others said: It refers to Ibrahim, because Ibrahim had promised his father that he would ask forgiveness for him, hoping for his conversion; this is His saying: ﴿I will ask forgiveness for you of my Lord,﴾ and His saying: ﴿I will surely ask forgiveness for you﴾ (the verse) indicates it; the reading of al-Hasan "wa'adaha abahu" with the letter ba' supports it.

﴿So when it became clear to him that he was an enemy of Allah [by his father's death], he disassociated himself from him.﴾ It was also said: its meaning is: ﴿when it became clear to him﴾ in the Hereafter ﴿that he was an enemy of Allah﴾, and that is in accordance with what has been reported in the traditions: that Ibrahim (ﷺ) will say on the Day of Resurrection: "O Lord, my father! O Lord, my father!" When it is the third time, Allah will show him [his father] and Ibrahim will say to him: "I used to command you in the world and you disobeyed me, and I will not abandon you today for anything; so take [my hem]," and he will cling to him until he wants to cross the Sirat with him. When he wants to pass him over it, Ibrahim (peace be upon him) looks back and there is his father in the form of a hyena; then he releases him and disassociates himself from him on that day.

On this interpretation the meaning of the statement is future: it will become clear and he will disassociate himself.

﴿Indeed Ibrahim was ever compassionate and forbearing﴾. They differed regarding its meaning. Shahr ibn Hawshab reported from Abdullah ibn Shaddad ibn al-Hadi, as a mursal report, that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was asked about "al-awwah" and said: "The humble one who is submissive and supplicating." Anas said: A woman spoke in the presence of the Prophet (ﷺ) something he disliked, and Umar (may Allah be pleased with him) rebuked her, so the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Turn away from her, for she is awwahah." It was asked: "O Messenger of Allah, what is the awwahah?" He said: "The humble one." [66]

Abdullah ibn Rabah reported from Ka'b concerning the words of Allah: ﴿Indeed Ibrahim was awwah﴾, that he would say "awwah" whenever he remembered the Fire.

Abdullah ibn Mas'ud and Ubayd ibn Umayr said: "al-awwah" is one who supplicates much. al-Dahhak said: it is one who gathers supplication.

al-A'mash reported from al-Hakam from Yahya ibn al-Jarrar who said: Abu al-Ubaydi, a man from the countryside who was blind, came to Ibn Mas'ud and said: "O Abd al-Rahman, who will ask when you do not ask? What is the awwah?" Ibn Mas'ud was moved with compassion for him and said: "The awwah is the merciful."

al-Hasan and Qatadah said: "The awwah is the merciful toward the servants of Allah." Abu Maysarah said: "The awwah is the merciful on the Day of Gathering." Atiyyah reported from Ibn Abbas: "The awwah is the believer, in Abyssinian." Ali ibn Abi Talhah reported from Ibn Abbas: "The awwah is the believer, the penitent." Mujahid: "The awwah is the believer, the certain [one]; it is reported [...] from Ibn Abbas and Ali; Ibn al-Hakam from al-Dahhak." ['Ikrimah said: "He is the one who is certain, in the language of Abyssinia. Do you not see that when you say something to an Abyssinian and he understands it, he says: 'awwah'?"] Ibn Abi Najih: "the trustworthy." al-Kalbi: "The awwah is the one who glorifies, who remembers Allah in the desolate, lonely land." 'Uqbah ibn 'Amir said: "The awwah is the one who remembers Allah much."

al-Hakam reported from al-Hasan ibn Muslim ibn [...] that a man used to remember Allah much and glorify Him, and this was mentioned to the Prophet (ﷺ), who said: "Indeed he is awwah." It is also said: he is the one who recites the Qur'an much.

Ibn Abbas said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) buried a dead person and said: "May Allah have mercy on you; indeed you were truly awwah," meaning the recitation of the Qur'an. [67] [[Tafsir al-Tabari: 11/69.]]

It is also said: he is the one who raises his voice with remembrance, supplication and the Qur'an and recites it much. Ibrahim (peace be upon him) used to say: "Ah from the Fire, before 'ah' no longer benefits." [[Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 8/275.]]

Al-Tha'alibi's commentary (al-Jawahir al-Hisan) on surah 9, verses 111–114 (part 2 of 2):

Shu'bah narrated from Abu Yunus al-Bahili, from a judge who used to collect hadith, from Abu Dhar, who said: A man used to circumambulate the House (the Ka'bah) and say in his supplication: "Awwah, awwah." Abu Dhar complained about him to the Prophet (ﷺ). He said: "Leave him, for he is an awwah." He (Abu Dhar) said: "So I went out one night, and there was the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) burying that man at night, with the lamp with him." [68] [[Tafsir al-Tabari: 11/69.]]

al-Nakha'i said: "The awwah is the jurist (faqih)." al-Farra' said: "He is the one who laments (yatauwahu) over sins." Sa'id ibn Jubayr said: "The awwah is the one who teaches goodness." 'Abd al-'Aziz ibn Yahya said: "He is the compassionate (mushfiq)," and Abu Bakr (may Allah be pleased with him) used to be called the awwah because of his compassion and mercy. 'Ata' said: "He is the one who turns back from a word that displeases Allah," and he also said: "He is the one who fears the Fire." Abu 'Ubaydah said: "He is the one who laments out of compassion and fear, the one who humbles himself out of certainty and adherence to obedience." al-Zajjaj said: "The statement of Abu 'Ubaydah combines everything that has been said about the awwah. Its root is from ta'awwuh, which is to hear from the chest a sound of sighing deeply (tanaffus al-sa'ada), and the verb from it is awwah and ta'awwah." al-Muthaqqib al-'Abdi said:

"When I rise to saddle her at night, / she laments a lament like a sorrowful man."

The rajaz poet said:

"So the shepherd cried 'awwah' and his dog barked, / and no verb of the form yaf'ilu is derived from it."

[He is] forbearing (halim) toward one who abuses him and harms him with what is disliked. It has been said that he (peace be upon him) asked forgiveness for his father when he promised him and reviled him, and his saying: ﴿Indeed, if you do not desist, I will surely stone you, so leave me for a long time﴾ [[Surah Maryam: 46.]], and he said to him: ﴿Peace be upon you. I will ask forgiveness for you from my Lord; indeed He is ever gracious to me﴾ [[Surah Maryam: 47.]]. Ibn 'Abbas said: "The halim is the lord (sayyid)."

Commentary of al-Tha'alibi (al-Jawahir al-Hisan) on surah 9, verse 111–114 (part 1 of 2):

﴿Indeed, Allah has purchased from the believers their lives and their properties.﴾

Muhammad ibn Ka'b al-Qurazi said: When the Ansar pledged allegiance to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) on the night of al-'Aqaba in Makkah, they were seventy souls. Abdullah ibn Rawaha said: "O Messenger of Allah, stipulate for your Lord and for yourself whatever you wish." He said: "I stipulate for my Lord that you worship Him and associate nothing with Him, and I stipulate for myself that you protect me from what you protect yourselves and your properties from." They said: "If we do that, what will we have?" He said: "Paradise." [60] [[Jami' al-Bayan of al-Tabari: 11/49.]]

Al-A'mash said: "Paradise." It is also the reading of Umar ibn al-Khattab (may Allah be pleased with him): ﴿they fight in the cause of Allah, so they kill and are killed﴾. Ibrahim al-Nakha'i, al-A'mash, Hamzah, al-Kisa'i and Khalaf read it with the object preceding the subject, in the sense that some of them are killed and the rest kill; the others read it with the subject preceding the object. ﴿A promise﴾ is in the accusative as a verbal noun, ﴿binding upon Him in the Torah, the Gospel and the Qur'an﴾. Then He congratulated them, the Mighty One, the Majestic, saying:
﴿So rejoice in your transaction which you have made, and that is the great triumph.﴾ Qatadah said: "He was the most expensive of their price." al-Hasan said: "Hear of a profitable transaction which Allah made with every believer. By Allah, there is not a believer on the face of the earth except that he has entered into this transaction."

He said: A Bedouin passed by the Prophet (ﷺ) while he was reciting this verse, and said: "Whose speech is this?" He said: "It is the speech of Allah." He said: "By Allah, it is a profitable transaction; we will neither cancel it nor ask for its cancellation." So he went out to the military expedition and was martyred. [[See: Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 8/268.]]

Abu al-Qasim al-Hasan ibn Muhammad al-Habibi recited to us. He said: Abu al-Hasan al-Aqili recited to us. Bishr ibn Musa al-Asadi recited to us. al-Asma'i recited to me, from Ja'far al-Sadiq (may Allah be pleased with him):

"Shall I sell the precious soul to its Lord? For among all creatures there is no price for it.
By it Paradises are purchased, if I sell it for something other than it; that would indeed be a loss.
If I lose my soul for a worldly thing I have obtained, then the world is lost and the price is lost too." [[Cf. Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 8/268, where the last hemistich is instead: "Indeed my soul is lost and the price is lost too."]]

Al-Sadiq used to say: "O you whose soul has no value, indeed your bodies have no price except Paradise, so do not sell them except for it."

Abu al-Qasim al-Habibi recited to us. al-Qadi Abu al-Rabi' Muhammad ibn Ali recited to us. Abu Ali al-Hasan ibn Asim al-Kufi recited to us:

"Whoever desires a lofty dome in Eden, high in the shade of Tuba, its structures elevated;
its price is the Chosen One, and by Allah He has sold it, so whoever wishes, and Jibril is calling to it."

Then He described them, saying: ﴿the repentant﴾, i.e., they are the repentant. Ibn Mas'ud read "al-ta'ibin al-'abidin" with the final word in the accusative. The commentators said: they repented from polytheism and were cleared of hypocrisy. ﴿The worshippers﴾: those who obey, who devoted sincere worship and testimony.

al-Hasan and Qatadah said: They are a people who made their bodies a means of worship in their night and day, worshipping Allah at all times, in ease and in hardship. ﴿The praisers﴾: those who praise Allah in every state and for every blessing. ﴿The wanderers﴾: the fasting ones.

al-A'mash reported from Abu Salih from Abu Hurayrah who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "The wanderers are the fasting ones." [61] [[Jami' al-Bayan of al-Tabari: 11/52.]]

Shayban ibn Abd al-Rahman reported from al-Ash'ath who said: I asked Sa'id ibn Jubayr about "the wanderers," and he said:
"They are the fasting ones. Do you not see that when Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, mentions the fasting ones, He does not mention the wanderers, and when He mentions the wanderers, He does not mention the fasting ones?"

Sufyan ibn 'Uyaynah said: "Indeed the fasting person is a wanderer, for he abandons all pleasures: food, drink and intercourse."

A poet said regarding fasting:
"You see him praying through his night and day, ever abundant in the remembrance of Allah, a wanderer."  [[Fath al-Qadir: 2/408.]]

al-Hasan said: "The wanderers are those who fast from what is lawful and refrain from what is unlawful. By Allah, here there are people whom we have seen fasting from what is lawful but not refraining from what is unlawful; Allah is displeased with them." 'Ata' said: "The wanderers are the warriors and the strivers." It is reported from Amr ibn Nafi' who said: I heard Ikrimah, when asked about the words of Allah the Exalted, "the wanderers," say: "They are the seekers of knowledge." ﴿The bowers, the prostrators﴾: meaning those who pray. ﴿Those who enjoin what is right and forbid what is wrong﴾. Bassam ibn Abdullah said: "The right is the Sunnah and the wrong is innovation."

﴿And those who guard the limits of Allah﴾. Ibn Abbas said: "Those who keep to the obedience of Allah." al-Hasan said: "The people who fulfil the pledge of Allah." ﴿And give good tidings to the believers.﴾

﴿It is not for the Prophet and those who believe to ask forgiveness for the polytheists...﴾ the verse. The scholars differed concerning the occasion of revelation of this verse.

al-Zuhri reported from Sa'id ibn al-Musayyab from his father who said: When death approached Abu Talib, the Prophet (ﷺ) entered upon him, and with him were Abu Jahl and Abdullah ibn Abi Umayyah. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said to him: "O uncle, you are the greatest of people in right over me and the best in word to me, and you are greater in right over me than my father. So say a word by which I may plead for you on the Day of Resurrection. Say: 'There is no god but Allah'; I will argue on your behalf with it before Allah."

Abu Jahl and Abdullah ibn Abi Umayyah said: "O Abu Talib, will you turn away from the religion of Abd al-Muttalib?" They kept speaking to him until the last thing he said was: "I am upon the religion of Abd al-Muttalib." The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "I will certainly ask forgiveness for you, O uncle, from Allah." [62] Then there was revealed: ﴿It is not for the Prophet and those who believe to ask forgiveness for the polytheists...﴾ the verse, and there was revealed: ﴿Indeed, you do not guide whom you love...﴾ [[Surah al-Qasas: 56.]] the verse. [[al-Mustadrak 2/336.]]

al-Hasan ibn al-Fadl said: "This is far-fetched, because the surah is among the last of the Qur'an to be revealed, and Abu Talib died at the beginning of Islam while the Prophet (ﷺ) was in Makkah."

Amr ibn Dinar said: The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Ibrahim asked forgiveness for his father while he was a polytheist, so I will not cease to ask forgiveness for Abu Talib until my Lord forbids me from it." His companions said: "We will surely ask forgiveness for our fathers just as the Prophet (ﷺ) asked forgiveness for his uncle."

Then Allah the Exalted revealed this verse. [[Ibn Hajar said in Fath al-Bari: "This has a difficulty, because Abu Talib's death was in Makkah before the Hijrah by agreement, and it is established that the Prophet (ﷺ) went to the grave of his mother when he performed 'umrah and asked his Lord to ask forgiveness for her, and this verse was revealed; and the principle is that revelation does not recur." Then he mentioned several narrations on this from various chains, until he said: "These chains support one another, and in them is an indication that the revelation of the verse was after the death of Abu Talib... and the delay of the revelation is supported by what preceded in the tafsir of Bara'ah concerning his (ﷺ) asking forgiveness for the hypocrites until the prohibition was revealed..." End of his words. (Fath al-Bari: 8/391, tafsir of Surah al-Qasas, hadith 4494.)]]

Ja'far ibn Awn reported from Musa ibn Ubaydah from Muhammad ibn Ka'b [he said: Muhammad ibn Abd al-Wahhab informed us, Ja'far ibn Awn informed us] [[Addition from Asbab al-Nuzul of al-Wahidi: 177.]] who said: It reached me that when Abu Talib became ill with the illness in which he died, the Quraysh said to him: "O Abu Talib, send to your nephew, so that he may send you something from this Paradise, and it will be a cure for you." The messenger went out until he found the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) sitting with Abu Bakr beside him. Zayd said: "Indeed your uncle says to you: 'O my nephew, I am old and a weak elder; call for me something from this garden of yours that you mention, of its food and drink, that may be a cure for me.'"

Abu Bakr said: "Indeed Allah has forbidden them to the disbelievers." He said: The messenger returned to them and said: "I conveyed to Muhammad what you sent me with, but he did not answer me with anything." Abu Bakr said: "Indeed Allah has forbidden them to the disbelievers." He said:

They pressed themselves upon him until he sent a messenger of his own, who found the messenger in his assembly and said to him the same thing. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Indeed Allah has forbidden both of them to the disbelievers, its food and its drink." Then he rose in his wake until he entered the house with him and found it filled with men. He said: "Leave me and my uncle." They said: "We will not do so, and you have no greater right to him than we do. If you have kinship, then we have kinship like yours." So he sat with him and said: "O uncle, may you be rewarded on my behalf with good. You took care of me when I was small, and you protected me when I was grown; so may you be rewarded on my behalf with good. O uncle, help me against yourself with a word by which I may plead for you before Allah on the Day of Resurrection." He said: "And what is it, O nephew?" He said: "Say: 'There is no god but Allah alone, with no partner.'" He said: "Indeed you are a sincere advisor to me. By Allah, were it not that I would be reproached for it after me, that it would be said: 'Your uncle panicked at death,' I would have gladdened your eye with it." Then the people shouted: "O Abu Talib, you are the head of the Hanifiyyah, the religion of the elders! Do not let the women of Quraysh say that I panicked at death." Then the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "I will not cease to ask forgiveness for you, until my Lord forbids me." So he asked forgiveness for him after he died. [63]

The Muslims said: "What prevented us from asking forgiveness for our fathers and our close relatives, when Ibrahim asked forgiveness for his father and this Muhammad asks forgiveness for his uncle?" So this verse was revealed.

The evidence, according to what has been said, is that Abu Talib died a disbeliever. Ibn Ishaq, Ibn Asakir and others narrated the hearing by al-Abbas, the uncle of the Prophet, of the testimony "There is no god but Allah" from Abu Talib. [[See Tarikh Dimashq: 70/245, ed. Dar Ihya' al-Turath; Sirah of Ibn Ishaq: 238; al-Mawahib al-Laduniyyah: 1/133; Tarikh al-Khamis: 1/300.]]

Abdullah ibn Hamid informed us, saying: al-Muzani informed us, saying: Ahmad ibn Najdah recounted to us, Sa'd ibn Mansur recounted to us, Abu al-Ahwas recounted to us, Abu Ishaq informed us, who said: Ali (peace be upon him) said when Abu Talib died: "I came to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and said: 'O Messenger of Allah, indeed your uncle...'" [[He mentioned an ugly word, as it is said, and Ali (peace be upon him) is too exalted to utter such words about an ordinary person, let alone about his own father.]] ... He said: "Go and bury him, and do not say anything until you come to me." So I went and buried him, then returned to the Prophet (ﷺ) with the dust still on me, and he invoked for me supplications that would not please me if I had all that is on the earth in exchange for them.

Abu Hurayrah and Buraydah said: When the Prophet (ﷺ) came to Makkah, he went to the grave of his mother Aminah and stood at it until the sun grew hot upon him, hoping to be permitted to ask forgiveness for her. Then there was revealed: ﴿It is not for the Prophet and those who believe...﴾ the verse. He stood, wept, and those around him wept. He said: "I asked my Lord for permission to visit her, and He permitted me; and I asked Him for permission to ask forgiveness for her, and He did not permit me. So visit the graves, for they remind you of death." We never saw anyone weep more than on that day.

Ali ibn Abi Talhah reported from Ibn Abbas: They used to ask forgiveness for their dead polytheists, so this verse was revealed, and they refrained from asking forgiveness; then He forbade them, but they did not cease asking forgiveness for the living until they died.

Qatadah said: Some men from among the Companions of the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "O Prophet of Allah, among our fathers were those who were good to neighbours, kept the ties of kinship, freed captives and kept their covenants. Should we not ask forgiveness for them?" The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Yes indeed, and by Allah, I will surely ask forgiveness for my father as Ibrahim asked forgiveness for his father." [65] Then Allah the Exalted revealed: ﴿It is not for the Prophet﴾, i.e., it is not fitting for the Prophet, ﴿and those who believe to ask forgiveness for the polytheists.﴾

The scholars of meanings said: What occurs in the Qur'an has two forms. One is in the sense of negation, as in His saying: ﴿It was not for you to cause its trees to grow﴾ [[Surah al-Naml: 60.]] and ﴿No soul could die except by the permission of Allah﴾ [[Surah Al 'Imran: 145.]]. The other is in the sense of prohibition, as in His saying: ﴿It is not for you to harm the Messenger of Allah﴾ [[Surah al-Ahzab: 53.]], and His saying: ﴿It is not for the Prophet and those who believe...﴾ is a prohibition.

﴿After it has become clear to them that they are companions of the Hellfire﴾, by their dying in disbelief. Some interpreters took the asking forgiveness in this verse to mean prayer. 'Ata' ibn Abi Rabah said: "I would never abandon praying over anyone from the people of this qiblah, even if she were an Abyssinian pregnant from fornication, for I have not heard that Allah has withheld prayer except from the polytheists." [[Tafsir al-Tabari: 11/61.]] Like His saying: ﴿It is not for the Prophet and those who believe to ask forgiveness...﴾ the verse. Then He excused His friend Ibrahim, peace be upon him, saying: ﴿And the asking of forgiveness by Ibrahim for his father was only because of a promise he had made to him...﴾ the verse.

Ali ibn Abi Talib (may Allah be pleased with him) said: Allah revealed His words, relating about Ibrahim (ﷺ), that he said: ﴿Peace be upon you. I will ask forgiveness for you of my Lord; indeed He is ever gracious to me.﴾ [[Surah Maryam: 47.]] [He said:] I heard a certain man asking forgiveness for his parents while they were both polytheists, so I said to him: "Do you ask forgiveness for two polytheists?" He said: "Did Ibrahim not ask forgiveness for his father?" I came to the Prophet (ﷺ) and related that to him, so Allah revealed this verse. [[Tafsir al-Tabari: 11/60.]]

And He revealed His words: ﴿There has already been for you an excellent example in Ibrahim... except for the saying of Ibrahim to his father, "I will surely ask forgiveness for you."﴾ [[Surah al-Mumtahanah: 4.]] And His words: ﴿except for a promise he had made to him﴾, meaning after his promise.

Some of them said: The pronoun in "iyyahu" refers to Ibrahim, because his father had promised him that he would become Muslim, and at that point Ibrahim said: ﴿I will ask forgiveness for you of my Lord.﴾ Others said: It refers to Ibrahim, because Ibrahim had promised his father that he would ask forgiveness for him, hoping for his conversion; this is His saying: ﴿I will ask forgiveness for you of my Lord,﴾ and His saying: ﴿I will surely ask forgiveness for you﴾ (the verse) indicates it; the reading of al-Hasan "wa'adaha abahu" with the letter ba' supports it.

﴿So when it became clear to him that he was an enemy of Allah [by his father's death], he disassociated himself from him.﴾ It was also said: its meaning is: ﴿when it became clear to him﴾ in the Hereafter ﴿that he was an enemy of Allah﴾, and that is in accordance with what has been reported in the traditions: that Ibrahim (ﷺ) will say on the Day of Resurrection: "O Lord, my father! O Lord, my father!" When it is the third time, Allah will show him [his father] and Ibrahim will say to him: "I used to command you in the world and you disobeyed me, and I will not abandon you today for anything; so take [my hem]," and he will cling to him until he wants to cross the Sirat with him. When he wants to pass him over it, Ibrahim (peace be upon him) looks back and there is his father in the form of a hyena; then he releases him and disassociates himself from him on that day.

On this interpretation the meaning of the statement is future: it will become clear and he will disassociate himself.

﴿Indeed Ibrahim was ever compassionate and forbearing﴾. They differed regarding its meaning. Shahr ibn Hawshab reported from Abdullah ibn Shaddad ibn al-Hadi, as a mursal report, that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was asked about "al-awwah" and said: "The humble one who is submissive and supplicating." Anas said: A woman spoke in the presence of the Prophet (ﷺ) something he disliked, and Umar (may Allah be pleased with him) rebuked her, so the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Turn away from her, for she is awwahah." It was asked: "O Messenger of Allah, what is the awwahah?" He said: "The humble one." [66]

Abdullah ibn Rabah reported from Ka'b concerning the words of Allah: ﴿Indeed Ibrahim was awwah﴾, that he would say "awwah" whenever he remembered the Fire.

Abdullah ibn Mas'ud and Ubayd ibn Umayr said: "al-awwah" is one who supplicates much. al-Dahhak said: it is one who gathers supplication.

al-A'mash reported from al-Hakam from Yahya ibn al-Jarrar who said: Abu al-Ubaydi, a man from the countryside who was blind, came to Ibn Mas'ud and said: "O Abd al-Rahman, who will ask when you do not ask? What is the awwah?" Ibn Mas'ud was moved with compassion for him and said: "The awwah is the merciful."

al-Hasan and Qatadah said: "The awwah is the merciful toward the servants of Allah." Abu Maysarah said: "The awwah is the merciful on the Day of Gathering." Atiyyah reported from Ibn Abbas: "The awwah is the believer, in Abyssinian." Ali ibn Abi Talhah reported from Ibn Abbas: "The awwah is the believer, the penitent." Mujahid: "The awwah is the believer, the certain [one]; it is reported [...] from Ibn Abbas and Ali; Ibn al-Hakam from al-Dahhak." ['Ikrimah said: "He is the one who is certain, in the language of Abyssinia. Do you not see that when you say something to an Abyssinian and he understands it, he says: 'awwah'?"] Ibn Abi Najih: "the trustworthy." al-Kalbi: "The awwah is the one who glorifies, who remembers Allah in the desolate, lonely land." 'Uqbah ibn 'Amir said: "The awwah is the one who remembers Allah much."

al-Hakam reported from al-Hasan ibn Muslim ibn [...] that a man used to remember Allah much and glorify Him, and this was mentioned to the Prophet (ﷺ), who said: "Indeed he is awwah." It is also said: he is the one who recites the Qur'an much.

Ibn Abbas said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) buried a dead person and said: "May Allah have mercy on you; indeed you were truly awwah," meaning the recitation of the Qur'an. [67] [[Tafsir al-Tabari: 11/69.]]

It is also said: he is the one who raises his voice with remembrance, supplication and the Qur'an and recites it much. Ibrahim (peace be upon him) used to say: "Ah from the Fire, before 'ah' no longer benefits." [[Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 8/275.]]

It has been said that he (peace be upon him) asked forgiveness for his father when he promised him and reviled him, and his saying: ﴿Indeed, if you do not desist, I will surely stone you, so leave me for a long time﴾ [[Surah Maryam: 46.]], and he said to him: ﴿Peace be upon you. I will ask forgiveness for you from my Lord; indeed He is ever gracious to me﴾ [[Surah Maryam: 47.]]. Ibn 'Abbas said: "The halim is the lord (sayyid)."

Commentary of al-Tha'alibi (al-Jawahir al-Hisan) on surah 9, verse 111–114 (part 1 of 2):

﴿Indeed, Allah has purchased from the believers their lives and their properties.﴾

Muhammad ibn Ka'b al-Qurazi said: When the Ansar pledged allegiance to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) on the night of al-'Aqaba in Makkah, they were seventy souls. Abdullah ibn Rawaha said: "O Messenger of Allah, stipulate for your Lord and for yourself whatever you wish." He said: "I stipulate for my Lord that you worship Him and associate nothing with Him, and I stipulate for myself that you protect me from what you protect yourselves and your properties from." They said: "If we do that, what will we have?" He said: "Paradise." [60] [[Jami' al-Bayan of al-Tabari: 11/49.]]

Al-A'mash said: "Paradise." It is also the reading of Umar ibn al-Khattab (may Allah be pleased with him): ﴿they fight in the cause of Allah, so they kill and are killed﴾. Ibrahim al-Nakha'i, al-A'mash, Hamzah, al-Kisa'i and Khalaf read it with the object preceding the subject, in the sense that some of them are killed and the rest kill; the others read it with the subject preceding the object. ﴿A promise﴾ is in the accusative as a verbal noun, ﴿binding upon Him in the Torah, the Gospel and the Qur'an﴾. Then He congratulated them, the Mighty One, the Majestic, saying:
﴿So rejoice in your transaction which you have made, and that is the great triumph.﴾ Qatadah said: "He was the most expensive of their price." al-Hasan said: "Hear of a profitable transaction which Allah made with every believer. By Allah, there is not a believer on the face of the earth except that he has entered into this transaction."

He said: A Bedouin passed by the Prophet (ﷺ) while he was reciting this verse, and said: "Whose speech is this?" He said: "It is the speech of Allah." He said: "By Allah, it is a profitable transaction; we will neither cancel it nor ask for its cancellation." So he went out to the military expedition and was martyred. [[See: Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 8/268.]]

Abu al-Qasim al-Hasan ibn Muhammad al-Habibi recited to us. He said: Abu al-Hasan al-Aqili recited to us. Bishr ibn Musa al-Asadi recited to us. al-Asma'i recited to me, from Ja'far al-Sadiq (may Allah be pleased with him):

"Shall I sell the precious soul to its Lord? For among all creatures there is no price for it.
By it Paradises are purchased, if I sell it for something other than it; that would indeed be a loss.
If I lose my soul for a worldly thing I have obtained, then the world is lost and the price is lost too." [[Cf. Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 8/268, where the last hemistich is instead: "Indeed my soul is lost and the price is lost too."]]

Al-Sadiq used to say: "O you whose soul has no value, indeed your bodies have no price except Paradise, so do not sell them except for it."

Abu al-Qasim al-Habibi recited to us. al-Qadi Abu al-Rabi' Muhammad ibn Ali recited to us. Abu Ali al-Hasan ibn Asim al-Kufi recited to us:

"Whoever desires a lofty dome in Eden, high in the shade of Tuba, its structures elevated;
its price is the Chosen One, and by Allah He has sold it, so whoever wishes, and Jibril is calling to it."

Then He described them, saying: ﴿the repentant﴾, i.e., they are the repentant. Ibn Mas'ud read "al-ta'ibin al-'abidin" with the final word in the accusative. The commentators said: they repented from polytheism and were cleared of hypocrisy. ﴿The worshippers﴾: those who obey, who devoted sincere worship and testimony.

al-Hasan and Qatadah said: They are a people who made their bodies a means of worship in their night and day, worshipping Allah at all times, in ease and in hardship. ﴿The praisers﴾: those who praise Allah in every state and for every blessing. ﴿The wanderers﴾: the fasting ones.

al-A'mash reported from Abu Salih from Abu Hurayrah who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "The wanderers are the fasting ones." [61] [[Jami' al-Bayan of al-Tabari: 11/52.]]

Shayban ibn Abd al-Rahman reported from al-Ash'ath who said: I asked Sa'id ibn Jubayr about "the wanderers," and he said:
"They are the fasting ones. Do you not see that when Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, mentions the fasting ones, He does not mention the wanderers, and when He mentions the wanderers, He does not mention the fasting ones?"

Sufyan ibn 'Uyaynah said: "Indeed the fasting person is a wanderer, for he abandons all pleasures: food, drink and intercourse."

A poet said regarding fasting:
"You see him praying through his night and day, ever abundant in the remembrance of Allah, a wanderer."  [[Fath al-Qadir: 2/408.]]

al-Hasan said: "The wanderers are those who fast from what is lawful and refrain from what is unlawful. By Allah, here there are people whom we have seen fasting from what is lawful but not refraining from what is unlawful; Allah is displeased with them." 'Ata' said: "The wanderers are the warriors and the strivers." It is reported from Amr ibn Nafi' who said: I heard Ikrimah, when asked about the words of Allah the Exalted, "the wanderers," say: "They are the seekers of knowledge." ﴿The bowers, the prostrators﴾: meaning those who pray. ﴿Those who enjoin what is right and forbid what is wrong﴾. Bassam ibn Abdullah said: "The right is the Sunnah and the wrong is innovation."

﴿And those who guard the limits of Allah﴾. Ibn Abbas said: "Those who keep to the obedience of Allah." al-Hasan said: "The people who fulfil the pledge of Allah." ﴿And give good tidings to the believers.﴾

﴿It is not for the Prophet and those who believe to ask forgiveness for the polytheists...﴾ the verse. The scholars differed concerning the occasion of revelation of this verse.

al-Zuhri reported from Sa'id ibn al-Musayyab from his father who said: When death approached Abu Talib, the Prophet (ﷺ) entered upon him, and with him were Abu Jahl and Abdullah ibn Abi Umayyah. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said to him: "O uncle, you are the greatest of people in right over me and the best in word to me, and you are greater in right over me than my father. So say a word by which I may plead for you on the Day of Resurrection. Say: 'There is no god but Allah'; I will argue on your behalf with it before Allah."

Abu Jahl and Abdullah ibn Abi Umayyah said: "O Abu Talib, will you turn away from the religion of Abd al-Muttalib?" They kept speaking to him until the last thing he said was: "I am upon the religion of Abd al-Muttalib." The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "I will certainly ask forgiveness for you, O uncle, from Allah." [62] Then there was revealed: ﴿It is not for the Prophet and those who believe to ask forgiveness for the polytheists...﴾ the verse, and there was revealed: ﴿Indeed, you do not guide whom you love...﴾ [[Surah al-Qasas: 56.]] the verse. [[al-Mustadrak 2/336.]]

al-Hasan ibn al-Fadl said: "This is far-fetched, because the surah is among the last of the Qur'an to be revealed, and Abu Talib died at the beginning of Islam while the Prophet (ﷺ) was in Makkah."

Amr ibn Dinar said: The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Ibrahim asked forgiveness for his father while he was a polytheist, so I will not cease to ask forgiveness for Abu Talib until my Lord forbids me from it." His companions said: "We will surely ask forgiveness for our fathers just as the Prophet (ﷺ) asked forgiveness for his uncle."

Then Allah the Exalted revealed this verse. [[Ibn Hajar said in Fath al-Bari: "This has a difficulty, because Abu Talib's death was in Makkah before the Hijrah by agreement, and it is established that the Prophet (ﷺ) went to the grave of his mother when he performed 'umrah and asked his Lord to ask forgiveness for her, and this verse was revealed; and the principle is that revelation does not recur." Then he mentioned several narrations on this from various chains, until he said: "These chains support one another, and in them is an indication that the revelation of the verse was after the death of Abu Talib... and the delay of the revelation is supported by what preceded in the tafsir of Bara'ah concerning his (ﷺ) asking forgiveness for the hypocrites until the prohibition was revealed..." End of his words. (Fath al-Bari: 8/391, tafsir of Surah al-Qasas, hadith 4494.)]]

Ja'far ibn Awn reported from Musa ibn Ubaydah from Muhammad ibn Ka'b [he said: Muhammad ibn Abd al-Wahhab informed us, Ja'far ibn Awn informed us] [[Addition from Asbab al-Nuzul of al-Wahidi: 177.]] who said: It reached me that when Abu Talib became ill with the illness in which he died, the Quraysh said to him: "O Abu Talib, send to your nephew, so that he may send you something from this Paradise, and it will be a cure for you." The messenger went out until he found the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) sitting with Abu Bakr beside him. Zayd said: "Indeed your uncle says to you: 'O my nephew, I am old and a weak elder; call for me something from this garden of yours that you mention, of its food and drink, that may be a cure for me.'"

Abu Bakr said: "Indeed Allah has forbidden them to the disbelievers." He said: The messenger returned to them and said: "I conveyed to Muhammad what you sent me with, but he did not answer me with anything." Abu Bakr said: "Indeed Allah has forbidden them to the disbelievers." He said:

They pressed themselves upon him until he sent a messenger of his own, who found the messenger in his assembly and said to him the same thing. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Indeed Allah has forbidden both of them to the disbelievers, its food and its drink." Then he rose in his wake until he entered the house with him and found it filled with men. He said: "Leave me and my uncle." They said: "We will not do so, and you have no greater right to him than we do. If you have kinship, then we have kinship like yours." So he sat with him and said: "O uncle, may you be rewarded on my behalf with good. You took care of me when I was small, and you protected me when I was grown; so may you be rewarded on my behalf with good. O uncle, help me against yourself with a word by which I may plead for you before Allah on the Day of Resurrection." He said: "And what is it, O nephew?" He said: "Say: 'There is no god but Allah alone, with no partner.'" He said: "Indeed you are a sincere advisor to me. By Allah, were it not that I would be reproached for it after me, that it would be said: 'Your uncle panicked at death,' I would have gladdened your eye with it." Then the people shouted: "O Abu Talib, you are the head of the Hanifiyyah, the religion of the elders! Do not let the women of Quraysh say that I panicked at death." Then the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "I will not cease to ask forgiveness for you, until my Lord forbids me." So he asked forgiveness for him after he died. [63]

The Muslims said: "What prevented us from asking forgiveness for our fathers and our close relatives, when Ibrahim asked forgiveness for his father and this Muhammad asks forgiveness for his uncle?" So this verse was revealed.

The evidence, according to what has been said, is that Abu Talib died a disbeliever. Ibn Ishaq, Ibn Asakir and others narrated the hearing by al-Abbas, the uncle of the Prophet, of the testimony "There is no god but Allah" from Abu Talib. [[See Tarikh Dimashq: 70/245, ed. Dar Ihya' al-Turath; Sirah of Ibn Ishaq: 238; al-Mawahib al-Laduniyyah: 1/133; Tarikh al-Khamis: 1/300.]]

Abdullah ibn Hamid informed us, saying: al-Muzani informed us, saying: Ahmad ibn Najdah recounted to us, Sa'd ibn Mansur recounted to us, Abu al-Ahwas recounted to us, Abu Ishaq informed us, who said: Ali (peace be upon him) said when Abu Talib died: "I came to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and said: 'O Messenger of Allah, indeed your uncle...'" [[He mentioned an ugly word, as it is said, and Ali (peace be upon him) is too exalted to utter such words about an ordinary person, let alone about his own father.]] ... He said: "Go and bury him, and do not say anything until you come to me." So I went and buried him, then returned to the Prophet (ﷺ) with the dust still on me, and he invoked for me supplications that would not please me if I had all that is on the earth in exchange for them.

Abu Hurayrah and Buraydah said: When the Prophet (ﷺ) came to Makkah, he went to the grave of his mother Aminah and stood at it until the sun grew hot upon him, hoping to be permitted to ask forgiveness for her. Then there was revealed: ﴿It is not for the Prophet and those who believe...﴾ the verse. He stood, wept, and those around him wept. He said: "I asked my Lord for permission to visit her, and He permitted me; and I asked Him for permission to ask forgiveness for her, and He did not permit me. So visit the graves, for they remind you of death." We never saw anyone weep more than on that day.

Ali ibn Abi Talhah reported from Ibn Abbas: They used to ask forgiveness for their dead polytheists, so this verse was revealed, and they refrained from asking forgiveness; then He forbade them, but they did not cease asking forgiveness for the living until they died.

Qatadah said: Some men from among the Companions of the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "O Prophet of Allah, among our fathers were those who were good to neighbours, kept the ties of kinship, freed captives and kept their covenants. Should we not ask forgiveness for them?" The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Yes indeed, and by Allah, I will surely ask forgiveness for my father as Ibrahim asked forgiveness for his father." [65] Then Allah the Exalted revealed: ﴿It is not for the Prophet﴾, i.e., it is not fitting for the Prophet, ﴿and those who believe to ask forgiveness for the polytheists.﴾

The scholars of meanings said: What occurs in the Qur'an has two forms. One is in the sense of negation, as in His saying: ﴿It was not for you to cause its trees to grow﴾ [[Surah al-Naml: 60.]] and ﴿No soul could die except by the permission of Allah﴾ [[Surah Al 'Imran: 145.]]. The other is in the sense of prohibition, as in His saying: ﴿It is not for you to harm the Messenger of Allah﴾ [[Surah al-Ahzab: 53.]], and His saying: ﴿It is not for the Prophet and those who believe...﴾ is a prohibition.

﴿After it has become clear to them that they are companions of the Hellfire﴾, by their dying in disbelief. Some interpreters took the asking forgiveness in this verse to mean prayer. 'Ata' ibn Abi Rabah said: "I would never abandon praying over anyone from the people of this qiblah, even if she were an Abyssinian pregnant from fornication, for I have not heard that Allah has withheld prayer except from the polytheists." [[Tafsir al-Tabari: 11/61.]] Like His saying: ﴿It is not for the Prophet and those who believe to ask forgiveness...﴾ the verse. Then He excused His friend Ibrahim, peace be upon him, saying: ﴿And the asking of forgiveness by Ibrahim for his father was only because of a promise he had made to him...﴾ the verse.

Ali ibn Abi Talib (may Allah be pleased with him) said: Allah revealed His words, relating about Ibrahim (ﷺ), that he said: ﴿Peace be upon you. I will ask forgiveness for you of my Lord; indeed He is ever gracious to me.﴾ [[Surah Maryam: 47.]] [He said:] I heard a certain man asking forgiveness for his parents while they were both polytheists, so I said to him: "Do you ask forgiveness for two polytheists?" He said: "Did Ibrahim not ask forgiveness for his father?" I came to the Prophet (ﷺ) and related that to him, so Allah revealed this verse. [[Tafsir al-Tabari: 11/60.]]

And He revealed His words: ﴿There has already been for you an excellent example in Ibrahim... except for the saying of Ibrahim to his father, "I will surely ask forgiveness for you."﴾ [[Surah al-Mumtahanah: 4.]] And His words: ﴿except for a promise he had made to him﴾, meaning after his promise.

Some of them said: The pronoun in "iyyahu" refers to Ibrahim, because his father had promised him that he would become Muslim, and at that point Ibrahim said: ﴿I will ask forgiveness for you of my Lord.﴾ Others said: It refers to Ibrahim, because Ibrahim had promised his father that he would ask forgiveness for him, hoping for his conversion; this is His saying: ﴿I will ask forgiveness for you of my Lord,﴾ and His saying: ﴿I will surely ask forgiveness for you﴾ (the verse) indicates it; the reading of al-Hasan "wa'adaha abahu" with the letter ba' supports it.

﴿So when it became clear to him that he was an enemy of Allah [by his father's death], he disassociated himself from him.﴾ It was also said: its meaning is: ﴿when it became clear to him﴾ in the Hereafter ﴿that he was an enemy of Allah﴾, and that is in accordance with what has been reported in the traditions: that Ibrahim (ﷺ) will say on the Day of Resurrection: "O Lord, my father! O Lord, my father!" When it is the third time, Allah will show him [his father] and Ibrahim will say to him: "I used to command you in the world and you disobeyed me, and I will not abandon you today for anything; so take [my hem]," and he will cling to him until he wants to cross the Sirat with him. When he wants to pass him over it, Ibrahim (peace be upon him) looks back and there is his father in the form of a hyena; then he releases him and disassociates himself from him on that day.

On this interpretation the meaning of the statement is future: it will become clear and he will disassociate himself.

﴿Indeed Ibrahim was ever compassionate and forbearing﴾. They differed regarding its meaning. Shahr ibn Hawshab reported from Abdullah ibn Shaddad ibn al-Hadi, as a mursal report, that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was asked about "al-awwah" and said: "The humble one who is submissive and supplicating." Anas said: A woman spoke in the presence of the Prophet (ﷺ) something he disliked, and Umar (may Allah be pleased with him) rebuked her, so the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Turn away from her, for she is awwahah." It was asked: "O Messenger of Allah, what is the awwahah?" He said: "The humble one." [66]

Abdullah ibn Rabah reported from Ka'b concerning the words of Allah: ﴿Indeed Ibrahim was awwah﴾, that he would say "awwah" whenever he remembered the Fire.

Abdullah ibn Mas'ud and Ubayd ibn Umayr said: "al-awwah" is one who supplicates much. al-Dahhak said: it is one who gathers supplication.

al-A'mash reported from al-Hakam from Yahya ibn al-Jarrar who said: Abu al-Ubaydi, a man from the countryside who was blind, came to Ibn Mas'ud and said: "O Abd al-Rahman, who will ask when you do not ask? What is the awwah?" Ibn Mas'ud was moved with compassion for him and said: "The awwah is the merciful."

al-Hasan and Qatadah said: "The awwah is the merciful toward the servants of Allah." Abu Maysarah said: "The awwah is the merciful on the Day of Gathering." Atiyyah reported from Ibn Abbas: "The awwah is the believer, in Abyssinian." Ali ibn Abi Talhah reported from Ibn Abbas: "The awwah is the believer, the penitent." Mujahid: "The awwah is the believer, the certain [one]; it is reported [...] from Ibn Abbas and Ali; Ibn al-Hakam from al-Dahhak." ['Ikrimah said: "He is the one who is certain, in the language of Abyssinia. Do you not see that when you say something to an Abyssinian and he understands it, he says: 'awwah'?"] Ibn Abi Najih: "the trustworthy." al-Kalbi: "The awwah is the one who glorifies, who remembers Allah in the desolate, lonely land." 'Uqbah ibn 'Amir said: "The awwah is the one who remembers Allah much."

al-Hakam reported from al-Hasan ibn Muslim ibn [...] that a man used to remember Allah much and glorify Him, and this was mentioned to the Prophet (ﷺ), who said: "Indeed he is awwah." It is also said: he is the one who recites the Qur'an much.

Ibn Abbas said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) buried a dead person and said: "May Allah have mercy on you; indeed you were truly awwah," meaning the recitation of the Qur'an. [67] [[Tafsir al-Tabari: 11/69.]]

It is also said: he is the one who raises his voice with remembrance, supplication and the Qur'an and recites it much. Ibrahim (peace be upon him) used to say: "Ah from the Fire, before 'ah' no longer benefits." [[Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 8/275.]]

Al-Tha'alibi's commentary (al-Jawahir al-Hisan) on surah 9, verses 111–114 (part 2 of 2):

Shu'bah narrated from Abu Yunus al-Bahili, from a judge who used to collect hadith, from Abu Dhar, who said: A man used to circumambulate the House (the Ka'bah) and say in his supplication: "Awwah, awwah." Abu Dhar complained about him to the Prophet (ﷺ). He said: "Leave him, for he is an awwah." He (Abu Dhar) said: "So I went out one night, and there was the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) burying that man at night, with the lamp with him." [68] [[Tafsir al-Tabari: 11/69.]]

al-Nakha'i said: "The awwah is the jurist (faqih)." al-Farra' said: "He is the one who laments (yatauwahu) over sins." Sa'id ibn Jubayr said: "The awwah is the one who teaches goodness." 'Abd al-'Aziz ibn Yahya said: "He is the compassionate (mushfiq)," and Abu Bakr (may Allah be pleased with him) used to be called the awwah because of his compassion and mercy.
