'Ata' said: "He is the one who turns back from a word that displeases Allah," and he also said: "He is the one who fears the Fire." Abu 'Ubaydah said: "He is the one who laments out of compassion and fear, the one who humbles himself out of certainty and adherence to obedience." al-Zajjaj said: "The statement of Abu 'Ubaydah combines everything that has been said about the awwah. Its root is from ta'awwuh, which is to hear from the chest a sound of sighing deeply (tanaffus al-sa'ada), and the verb from it is awwah and ta'awwah." al-Muthaqqib al-'Abdi said:

"When I rise to saddle her at night, / she laments a lament like a sorrowful man."

The rajaz poet said:

"So the shepherd cried 'awwah' and his dog barked, / and no verb of the form yaf'ilu is derived from it."

[He is] forbearing (halim) toward one who abuses him and harms him with what is disliked. It has been said that he (peace be upon him) asked forgiveness for his father when he promised him and reviled him, and his saying: ﴿Indeed, if you do not desist, I will surely stone you, so leave me for a long time﴾ [[Surah Maryam: 46.]], and he said to him: ﴿Peace be upon you. I will ask forgiveness for you from my Lord; indeed He is ever gracious to me﴾ [[Surah Maryam: 47.]]. Ibn 'Abbas said: "The halim is the lord (sayyid)."

Commentary of al-Tha'alibi (al-Jawahir al-Hisan) on surah 9, verses 115–121 (part 1 of 2):

﴿And Allah would not let a people go astray after He has guided them﴾. He says: And Allah would not [judge] against you with misguidance after you asked forgiveness for the polytheists, before He had sent down to you the prohibition.

Mujahid said: It is Allah's clarification to the believers regarding abandoning the seeking of forgiveness for the polytheists, specifically, and His clarification to them regarding His disobedience and obedience, generally. So do or abstain.

Muqatil and al-Kalbi said: When Allah the Exalted sent down the obligations, the people acted upon them, then He abrogated them in the Qur'an. Some people were absent and were still acting on the first command, regarding the qibla, wine, and similar matters. They asked the Messenger of Allah ﷺ about this, so Allah the Exalted revealed: ﴿And Allah would not let a people go astray after He has guided them﴾, meaning: Allah would not nullify the deeds of a people who acted upon what had been abrogated, ﴿until He makes clear to them﴾.

Al-Dahhak said: ﴿And Allah would not let a people go astray …until He makes clear to them﴾ what they should do and what they should avoid. ﴿Indeed, Allah is Knowing of all things﴾. Then He magnified Himself, saying: ﴿Indeed, to Allah belongs the dominion of the heavens and the earth﴾, meaning He judges within them as He wills. ﴿He gives life and causes death, and you have not, besides Allah, any protector or helper﴾.

﴿Allah has certainly turned in forgiveness to the Prophet﴾. Ibn 'Abbas said: Whoever Allah has turned to in forgiveness, He will never punish him eternally.

The scholars differed regarding the meaning of "turning in forgiveness" (tawbah) toward the Prophet ﷺ. The people of tafsir (exegesis) said: it refers to his permission to the hypocrites to remain behind from them. The people of ma'ani (the science of meanings) said: it is the opening phrase of a statement, not the subject of their repentance. It is mentioned together with them, like His saying ﴿...then indeed for Allah is one-fifth of it and for the Messenger﴾ and similar, and ﴿the Emigrants and the Helpers who followed him in the hour of hardship﴾, meaning in the time of hardship, without intending a specific hour. Jabir said: The hardship of the mounts, the hardship of provisions, and the hardship of water.

Al-Hasan said: The Muslims would go out on a camel that they took turns riding: a man would ride for a while, then dismount and his companion would ride. Likewise their provisions were moldy dates, barley, and foul-smelling fat. A group of them would go out with nothing but a few dates shared among them. When hunger reached one of them, he would take a date and chew it until he tasted it, then give it to his companion, who would suck it, then drink a sip of water over it, and so on until it reached the last of them, and nothing of the date was left but the pit. They went on in intense heat, while the Messenger of Allah ﷺ was [aware of] their charity and their certainty.

Ibn 'Abbas said: It was said to 'Umar ibn al-Khattab (may Allah be pleased with him): What about the matter of the hardship? 'Umar said: We went out with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ in intense heat. We alighted at a station where we were struck by thirst, until we said: Surely our necks will be cut. A man would go seeking water and not return until he thought his neck would be severed, and a man would slaughter his camel, squeeze its stomach contents, drink them, and place the remainder on his liver. Then Abu Bakr al-Siddiq (may Allah be pleased with him) said to the Messenger of Allah: Allah has accustomed you to good in supplication, so supplicate for us. He said: "Do you wish that?" He said: Yes. So he raised his hands and did not lower them until the sky was overshadowed by clouds, then it poured, and they filled what they had. Then we went to look, and we did not find that it had passed beyond the camp. [Al-Durr al-Manthur: 3/286.]

﴿After the hearts of a faction of them had nearly swerved﴾, meaning: the hearts of a group of them nearly inclined because of the severity of the trial. The common readers recited ﴿taziğ﴾ with a "t" (tazigh), and its evidence is the reading of 'Abdullah, who said: [zaghiyyahum] [So in the manuscript]. Hamzah, al-A'mash, al-Jahdari, and al-'Abbas ibn Zayd al-Thaqafi recited it with a "y" (yazigh). Al-A'mash said: I recited it with "y" intending the feminine verb to be deferred, and in it is an implied subject. ﴿Then He turned to them in forgiveness; indeed, He is Kind and Merciful to them﴾.

﴿And to the three who were left behind﴾, meaning: He turned in forgiveness to the three who stayed behind from the expedition of Tabuk and did not go out. It was also said: they were left behind from the repentance of Abu Lubabah and his companions, and their matter was deferred, and the custom had already passed.

'Ikrimah and Humayd recited ﴿khalafu﴾ with a fatha on the kha and lam and without doubling, meaning [it was delayed behind] the Messenger of Allah ﷺ.

It is related from Ja'far ibn Muhammad al-Sadiq (may Allah be pleased with him) that he recited: ﴿khalafu﴾ [khalifu]. The reading of al-A'mash: ﴿wa 'ala al-thalathati al-mukhallafin﴾. They were Ka'b ibn Malik, the poet, Murarah ibn al-Rabi', and Hilal ibn Umayyah, all of them from the Ansar.

'Ubayd related from 'Abdullah ibn Ka'b ibn Malik al-Ansari, from his father 'Abdullah ibn Ka'b, who was the guide of his father Ka'b when his sight was afflicted. He said: I heard Ka'b ibn Malik relate his account of when he remained behind from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. He said: I never stayed behind from the Prophet ﷺ in any expedition he undertook, until the expedition of Tabuk, except Badr. The Prophet ﷺ did not rebuke anyone who stayed behind from Badr; he only went out intending the caravan, and Quraysh came out to protect their caravan, and they met without an appointment, as Allah the Mighty and Majestic said. By my life, the most honorable of the Messenger of Allah's ﷺ battles among the people was Badr, and I would not have wished that I had witnessed it instead of my pledge on the night of 'Aqabah, when we pledged ourselves to Islam. Then I did not stay behind from the Prophet ﷺ in any expedition he undertook, until the expedition of Tabuk. The people were summoned to depart at a time when the shade was pleasant and the fruit was ripe. The Prophet ﷺ rarely intended an expedition without concealing it by means of another, and he would say: "War is deception." So the Prophet ﷺ intended, in the expedition of Tabuk, that the people prepare for it fully. I was at my easiest, having prepared two mounts, and I was at my most capable in myself for jihad, yet I was inclining toward the shade and the goodness of the fruit. I remained like this until the Prophet ﷺ set out in the morning, and that was on Thursday, and he loved to depart on Thursday. He set out in the morning, and I said: I will go tomorrow to the market to buy my equipment, then I will catch up with them. I went to the market the next day, but some of my affairs became difficult for me, so I returned, saying: I will return tomorrow, God willing, and catch up with them. Again some of my affairs became difficult for me, and I kept on like this until my sin caught up with me, and I stayed behind from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. I began walking in the markets and wandering around Medina, and it grieved me that I saw none who stayed behind except a man accused of hypocrisy or a man whom Allah had excused among the weak. The people were numerous and were not gathered by any register. The total number of those who stayed behind from the Prophet ﷺ was about eighty-some men. The Prophet ﷺ did not mention me until he reached Tabuk, and while he was sitting at Tabuk he said: "What did Ka'b ibn Malik do?" [69]

Some men of my tribe said: O Prophet of Allah, his wealth and his gazing at his sides have detained him. Mu'adh ibn Jabal said to him: What an evil thing you have said! By Allah, O Prophet of Allah, we know nothing but good about him. While they were in that state, suddenly a man appeared in white, a mirage carrying him along. The Prophet ﷺ said: "Be Abu Khaythamah al-Ansari." He was the one who gave a sa' of dates in charity, and the hypocrites mocked him. When the Prophet ﷺ had completed the expedition of Tabuk and returned to Medina, I began to devise [an excuse] to escape the displeasure of the Prophet ﷺ, seeking help in that from every man of sound opinion among my family. When it was said that the Prophet ﷺ had [gone to pray] at dawn, falsehood departed from me, and I knew that I would not be saved except by truthfulness. The Prophet ﷺ entered and prayed two rak'ahs in the mosque, then sat down for the people. When he did that, those who had stayed behind came to him, swearing oaths to him and offering excuses, and he sought forgiveness for them. He accepted their outward profession and left their inner states to Allah the Exalted. I entered the mosque, and there he was sitting. When he saw me, he smiled the smile of one who is angry. I came and sat before him, and he said: "Had you not bought your mount?" [70] I said: Yes, O Messenger of Allah. He said: "Then what kept you back?" [71]

I said: By Allah, if I were sitting before anyone else among the people other than you, I would have escaped his anger with an excuse, for I have been granted eloquence in argument. But I know, O Prophet of Allah, that if I tell you a lie today, to make you pleased with me, Allah will likely reveal it to you. By Allah, O Prophet of Allah, I was never more at ease, nor more free of burden, than when I stayed behind from you.

He ﷺ said: "As for this, he has spoken truthfully. Get up until Allah decides regarding you."

I got up, and some men of my tribe were following me. They said: By Allah, we do not know you to have committed a sin before this. Why did you not offer an excuse to the Prophet ﷺ, so that he would be pleased with you about it? The Prophet's ﷺ seeking forgiveness for you would have been sufficient for your sin. And you did not place yourself in a position where you do not know what will be decided for you! They continued to reproach me until I resolved to return and deny my own statement. I said: Has anyone else said this statement besides me? They said: Yes, two men said what you said: Hilal ibn Umayyah al-Waqifi and Abu Murarah ibn Rabi'ah al-'Amiri. They mentioned two righteous men who had witnessed Badr, in whom I had an example. I said: By Allah, I will not return to him on this matter ever, nor will I deny myself.

He said: The Prophet ﷺ forbade the people from speaking to us, the three of us, among those who stayed behind from him. He said: I began going out to the market, and no one would speak to me. The people turned strange toward us until they were no longer the people we knew, and the walls became strange to us until they were no longer the walls we knew, and the earth became strange to us until it was no longer the earth we knew. [I was the strongest of my companions. I would go out and wander through the markets, come to the mosque, enter, and come to the Prophet ﷺ and greet him. I would say to myself: Did he move his lips with the greeting? When I stood and approached to pray, he would look at me with the corner of his eye, and when I looked at him, he turned away from me. The harshness of the Muslims toward me was prolonged until it was hard on me. I climbed over the wall of the garden of Abu Qatadah, who was my cousin and the dearest of people to me. I greeted him, but by Allah, he did not return my greeting. I said to him: O Abu Qatadah, I ask you by Allah, do you know that I love Allah and His Messenger? He was silent. I repeated my plea, and he said: Allah and His Messenger know best. My eyes overflowed, and I turned away until I climbed over the walls. While I was walking in the market, suddenly a Nabataean Christian man from the Nabataeans of Syria came, bringing food to sell, and saying: Who will show me Ka'b ibn Malik? The people began pointing to me, and he came to me and handed me a letter from the king of Ghassan. In it was: "To proceed: it has reached us that your companion has treated you harshly and cast you out. [You are not in a house of loss or humiliation.] So join us, and we will console you." I said: This is also a trial and an honor. So I heated the oven and burned the letter. When forty nights had passed of the time of the Prophet's ﷺ prohibition of our speaking, suddenly a messenger of the Prophet ﷺ came to me and said: "Withdraw from your wife." I said: Shall I divorce her? He said: "No, but do not approach her." He sent the same message to my two companions. I said to my wife: Go to your family and stay with them until Allah decides this matter. The wife of Hilal came and said: O Prophet of Allah, Hilal ibn Umayyah is a frail old man; will you permit me to serve him? He said: "Yes, but let him not approach you." She said: O Prophet of Allah, by Allah, he has no inclination toward anything; he has been constantly weeping night and day since what happened to him. He said: Some of my family said to me: If only you had asked the Messenger of Allah ﷺ about your wife, since he permitted Hilal's wife to serve him. I said: I will not ask the Messenger of Allah about her, and I do not know what he will say if I ask him about her, while I am a young man.

When fifty nights had passed since the Prophet ﷺ forbade speaking to us, I prayed the dawn prayer on the roof of a house, and I sat in the state that Allah the Mighty and Majestic described: ﴿the earth became constricted for them despite its vastness, and their souls became constricted for them﴾, and I heard a voice from the mountain of Sal': "O Ka'b ibn Malik, rejoice!" I fell down prostrate and knew that Allah had brought relief. Then a man came racing on a horse, and the voice was faster than his horse. [When the one whose voice I heard came to me to give good news, I took off my garment and gave it to him in return for his good news, and I borrowed two garments and wore them.] [From the tafsir of al-Tabari; and in the Musnad of Ahmad: I gave him my garment as a reward for the good news, and I wore two other garments.] He said: Our repentance was revealed to the Prophet ﷺ at two-thirds of the night. Umm Salamah said that evening: O Prophet of Allah, will you not give good news to Ka'b ibn Malik? He said: "If so, the people will rush to you and keep you from sleep for the rest of the night." Umm Salamah had been kind in my matter and grieved over my situation. I went out to the Prophet ﷺ and found him sitting in the mosque with the Muslims around him. Talhah ibn 'Ubaydullah rose to me, hurrying until he shook my hand, and said: "May the repentance of Allah upon you be pleasant for you." By Allah, no man of the Emigrants rose to me except him. Ka'b would never forget this for Talhah.

Ka'b said: When I greeted the Messenger of Allah and said: O Prophet of Allah, is this from Allah or from you? He said: "Rather, it is from Allah." Then he recited to them: ﴿Certainly Allah has turned in forgiveness to the Prophet and the Emigrants﴾ up to His saying ﴿and be with the truthful﴾. I said: O Prophet of Allah, from my repentance is that I should not speak of it except that I withdraw all my wealth as charity to Allah and His Messenger. He said: "Keep some of your wealth for yourself, for it is better for you." I said: Then I will keep my share from Khaybar. He said: Allah has not bestowed upon me any blessing after Islam greater in my soul than my truthfulness with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, when I and my two companions spoke truthfully, so that we would not lie and perish as those others perished. Indeed, I hope that Allah the Mighty and Majestic has not tested anyone in truthfulness [since I mentioned that to the Messenger of Allah, more greatly than He tested me. By Allah, I have not intentionally lied since I said that to the Messenger of Allah until this day]. [From the tafsir of al-Tabari.] And I hope that Allah the Mighty and Majestic will preserve me for what remains. This is what has reached us of the account of the three who were left behind. [See the tafsir of al-Tabari: 11/81–83, and the Musnad of Ahmad: 6/387–390.]

﴿Until, when the earth became constricted for them despite its vastness﴾. The exegetes said: meaning the earth became constricted for them in its entirety. ﴿And their souls became constricted for them﴾ [their hearts became constricted with worry and loneliness], ﴿and they thought that there is no refuge from Allah except in Him﴾. I heard al-Hasan ibn Muhammad ibn Ja'far al-Naysaburi, Ibrahim ibn Muhammad ibn Zayd al-Naysaburi, and 'Abdullah Khatan, governor of the land of Iraq, say: Abu Bakr al-Warraq was asked about sincere repentance (tawbah nasuhah). He said: It is that the earth becomes constricted for us despite its vastness, and our souls become constricted for us, like the repentance of Ka'b and his companion. ﴿Then He turned to them in forgiveness﴾, a repetition of emphasis, ﴿that they may repent﴾; so this is by His repentance.

I heard Abu al-Qasim ibn Abi Bakr al-Sadusi, I heard Abu Sa'id Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Rumayh al-Zaydi, I heard al-Hasan ibn 'Ali al-Damghani say: Abu Yazid said: I erred in four things. In the beginning, with Allah the Exalted, I thought I loved Him, and then He loved me. Allah the Exalted says: ﴿He loves them and they love Him﴾ [Surah al-Ma'idah: 54]. I thought I was pleased with Him, and then He was pleased with me. Allah the Exalted says: ﴿Allah is pleased with them and they are pleased with Him﴾. I thought I remembered Him, and then He remembered me. Allah the Exalted says: ﴿And the remembrance of Allah is greater﴾ [Surah al-'Ankabut: 45]. I wished to repent, and then He repented to me. Allah the Exalted says: ﴿Then He turned to them that they may repent; indeed, Allah is the Accepter of repentance, the Merciful.﴾

﴿O you who have believed, fear Allah and be with the truthful.﴾ Nafi' said: meaning with Muhammad and his companions. Sa'id ibn Jubayr: with Abu Bakr and 'Umar. Ibn Juraij and Ibn Hibban: with the Emigrants, its evidence being His saying: ﴿For the poor Emigrants … it is those who are the truthful﴾ [Surah al-Hashr: 8].

Abdullah ibn Muhammad ibn Abdullah informed me, Muhammad ibn 'Uthman ibn al-Hasan, Muhammad ibn al-Husayn ibn Salih, 'Ali ibn Ja'far ibn Musa, Jandal ibn Wāliq, Muhammad ibn 'Umar al-Mazini, al-Kalbi, from Abu Salih, from Ibn 'Abbas, regarding this verse: ﴿O you who have believed, fear Allah and be with the truthful﴾. He said: With 'Ali ibn Abi Talib and his companions. [See: Nazm Durar al-Simtayn, p. 91, and Shawahid al-Tanzil of al-Hasakani: 1/342.]

And 'Abdullah Muhammad ibn 'Uthman informed me, Muhammad ibn al-Hasan, 'Ali ibn al-'Abbas al-Maqani'i, Ja'far ibn Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, Ahmad ibn Subayh al-Asadi, Mufaddal ibn Salih, from Jabir, from Abu Ja'far, regarding His saying: ﴿and be with the truthful﴾, he said: With the family of Muhammad (ﷺ).

Yaman ibn Rabab: Be truthful as the three who were left behind were truthful.

Ibn 'Abbas: With those whose intentions were sincere, whose hearts and deeds were upright, and who went out with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ to Tabuk, with sincerity and intention.

Qatadah: It means truthfulness of intention. He said: or truthfulness by night and day, in secret and in public. Ibn Mas'ud used to say: ﴿kunu ma'a al-sadiqin﴾ [be with the truthful], and he would recite it so. Ibn 'Abbas (may Allah be pleased with him) related it from the Prophet (ﷺ).

Abdullah ibn Hamid informed us. Abdullah ibn Muhammad ibn al-Husayn. Muhammad ibn Yahya, Wahb ibn Jarir, from Shu'ayb ibn Amr ibn Zayd, from Abu Ubayda, from Abdullah, who said: "Lying is not permissible, whether in earnest or in jest, nor that one of you promises his child something and then does not fulfil it. Recite, if you wish, the verse: ﴿O you who have believed, fear Allah and be with the truthful.﴾ Do you think there is any allowance for lying?"

﴿The people of Madinah and those of the Bedouins around them were not to remain behind from the Messenger of Allah when he went out to fight, nor to prefer their own selves over his self.﴾ The phrase "ma kana li-ahl al-Madinah" has the outward form of a report, but its meaning is a prohibition, like His saying: ﴿It is not for you to harm the Messenger of Allah﴾ [[Surat al-Ahzab: 53.]]. "Those of the Bedouins around them" means the dwellers of the desert: Muzaynah, Juhaynah, Aslam, Ghifar and Ashja'. "Not to remain behind from the Messenger of Allah" means when he goes out to fight. "Nor to prefer their own selves over his self" means in accompanying him, aiding him, and striving alongside him.

Al-Hasan said: it means they should not prefer their own selves to be spared the hardships that befall the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ).

﴿That is because they will not suffer thirst (ẓama') (i.e., thirst), and that is, in the Way of Allah, nor fatigue (naṣab) (i.e., weariness), nor hunger (makhmasa) (i.e., famine).﴾ Abd ibn Umayr recited "ẓama'" with the long vowel, and both are dialectal forms, like khaṭa and khaṭa'. ﴿Nor do they tread upon any ground that enrages the disbelievers, nor do they gain any gain from an enemy﴾, meaning they do not obtain anything from their enemy, whether by killing, capture, booty or seizure. It is said: "nilt al-shay'," so it is "manīl." ﴿Except that a righteous deed is recorded for them thereby.﴾ Ibn Abbas said: for every fright that reaches them in the Way of Allah, seventy thousand good deeds are recorded. ﴿Indeed, Allah does not waste the reward of the good-doers.﴾ So if thirst reaches them, Allah gives them drink from the River of Life (nahr al-hayawan), and they will never thirst again. If fatigue reaches them, Allah gives them honey from the River of Life, and fatigue does not touch them. Whoever goes out in the Way of Allah does not set down a foot, a hand, a side, a nose or a knee in prostration, bowing, walking or sleeping in any spot of the lands of Allah, except that Allah grants him the rank of martyrdom and intercession.

They differed concerning the ruling of this verse. Qatadah said: this is specific to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) when he himself goes out to fight, so no one has the right to remain behind from him, unless the Muslims have no need or necessity for it.

He said: It has been related to us that the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Were it not that I would burden my community, I would not remain behind any expedition that goes out in the Way of Allah. But I find no provision, so I take them with me, and it burdens me to leave them after me." [73] [[Musnad Ahmad: 2/502.]]

Al-Walid ibn Muslim said: I heard al-Awza'i, Ibn al-Mubarak, al-Fazari, al-Sab'i, Ibn Jabir and Sa'id ibn Abd al-Aziz say concerning this verse: it applies to the beginning of this community and to its end.

Ibn Zayd said: this was when the people of Islam were few; when they became many, Allah abrogated it (naskh) and permitted remaining behind for whoever wishes. He said: ﴿The believers should not all go forth﴾ up to the verse. ﴿Nor do they spend any expense, small or great, nor even a whip's lash, nor do they cross any valley on their march, going forward or back, except that it is recorded for them﴾, meaning their traces and steps, ﴿that Allah may reward them with the best of what they were doing.﴾ That is, with reward, and He will admit them to Paradise without reckoning.

Ibn Abbas said: Abu Umar al-Furati informed us, by my reading to him: Abu Musa informed us, Musaddad informed us, from Harun ibn Abdullah al-Jammal, Ibn Abi Fudayk informed us, from al-Khalil ibn Abdullah, from al-Husayn, from Ali ibn Abi Talib, Abu al-Darda', Abu Hurayrah, Abu Umamah al-Bahili, Abdullah ibn Amr, Abdullah ibn Umar, Jabir ibn Abdullah and Imran ibn Husayn, all of whom narrate from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) that he said: "Whoever sends an expense in the Way of Allah and remains in his house, for him is seven hundred dirhams for every dirham. Whoever goes out to fight himself and spends in that cause, for him on the Day of Resurrection is seven hundred thousand dirhams for every dirham." Then he recited this verse: ﴿And Allah multiplies [the reward] for whom He wills.﴾ [[Surat al-Baqarah: 261; the hadith is in Sunan Ibn Majah: 2/922, no. 2761.]]

Commentary of al-Tha'alibi (al-Jawahir al-Hisan) on surah 9, verses 115–121 (part 1 of 2):

﴿And Allah would not let a people go astray after He has guided them﴾. He says: And Allah would not [judge] against you with misguidance after you asked forgiveness for the polytheists, before He had sent down to you the prohibition.

Mujahid said: It is Allah's clarification to the believers regarding abandoning the seeking of forgiveness for the polytheists, specifically, and His clarification to them regarding His disobedience and obedience, generally. So do or abstain.

Muqatil and al-Kalbi said: When Allah the Exalted sent down the obligations, the people acted upon them, then He abrogated them in the Qur'an. Some people were absent and were still acting on the first command, regarding the qibla, wine, and similar matters. They asked the Messenger of Allah ﷺ about this, so Allah the Exalted revealed: ﴿And Allah would not let a people go astray after He has guided them﴾, meaning: Allah would not nullify the deeds of a people who acted upon what had been abrogated, ﴿until He makes clear to them﴾.

Al-Dahhak said: ﴿And Allah would not let a people go astray …until He makes clear to them﴾ what they should do and what they should avoid. ﴿Indeed, Allah is Knowing of all things﴾. Then He magnified Himself, saying: ﴿Indeed, to Allah belongs the dominion of the heavens and the earth﴾, meaning He judges within them as He wills. ﴿He gives life and causes death, and you have not, besides Allah, any protector or helper﴾.

﴿Allah has certainly turned in forgiveness to the Prophet﴾. Ibn 'Abbas said: Whoever Allah has turned to in forgiveness, He will never punish him eternally.

The scholars differed regarding the meaning of "turning in forgiveness" (tawbah) toward the Prophet ﷺ. The people of tafsir (exegesis) said: it refers to his permission to the hypocrites to remain behind from them. The people of ma'ani (the science of meanings) said: it is the opening phrase of a statement, not the subject of their repentance. It is mentioned together with them, like His saying ﴿...then indeed for Allah is one-fifth of it and for the Messenger﴾ and similar, and ﴿the Emigrants and the Helpers who followed him in the hour of hardship﴾, meaning in the time of hardship, without intending a specific hour. Jabir said: The hardship of the mounts, the hardship of provisions, and the hardship of water.

Al-Hasan said: The Muslims would go out on a camel that they took turns riding: a man would ride for a while, then dismount and his companion would ride. Likewise their provisions were moldy dates, barley, and foul-smelling fat. A group of them would go out with nothing but a few dates shared among them. When hunger reached one of them, he would take a date and chew it until he tasted it, then give it to his companion, who would suck it, then drink a sip of water over it, and so on until it reached the last of them, and nothing of the date was left but the pit. They went on in intense heat, while the Messenger of Allah ﷺ was [aware of] their charity and their certainty.

Ibn 'Abbas said: It was said to 'Umar ibn al-Khattab (may Allah be pleased with him): What about the matter of the hardship? 'Umar said: We went out with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ in intense heat. We alighted at a station where we were struck by thirst, until we said: Surely our necks will be cut. A man would go seeking water and not return until he thought his neck would be severed, and a man would slaughter his camel, squeeze its stomach contents, drink them, and place the remainder on his liver. Then Abu Bakr al-Siddiq (may Allah be pleased with him) said to the Messenger of Allah: Allah has accustomed you to good in supplication, so supplicate for us. He said: "Do you wish that?" He said: Yes. So he raised his hands and did not lower them until the sky was overshadowed by clouds, then it poured, and they filled what they had. Then we went to look, and we did not find that it had passed beyond the camp. [Al-Durr al-Manthur: 3/286.]

﴿After the hearts of a faction of them had nearly swerved﴾, meaning: the hearts of a group of them nearly inclined because of the severity of the trial. The common readers recited ﴿taziğ﴾ with a "t" (tazigh), and its evidence is the reading of 'Abdullah, who said: [zaghiyyahum] [So in the manuscript]. Hamzah, al-A'mash, al-Jahdari, and al-'Abbas ibn Zayd al-Thaqafi recited it with a "y" (yazigh). Al-A'mash said: I recited it with "y" intending the feminine verb to be deferred, and in it is an implied subject. ﴿Then He turned to them in forgiveness; indeed, He is Kind and Merciful to them﴾.

﴿And to the three who were left behind﴾, meaning: He turned in forgiveness to the three who stayed behind from the expedition of Tabuk and did not go out. It was also said: they were left behind from the repentance of Abu Lubabah and his companions, and their matter was deferred, and the custom had already passed.

'Ikrimah and Humayd recited ﴿khalafu﴾ with a fatha on the kha and lam and without doubling, meaning [it was delayed behind] the Messenger of Allah ﷺ.

It is related from Ja'far ibn Muhammad al-Sadiq (may Allah be pleased with him) that he recited: ﴿khalafu﴾ [khalifu]. The reading of al-A'mash: ﴿wa 'ala al-thalathati al-mukhallafin﴾. They were Ka'b ibn Malik, the poet, Murarah ibn al-Rabi', and Hilal ibn Umayyah, all of them from the Ansar.

'Ubayd related from 'Abdullah ibn Ka'b ibn Malik al-Ansari, from his father 'Abdullah ibn Ka'b, who was the guide of his father Ka'b when his sight was afflicted. He said: I heard Ka'b ibn Malik relate his account of when he remained behind from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. He said: I never stayed behind from the Prophet ﷺ in any expedition he undertook, until the expedition of Tabuk, except Badr. The Prophet ﷺ did not rebuke anyone who stayed behind from Badr; he only went out intending the caravan, and Quraysh came out to protect their caravan, and they met without an appointment, as Allah the Mighty and Majestic said. By my life, the most honorable of the Messenger of Allah's ﷺ battles among the people was Badr, and I would not have wished that I had witnessed it instead of my pledge on the night of 'Aqabah, when we pledged ourselves to Islam. Then I did not stay behind from the Prophet ﷺ in any expedition he undertook, until the expedition of Tabuk. The people were summoned to depart at a time when the shade was pleasant and the fruit was ripe. The Prophet ﷺ rarely intended an expedition without concealing it by means of another, and he would say: "War is deception." So the Prophet ﷺ intended, in the expedition of Tabuk, that the people prepare for it fully. I was at my easiest, having prepared two mounts, and I was at my most capable in myself for jihad, yet I was inclining toward the shade and the goodness of the fruit. I remained like this until the Prophet ﷺ set out in the morning, and that was on Thursday, and he loved to depart on Thursday. He set out in the morning, and I said: I will go tomorrow to the market to buy my equipment, then I will catch up with them. I went to the market the next day, but some of my affairs became difficult for me, so I returned, saying: I will return tomorrow, God willing, and catch up with them. Again some of my affairs became difficult for me, and I kept on like this until my sin caught up with me, and I stayed behind from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. I began walking in the markets and wandering around Medina, and it grieved me that I saw none who stayed behind except a man accused of hypocrisy or a man whom Allah had excused among the weak. The people were numerous and were not gathered by any register. The total number of those who stayed behind from the Prophet ﷺ was about eighty-some men. The Prophet ﷺ did not mention me until he reached Tabuk, and while he was sitting at Tabuk he said: "What did Ka'b ibn Malik do?" [69]

Some men of my tribe said: O Prophet of Allah, his wealth and his gazing at his sides have detained him. Mu'adh ibn Jabal said to him: What an evil thing you have said! By Allah, O Prophet of Allah, we know nothing but good about him. While they were in that state, suddenly a man appeared in white, a mirage carrying him along. The Prophet ﷺ said: "Be Abu Khaythamah al-Ansari." He was the one who gave a sa' of dates in charity, and the hypocrites mocked him. When the Prophet ﷺ had completed the expedition of Tabuk and returned to Medina, I began to devise [an excuse] to escape the displeasure of the Prophet ﷺ, seeking help in that from every man of sound opinion among my family. When it was said that the Prophet ﷺ had [gone to pray] at dawn, falsehood departed from me, and I knew that I would not be saved except by truthfulness. The Prophet ﷺ entered and prayed two rak'ahs in the mosque, then sat down for the people. When he did that, those who had stayed behind came to him, swearing oaths to him and offering excuses, and he sought forgiveness for them. He accepted their outward profession and left their inner states to Allah the Exalted. I entered the mosque, and there he was sitting. When he saw me, he smiled the smile of one who is angry. I came and sat before him, and he said: "Had you not bought your mount?" [70] I said: Yes, O Messenger of Allah. He said: "Then what kept you back?" [71]

I said: By Allah, if I were sitting before anyone else among the people other than you, I would have escaped his anger with an excuse, for I have been granted eloquence in argument. But I know, O Prophet of Allah, that if I tell you a lie today, to make you pleased with me, Allah will likely reveal it to you. By Allah, O Prophet of Allah, I was never more at ease, nor more free of burden, than when I stayed behind from you.

He ﷺ said: "As for this, he has spoken truthfully. Get up until Allah decides regarding you."

I got up, and some men of my tribe were following me. They said: By Allah, we do not know you to have committed a sin before this. Why did you not offer an excuse to the Prophet ﷺ, so that he would be pleased with you about it? The Prophet's ﷺ seeking forgiveness for you would have been sufficient for your sin. And you did not place yourself in a position where you do not know what will be decided for you! They continued to reproach me until I resolved to return and deny my own statement. I said: Has anyone else said this statement besides me? They said: Yes, two men said what you said: Hilal ibn Umayyah al-Waqifi and Abu Murarah ibn Rabi'ah al-'Amiri. They mentioned two righteous men who had witnessed Badr, in whom I had an example. I said: By Allah, I will not return to him on this matter ever, nor will I deny myself.

He said: The Prophet ﷺ forbade the people from speaking to us, the three of us, among those who stayed behind from him. He said: I began going out to the market, and no one would speak to me. The people turned strange toward us until they were no longer the people we knew, and the walls became strange to us until they were no longer the walls we knew, and the earth became strange to us until it was no longer the earth we knew. [I was the strongest of my companions. I would go out and wander through the markets, come to the mosque, enter, and come to the Prophet ﷺ and greet him. I would say to myself: Did he move his lips with the greeting? When I stood and approached to pray, he would look at me with the corner of his eye, and when I looked at him, he turned away from me. The harshness of the Muslims toward me was prolonged until it was hard on me. I climbed over the wall of the garden of Abu Qatadah, who was my cousin and the dearest of people to me. I greeted him, but by Allah, he did not return my greeting. I said to him: O Abu Qatadah, I ask you by Allah, do you know that I love Allah and His Messenger? He was silent. I repeated my plea, and he said: Allah and His Messenger know best. My eyes overflowed, and I turned away until I climbed over the walls. While I was walking in the market, suddenly a Nabataean Christian man from the Nabataeans of Syria came, bringing food to sell, and saying: Who will show me Ka'b ibn Malik? The people began pointing to me, and he came to me and handed me a letter from the king of Ghassan. In it was: "To proceed: it has reached us that your companion has treated you harshly and cast you out. [You are not in a house of loss or humiliation.] So join us, and we will console you." I said: This is also a trial and an honor. So I heated the oven and burned the letter. When forty nights had passed of the time of the Prophet's ﷺ prohibition of our speaking, suddenly a messenger of the Prophet ﷺ came to me and said: "Withdraw from your wife." I said: Shall I divorce her? He said: "No, but do not approach her." He sent the same message to my two companions. I said to my wife: Go to your family and stay with them until Allah decides this matter. The wife of Hilal came and said: O Prophet of Allah, Hilal ibn Umayyah is a frail old man; will you permit me to serve him? He said: "Yes, but let him not approach you." She said: O Prophet of Allah, by Allah, he has no inclination toward anything; he has been constantly weeping night and day since what happened to him. He said: Some of my family said to me: If only you had asked the Messenger of Allah ﷺ about your wife, since he permitted Hilal's wife to serve him. I said: I will not ask the Messenger of Allah about her, and I do not know what he will say if I ask him about her, while I am a young man.

When fifty nights had passed since the Prophet ﷺ forbade speaking to us, I prayed the dawn prayer on the roof of a house, and I sat in the state that Allah the Mighty and Majestic described: ﴿the earth became constricted for them despite its vastness, and their souls became constricted for them﴾, and I heard a voice from the mountain of Sal': "O Ka'b ibn Malik, rejoice!" I fell down prostrate and knew that Allah had brought relief. Then a man came racing on a horse, and the voice was faster than his horse. [When the one whose voice I heard came to me to give good news, I took off my garment and gave it to him in return for his good news, and I borrowed two garments and wore them.] [From the tafsir of al-Tabari; and in the Musnad of Ahmad: I gave him my garment as a reward for the good news, and I wore two other garments.] He said: Our repentance was revealed to the Prophet ﷺ at two-thirds of the night. Umm Salamah said that evening: O Prophet of Allah, will you not give good news to Ka'b ibn Malik? He said: "If so, the people will rush to you and keep you from sleep for the rest of the night." Umm Salamah had been kind in my matter and grieved over my situation. I went out to the Prophet ﷺ and found him sitting in the mosque with the Muslims around him. Talhah ibn 'Ubaydullah rose to me, hurrying until he shook my hand, and said: "May the repentance of Allah upon you be pleasant for you." By Allah, no man of the Emigrants rose to me except him. Ka'b would never forget this for Talhah.

Ka'b said: When I greeted the Messenger of Allah and said: O Prophet of Allah, is this from Allah or from you? He said: "Rather, it is from Allah." Then he recited to them: ﴿Certainly Allah has turned in forgiveness to the Prophet and the Emigrants﴾ up to His saying ﴿and be with the truthful﴾. I said: O Prophet of Allah, from my repentance is that I should not speak of it except that I withdraw all my wealth as charity to Allah and His Messenger. He said: "Keep some of your wealth for yourself, for it is better for you." I said: Then I will keep my share from Khaybar. He said: Allah has not bestowed upon me any blessing after Islam greater in my soul than my truthfulness with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, when I and my two companions spoke truthfully, so that we would not lie and perish as those others perished. Indeed, I hope that Allah the Mighty and Majestic has not tested anyone in truthfulness [since I mentioned that to the Messenger of Allah, more greatly than He tested me. By Allah, I have not intentionally lied since I said that to the Messenger of Allah until this day]. [From the tafsir of al-Tabari.] And I hope that Allah the Mighty and Majestic will preserve me for what remains. This is what has reached us of the account of the three who were left behind. [See the tafsir of al-Tabari: 11/81–83, and the Musnad of Ahmad: 6/387–390.]

﴿Until, when the earth became constricted for them despite its vastness﴾. The exegetes said: meaning the earth became constricted for them in its entirety. ﴿And their souls became constricted for them﴾ [their hearts became constricted with worry and loneliness], ﴿and they thought that there is no refuge from Allah except in Him﴾. I heard al-Hasan ibn Muhammad ibn Ja'far al-Naysaburi, Ibrahim ibn Muhammad ibn Zayd al-Naysaburi, and 'Abdullah Khatan, governor of the land of Iraq, say: Abu Bakr al-Warraq was asked about sincere repentance (tawbah nasuhah). He said: It is that the earth becomes constricted for us despite its vastness, and our souls become constricted for us, like the repentance of Ka'b and his companion. ﴿Then He turned to them in forgiveness﴾, a repetition of emphasis, ﴿that they may repent﴾; so this is by His repentance.

I heard Abu al-Qasim ibn Abi Bakr al-Sadusi, I heard Abu Sa'id Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Rumayh al-Zaydi, I heard al-Hasan ibn 'Ali al-Damghani say: Abu Yazid said: I erred in four things. In the beginning, with Allah the Exalted, I thought I loved Him, and then He loved me. Allah the Exalted says: ﴿He loves them and they love Him﴾ [Surah al-Ma'idah: 54]. I thought I was pleased with Him, and then He was pleased with me. Allah the Exalted says: ﴿Allah is pleased with them and they are pleased with Him﴾. I thought I remembered Him, and then He remembered me. Allah the Exalted says: ﴿And the remembrance of Allah is greater﴾ [Surah al-'Ankabut: 45]. I wished to repent, and then He repented to me. Allah the Exalted says: ﴿Then He turned to them that they may repent; indeed, Allah is the Accepter of repentance, the Merciful.﴾

﴿O you who have believed, fear Allah and be with the truthful.﴾ Nafi' said: meaning with Muhammad and his companions. Sa'id ibn Jubayr: with Abu Bakr and 'Umar. Ibn Juraij and Ibn Hibban: with the Emigrants, its evidence being His saying: ﴿For the poor Emigrants … it is those who are the truthful﴾ [Surah al-Hashr: 8].

Abdullah ibn Muhammad ibn Abdullah informed me, Muhammad ibn 'Uthman ibn al-Hasan, Muhammad ibn al-Husayn ibn Salih, 'Ali ibn Ja'far ibn Musa, Jandal ibn Wāliq, Muhammad ibn 'Umar al-Mazini, al-Kalbi, from Abu Salih, from Ibn 'Abbas, regarding this verse: ﴿O you who have believed, fear Allah and be with the truthful﴾. He said: With 'Ali ibn Abi Talib and his companions. [See: Nazm Durar al-Simtayn, p. 91, and Shawahid al-Tanzil of al-Hasakani: 1/342.]

And 'Abdullah Muhammad ibn 'Uthman informed me, Muhammad ibn al-Hasan, 'Ali ibn al-'Abbas al-Maqani'i, Ja'far ibn Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, Ahmad ibn Subayh al-Asadi, Mufaddal ibn Salih, from Jabir, from Abu Ja'far, regarding His saying: ﴿and be with the truthful﴾, he said: With the family of Muhammad (ﷺ).

Yaman ibn Rabab: Be truthful as the three who were left behind were truthful.

Ibn 'Abbas: With those whose intentions were sincere, whose hearts and deeds were upright, and who went out with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ to Tabuk, with sincerity and intention.

Qatadah: It means truthfulness of intention. He said: or truthfulness by night and day, in secret and in public. Ibn Mas'ud used to say: ﴿kunu ma'a al-sadiqin﴾ [be with the truthful], and he would recite it so. Ibn 'Abbas (may Allah be pleased with him) related it from the Prophet (ﷺ).

Abdullah ibn Hamid informed us. Abdullah ibn Muhammad ibn al-Husayn. Muhammad ibn Yahya, Wahb ibn Jarir, from Shu'ayb ibn Amr ibn Zayd, from Abu Ubayda, from Abdullah, who said: "Lying is not permissible, whether in earnest or in jest, nor that one of you promises his child something and then does not fulfil it. Recite, if you wish, the verse: ﴿O you who have believed, fear Allah and be with the truthful.﴾ Do you think there is any allowance for lying?"

﴿The people of Madinah and those of the Bedouins around them were not to remain behind from the Messenger of Allah when he went out to fight, nor to prefer their own selves over his self.﴾ The phrase "ma kana li-ahl al-Madinah" has the outward form of a report, but its meaning is a prohibition, like His saying: ﴿It is not for you to harm the Messenger of Allah﴾ [[Surat al-Ahzab: 53.]]. "Those of the Bedouins around them" means the dwellers of the desert: Muzaynah, Juhaynah, Aslam, Ghifar and Ashja'. "Not to remain behind from the Messenger of Allah" means when he goes out to fight. "Nor to prefer their own selves over his self" means in accompanying him, aiding him, and striving alongside him.

Al-Hasan said: it means they should not prefer their own selves to be spared the hardships that befall the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ).

﴿That is because they will not suffer thirst (ẓama') (i.e., thirst), and that is, in the Way of Allah, nor fatigue (naṣab) (i.e., weariness), nor hunger (makhmasa) (i.e., famine).﴾ Abd ibn Umayr recited "ẓama'" with the long vowel, and both are dialectal forms, like khaṭa and khaṭa'. ﴿Nor do they tread upon any ground that enrages the disbelievers, nor do they gain any gain from an enemy﴾, meaning they do not obtain anything from their enemy, whether by killing, capture, booty or seizure. It is said: "nilt al-shay'," so it is "manīl." ﴿Except that a righteous deed is recorded for them thereby.﴾ Ibn Abbas said: for every fright that reaches them in the Way of Allah, seventy thousand good deeds are recorded. ﴿Indeed, Allah does not waste the reward of the good-doers.﴾ So if thirst reaches them, Allah gives them drink from the River of Life (nahr al-hayawan), and they will never thirst again. If fatigue reaches them, Allah gives them honey from the River of Life, and fatigue does not touch them. Whoever goes out in the Way of Allah does not set down a foot, a hand, a side, a nose or a knee in prostration, bowing, walking or sleeping in any spot of the lands of Allah, except that Allah grants him the rank of martyrdom and intercession.

They differed concerning the ruling of this verse. Qatadah said: this is specific to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) when he himself goes out to fight, so no one has the right to remain behind from him, unless the Muslims have no need or necessity for it.

He said: It has been related to us that the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Were it not that I would burden my community, I would not remain behind any expedition that goes out in the Way of Allah. But I find no provision, so I take them with me, and it burdens me to leave them after me." [73] [[Musnad Ahmad: 2/502.]]

Al-Walid ibn Muslim said: I heard al-Awza'i, Ibn al-Mubarak, al-Fazari, al-Sab'i, Ibn Jabir and Sa'id ibn Abd al-Aziz say concerning this verse: it applies to the beginning of this community and to its end.

Ibn Zayd said: this was when the people of Islam were few; when they became many, Allah abrogated it (naskh) and permitted remaining behind for whoever wishes. He said: ﴿The believers should not all go forth﴾ up to the verse. ﴿Nor do they spend any expense, small or great, nor even a whip's lash, nor do they cross any valley on their march, going forward or back, except that it is recorded for them﴾, meaning their traces and steps, ﴿that Allah may reward them with the best of what they were doing.﴾ That is, with reward, and He will admit them to Paradise without reckoning.

Ibn Abbas said: Abu Umar al-Furati informed us, by my reading to him: Abu Musa informed us, Musaddad informed us, from Harun ibn Abdullah al-Jammal, Ibn Abi Fudayk informed us, from al-Khalil ibn Abdullah, from al-Husayn, from Ali ibn Abi Talib, Abu al-Darda', Abu Hurayrah, Abu Umamah al-Bahili, Abdullah ibn Amr, Abdullah ibn Umar, Jabir ibn Abdullah and Imran ibn Husayn, all of whom narrate from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) that he said: "Whoever sends an expense in the Way of Allah and remains in his house, for him is seven hundred dirhams for every dirham. Whoever goes out to fight himself and spends in that cause, for him on the Day of Resurrection is seven hundred thousand dirhams for every dirham." Then he recited this verse: ﴿And Allah multiplies [the reward] for whom He wills.﴾ [[Surat al-Baqarah: 261; the hadith is in Sunan Ibn Majah: 2/922, no. 2761.]]

Commentary of al-Tha'alibi (al-Jawahir al-Hisan) on surah 9, verses 115–121 (part 1 of 2):

﴿And Allah would not let a people go astray after He has guided them﴾. He says: And Allah would not [judge] against you with misguidance after you asked forgiveness for the polytheists, before He had sent down to you the prohibition.

Mujahid said: It is Allah's clarification to the believers regarding abandoning the seeking of forgiveness for the polytheists, specifically, and His clarification to them regarding His disobedience and obedience, generally. So do or abstain.

Muqatil and al-Kalbi said: When Allah the Exalted sent down the obligations, the people acted upon them, then He abrogated them in the Qur'an. Some people were absent and were still acting on the first command, regarding the qibla, wine, and similar matters. They asked the Messenger of Allah ﷺ about this, so Allah the Exalted revealed: ﴿And Allah would not let a people go astray after He has guided them﴾, meaning: Allah would not nullify the deeds of a people who acted upon what had been abrogated, ﴿until He makes clear to them﴾.

Al-Dahhak said: ﴿And Allah would not let a people go astray …until He makes clear to them﴾ what they should do and what they should avoid. ﴿Indeed, Allah is Knowing of all things﴾. Then He magnified Himself, saying: ﴿Indeed, to Allah belongs the dominion of the heavens and the earth﴾, meaning He judges within them as He wills. ﴿He gives life and causes death, and you have not, besides Allah, any protector or helper﴾.

﴿Allah has certainly turned in forgiveness to the Prophet﴾. Ibn 'Abbas said: Whoever Allah has turned to in forgiveness, He will never punish him eternally.

The scholars differed regarding the meaning of "turning in forgiveness" (tawbah) toward the Prophet ﷺ. The people of tafsir (exegesis) said: it refers to his permission to the hypocrites to remain behind from them. The people of ma'ani (the science of meanings) said: it is the opening phrase of a statement, not the subject of their repentance. It is mentioned together with them, like His saying ﴿...then indeed for Allah is one-fifth of it and for the Messenger﴾ and similar, and ﴿the Emigrants and the Helpers who followed him in the hour of hardship﴾, meaning in the time of hardship, without intending a specific hour. Jabir said: The hardship of the mounts, the hardship of provisions, and the hardship of water.

Al-Hasan said: The Muslims would go out on a camel that they took turns riding: a man would ride for a while, then dismount and his companion would ride. Likewise their provisions were moldy dates, barley, and foul-smelling fat. A group of them would go out with nothing but a few dates shared among them. When hunger reached one of them, he would take a date and chew it until he tasted it, then give it to his companion, who would suck it, then drink a sip of water over it, and so on until it reached the last of them, and nothing of the date was left but the pit. They went on in intense heat, while the Messenger of Allah ﷺ was [aware of] their charity and their certainty.

Ibn 'Abbas said: It was said to 'Umar ibn al-Khattab (may Allah be pleased with him): What about the matter of the hardship? 'Umar said: We went out with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ in intense heat. We alighted at a station where we were struck by thirst, until we said: Surely our necks will be cut. A man would go seeking water and not return until he thought his neck would be severed, and a man would slaughter his camel, squeeze its stomach contents, drink them, and place the remainder on his liver. Then Abu Bakr al-Siddiq (may Allah be pleased with him) said to the Messenger of Allah: Allah has accustomed you to good in supplication, so supplicate for us. He said: "Do you wish that?" He said: Yes. So he raised his hands and did not lower them until the sky was overshadowed by clouds, then it poured, and they filled what they had. Then we went to look, and we did not find that it had passed beyond the camp. [Al-Durr al-Manthur: 3/286.]

﴿After the hearts of a faction of them had nearly swerved﴾, meaning: the hearts of a group of them nearly inclined because of the severity of the trial. The common readers recited ﴿taziğ﴾ with a "t" (tazigh), and its evidence is the reading of 'Abdullah, who said: [zaghiyyahum] [So in the manuscript]. Hamzah, al-A'mash, al-Jahdari, and al-'Abbas ibn Zayd al-Thaqafi recited it with a "y" (yazigh). Al-A'mash said: I recited it with "y" intending the feminine verb to be deferred, and in it is an implied subject. ﴿Then He turned to them in forgiveness; indeed, He is Kind and Merciful to them﴾.

﴿And to the three who were left behind﴾, meaning: He turned in forgiveness to the three who stayed behind from the expedition of Tabuk and did not go out. It was also said: they were left behind from the repentance of Abu Lubabah and his companions, and their matter was deferred, and the custom had already passed.

'Ikrimah and Humayd recited ﴿khalafu﴾ with a fatha on the kha and lam and without doubling, meaning [it was delayed behind] the Messenger of Allah ﷺ.

It is related from Ja'far ibn Muhammad al-Sadiq (may Allah be pleased with him) that he recited: ﴿khalafu﴾ [khalifu]. The reading of al-A'mash: ﴿wa 'ala al-thalathati al-mukhallafin﴾. They were Ka'b ibn Malik, the poet, Murarah ibn al-Rabi', and Hilal ibn Umayyah, all of them from the Ansar.

'Ubayd related from 'Abdullah ibn Ka'b ibn Malik al-Ansari, from his father 'Abdullah ibn Ka'b, who was the guide of his father Ka'b when his sight was afflicted. He said: I heard Ka'b ibn Malik relate his account of when he remained behind from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. He said: I never stayed behind from the Prophet ﷺ in any expedition he undertook, until the expedition of Tabuk, except Badr. The Prophet ﷺ did not rebuke anyone who stayed behind from Badr; he only went out intending the caravan, and Quraysh came out to protect their caravan, and they met without an appointment, as Allah the Mighty and Majestic said. By my life, the most honorable of the Messenger of Allah's ﷺ battles among the people was Badr, and I would not have wished that I had witnessed it instead of my pledge on the night of 'Aqabah, when we pledged ourselves to Islam. Then I did not stay behind from the Prophet ﷺ in any expedition he undertook, until the expedition of Tabuk. The people were summoned to depart at a time when the shade was pleasant and the fruit was ripe. The Prophet ﷺ rarely intended an expedition without concealing it by means of another, and he would say: "War is deception." So the Prophet ﷺ intended, in the expedition of Tabuk, that the people prepare for it fully. I was at my easiest, having prepared two mounts, and I was at my most capable in myself for jihad, yet I was inclining toward the shade and the goodness of the fruit. I remained like this until the Prophet ﷺ set out in the morning, and that was on Thursday, and he loved to depart on Thursday. He set out in the morning, and I said: I will go tomorrow to the market to buy my equipment, then I will catch up with them. I went to the market the next day, but some of my affairs became difficult for me, so I returned, saying: I will return tomorrow, God willing, and catch up with them. Again some of my affairs became difficult for me, and I kept on like this until my sin caught up with me, and I stayed behind from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. I began walking in the markets and wandering around Medina, and it grieved me that I saw none who stayed behind except a man accused of hypocrisy or a man whom Allah had excused among the weak. The people were numerous and were not gathered by any register. The total number of those who stayed behind from the Prophet ﷺ was about eighty-some men. The Prophet ﷺ did not mention me until he reached Tabuk, and while he was sitting at Tabuk he said: "What did Ka'b ibn Malik do?" [69]

Some men of my tribe said: O Prophet of Allah, his wealth and his gazing at his sides have detained him. Mu'adh ibn Jabal said to him: What an evil thing you have said! By Allah, O Prophet of Allah, we know nothing but good about him. While they were in that state, suddenly a man appeared in white, a mirage carrying him along. The Prophet ﷺ said: "Be Abu Khaythamah al-Ansari." He was the one who gave a sa' of dates in charity, and the hypocrites mocked him. When the Prophet ﷺ had completed the expedition of Tabuk and returned to Medina, I began to devise [an excuse] to escape the displeasure of the Prophet ﷺ, seeking help in that from every man of sound opinion among my family. When it was said that the Prophet ﷺ had [gone to pray] at dawn, falsehood departed from me, and I knew that I would not be saved except by truthfulness. The Prophet ﷺ entered and prayed two rak'ahs in the mosque, then sat down for the people. When he did that, those who had stayed behind came to him, swearing oaths to him and offering excuses, and he sought forgiveness for them. He accepted their outward profession and left their inner states to Allah the Exalted. I entered the mosque, and there he was sitting. When he saw me, he smiled the smile of one who is angry. I came and sat before him, and he said: "Had you not bought your mount?" [70] I said: Yes, O Messenger of Allah. He said: "Then what kept you back?" [71]

I said: By Allah, if I were sitting before anyone else among the people other than you, I would have escaped his anger with an excuse, for I have been granted eloquence in argument. But I know, O Prophet of Allah, that if I tell you a lie today, to make you pleased with me, Allah will likely reveal it to you. By Allah, O Prophet of Allah, I was never more at ease, nor more free of burden, than when I stayed behind from you.

He ﷺ said: "As for this, he has spoken truthfully. Get up until Allah decides regarding you."

I got up, and some men of my tribe were following me. They said: By Allah, we do not know you to have committed a sin before this. Why did you not offer an excuse to the Prophet ﷺ, so that he would be pleased with you about it? The Prophet's ﷺ seeking forgiveness for you would have been sufficient for your sin. And you did not place yourself in a position where you do not know what will be decided for you! They continued to reproach me until I resolved to return and deny my own statement. I said: Has anyone else said this statement besides me? They said: Yes, two men said what you said: Hilal ibn Umayyah al-Waqifi and Abu Murarah ibn Rabi'ah al-'Amiri. They mentioned two righteous men who had witnessed Badr, in whom I had an example. I said: By Allah, I will not return to him on this matter ever, nor will I deny myself.

He said: The Prophet ﷺ forbade the people from speaking to us, the three of us, among those who stayed behind from him. He said: I began going out to the market, and no one would speak to me. The people turned strange toward us until they were no longer the people we knew, and the walls became strange to us until they were no longer the walls we knew, and the earth became strange to us until it was no longer the earth we knew. [I was the strongest of my companions. I would go out and wander through the markets, come to the mosque, enter, and come to the Prophet ﷺ and greet him. I would say to myself: Did he move his lips with the greeting? When I stood and approached to pray, he would look at me with the corner of his eye, and when I looked at him, he turned away from me. The harshness of the Muslims toward me was prolonged until it was hard on me. I climbed over the wall of the garden of Abu Qatadah, who was my cousin and the dearest of people to me. I greeted him, but by Allah, he did not return my greeting. I said to him: O Abu Qatadah, I ask you by Allah, do you know that I love Allah and His Messenger? He was silent. I repeated my plea, and he said: Allah and His Messenger know best. My eyes overflowed, and I turned away until I climbed over the walls. While I was walking in the market, suddenly a Nabataean Christian man from the Nabataeans of Syria came, bringing food to sell, and saying: Who will show me Ka'b ibn Malik? The people began pointing to me, and he came to me and handed me a letter from the king of Ghassan. In it was: "To proceed: it has reached us that your companion has treated you harshly and cast you out. [You are not in a house of loss or humiliation.] So join us, and we will console you." I said: This is also a trial and an honor. So I heated the oven and burned the letter. When forty nights had passed of the time of the Prophet's ﷺ prohibition of our speaking, suddenly a messenger of the Prophet ﷺ came to me and said: "Withdraw from your wife." I said: Shall I divorce her? He said: "No, but do not approach her." He sent the same message to my two companions. I said to my wife: Go to your family and stay with them until Allah decides this matter. The wife of Hilal came and said: O Prophet of Allah, Hilal ibn Umayyah is a frail old man; will you permit me to serve him? He said: "Yes, but let him not approach you." She said: O Prophet of Allah, by Allah, he has no inclination toward anything; he has been constantly weeping night and day since what happened to him. He said: Some of my family said to me: If only you had asked the Messenger of Allah ﷺ about your wife, since he permitted Hilal's wife to serve him. I said: I will not ask the Messenger of Allah about her, and I do not know what he will say if I ask him about her, while I am a young man.

When fifty nights had passed since the Prophet ﷺ forbade speaking to us, I prayed the dawn prayer on the roof of a house, and I sat in the state that Allah the Mighty and Majestic described: ﴿the earth became constricted for them despite its vastness, and their souls became constricted for them﴾, and I heard a voice from the mountain of Sal': "O Ka'b ibn Malik, rejoice!" I fell down prostrate and knew that Allah had brought relief. Then a man came racing on a horse, and the voice was faster than his horse. [When the one whose voice I heard came to me to give good news, I took off my garment and gave it to him in return for his good news, and I borrowed two garments and wore them.] [From the tafsir of al-Tabari; and in the Musnad of Ahmad: I gave him my garment as a reward for the good news, and I wore two other garments.] He said: Our repentance was revealed to the Prophet ﷺ at two-thirds of the night. Umm Salamah said that evening: O Prophet of Allah, will you not give good news to Ka'b ibn Malik? He said: "If so, the people will rush to you and keep you from sleep for the rest of the night." Umm Salamah had been kind in my matter and grieved over my situation. I went out to the Prophet ﷺ and found him sitting in the mosque with the Muslims around him. Talhah ibn 'Ubaydullah rose to me, hurrying until he shook my hand, and said: "May the repentance of Allah upon you be pleasant for you." By Allah, no man of the Emigrants rose to me except him. Ka'b would never forget this for Talhah.

Ka'b said: When I greeted the Messenger of Allah and said: O Prophet of Allah, is this from Allah or from you? He said: "Rather, it is from Allah." Then he recited to them: ﴿Certainly Allah has turned in forgiveness to the Prophet and the Emigrants﴾ up to His saying ﴿and be with the truthful﴾. I said: O Prophet of Allah, from my repentance is that I should not speak of it except that I withdraw all my wealth as charity to Allah and His Messenger. He said: "Keep some of your wealth for yourself, for it is better for you." I said: Then I will keep my share from Khaybar. He said: Allah has not bestowed upon me any blessing after Islam greater in my soul than my truthfulness with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, when I and my two companions spoke truthfully, so that we would not lie and perish as those others perished. Indeed, I hope that Allah the Mighty and Majestic has not tested anyone in truthfulness [since I mentioned that to the Messenger of Allah, more greatly than He tested me. By Allah, I have not intentionally lied since I said that to the Messenger of Allah until this day]. [From the tafsir of al-Tabari.] And I hope that Allah the Mighty and Majestic will preserve me for what remains. This is what has reached us of the account of the three who were left behind. [See the tafsir of al-Tabari: 11/81–83, and the Musnad of Ahmad: 6/387–390.]

﴿Until, when the earth became constricted for them despite its vastness﴾. The exegetes said: meaning the earth became constricted for them in its entirety. ﴿And their souls became constricted for them﴾ [their hearts became constricted with worry and loneliness], ﴿and they thought that there is no refuge from Allah except in Him﴾. I heard al-Hasan ibn Muhammad ibn Ja'far al-Naysaburi, Ibrahim ibn Muhammad ibn Zayd al-Naysaburi, and 'Abdullah Khatan, governor of the land of Iraq, say: Abu Bakr al-Warraq was asked about sincere repentance (tawbah nasuhah). He said: It is that the earth becomes constricted for us despite its vastness, and our souls become constricted for us, like the repentance of Ka'b and his companion. ﴿Then He turned to them in forgiveness﴾, a repetition of emphasis, ﴿that they may repent﴾; so this is by His repentance.

I heard Abu al-Qasim ibn Abi Bakr al-Sadusi, I heard Abu Sa'id Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Rumayh al-Zaydi, I heard al-Hasan ibn 'Ali al-Damghani say: Abu Yazid said: I erred in four things. In the beginning, with Allah the Exalted, I thought I loved Him, and then He loved me. Allah the Exalted says: ﴿He loves them and they love Him﴾ [Surah al-Ma'idah: 54]. I thought I was pleased with Him, and then He was pleased with me. Allah the Exalted says: ﴿Allah is pleased with them and they are pleased with Him﴾. I thought I remembered Him, and then He remembered me. Allah the Exalted says: ﴿And the remembrance of Allah is greater﴾ [Surah al-'Ankabut: 45]. I wished to repent, and then He repented to me. Allah the Exalted says: ﴿Then He turned to them that they may repent; indeed, Allah is the Accepter of repentance, the Merciful.﴾

﴿O you who have believed, fear Allah and be with the truthful.﴾ Nafi' said: meaning with Muhammad and his companions. Sa'id ibn Jubayr: with Abu Bakr and 'Umar. Ibn Juraij and Ibn Hibban: with the Emigrants, its evidence being His saying: ﴿For the poor Emigrants … it is those who are the truthful﴾ [Surah al-Hashr: 8].

Abdullah ibn Muhammad ibn Abdullah informed me, Muhammad ibn 'Uthman ibn al-Hasan, Muhammad ibn al-Husayn ibn Salih, 'Ali ibn Ja'far ibn Musa, Jandal ibn Wāliq, Muhammad ibn 'Umar al-Mazini, al-Kalbi, from Abu Salih, from Ibn 'Abbas, regarding this verse: ﴿O you who have believed, fear Allah and be with the truthful﴾. He said: With 'Ali ibn Abi Talib and his companions. [See: Nazm Durar al-Simtayn, p. 91, and Shawahid al-Tanzil of al-Hasakani: 1/342.]

And 'Abdullah Muhammad ibn 'Uthman informed me, Muhammad ibn al-Hasan, 'Ali ibn al-'Abbas al-Maqani'i, Ja'far ibn Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, Ahmad ibn Subayh al-Asadi, Mufaddal ibn Salih, from Jabir, from Abu Ja'far, regarding His saying: ﴿and be with the truthful﴾, he said: With the family of Muhammad (ﷺ).

Yaman ibn Rabab: Be truthful as the three who were left behind were truthful.

Ibn 'Abbas: With those whose intentions were sincere, whose hearts and deeds were upright, and who went out with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ to Tabuk, with sincerity and intention.

Qatadah: It means truthfulness of intention. He said: or truthfulness by night and day, in secret and in public. Ibn Mas'ud used to say: ﴿kunu ma'a al-sadiqin﴾ [be with the truthful], and he would recite it so. Ibn 'Abbas (may Allah be pleased with him) related it from the Prophet (ﷺ).

Abdullah ibn Hamid informed us. Abdullah ibn Muhammad ibn al-Husayn. Muhammad ibn Yahya, Wahb ibn Jarir, from Shu'ayb ibn Amr ibn Zayd, from Abu Ubayda, from Abdullah, who said: "Lying is not permissible, whether in earnest or in jest, nor that one of you promises his child something and then does not fulfil it. Recite, if you wish, the verse: ﴿O you who have believed, fear Allah and be with the truthful.﴾ Do you think there is any allowance for lying?"

﴿The people of Madinah and those of the Bedouins around them were not to remain behind from the Messenger of Allah when he went out to fight, nor to prefer their own selves over his self.﴾ The phrase "ma kana li-ahl al-Madinah" has the outward form of a report, but its meaning is a prohibition, like His saying: ﴿It is not for you to harm the Messenger of Allah﴾ [[Surat al-Ahzab: 53.]]. "Those of the Bedouins around them" means the dwellers of the desert: Muzaynah, Juhaynah, Aslam, Ghifar and Ashja'. "Not to remain behind from the Messenger of Allah" means when he goes out to fight. "Nor to prefer their own selves over his self" means in accompanying him, aiding him, and striving alongside him.

Al-Hasan said: it means they should not prefer their own selves to be spared the hardships that befall the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ).

﴿That is because they will not suffer thirst (ẓama') (i.e., thirst), and that is, in the Way of Allah, nor fatigue (naṣab) (i.e., weariness), nor hunger (makhmasa) (i.e., famine).﴾ Abd ibn Umayr recited "ẓama'" with the long vowel, and both are dialectal forms, like khaṭa and khaṭa'. ﴿Nor do they tread upon any ground that enrages the disbelievers, nor do they gain any gain from an enemy﴾, meaning they do not obtain anything from their enemy, whether by killing, capture, booty or seizure. It is said: "nilt al-shay'," so it is "manīl." ﴿Except that a righteous deed is recorded for them thereby.﴾ Ibn Abbas said: for every fright that reaches them in the Way of Allah, seventy thousand good deeds are recorded. ﴿Indeed, Allah does not waste the reward of the good-doers.﴾ So if thirst reaches them, Allah gives them drink from the River of Life (nahr al-hayawan), and they will never thirst again. If fatigue reaches them, Allah gives them honey from the River of Life, and fatigue does not touch them. Whoever goes out in the Way of Allah does not set down a foot, a hand, a side, a nose or a knee in prostration, bowing, walking or sleeping in any spot of the lands of Allah, except that Allah grants him the rank of martyrdom and intercession.

They differed concerning the ruling of this verse. Qatadah said: this is specific to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) when he himself goes out to fight, so no one has the right to remain behind from him, unless the Muslims have no need or necessity for it.

He said: It has been related to us that the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Were it not that I would burden my community, I would not remain behind any expedition that goes out in the Way of Allah. But I find no provision, so I take them with me, and it burdens me to leave them after me." [73] [[Musnad Ahmad: 2/502.]]

Al-Walid ibn Muslim said: I heard al-Awza'i, Ibn al-Mubarak, al-Fazari, al-Sab'i, Ibn Jabir and Sa'id ibn Abd al-Aziz say concerning this verse: it applies to the beginning of this community and to its end.

Ibn Zayd said: this was when the people of Islam were few; when they became many, Allah abrogated it (naskh) and permitted remaining behind for whoever wishes. He said: ﴿The believers should not all go forth﴾ up to the verse. ﴿Nor do they spend any expense, small or great, nor even a whip's lash, nor do they cross any valley on their march, going forward or back, except that it is recorded for them﴾, meaning their traces and steps, ﴿that Allah may reward them with the best of what they were doing.﴾ That is, with reward, and He will admit them to Paradise without reckoning.

Ibn Abbas said: Abu Umar al-Furati informed us, by my reading to him: Abu Musa informed us, Musaddad informed us, from Harun ibn Abdullah al-Jammal, Ibn Abi Fudayk informed us, from al-Khalil ibn Abdullah, from al-Husayn, from Ali ibn Abi Talib, Abu al-Darda', Abu Hurayrah, Abu Umamah al-Bahili, Abdullah ibn Amr, Abdullah ibn Umar, Jabir ibn Abdullah and Imran ibn Husayn, all of whom narrate from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) that he said: "Whoever sends an expense in the Way of Allah and remains in his house, for him is seven hundred dirhams for every dirham. Whoever goes out to fight himself and spends in that cause, for him on the Day of Resurrection is seven hundred thousand dirhams for every dirham." Then he recited this verse: ﴿And Allah multiplies [the reward] for whom He wills.﴾ [[Surat al-Baqarah: 261; the hadith is in Sunan Ibn Majah: 2/922, no. 2761.]]

Commentary of al-Tha'alibi (al-Jawahir al-Hisan) on surah 9, verses 115–121 (part 1 of 2):

﴿And Allah would not let a people go astray after He has guided them﴾. He says: And Allah would not [judge] against you with misguidance after you asked forgiveness for the polytheists, before He had sent down to you the prohibition.

Mujahid said: It is Allah's clarification to the believers regarding abandoning the seeking of forgiveness for the polytheists, specifically, and His clarification to them regarding His disobedience and obedience, generally. So do or abstain.

Muqatil and al-Kalbi said: When Allah the Exalted sent down the obligations, the people acted upon them, then He abrogated them in the Qur'an. Some people were absent and were still acting on the first command, regarding the qibla, wine, and similar matters. They asked the Messenger of Allah ﷺ about this, so Allah the Exalted revealed: ﴿And Allah would not let a people go astray after He has guided them﴾, meaning: Allah would not nullify the deeds of a people who acted upon what had been abrogated, ﴿until He makes clear to them﴾.

Al-Dahhak said: ﴿And Allah would not let a people go astray …until He makes clear to them﴾ what they should do and what they should avoid. ﴿Indeed, Allah is Knowing of all things﴾. Then He magnified Himself, saying: ﴿Indeed, to Allah belongs the dominion of the heavens and the earth﴾, meaning He judges within them as He wills. ﴿He gives life and causes death, and you have not, besides Allah, any protector or helper﴾.

﴿Allah has certainly turned in forgiveness to the Prophet﴾. Ibn 'Abbas said: Whoever Allah has turned to in forgiveness, He will never punish him eternally.

The scholars differed regarding the meaning of "turning in forgiveness" (tawbah) toward the Prophet ﷺ. The people of tafsir (exegesis) said: it refers to his permission to the hypocrites to remain behind from them. The people of ma'ani (the science of meanings) said: it is the opening phrase of a statement, not the subject of their repentance. It is mentioned together with them, like His saying ﴿...then indeed for Allah is one-fifth of it and for the Messenger﴾ and similar, and ﴿the Emigrants and the Helpers who followed him in the hour of hardship﴾, meaning in the time of hardship, without intending a specific hour. Jabir said: The hardship of the mounts, the hardship of provisions, and the hardship of water.

Al-Hasan said: The Muslims would go out on a camel that they took turns riding: a man would ride for a while, then dismount and his companion would ride. Likewise their provisions were moldy dates, barley, and foul-smelling fat. A group of them would go out with nothing but a few dates shared among them. When hunger reached one of them, he would take a date and chew it until he tasted it, then give it to his companion, who would suck it, then drink a sip of water over it, and so on until it reached the last of them, and nothing of the date was left but the pit. They went on in intense heat, while the Messenger of Allah ﷺ was [aware of] their charity and their certainty.

Ibn 'Abbas said: It was said to 'Umar ibn al-Khattab (may Allah be pleased with him): What about the matter of the hardship? 'Umar said: We went out with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ in intense heat. We alighted at a station where we were struck by thirst, until we said: Surely our necks will be cut. A man would go seeking water and not return until he thought his neck would be severed, and a man would slaughter his camel, squeeze its stomach contents, drink them, and place the remainder on his liver. Then Abu Bakr al-Siddiq (may Allah be pleased with him) said to the Messenger of Allah: Allah has accustomed you to good in supplication, so supplicate for us. He said: "Do you wish that?" He said: Yes. So he raised his hands and did not lower them until the sky was overshadowed by clouds, then it poured, and they filled what they had. Then we went to look, and we did not find that it had passed beyond the camp. [Al-Durr al-Manthur: 3/286.]

﴿After the hearts of a faction of them had nearly swerved﴾, meaning: the hearts of a group of them nearly inclined because of the severity of the trial. The common readers recited ﴿taziğ﴾ with a "t" (tazigh), and its evidence is the reading of 'Abdullah, who said: [zaghiyyahum] [So in the manuscript]. Hamzah, al-A'mash, al-Jahdari, and al-'Abbas ibn Zayd al-Thaqafi recited it with a "y" (yazigh). Al-A'mash said: I recited it with "y" intending the feminine verb to be deferred, and in it is an implied subject. ﴿Then He turned to them in forgiveness; indeed, He is Kind and Merciful to them﴾.

﴿And to the three who were left behind﴾, meaning: He turned in forgiveness to the three who stayed behind from the expedition of Tabuk and did not go out. It was also said: they were left behind from the repentance of Abu Lubabah and his companions, and their matter was deferred, and the custom had already passed.

'Ikrimah and Humayd recited ﴿khalafu﴾ with a fatha on the kha and lam and without doubling, meaning [it was delayed behind] the Messenger of Allah ﷺ.
