I greeted him, but by Allah, he did not return my greeting. I said to him: O Abu Qatadah, I ask you by Allah, do you know that I love Allah and His Messenger? He was silent. I repeated my plea, and he said: Allah and His Messenger know best. My eyes overflowed, and I turned away until I climbed over the walls. While I was walking in the market, suddenly a Nabataean Christian man from the Nabataeans of Syria came, bringing food to sell, and saying: Who will show me Ka'b ibn Malik? The people began pointing to me, and he came to me and handed me a letter from the king of Ghassan. In it was: "To proceed: it has reached us that your companion has treated you harshly and cast you out. [You are not in a house of loss or humiliation.] So join us, and we will console you." I said: This is also a trial and an honor. So I heated the oven and burned the letter. When forty nights had passed of the time of the Prophet's ﷺ prohibition of our speaking, suddenly a messenger of the Prophet ﷺ came to me and said: "Withdraw from your wife." I said: Shall I divorce her? He said: "No, but do not approach her." He sent the same message to my two companions. I said to my wife: Go to your family and stay with them until Allah decides this matter. The wife of Hilal came and said: O Prophet of Allah, Hilal ibn Umayyah is a frail old man; will you permit me to serve him? He said: "Yes, but let him not approach you." She said: O Prophet of Allah, by Allah, he has no inclination toward anything; he has been constantly weeping night and day since what happened to him. He said: Some of my family said to me: If only you had asked the Messenger of Allah ﷺ about your wife, since he permitted Hilal's wife to serve him. I said: I will not ask the Messenger of Allah about her, and I do not know what he will say if I ask him about her, while I am a young man.

When fifty nights had passed since the Prophet ﷺ forbade speaking to us, I prayed the dawn prayer on the roof of a house, and I sat in the state that Allah the Mighty and Majestic described: ﴿the earth became constricted for them despite its vastness, and their souls became constricted for them﴾, and I heard a voice from the mountain of Sal': "O Ka'b ibn Malik, rejoice!" I fell down prostrate and knew that Allah had brought relief. Then a man came racing on a horse, and the voice was faster than his horse. [When the one whose voice I heard came to me to give good news, I took off my garment and gave it to him in return for his good news, and I borrowed two garments and wore them.] [From the tafsir of al-Tabari; and in the Musnad of Ahmad: I gave him my garment as a reward for the good news, and I wore two other garments.] He said: Our repentance was revealed to the Prophet ﷺ at two-thirds of the night. Umm Salamah said that evening: O Prophet of Allah, will you not give good news to Ka'b ibn Malik? He said: "If so, the people will rush to you and keep you from sleep for the rest of the night." Umm Salamah had been kind in my matter and grieved over my situation. I went out to the Prophet ﷺ and found him sitting in the mosque with the Muslims around him. Talhah ibn 'Ubaydullah rose to me, hurrying until he shook my hand, and said: "May the repentance of Allah upon you be pleasant for you." By Allah, no man of the Emigrants rose to me except him. Ka'b would never forget this for Talhah.

Ka'b said: When I greeted the Messenger of Allah and said: O Prophet of Allah, is this from Allah or from you? He said: "Rather, it is from Allah." Then he recited to them: ﴿Certainly Allah has turned in forgiveness to the Prophet and the Emigrants﴾ up to His saying ﴿and be with the truthful﴾. I said: O Prophet of Allah, from my repentance is that I should not speak of it except that I withdraw all my wealth as charity to Allah and His Messenger. He said: "Keep some of your wealth for yourself, for it is better for you." I said: Then I will keep my share from Khaybar. He said: Allah has not bestowed upon me any blessing after Islam greater in my soul than my truthfulness with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, when I and my two companions spoke truthfully, so that we would not lie and perish as those others perished. Indeed, I hope that Allah the Mighty and Majestic has not tested anyone in truthfulness [since I mentioned that to the Messenger of Allah, more greatly than He tested me. By Allah, I have not intentionally lied since I said that to the Messenger of Allah until this day]. [From the tafsir of al-Tabari.] And I hope that Allah the Mighty and Majestic will preserve me for what remains. This is what has reached us of the account of the three who were left behind. [See the tafsir of al-Tabari: 11/81–83, and the Musnad of Ahmad: 6/387–390.]

﴿Until, when the earth became constricted for them despite its vastness﴾. The exegetes said: meaning the earth became constricted for them in its entirety. ﴿And their souls became constricted for them﴾ [their hearts became constricted with worry and loneliness], ﴿and they thought that there is no refuge from Allah except in Him﴾. I heard al-Hasan ibn Muhammad ibn Ja'far al-Naysaburi, Ibrahim ibn Muhammad ibn Zayd al-Naysaburi, and 'Abdullah Khatan, governor of the land of Iraq, say: Abu Bakr al-Warraq was asked about sincere repentance (tawbah nasuhah). He said: It is that the earth becomes constricted for us despite its vastness, and our souls become constricted for us, like the repentance of Ka'b and his companion. ﴿Then He turned to them in forgiveness﴾, a repetition of emphasis, ﴿that they may repent﴾; so this is by His repentance.

I heard Abu al-Qasim ibn Abi Bakr al-Sadusi, I heard Abu Sa'id Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Rumayh al-Zaydi, I heard al-Hasan ibn 'Ali al-Damghani say: Abu Yazid said: I erred in four things. In the beginning, with Allah the Exalted, I thought I loved Him, and then He loved me. Allah the Exalted says: ﴿He loves them and they love Him﴾ [Surah al-Ma'idah: 54]. I thought I was pleased with Him, and then He was pleased with me. Allah the Exalted says: ﴿Allah is pleased with them and they are pleased with Him﴾. I thought I remembered Him, and then He remembered me. Allah the Exalted says: ﴿And the remembrance of Allah is greater﴾ [Surah al-'Ankabut: 45]. I wished to repent, and then He repented to me. Allah the Exalted says: ﴿Then He turned to them that they may repent; indeed, Allah is the Accepter of repentance, the Merciful.﴾

﴿O you who have believed, fear Allah and be with the truthful.﴾ Nafi' said: meaning with Muhammad and his companions. Sa'id ibn Jubayr: with Abu Bakr and 'Umar. Ibn Juraij and Ibn Hibban: with the Emigrants, its evidence being His saying: ﴿For the poor Emigrants … it is those who are the truthful﴾ [Surah al-Hashr: 8].

Abdullah ibn Muhammad ibn Abdullah informed me, Muhammad ibn 'Uthman ibn al-Hasan, Muhammad ibn al-Husayn ibn Salih, 'Ali ibn Ja'far ibn Musa, Jandal ibn Wāliq, Muhammad ibn 'Umar al-Mazini, al-Kalbi, from Abu Salih, from Ibn 'Abbas, regarding this verse: ﴿O you who have believed, fear Allah and be with the truthful﴾. He said: With 'Ali ibn Abi Talib and his companions. [See: Nazm Durar al-Simtayn, p. 91, and Shawahid al-Tanzil of al-Hasakani: 1/342.]

And 'Abdullah Muhammad ibn 'Uthman informed me, Muhammad ibn al-Hasan, 'Ali ibn al-'Abbas al-Maqani'i, Ja'far ibn Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, Ahmad ibn Subayh al-Asadi, Mufaddal ibn Salih, from Jabir, from Abu Ja'far, regarding His saying: ﴿and be with the truthful﴾, he said: With the family of Muhammad (ﷺ).

Yaman ibn Rabab: Be truthful as the three who were left behind were truthful.

Ibn 'Abbas: With those whose intentions were sincere, whose hearts and deeds were upright, and who went out with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ to Tabuk, with sincerity and intention.

Qatadah: It means truthfulness of intention. He said: or truthfulness by night and day, in secret and in public. Ibn Mas'ud used to say: ﴿kunu ma'a al-sadiqin﴾ [be with the truthful], and he would recite it so. Ibn 'Abbas (may Allah be pleased with him) related it from the Prophet (ﷺ).

Abdullah ibn Hamid informed us. Abdullah ibn Muhammad ibn al-Husayn. Muhammad ibn Yahya, Wahb ibn Jarir, from Shu'ayb ibn Amr ibn Zayd, from Abu Ubayda, from Abdullah, who said: "Lying is not permissible, whether in earnest or in jest, nor that one of you promises his child something and then does not fulfil it. Recite, if you wish, the verse: ﴿O you who have believed, fear Allah and be with the truthful.﴾ Do you think there is any allowance for lying?"

﴿The people of Madinah and those of the Bedouins around them were not to remain behind from the Messenger of Allah when he went out to fight, nor to prefer their own selves over his self.﴾ The phrase "ma kana li-ahl al-Madinah" has the outward form of a report, but its meaning is a prohibition, like His saying: ﴿It is not for you to harm the Messenger of Allah﴾ [[Surat al-Ahzab: 53.]]. "Those of the Bedouins around them" means the dwellers of the desert: Muzaynah, Juhaynah, Aslam, Ghifar and Ashja'. "Not to remain behind from the Messenger of Allah" means when he goes out to fight. "Nor to prefer their own selves over his self" means in accompanying him, aiding him, and striving alongside him.

Al-Hasan said: it means they should not prefer their own selves to be spared the hardships that befall the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ).

﴿That is because they will not suffer thirst (ẓama') (i.e., thirst), and that is, in the Way of Allah, nor fatigue (naṣab) (i.e., weariness), nor hunger (makhmasa) (i.e., famine).﴾ Abd ibn Umayr recited "ẓama'" with the long vowel, and both are dialectal forms, like khaṭa and khaṭa'. ﴿Nor do they tread upon any ground that enrages the disbelievers, nor do they gain any gain from an enemy﴾, meaning they do not obtain anything from their enemy, whether by killing, capture, booty or seizure. It is said: "nilt al-shay'," so it is "manīl." ﴿Except that a righteous deed is recorded for them thereby.﴾ Ibn Abbas said: for every fright that reaches them in the Way of Allah, seventy thousand good deeds are recorded. ﴿Indeed, Allah does not waste the reward of the good-doers.﴾ So if thirst reaches them, Allah gives them drink from the River of Life (nahr al-hayawan), and they will never thirst again. If fatigue reaches them, Allah gives them honey from the River of Life, and fatigue does not touch them. Whoever goes out in the Way of Allah does not set down a foot, a hand, a side, a nose or a knee in prostration, bowing, walking or sleeping in any spot of the lands of Allah, except that Allah grants him the rank of martyrdom and intercession.

They differed concerning the ruling of this verse. Qatadah said: this is specific to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) when he himself goes out to fight, so no one has the right to remain behind from him, unless the Muslims have no need or necessity for it.

He said: It has been related to us that the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Were it not that I would burden my community, I would not remain behind any expedition that goes out in the Way of Allah. But I find no provision, so I take them with me, and it burdens me to leave them after me." [73] [[Musnad Ahmad: 2/502.]]

Al-Walid ibn Muslim said: I heard al-Awza'i, Ibn al-Mubarak, al-Fazari, al-Sab'i, Ibn Jabir and Sa'id ibn Abd al-Aziz say concerning this verse: it applies to the beginning of this community and to its end.

Ibn Zayd said: this was when the people of Islam were few; when they became many, Allah abrogated it (naskh) and permitted remaining behind for whoever wishes. He said: ﴿The believers should not all go forth﴾ up to the verse. ﴿Nor do they spend any expense, small or great, nor even a whip's lash, nor do they cross any valley on their march, going forward or back, except that it is recorded for them﴾, meaning their traces and steps, ﴿that Allah may reward them with the best of what they were doing.﴾ That is, with reward, and He will admit them to Paradise without reckoning.

Ibn Abbas said: Abu Umar al-Furati informed us, by my reading to him: Abu Musa informed us, Musaddad informed us, from Harun ibn Abdullah al-Jammal, Ibn Abi Fudayk informed us, from al-Khalil ibn Abdullah, from al-Husayn, from Ali ibn Abi Talib, Abu al-Darda', Abu Hurayrah, Abu Umamah al-Bahili, Abdullah ibn Amr, Abdullah ibn Umar, Jabir ibn Abdullah and Imran ibn Husayn, all of whom narrate from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) that he said: "Whoever sends an expense in the Way of Allah and remains in his house, for him is seven hundred dirhams for every dirham. Whoever goes out to fight himself and spends in that cause, for him on the Day of Resurrection is seven hundred thousand dirhams for every dirham." Then he recited this verse: ﴿And Allah multiplies [the reward] for whom He wills.﴾ [[Surat al-Baqarah: 261; the hadith is in Sunan Ibn Majah: 2/922, no. 2761.]]

**Commentary of al-Tha'alibi (al-Jawahir al-Hisan) on Surah 9, verses 122–129:**

﴿وَما كانَ الْمُؤْمِنُونَ لِيَنْفِرُوا كَافَّةً﴾ (It is not for the believers to go forth all together) etc.

Ibn ʿAbbas, in the narration of al-Kalbi, said: When the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) went out on a campaign, none stayed behind except the hypocrites and those who made excuses. When Allah the Exalted revealed the faults of the hypocrites and their hypocrisy during the expedition to Tabuk, the believers said: "By Allah, we will not stay behind from any future campaign the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) undertakes, nor from any expedition, ever."

When the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) ordered the expeditions (*sarāyā*, small military detachments) to fight, the Muslims all went forth to the campaigns and left the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) alone in Medina. So Allah the Exalted revealed: ﴿It is not for the believers to go forth all together﴾, meaning: it is not permissible for them to all go out to the enemy and leave the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) alone.

﴿Why should not a group from every division of them go forth﴾, i.e., why should not a company (*firqah*, a tribe) from each of them, a group (*ṭāʾifah*), ﴿that they may gain understanding in the religion﴾, meaning the group that remains sitting (at home). So when the expeditions return, and something has been revealed after they left, Allah's words ﴿those who remain behind﴾ are addressed to them. They say to them when they return: "Allah has revealed to your Prophet a Qur'an after you left, and we have learned it." So the expeditions remain, learning what Allah has revealed to their Prophet after them, and He sends other expeditions. This is the meaning of ﴿that they may gain understanding in the religion, and that they may warn their people when they return to them﴾, and inform them of the matter, ﴿so that they may beware﴾, and not act contrary to it.

Al-Hasan said: This understanding and warning refers to the group that went forth. The meaning of the verse is: ﴿that they may gain understanding in the religion﴾, i.e., that they may perceive and be certain of what Allah shows them of the victory over the polytheists and the support of the religion. ﴿And that they may warn their people﴾, i.e., the unbelievers, ﴿when they return to them﴾ from the struggle (*jihād*), so that they inform them of Allah's support for the Prophet and the believers, and tell them that they have no strength (*lā yadān*, i.e., no power) to fight the Prophet (ﷺ) and the believers. ﴿So that they may beware﴾ of fighting the Prophet (ﷺ), lest there befall them what befell their companions among the unbelievers.

Al-Kalbi said: There is another explanation for it. It is mentioned that some clans of Banu Asad ibn Khuzaymah were afflicted by a severe drought and displayed the two testimonies (of faith), though they were not believers in secret, and they came until they alighted at Medina. They fouled its roads with their dung and drove up its prices, so Allah the Exalted revealed this verse. (Asbab al-nuzul of al-Wahidi, p. 266; the material in brackets is from it.)

Mujahid said: It concerns the Companions of the Prophet (ﷺ) who went out into the deserts, and they encountered from the people kindness and abundance, and they invited whoever they met to guidance. The people said to them: "We see you have only left your companion and come to us." They felt distress over that and all of them came back from the desert until they entered upon the Prophet (ﷺ). So Allah the Exalted revealed: ﴿It is not for the believers to go forth all together. Why should not a group from every division of them go forth, that they may gain understanding in the religion﴾, and listen to what has been revealed to them, ﴿and that they may warn their people﴾, all the people, ﴿when they return to them﴾, and call them to Allah, ﴿so that they may beware﴾ of Allah's might and vengeance by following and obeying them. And one group remained, seeking forgiveness.

ʿIkrimah said: When the verse ﴿If you do not go forth, He will punish you with a painful punishment﴾ and ﴿It was not for the people of Medina and those around them of the Bedouins...﴾ was revealed, the hypocrites among the people of the desert, who had stayed behind from Muhammad and had not gone forth with him, said (this). Some of the Companions of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) had gone out into the desert to their people to instruct them. So Allah the Exalted revealed this verse concerning those excuse-makers.

It is narrated from ʿAbd al-Razzaq ibn Hammam, regarding His words ﴿Why should not a group from every division of them go forth, that they may gain understanding in the religion and warn their people when they return to them﴾, that he said: They are the people of hadith.

﴿O you who believe, fight those of the unbelievers who are near to you﴾. They were commanded to fight those nearest to them in dwelling and kinship.

Ibn ʿAbbas said: Like Qurayzah, al-Nadir, Khaybar, Fadak and the like.

Ibn ʿUmar said: He meant by them the Romans, because they were the inhabitants of Syria at that time, and Syria was nearer to Medina than Iraq.

Al-Hasan, when asked about fighting the Romans and the Daylam, would recite this verse. (It is also said that it refers to the Arabs; this was said by Ibn Zayd. See Zad al-Masir, 3/351.)

﴿And let them find in you harshness﴾, i.e., severity and zeal. Al-Dahhak said: roughness (*jafāʾ*). Al-Hasan said: patience in striving against them. ﴿And know that Allah is with the God-fearing﴾, by aid and victory.

﴿And when a surah is revealed, some of them say: "Which of you has had his faith increased by this?"﴾ The common reading (of the Qurrāʾ) is with a *ḍamma* on the *yāʾ* because of the *hāʾ* (i.e., *ayyukum*). ʿUbayd ibn ʿUmayr read *ayyakum* with a *fatḥa* on the *yāʾ*. Both are correct. ﴿It has increased their faith﴾. Allah the Exalted said: ﴿As for those who believe, it has increased their faith﴾, i.e., certainty, sincerity and affirmation.

Al-Rabiʿ said: (it increased them in) fear (*khashyah*). ﴿And they rejoice﴾, i.e., they are delighted at the revelation of the Qur'an.

From al-Dahhak, from Ibn ʿAbbas: (﴿And when a surah is revealed﴾) means a clear (*muḥkamah*) surah containing the lawful and the unlawful. ﴿Some of them say: "Which of you has had his faith increased by this?"﴾ ﴿As for those who believe, it has increased their faith﴾ and affirmation regarding the obligations, together with their faith in the Most Merciful. ﴿And they rejoice﴾ at the revelation of the obligations. ﴿But as for those in whose hearts is a disease﴾, meaning doubt and hypocrisy, ﴿it has increased them in filth upon their filth﴾, i.e., disbelief upon their disbelief, misguidance upon their misguidance, and doubt upon their doubt.

Muqatil said: sin upon their sin. ﴿And they die while they are disbelievers.﴾ Mujahid said regarding this verse: Faith increases and decreases.

ʿUmar ibn al-Khattab (may Allah be pleased with him) said: If the faith of Abu Bakr (may Allah be pleased with him) were weighed against the faith of all the people of the earth, it would outweigh them. Yes, faith indeed increases and decreases, he said it three times.

Zayd al-Shami narrated from Dharr, who said: ʿUmar would take the hand of a man or two of his companions and say: "Come, let us increase in faith."

ʿAli ibn Abi Talib (peace be upon him) said: Faith appears as a white speck in the heart; as faith grows greater, the whiteness spreads until the whole heart becomes white. And hypocrisy appears as a black speck in the heart; as hypocrisy grows, that blackness increases until the whole heart becomes black. By Allah, if you split open the heart of a believer, you would find it white, and if you split open the heart of a hypocrite, you would find it black.

Al-Hasan wrote to ʿUmar ibn al-Khattab (may Allah be pleased with him): Faith has paths, laws, limits and obligations; whoever completes them completes his faith, and whoever does not complete them has not completed his faith.

Ibn al-Mubarak said, from al-Hasan: "Except for kinship," with the increase of faith, or I would reject the Book of Allah the Exalted.

﴿Do they not see﴾: the common readers read it with *yāʾ*, as a report about the hypocrites mentioned. Hamzah and Yaʿqub read *tarawna* with *tāʾ*, addressing the believers; this is the reading of Ubayy ibn Kaʿb. Al-Aʿmash read *awa lam tara*, and Talhah read *awa lā tarā*, which is the reading of ʿAbd Allah ibn ʿUmar. ﴿That they are tested once or twice every year﴾, i.e., are examined. He said: they lie one or two lies, and they pray in it (i.e., during it). Mujahid said: they are tested by drought and high prices. ʿAtiyyah said: by illnesses and pains, and these are the precursors of death.

Qatadah said: by raids and jihad. It is also said: by the enemy. It is also said: they are tested, so they recognize (the truth) once and deny it another time. Murrah al-Hamdani said: they are tested, they disbelieve. Muqatil ibn Hayyan said: they are exposed by displaying their hypocrisy. ʿIkrimah said: they practise hypocrisy, then believe, then practise hypocrisy again, just as they break their covenant once or twice a year. (See Zad al-Masir, 3/353.) ﴿Then they do not repent﴾ of their breaking (of covenant), ﴿nor do they take heed﴾ [by what Allah has done to them].

When they broke their covenants, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) would send expeditions against them, and they would kill them.

Al-Hasan: They are tested by striving in the way of Allah with His Messenger, and they see the truth of Allah's promise of victory and triumph over whoever Allah opposes. ﴿Then they do not repent﴾ despite what they see of the truth of Allah's promise, and they do not take admonition. Al-Dahhak: They are tested by high prices, affliction, withholding of rain, and the loss of fruits; then they do not return from their hypocrisy, nor do they reflect on the greatness of Allah. In the reading of ʿAbd Allah: ﴿Nor do they remember﴾.

﴿And when a surah is revealed﴾ containing the disgrace and rebuke of the hypocrites, ﴿some of them look at others﴾. This is an abridged expression, its implied meaning being: they look at one another and say, or signal: ﴿"Does anyone see you?"﴾ if you stand up. If they did not see anyone, they would leave the mosque; if they noticed someone seeing them, they would stand up and go away. ﴿Then they turn away﴾ from faith in it. Al-Dahhak said: ﴿"Does anyone see you?"﴾ means: that anyone among them might discover your inner secrets, for fear of being killed. Allah said: ﴿Allah has turned their hearts away from faith in the Qur'an﴾ ﴿because they are a people who do not understand.﴾ Ibn ʿAbbas said: Do not say when you have prayed: "We have departed from the prayer," for a people departed and Allah turned their hearts. Rather say: "We have completed the prayer." (Tafsir al-Tabari, 11/99–101.)

﴿There has certainly come to you a Messenger from among yourselves﴾. The common reading is with a *ḍamma* on the *fāʾ*, i.e., from your lineage: you know his lineage and his noble standing, and that he is from a tribe of the Arabs, from the sons of Ismaʿil. Ibn ʿAbbas said: There is no tribe among the Arabs except that the Prophet (ﷺ) was born to them, their Mudar, their Rabiʿah and their Yemen. (Tarikh Dimashq, 3/95, ed. Dar al-Fikr.)

Al-Sadiq said: He was not touched by anything from the births of the Jahiliyyah.

We were informed by Abu ʿAbd Allah ibn Hamid, who said: Hamid ibn Muhammad told us, ʿAli ibn ʿAbd al-ʿAziz told us, Muhammad ibn Abi Hashim told me, from al-Madani, from Abu al-Huwayrith, from Ibn ʿAbbas, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "I was not born of the illicit unions of the people of the Jahiliyyah; I was born only of marriages like the marriages of Islam." (al-Mu'jam al-Kabir, 10/329, no. 10812.) [74] For Allah the Exalted made him from among themselves; so do not envy him for what Allah has given him of prophethood and honour.

Ibn ʿAbbas, Ibn Thaʿlabah, ʿAbd Allah ibn Fasit al-Makki, Ibn Muhaysin and al-Zuhri read *min anfasikum* with a *fatḥa* on the *fāʾ*, meaning: from your most noble and excellent. From your saying: "a precious thing" (*shayʾ nafīs*) when it is desired. Yaman said: from the highest of you in lineage. ﴿He is mighty﴾, severe, ﴿against him is what distresses you﴾: *mā* is an extra particle; the meaning is your distress (*ʿanatakum*), which is the arrival of hardship and harm upon you. Ibn ʿAbbas said: what misguides you. Al-Dahhak and al-Kalbi said: what makes you sinful. Al-ʿUtaybi said: your distress and your harm. Ibn al-Anbari said: what causes you to perish. ﴿Ardent over you﴾, i.e., over your faith, your guidance and your righteousness. Qatadah said: ardent over your misguided, that Allah may guide them. Al-Farra' said: *al-ḥarīṣ* is the miserly, that you should enter the Fire.

﴿Kind and merciful to the believers.﴾ It is said: *ra'ūf* means gentle and compassionate; *raḥīm* means merciful. It is said: *ra'ūf* to the obedient, *raḥīm* to the sinners; *ra'ūf* to His servants, *raḥīm* to His friends; *ra'ūf* to whoever sees him, *raḥīm* to whoever has not seen him.

ʿAbd al-ʿAziz ibn Yahya said: The arrangement of the verse: ﴿There has certainly come to you a Messenger from among yourselves, mighty, ardent over you, kind and merciful to the believers, against whom what distresses you is grievous to him.﴾ He is concerned with nothing but your affair, and he is the one who stands in intercession, so do not be distressed by what distresses you, as long as you adhere to his sunnah, for nothing pleases him except your entry into Paradise,

due to his saying (ﷺ): "Whoever leaves behind wealth, it is for his heirs; and whoever leaves behind a debt or dependants, it is upon me and to me." [75]

﴿But if they turn away﴾, i.e., turn away from faith and oppose you, ﴿say: "Allah is sufficient for me; there is no god but He. In Him I have put my trust, and He is the Lord of the Mighty Throne."﴾ The common reading is with a *kasra* on the *mīm* in *al-ʿarsh* (as a genitive). Ibn Muhaysin read *al-ʿaẓīm* with a *ḍamma*, as an adjective of the Lord. Al-Husayn ibn al-Fadl said: Allah did not gather for any of the prophets two of His names together except for the Prophet (ﷺ), for He said: ﴿kind and merciful to the believers﴾, and He said: ﴿Indeed, Allah is to the people Kind, Merciful.﴾ [[Surah al-Baqarah: 143.]]

Ubayy ibn Kaʿb said: The most recent of the Qur'an to be given to Allah the Exalted is ﴿There has certainly come to you a Messenger﴾ to the end of the surah.

**Commentary of al-Tha'alibi (al-Jawahir al-Hisan) on Surah 9, verses 122–129:**

Ibn ʿAbbas, in the narration of al-Kalbi, said: When the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) went out on a campaign, none stayed behind except the hypocrites and those who made excuses. When Allah the Exalted revealed the faults of the hypocrites and their hypocrisy during the expedition to Tabuk, the believers said: "By Allah, we will not stay behind from any future campaign the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) undertakes, nor from any expedition, ever."

When the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) ordered the expeditions (*sarāyā*, small military detachments) to fight, the Muslims all went forth to the campaigns and left the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) alone in Medina. So Allah the Exalted revealed: ﴿It is not for the believers to go forth all together﴾, meaning: it is not permissible for them to all go out to the enemy and leave the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) alone.

﴿Why should not a group from every division of them go forth﴾, i.e., why should not a company (*firqah*, a tribe) from each of them, a group (*ṭāʾifah*), ﴿that they may gain understanding in the religion﴾, meaning the group that remains sitting (at home). So when the expeditions return, and something has been revealed after they left, Allah's words ﴿those who remain behind﴾ are addressed to them. They say to them when they return: "Allah has revealed to your Prophet a Qur'an after you left, and we have learned it." So the expeditions remain, learning what Allah has revealed to their Prophet after them, and He sends other expeditions. This is the meaning of ﴿that they may gain understanding in the religion, and that they may warn their people when they return to them﴾, and inform them of the matter, ﴿so that they may beware﴾, and not act contrary to it.

Al-Hasan said: This understanding and warning refers to the group that went forth. The meaning of the verse is: ﴿that they may gain understanding in the religion﴾, i.e., that they may perceive and be certain of what Allah shows them of the victory over the polytheists and the support of the religion. ﴿And that they may warn their people﴾, i.e., the unbelievers, ﴿when they return to them﴾ from the struggle (*jihād*), so that they inform them of Allah's support for the Prophet and the believers, and tell them that they have no strength (*lā yadān*, i.e., no power) to fight the Prophet (ﷺ) and the believers. ﴿So that they may beware﴾ of fighting the Prophet (ﷺ), lest there befall them what befell their companions among the unbelievers.

Al-Kalbi said: There is another explanation for it. It is mentioned that some clans of Banu Asad ibn Khuzaymah were afflicted by a severe drought and displayed the two testimonies (of faith), though they were not believers in secret, and they came until they alighted at Medina. They fouled its roads with their dung and drove up its prices, so Allah the Exalted revealed this verse. (Asbab al-nuzul of al-Wahidi, p. 266; the material in brackets is from it.)

Mujahid said: It concerns the Companions of the Prophet (ﷺ) who went out into the deserts, and they encountered from the people kindness and abundance, and they invited whoever they met to guidance. Why should not a group from every division of them go forth, that they may gain understanding in the religion﴾, and listen to what has been revealed to them, ﴿and that they may warn their people﴾, all the people, ﴿when they return to them﴾, and call them to Allah, ﴿so that they may beware﴾ of Allah's might and vengeance by following and obeying them. ʿIkrimah said: When the verse ﴿If you do not go forth, He will punish you with a painful punishment﴾ and ﴿It was not for the people of Medina and those around them of the Bedouins...﴾ was revealed, the hypocrites among the people of the desert, who had stayed behind from Muhammad and had not gone forth with him, said (this). **Commentary of al-Tha'alibi (al-Jawahir al-Hisan) on Surah 9, verses 122–129:**

﴿وَما كانَ الْمُؤْمِنُونَ لِيَنْفِرُوا كَافَّةً﴾ (It is not for the believers to go forth all together) etc.

Ibn ʿAbbas, in the narration of al-Kalbi, said: When the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) went out on a campaign, none stayed behind except the hypocrites and those who made excuses. When Allah the Exalted revealed the faults of the hypocrites and their hypocrisy during the expedition to Tabuk, the believers said: "By Allah, we will not stay behind from any future campaign the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) undertakes, nor from any expedition, ever."

When the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) ordered the expeditions (*sarāyā*, small military detachments) to fight, the Muslims all went forth to the campaigns and left the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) alone in Medina. So Allah the Exalted revealed: ﴿It is not for the believers to go forth all together﴾, meaning: it is not permissible for them to all go out to the enemy and leave the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) alone.

﴿Why should not a group from every division of them go forth﴾, i.e., why should not a company (*firqah*, a tribe) from each of them, a group (*ṭāʾifah*), ﴿that they may gain understanding in the religion﴾, meaning the group that remains sitting (at home). So when the expeditions return, and something has been revealed after they left, Allah's words ﴿those who remain behind﴾ are addressed to them. They say to them when they return: "Allah has revealed to your Prophet a Qur'an after you left, and we have learned it." So the expeditions remain, learning what Allah has revealed to their Prophet after them, and He sends other expeditions. This is the meaning of ﴿that they may gain understanding in the religion, and that they may warn their people when they return to them﴾, and inform them of the matter, ﴿so that they may beware﴾, and not act contrary to it.

Al-Hasan said: This understanding and warning refers to the group that went forth. The meaning of the verse is: ﴿that they may gain understanding in the religion﴾, i.e., that they may perceive and be certain of what Allah shows them of the victory over the polytheists and the support of the religion. ﴿And that they may warn their people﴾, i.e., the unbelievers, ﴿when they return to them﴾ from the struggle (*jihād*), so that they inform them of Allah's support for the Prophet and the believers, and tell them that they have no strength (*lā yadān*, i.e., no power) to fight the Prophet (ﷺ) and the believers. ﴿So that they may beware﴾ of fighting the Prophet (ﷺ), lest there befall them what befell their companions among the unbelievers.

Al-Kalbi said: There is another explanation for it. It is mentioned that some clans of Banu Asad ibn Khuzaymah were afflicted by a severe drought and displayed the two testimonies (of faith), though they were not believers in secret, and they came until they alighted at Medina. They fouled its roads with their dung and drove up its prices, so Allah the Exalted revealed this verse. (Asbab al-nuzul of al-Wahidi, p. 266; the material in brackets is from it.)

Mujahid said: It concerns the Companions of the Prophet (ﷺ) who went out into the deserts, and they encountered from the people kindness and abundance, and they invited whoever they met to guidance. The people said to them: "We see you have only left your companion and come to us." They felt distress over that and all of them came back from the desert until they entered upon the Prophet (ﷺ). So Allah the Exalted revealed: ﴿It is not for the believers to go forth all together. Why should not a group from every division of them go forth, that they may gain understanding in the religion﴾, and listen to what has been revealed to them, ﴿and that they may warn their people﴾, all the people, ﴿when they return to them﴾, and call them to Allah, ﴿so that they may beware﴾ of Allah's might and vengeance by following and obeying them. And one group remained, seeking forgiveness.

ʿIkrimah said: When the verse ﴿If you do not go forth, He will punish you with a painful punishment﴾ and ﴿It was not for the people of Medina and those around them of the Bedouins...﴾ was revealed, the hypocrites among the people of the desert, who had stayed behind from Muhammad and had not gone forth with him, said (this). Some of the Companions of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) had gone out into the desert to their people to instruct them. So Allah the Exalted revealed this verse concerning those excuse-makers.

It is narrated from ʿAbd al-Razzaq ibn Hammam, regarding His words ﴿Why should not a group from every division of them go forth, that they may gain understanding in the religion and warn their people when they return to them﴾, that he said: They are the people of hadith.

﴿O you who believe, fight those of the unbelievers who are near to you﴾. They were commanded to fight those nearest to them in dwelling and kinship.

Ibn ʿAbbas said: Like Qurayzah, al-Nadir, Khaybar, Fadak and the like.

Ibn ʿUmar said: He meant by them the Romans, because they were the inhabitants of Syria at that time, and Syria was nearer to Medina than Iraq.

Al-Hasan, when asked about fighting the Romans and the Daylam, would recite this verse. (It is also said that it refers to the Arabs; this was said by Ibn Zayd. See Zad al-Masir, 3/351.)

﴿And let them find in you harshness﴾, i.e., severity and zeal. Al-Dahhak said: roughness (*jafāʾ*). Al-Hasan said: patience in striving against them. ﴿And know that Allah is with the God-fearing﴾, by aid and victory.

﴿And when a surah is revealed, some of them say: "Which of you has had his faith increased by this?"﴾ The common reading (of the Qurrāʾ) is with a *ḍamma* on the *yāʾ* because of the *hāʾ* (i.e., *ayyukum*). ʿUbayd ibn ʿUmayr read *ayyakum* with a *fatḥa* on the *yāʾ*. Both are correct. ﴿It has increased their faith﴾. Allah the Exalted said: ﴿As for those who believe, it has increased their faith﴾, i.e., certainty, sincerity and affirmation.

Al-Rabiʿ said: (it increased them in) fear (*khashyah*). ﴿And they rejoice﴾, i.e., they are delighted at the revelation of the Qur'an.

From al-Dahhak, from Ibn ʿAbbas: (﴿And when a surah is revealed﴾) means a clear (*muḥkamah*) surah containing the lawful and the unlawful. ﴿Some of them say: "Which of you has had his faith increased by this?"﴾ ﴿As for those who believe, it has increased their faith﴾ and affirmation regarding the obligations, together with their faith in the Most Merciful. ﴿And they rejoice﴾ at the revelation of the obligations. ﴿But as for those in whose hearts is a disease﴾, meaning doubt and hypocrisy, ﴿it has increased them in filth upon their filth﴾, i.e., disbelief upon their disbelief, misguidance upon their misguidance, and doubt upon their doubt.

Muqatil said: sin upon their sin. ﴿And they die while they are disbelievers.﴾ Mujahid said regarding this verse: Faith increases and decreases.

ʿUmar ibn al-Khattab (may Allah be pleased with him) said: If the faith of Abu Bakr (may Allah be pleased with him) were weighed against the faith of all the people of the earth, it would outweigh them. Yes, faith indeed increases and decreases, he said it three times.

Zayd al-Shami narrated from Dharr, who said: ʿUmar would take the hand of a man or two of his companions and say: "Come, let us increase in faith."

ʿAli ibn Abi Talib (peace be upon him) said: Faith appears as a white speck in the heart; as faith grows greater, the whiteness spreads until the whole heart becomes white. And hypocrisy appears as a black speck in the heart; as hypocrisy grows, that blackness increases until the whole heart becomes black. By Allah, if you split open the heart of a believer, you would find it white, and if you split open the heart of a hypocrite, you would find it black.

Al-Hasan wrote to ʿUmar ibn al-Khattab (may Allah be pleased with him): Faith has paths, laws, limits and obligations; whoever completes them completes his faith, and whoever does not complete them has not completed his faith.

Ibn al-Mubarak said, from al-Hasan: "Except for kinship," with the increase of faith, or I would reject the Book of Allah the Exalted.

﴿Do they not see﴾: the common readers read it with *yāʾ*, as a report about the hypocrites mentioned. Hamzah and Yaʿqub read *tarawna* with *tāʾ*, addressing the believers; this is the reading of Ubayy ibn Kaʿb. Al-Aʿmash read *awa lam tara*, and Talhah read *awa lā tarā*, which is the reading of ʿAbd Allah ibn ʿUmar. ﴿That they are tested once or twice every year﴾, i.e., are examined. He said: they lie one or two lies, and they pray in it (i.e., during it). Mujahid said: they are tested by drought and high prices. ʿAtiyyah said: by illnesses and pains, and these are the precursors of death.

Qatadah said: by raids and jihad. It is also said: by the enemy. It is also said: they are tested, so they recognize (the truth) once and deny it another time. Murrah al-Hamdani said: they are tested, they disbelieve. Muqatil ibn Hayyan said: they are exposed by displaying their hypocrisy. ʿIkrimah said: they practise hypocrisy, then believe, then practise hypocrisy again, just as they break their covenant once or twice a year. (See Zad al-Masir, 3/353.) ﴿Then they do not repent﴾ of their breaking (of covenant), ﴿nor do they take heed﴾ [by what Allah has done to them].

When they broke their covenants, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) would send expeditions against them, and they would kill them.

Al-Hasan: They are tested by striving in the way of Allah with His Messenger, and they see the truth of Allah's promise of victory and triumph over whoever Allah opposes. ﴿Then they do not repent﴾ despite what they see of the truth of Allah's promise, and they do not take admonition. Al-Dahhak: They are tested by high prices, affliction, withholding of rain, and the loss of fruits; then they do not return from their hypocrisy, nor do they reflect on the greatness of Allah. In the reading of ʿAbd Allah: ﴿Nor do they remember﴾.

﴿And when a surah is revealed﴾ containing the disgrace and rebuke of the hypocrites, ﴿some of them look at others﴾. This is an abridged expression, its implied meaning being: they look at one another and say, or signal: ﴿"Does anyone see you?"﴾ if you stand up. If they did not see anyone, they would leave the mosque; if they noticed someone seeing them, they would stand up and go away. ﴿Then they turn away﴾ from faith in it. Al-Dahhak said: ﴿"Does anyone see you?"﴾ means: that anyone among them might discover your inner secrets, for fear of being killed. Allah said: ﴿Allah has turned their hearts away from faith in the Qur'an﴾ ﴿because they are a people who do not understand.﴾ Ibn ʿAbbas said: Do not say when you have prayed: "We have departed from the prayer," for a people departed and Allah turned their hearts. Rather say: "We have completed the prayer." (Tafsir al-Tabari, 11/99–101.)

﴿There has certainly come to you a Messenger from among yourselves﴾. The common reading is with a *ḍamma* on the *fāʾ*, i.e., from your lineage: you know his lineage and his noble standing, and that he is from a tribe of the Arabs, from the sons of Ismaʿil. Ibn ʿAbbas said: There is no tribe among the Arabs except that the Prophet (ﷺ) was born to them, their Mudar, their Rabiʿah and their Yemen. (Tarikh Dimashq, 3/95, ed. Dar al-Fikr.)

Al-Sadiq said: He was not touched by anything from the births of the Jahiliyyah.

We were informed by Abu ʿAbd Allah ibn Hamid, who said: Hamid ibn Muhammad told us, ʿAli ibn ʿAbd al-ʿAziz told us, Muhammad ibn Abi Hashim told me, from al-Madani, from Abu al-Huwayrith, from Ibn ʿAbbas, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "I was not born of the illicit unions of the people of the Jahiliyyah; I was born only of marriages like the marriages of Islam." (al-Mu'jam al-Kabir, 10/329, no. 10812.) [74] For Allah the Exalted made him from among themselves; so do not envy him for what Allah has given him of prophethood and honour.

Ibn ʿAbbas, Ibn Thaʿlabah, ʿAbd Allah ibn Fasit al-Makki, Ibn Muhaysin and al-Zuhri read *min anfasikum* with a *fatḥa* on the *fāʾ*, meaning: from your most noble and excellent. From your saying: "a precious thing" (*shayʾ nafīs*) when it is desired. Yaman said: from the highest of you in lineage. ﴿He is mighty﴾, severe, ﴿against him is what distresses you﴾: *mā* is an extra particle; the meaning is your distress (*ʿanatakum*), which is the arrival of hardship and harm upon you. Ibn ʿAbbas said: what misguides you. Al-Dahhak and al-Kalbi said: what makes you sinful. Al-ʿUtaybi said: your distress and your harm. Ibn al-Anbari said: what causes you to perish. ﴿Ardent over you﴾, i.e., over your faith, your guidance and your righteousness. Qatadah said: ardent over your misguided, that Allah may guide them. Al-Farra' said: *al-ḥarīṣ* is the miserly, that you should enter the Fire.

﴿Kind and merciful to the believers.﴾ It is said: *ra'ūf* means gentle and compassionate; *raḥīm* means merciful. It is said: *ra'ūf* to the obedient, *raḥīm* to the sinners; *ra'ūf* to His servants, *raḥīm* to His friends; *ra'ūf* to whoever sees him, *raḥīm* to whoever has not seen him.

ʿAbd al-ʿAziz ibn Yahya said: The arrangement of the verse: ﴿There has certainly come to you a Messenger from among yourselves, mighty, ardent over you, kind and merciful to the believers, against whom what distresses you is grievous to him.﴾ He is concerned with nothing but your affair, and he is the one who stands in intercession, so do not be distressed by what distresses you, as long as you adhere to his sunnah, for nothing pleases him except your entry into Paradise,

due to his saying (ﷺ): "Whoever leaves behind wealth, it is for his heirs; and whoever leaves behind a debt or dependants, it is upon me and to me." [75]

﴿But if they turn away﴾, i.e., turn away from faith and oppose you, ﴿say: "Allah is sufficient for me; there is no god but He. In Him I have put my trust, and He is the Lord of the Mighty Throne."﴾ The common reading is with a *kasra* on the *mīm* in *al-ʿarsh* (as a genitive). Ibn Muhaysin read *al-ʿaẓīm* with a *ḍamma*, as an adjective of the Lord. Al-Husayn ibn al-Fadl said: Allah did not gather for any of the prophets two of His names together except for the Prophet (ﷺ), for He said: ﴿kind and merciful to the believers﴾, and He said: ﴿Indeed, Allah is to the people Kind, Merciful.﴾ [[Surah al-Baqarah: 143.]]

Yahya ibn Jaʿdah said: ʿUmar ibn al-Khattab (may Allah be pleased with him) said: No verse is established in the Mushaf until two men testify to it. Then a man from the Ansar came with the two verses at the end of Surah al-Tawbah, *"Laqad jāʾakum"*. ʿUmar said: "By Allah, I will not ask you for proof of them. That is how the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) acted." So he recorded them. They are said by some to be the last verses sent down from heaven, and the last complete surah revealed was Surah Bara'ah (al-Tawbah).

We were informed by Abu ʿAbd Allah ibn Hamid, from Muhammad ibn al-Hasan, from ʿAli ibn ʿAbd al-ʿAziz, from Hajjaj, from Hammam, from Qatadah, who said: The last of the Qur'an to descend from heaven are these two verses, the conclusion of Bara'ah: ﴿There has certainly come to you a Messenger from among yourselves﴾ to His words ﴿the Lord of the Mighty Throne.﴾

Ubayy ibn Kaʿb said: The most recent of the Qur'an to be given to Allah the Exalted is ﴿There has certainly come to you a Messenger﴾ to the end of the surah.

From your saying: "a precious thing" (*shayʾ nafīs*) when it is desired. Yaman said: from the highest of you in lineage. ﴿He is mighty﴾, severe, ﴿against him is what distresses you﴾: *mā* is an extra particle; the meaning is your distress (*ʿanatakum*), which is the arrival of hardship and harm upon you. Ibn ʿAbbas said: what misguides you. Al-Dahhak and al-Kalbi said: what makes you sinful. Al-ʿUtaybi said: your distress and your harm. Ibn al-Anbari said: what causes you to perish. ﴿Ardent over you﴾, i.e., over your faith, your guidance and your righteousness. Qatadah said: ardent over your misguided, that Allah may guide them. Al-Farra' said: *al-ḥarīṣ* is the miserly, that you should enter the Fire.

ʿAbd al-ʿAziz ibn Yahya said: The arrangement of the verse: ﴿There has certainly come to you a Messenger from among yourselves, mighty, ardent over you, kind and merciful to the believers, against whom what distresses you is grievous to him.﴾ He is concerned with nothing but your affair, and he is the one who stands in intercession, so do not be distressed by what distresses you, as long as you adhere to his sunnah, for nothing pleases him except your entry into Paradise,

due to his saying (ﷺ): "Whoever leaves behind wealth, it is for his heirs; and whoever leaves behind a debt or dependants, it is upon me and to me." [75]

﴿But if they turn away﴾, i.e., turn away from faith and oppose you, ﴿say: "Allah is sufficient for me; there is no god but He. **Commentary of al-Tha'alibi (al-Jawahir al-Hisan) on Surah 9, verses 122–129:**

Ibn ʿAbbas, in the narration of al-Kalbi, said: When the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) went out on a campaign, none stayed behind except the hypocrites and those who made excuses. When Allah the Exalted revealed the faults of the hypocrites and their hypocrisy during the expedition to Tabuk, the believers said: "By Allah, we will not stay behind from any future campaign the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) undertakes, nor from any expedition, ever."

When the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) ordered the expeditions (*sarāyā*, small military detachments) to fight, the Muslims all went forth to the campaigns and left the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) alone in Medina. So Allah the Exalted revealed: ﴿It is not for the believers to go forth all together﴾, meaning: it is not permissible for them to all go out to the enemy and leave the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) alone.

﴿Why should not a group from every division of them go forth﴾, i.e., why should not a company (*firqah*, a tribe) from each of them, a group (*ṭāʾifah*), ﴿that they may gain understanding in the religion﴾, meaning the group that remains sitting (at home). So when the expeditions return, and something has been revealed after they left, Allah's words ﴿those who remain behind﴾ are addressed to them. They say to them when they return: "Allah has revealed to your Prophet a Qur'an after you left, and we have learned it." So the expeditions remain, learning what Allah has revealed to their Prophet after them, and He sends other expeditions. This is the meaning of ﴿that they may gain understanding in the religion, and that they may warn their people when they return to them﴾, and inform them of the matter, ﴿so that they may beware﴾, and not act contrary to it.

Al-Hasan said: This understanding and warning refers to the group that went forth. The meaning of the verse is: ﴿that they may gain understanding in the religion﴾, i.e., that they may perceive and be certain of what Allah shows them of the victory over the polytheists and the support of the religion. ﴿And that they may warn their people﴾, i.e., the unbelievers, ﴿when they return to them﴾ from the struggle (*jihād*), so that they inform them of Allah's support for the Prophet and the believers, and tell them that they have no strength (*lā yadān*, i.e., no power) to fight the Prophet (ﷺ) and the believers. ﴿So that they may beware﴾ of fighting the Prophet (ﷺ), lest there befall them what befell their companions among the unbelievers.

Al-Kalbi said: There is another explanation for it. It is mentioned that some clans of Banu Asad ibn Khuzaymah were afflicted by a severe drought and displayed the two testimonies (of faith), though they were not believers in secret, and they came until they alighted at Medina. They fouled its roads with their dung and drove up its prices, so Allah the Exalted revealed this verse. (Asbab al-nuzul of al-Wahidi, p. 266; the material in brackets is from it.)

Mujahid said: It concerns the Companions of the Prophet (ﷺ) who went out into the deserts, and they encountered from the people kindness and abundance, and they invited whoever they met to guidance. The people said to them: "We see you have only left your companion and come to us." They felt distress over that and all of them came back from the desert until they entered upon the Prophet (ﷺ). So Allah the Exalted revealed: ﴿It is not for the believers to go forth all together. Why should not a group from every division of them go forth, that they may gain understanding in the religion﴾, and listen to what has been revealed to them, ﴿and that they may warn their people﴾, all the people, ﴿when they return to them﴾, and call them to Allah, ﴿so that they may beware﴾ of Allah's might and vengeance by following and obeying them. And one group remained, seeking forgiveness.

ʿIkrimah said: When the verse ﴿If you do not go forth, He will punish you with a painful punishment﴾ and ﴿It was not for the people of Medina and those around them of the Bedouins...﴾ was revealed, the hypocrites among the people of the desert, who had stayed behind from Muhammad and had not gone forth with him, said (this). Some of the Companions of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) had gone out into the desert to their people to instruct them. So Allah the Exalted revealed this verse concerning those excuse-makers.

It is narrated from ʿAbd al-Razzaq ibn Hammam, regarding His words ﴿Why should not a group from every division of them go forth, that they may gain understanding in the religion and warn their people when they return to them﴾, that he said: They are the people of hadith.

﴿O you who believe, fight those of the unbelievers who are near to you﴾. They were commanded to fight those nearest to them in dwelling and kinship.

Ibn ʿAbbas said: Like Qurayzah, al-Nadir, Khaybar, Fadak and the like.

Ibn ʿUmar said: He meant by them the Romans, because they were the inhabitants of Syria at that time, and Syria was nearer to Medina than Iraq.

Al-Hasan, when asked about fighting the Romans and the Daylam, would recite this verse. (It is also said that it refers to the Arabs; this was said by Ibn Zayd. See Zad al-Masir, 3/351.)

﴿And let them find in you harshness﴾, i.e., severity and zeal. Al-Dahhak said: roughness (*jafāʾ*). Al-Hasan said: patience in striving against them. ﴿And know that Allah is with the God-fearing﴾, by aid and victory.

﴿And when a surah is revealed, some of them say: "Which of you has had his faith increased by this?"﴾ The common reading (of the Qurrāʾ) is with a *ḍamma* on the *yāʾ* because of the *hāʾ* (i.e., *ayyukum*). ʿUbayd ibn ʿUmayr read *ayyakum* with a *fatḥa* on the *yāʾ*. Both are correct. ﴿It has increased their faith﴾. Allah the Exalted said: ﴿As for those who believe, it has increased their faith﴾, i.e., certainty, sincerity and affirmation.

Al-Rabiʿ said: (it increased them in) fear (*khashyah*). ﴿And they rejoice﴾, i.e., they are delighted at the revelation of the Qur'an.

From al-Dahhak, from Ibn ʿAbbas: (﴿And when a surah is revealed﴾) means a clear (*muḥkamah*) surah containing the lawful and the unlawful. ﴿Some of them say: "Which of you has had his faith increased by this?"﴾ ﴿As for those who believe, it has increased their faith﴾ and affirmation regarding the obligations, together with their faith in the Most Merciful. ﴿And they rejoice﴾ at the revelation of the obligations. ﴿But as for those in whose hearts is a disease﴾, meaning doubt and hypocrisy, ﴿it has increased them in filth upon their filth﴾, i.e., disbelief upon their disbelief, misguidance upon their misguidance, and doubt upon their doubt.

Muqatil said: sin upon their sin. ﴿And they die while they are disbelievers.﴾ Mujahid said regarding this verse: Faith increases and decreases.

ʿUmar ibn al-Khattab (may Allah be pleased with him) said: If the faith of Abu Bakr (may Allah be pleased with him) were weighed against the faith of all the people of the earth, it would outweigh them. Yes, faith indeed increases and decreases, he said it three times.

Zayd al-Shami narrated from Dharr, who said: ʿUmar would take the hand of a man or two of his companions and say: "Come, let us increase in faith."

ʿAli ibn Abi Talib (peace be upon him) said: Faith appears as a white speck in the heart; as faith grows greater, the whiteness spreads until the whole heart becomes white. And hypocrisy appears as a black speck in the heart; as hypocrisy grows, that blackness increases until the whole heart becomes black. By Allah, if you split open the heart of a believer, you would find it white, and if you split open the heart of a hypocrite, you would find it black.

Al-Hasan wrote to ʿUmar ibn al-Khattab (may Allah be pleased with him): Faith has paths, laws, limits and obligations; whoever completes them completes his faith, and whoever does not complete them has not completed his faith.

Ibn al-Mubarak said, from al-Hasan: "Except for kinship," with the increase of faith, or I would reject the Book of Allah the Exalted.

﴿Do they not see﴾: the common readers read it with *yāʾ*, as a report about the hypocrites mentioned. Hamzah and Yaʿqub read *tarawna* with *tāʾ*, addressing the believers; this is the reading of Ubayy ibn Kaʿb. Al-Aʿmash read *awa lam tara*, and Talhah read *awa lā tarā*, which is the reading of ʿAbd Allah ibn ʿUmar. ﴿That they are tested once or twice every year﴾, i.e., are examined. He said: they lie one or two lies, and they pray in it (i.e., during it). Mujahid said: they are tested by drought and high prices. ʿAtiyyah said: by illnesses and pains, and these are the precursors of death.

Qatadah said: by raids and jihad. It is also said: by the enemy. It is also said: they are tested, so they recognize (the truth) once and deny it another time. Murrah al-Hamdani said: they are tested, they disbelieve. Muqatil ibn Hayyan said: they are exposed by displaying their hypocrisy. ʿIkrimah said: they practise hypocrisy, then believe, then practise hypocrisy again, just as they break their covenant once or twice a year. (See Zad al-Masir, 3/353.) ﴿Then they do not repent﴾ of their breaking (of covenant), ﴿nor do they take heed﴾ [by what Allah has done to them].

When they broke their covenants, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) would send expeditions against them, and they would kill them.

Al-Dahhak: They are tested by high prices, affliction, withholding of rain, and the loss of fruits; then they do not return from their hypocrisy, nor do they reflect on the greatness of Allah. In the reading of ʿAbd Allah: ﴿Nor do they remember﴾.

﴿And when a surah is revealed﴾ containing the disgrace and rebuke of the hypocrites, ﴿some of them look at others﴾. This is an abridged expression, its implied meaning being: they look at one another and say, or signal: ﴿"Does anyone see you?"﴾ if you stand up. If they did not see anyone, they would leave the mosque; if they noticed someone seeing them, they would stand up and go away. ﴿Then they turn away﴾ from faith in it. Al-Dahhak said: ﴿"Does anyone see you?"﴾ means: that anyone among them might discover your inner secrets, for fear of being killed. Allah said: ﴿Allah has turned their hearts away from faith in the Qur'an﴾ ﴿because they are a people who do not understand.﴾ Ibn ʿAbbas said: Do not say when you have prayed: "We have departed from the prayer," for a people departed and Allah turned their hearts. Rather say: "We have completed the prayer." (Tafsir al-Tabari, 11/99–101.)

﴿There has certainly come to you a Messenger from among yourselves﴾. The common reading is with a *ḍamma* on the *fāʾ*, i.e., from your lineage: you know his lineage and his noble standing, and that he is from a tribe of the Arabs, from the sons of Ismaʿil. From al-Dahhak, from Ibn ʿAbbas: (﴿And when a surah is revealed﴾) means a clear (*muḥkamah*) surah containing the lawful and the unlawful. ﴿Some of them say: "Which of you has had his faith increased by this?"﴾ ﴿As for those who believe, it has increased their faith﴾ and affirmation regarding the obligations, together with their faith in the Most Merciful. ﴿And they rejoice﴾ at the revelation of the obligations. ﴿But as for those in whose hearts is a disease﴾, meaning doubt and hypocrisy, ﴿it has increased them in filth upon their filth﴾, i.e., disbelief upon their disbelief, misguidance upon their misguidance, and doubt upon their doubt.

Muqatil said: sin upon their sin. ﴿And they die while they are disbelievers.﴾ Mujahid said regarding this verse: Faith increases and decreases.

ʿUmar ibn al-Khattab (may Allah be pleased with him) said: If the faith of Abu Bakr (may Allah be pleased with him) were weighed against the faith of all the people of the earth, it would outweigh them. Yes, faith indeed increases and decreases, he said it three times.

Zayd al-Shami narrated from Dharr, who said: ʿUmar would take the hand of a man or two of his companions and say: "Come, let us increase in faith."

ʿAli ibn Abi Talib (peace be upon him) said: Faith appears as a white speck in the heart; as faith grows greater, the whiteness spreads until the whole heart becomes white. And hypocrisy appears as a black speck in the heart; as hypocrisy grows, that blackness increases until the whole heart becomes black. By Allah, if you split open the heart of a believer, you would find it white, and if you split open the heart of a hypocrite, you would find it black.

Al-Hasan wrote to ʿUmar ibn al-Khattab (may Allah be pleased with him): Faith has paths, laws, limits and obligations; whoever completes them completes his faith, and whoever does not complete them has not completed his faith.

Ibn al-Mubarak said, from al-Hasan: "Except for kinship," with the increase of faith, or I would reject the Book of Allah the Exalted.

﴿Do they not see﴾: the common readers read it with *yāʾ*, as a report about the hypocrites mentioned. Hamzah and Yaʿqub read *tarawna* with *tāʾ*, addressing the believers; this is the reading of Ubayy ibn Kaʿb. Al-Aʿmash read *awa lam tara*, and Talhah read *awa lā tarā*, which is the reading of ʿAbd Allah ibn ʿUmar. ﴿That they are tested once or twice every year﴾, i.e., are examined. He said: they lie one or two lies, and they pray in it (i.e., during it). Mujahid said: they are tested by drought and high prices. ʿAtiyyah said: by illnesses and pains, and these are the precursors of death.

Qatadah said: by raids and jihad. It is also said: by the enemy. It is also said: they are tested, so they recognize (the truth) once and deny it another time. Murrah al-Hamdani said: they are tested, they disbelieve. Muqatil ibn Hayyan said: they are exposed by displaying their hypocrisy. ʿIkrimah said: they practise hypocrisy, then believe, then practise hypocrisy again, just as they break their covenant once or twice a year. (See Zad al-Masir, 3/353.) ﴿Then they do not repent﴾ of their breaking (of covenant), ﴿nor do they take heed﴾ [by what Allah has done to them].

When they broke their covenants, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) would send expeditions against them, and they would kill them.

Al-Hasan: They are tested by striving in the way of Allah with His Messenger, and they see the truth of Allah's promise of victory and triumph over whoever Allah opposes. ﴿Then they do not repent﴾ despite what they see of the truth of Allah's promise, and they do not take admonition. Al-Dahhak: They are tested by high prices, affliction, withholding of rain, and the loss of fruits; then they do not return from their hypocrisy, nor do they reflect on the greatness of Allah. In the reading of ʿAbd Allah: ﴿Nor do they remember﴾.

﴿And when a surah is revealed﴾ containing the disgrace and rebuke of the hypocrites, ﴿some of them look at others﴾. This is an abridged expression, its implied meaning being: they look at one another and say, or signal: ﴿"Does anyone see you?"﴾ if you stand up. If they did not see anyone, they would leave the mosque; if they noticed someone seeing them, they would stand up and go away. ﴿Then they turn away﴾ from faith in it. Al-Dahhak said: ﴿"Does anyone see you?"﴾ means: that anyone among them might discover your inner secrets, for fear of being killed. Allah said: ﴿Allah has turned their hearts away from faith in the Qur'an﴾ ﴿because they are a people who do not understand.﴾ Ibn ʿAbbas said: Do not say when you have prayed: "We have departed from the prayer," for a people departed and Allah turned their hearts. Rather say: "We have completed the prayer." (Tafsir al-Tabari, 11/99–101.)

﴿There has certainly come to you a Messenger from among yourselves﴾. The common reading is with a *ḍamma* on the *fāʾ*, i.e., from your lineage: you know his lineage and his noble standing, and that he is from a tribe of the Arabs, from the sons of Ismaʿil. Ibn ʿAbbas said: There is no tribe among the Arabs except that the Prophet (ﷺ) was born to them, their Mudar, their Rabiʿah and their Yemen. (Tarikh Dimashq, 3/95, ed. Dar al-Fikr.)

Al-Sadiq said: He was not touched by anything from the births of the Jahiliyyah.

We were informed by Abu ʿAbd Allah ibn Hamid, who said: Hamid ibn Muhammad told us, ʿAli ibn ʿAbd al-ʿAziz told us, Muhammad ibn Abi Hashim told me, from al-Madani, from Abu al-Huwayrith, from Ibn ʿAbbas, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "I was not born of the illicit unions of the people of the Jahiliyyah; I was born only of marriages like the marriages of Islam." From your saying: "a precious thing" (*shayʾ nafīs*) when it is desired. Yaman said: from the highest of you in lineage. ﴿He is mighty﴾, severe, ﴿against him is what distresses you﴾: *mā* is an extra particle; the meaning is your distress (*ʿanatakum*), which is the arrival of hardship and harm upon you. Ibn ʿAbbas said: what misguides you. Al-Dahhak and al-Kalbi said: what makes you sinful. Al-ʿUtaybi said: your distress and your harm. Ibn al-Anbari said: what causes you to perish. ﴿Ardent over you﴾, i.e., over your faith, your guidance and your righteousness. Qatadah said: ardent over your misguided, that Allah may guide them. Al-Farra' said: *al-ḥarīṣ* is the miserly, that you should enter the Fire.

﴿Kind and merciful to the believers.﴾ It is said: *ra'ūf* means gentle and compassionate; *raḥīm* means merciful. It is said: *ra'ūf* to the obedient, *raḥīm* to the sinners; *ra'ūf* to His servants, *raḥīm* to His friends; *ra'ūf* to whoever sees him, *raḥīm* to whoever has not seen him.

ʿAbd al-ʿAziz ibn Yahya said: The arrangement of the verse: ﴿There has certainly come to you a Messenger from among yourselves, mighty, ardent over you, kind and merciful to the believers, against whom what distresses you is grievous to him.﴾ He is concerned with nothing but your affair, and he is the one who stands in intercession, so do not be distressed by what distresses you, as long as you adhere to his sunnah, for nothing pleases him except your entry into Paradise,

due to his saying (ﷺ): "Whoever leaves behind wealth, it is for his heirs; and whoever leaves behind a debt or dependants, it is upon me and to me." [75]

﴿But if they turn away﴾, i.e., turn away from faith and oppose you, ﴿say: "Allah is sufficient for me; there is no god but He. In Him I have put my trust, and He is the Lord of the Mighty Throne."﴾ The common reading is with a *kasra* on the *mīm* in *al-ʿarsh* (as a genitive). Ibn Muhaysin read *al-ʿaẓīm* with a *ḍamma*, as an adjective of the Lord. Al-Husayn ibn al-Fadl said: Allah did not gather for any of the prophets two of His names together except for the Prophet (ﷺ), for He said: ﴿kind and merciful to the believers﴾, and He said: ﴿Indeed, Allah is to the people Kind, Merciful.﴾ [[Surah al-Baqarah: 143.]]

Ubayy ibn Kaʿb said: The most recent of the Qur'an to be given to Allah the Exalted is ﴿There has certainly come to you a Messenger﴾ to the end of the surah.

﴿وَما كانَ الْمُؤْمِنُونَ لِيَنْفِرُوا كَافَّةً﴾ (It is not for the believers to go forth all together) etc.
